S 级 系统治疗 前瞻/干预性(非随机) IF 44.5
靶向具核梭杆菌：甲硝唑联合替雷利珠单抗及呋喹替尼治疗MSS结直肠癌的多中心II期研究
Targeting F.nucleatum with metronidazole plus tislelizumab and fruquintinib in MSS colorectal cancer: A multicenter phase 2 study.
Cancer Cell · 2026-11 · Jiang S, Lin X, Ni L, Zhang Y, Chen H, Liu C, et al.
研究背景：具核梭杆菌（Fusobacterium nucleatum）与结直肠癌化疗耐药及免疫逃逸相关，但针对该菌的治疗策略仍十分有限，尤其在微卫星稳定（MSS）型结直肠癌这一免疫治疗难点人群中缺乏有效方案。
核心结果：这项多中心单臂2期试验纳入33例具核梭杆菌阳性MSS转移性结直肠癌患者，接受替雷利珠单抗+呋喹替尼+甲硝唑联合治疗，达到主要终点，中位无进展生存期为6.0个月，客观缓解率19.4%、疾病控制率83.9%；3级治疗相关不良事件发生率为30.3%，无4级或5级事件。宏基因组分析显示甲硝唑可降低具核梭杆菌丰度，探索性分析提示临床获益与乳杆菌属富集相关、无应答与肠球菌属相关，且将应答者粪菌移植至无菌小鼠可增强细胞毒性CD8 T细胞介导的抗肿瘤效应。
意义与启示：该研究首次在MSS结直肠癌中验证“抗菌+免疫+抗血管”三联策略的可行性与疗效，为以肠道菌群为靶点克服免疫治疗耐药提供了临床证据；对课题的启示在于可将具核梭杆菌等特定菌群作为生物标志物富集人群，并探索菌群调控（抗生素/粪菌移植）与免疫联合的协同机制。
评分明细：设计 22/30 · 验证 8/15 · 机制 11/15 · 影响力 20/20 · 契合度 18/20 = 79/100 ｜ 等级理由：多中心前瞻性II期试验达主要终点，首次验证靶向菌群联合方案在MSS肠癌的疗效，具实践改变潜力。

S 级 综合及其他 系统综述/Meta IF 88.5
林奇综合征：从生物学到临床管理的综合综述
Lynch syndrome.
Lancet (london, England) · 2026-11 · Ryan NAJ, Gallon R, McVeigh T, Monahan KJ, Moeslein G, Church DN, et al.
研究背景：Lynch综合征是最常见的遗传性癌症易感综合征，约每350-450人中即有1例，但多数携带者仍未获诊断，构成巨大且可预防的公共卫生负担；该病由DNA错配修复（MMR）基因胚系致病变异引起，显著且异质地升高结直肠癌、子宫内膜癌及多种肠外肿瘤风险。
核心结果：综述系统整合了Lynch综合征全程管理进展：以肿瘤MMR缺陷普筛为核心的分子诊断策略显著改善了病例识别，并使针对高危亲属的胚系检测与级联筛查成为可能；结肠镜监测、阿司匹林化学预防与降低风险手术等预防手段有效，但需按基因型与个体情况实施；MMR缺陷肿瘤的免疫原性生物学使免疫检查点抑制剂带来显著获益，疫苗等拦截策略亦展现前景。同时指出诊断路径各环节存在明显脱落与医疗可及性不均等问题。
意义与启示：该综述提示在结直肠癌（含肝转移）诊疗中应常规开展MMR/MSI检测以识别Lynch综合征及指导免疫治疗，并强调将分子筛查、遗传咨询、家系级联检测与基因型个体化预防整合为公平可及的全程管理体系，对本课题的遗传筛查路径设计与免疫治疗人群选择具有直接启示。
评分明细：设计 20/30 · 验证 10/15 · 机制 10/15 · 影响力 20/20 · 契合度 18/20 = 78/100 ｜ 等级理由：发表于高影响因子期刊的综合性综述，全面覆盖林奇综合征诊疗全流程，对临床实践有指导意义。

S 级 转化研究 基础机制 IF 45.8
干细胞样CD4+ T细胞分化与结直肠癌外周免疫招募机制
Differentiation of stem-like CD4
Science (new York, N.Y.) · 2026-11 · Zhang Y, Nie H, Dai Z, Zhao L, Wan Y, Wang Y, et al.
研究背景：癌症免疫治疗策略多聚焦于瘤内免疫抑制微环境，而对外周T细胞的扩增及促进其向肿瘤募集的研究尚不充分；本研究利用成像质谱流式技术分析结直肠癌（CRC）患者样本，探讨干细胞样CD4⁺ T细胞的分化及其意义。
核心结果：在CRC患者中观察到辅助性T细胞1（Th1）样表型与干细胞样CD4⁺ T细胞分化相关，该类细胞可能在外周被扩增并向肿瘤募集；成像质谱流式揭示了肿瘤组织中CD4⁺ T细胞亚群的空间分布特征（摘要信息有限，具体效应量未提供）。
意义与启示：提示外周干细胞样CD4⁺ T细胞的分化与募集可作为增强CRC免疫治疗的新靶点，为课题中关注外周免疫启动而非仅瘤内微环境提供依据。
评分明细：设计 18/30 · 验证 8/15 · 机制 14/15 · 影响力 20/20 · 契合度 16/20 = 76/100 ｜ 等级理由：基于影像质谱流式的人体样本机制研究，创新性强但尚无临床干预验证，暂不改变实践。

S 级 转化研究 基础机制 IF 20.8
肠道菌群调控瘤内胆固醇代谢生成4-胆甾烯-3-酮抑制结直肠癌
Microbiota-based modulation of intratumoral cholesterol metabolism for colorectal cancer treatment.
Nature Metabolism · 2026-11 · Wu J, Li L, Lai Y, Li J, Asthana P, Zhai L, et al.
研究背景：结直肠癌中胆固醇蓄积促进肿瘤进展，但全身性降胆固醇治疗获益有限且存在安全性隐患，因此需要寻找选择性靶向肿瘤内胆固醇代谢的新策略。
核心结果：研究发现肠道菌群代谢胆固醇生成的4-胆甾烯-3-酮（4-C-3）在CRC患者粪便和肿瘤样本中显著减少；4-C-3在CRC细胞系、患者来源类器官和异种移植模型中均抑制肿瘤生长，机制上通过抑制EGFR激活并使突变型致癌KRAS稳定于失活状态，从而克服KRAS驱动的抗EGFR治疗耐药；利用天然产4-C-3的Oscillibacter ruminantium或工程化非致病性大肠杆菌恢复4-C-3，可降低瘤内胆固醇并在临床前模型中诱导肿瘤消退且无明显毒性。
意义与启示：该研究揭示了一条可通过微生物组工程调控的菌群-胆固醇代谢通路，为选择性靶向CRC并克服抗EGFR耐药提供了新的治疗思路，提示工程菌或特定菌株可作为潜在的辅助治疗手段。
评分明细：设计 22/30 · 验证 10/15 · 机制 14/15 · 影响力 14/20 · 契合度 16/20 = 76/100 ｜ 等级理由：临床前多模型验证但尚未进入临床试验，机制创新性强但实践改变需进一步人体研究。

S 级 系统治疗 其他 IF 44.5
抗生素靶向厌氧菌逆转结直肠癌促瘤菌群失调
Antibiotics counteracting tumor-promoting dysbiosis in colorectal cancer.
Cancer Cell · 2026-11 · Zitvogel L, Fidelle M, Kroemer G
研究背景：抗生素通常被认为会破坏肠道菌群并削弱免疫检查点阻断疗效，但特定靶向厌氧菌的抗生素策略是否能在结直肠癌中逆转促癌菌群失调尚不明确。
核心结果：Jiang等在Cancer Cell报道，在Fusobacterium nucleatum阳性的微卫星稳定型转移性结直肠癌中，脉冲式厌氧菌靶向甲硝唑联合抗PD-1抗体及VEGFR抑制剂取得令人鼓舞的无进展生存期，且选择性瓦解致病共生菌网络而不引起全局性菌群失调。
意义与启示：该研究提示精准靶向促癌厌氧菌（如F. nucleatum）可解除免疫检查点阻断抵抗，为MSS型mCRC提供了菌群导向的联合治疗新策略，并启示课题应关注菌群特异性干预而非广谱抗生素。
评分明细：设计 18/30 · 验证 8/15 · 机制 10/15 · 影响力 20/20 · 契合度 18/20 = 74/100 ｜ 等级理由：Cancer Cell述评，基于Jiang等前瞻性研究，提出菌群靶向联合治疗新策略，具改变MSS mCRC实践潜力。

S 级 转化研究 基础机制 IF 21.7
CARM1通过H3R17me2a/FUS上调介导结直肠癌缺氧相关化疗耐药
CARM1 orchestrates hypoxia-mediated chemoresistance through the H3R17me2a/FUS upregulation in colorectal cancer.
Drug Resistance Updates : Reviews and Commentaries in Antimicrobial and Anticancer Chemotherapy · 2026-11 · Fu JL, Lin SC, Hsu PL, Lin TC, Tai YJ, Chang KL, et al.
研究背景：缺氧是结直肠癌化疗耐药的重要驱动因素，但其背后的表观遗传机制尚不清楚。本研究旨在鉴定介导该过程的关键表观遗传调控因子及其作用通路。
核心结果：研究发现CARM1在恶性上皮细胞中高表达且与不良预后相关；缺氧通过ERK-EGR1通路转录上调CARM1，同时抑制DUSP2以维持该轴激活。CARM1通过催化FUS启动子区H3R17me2a上调FUS表达，减少基因毒性应激诱导的DNA损伤从而促进耐药；敲除CARM1可使p53野生型（HCT116）和p53突变型（HT-29）细胞对化疗敏感。奥沙利铂耐药细胞即使在常氧下也通过持续抑制DUSP2维持高CARM1/FUS水平，且CARM1抑制剂EZM2302可破坏该轴并增强难治性原位小鼠模型的化疗疗效。
意义与启示：该研究揭示了EGR1-CARM1-FUS轴是结直肠癌化疗耐药的关键驱动通路，提示CARM1可作为克服耐药的潜在表观遗传治疗靶点，并为耐药细胞与缺氧适应细胞共享信号特征提供了新认识。
评分明细：设计 18/30 · 验证 10/15 · 机制 14/15 · 影响力 14/20 · 契合度 16/20 = 72/100 ｜ 等级理由：基础机制研究，但发现可成药靶点CARM1并在小鼠模型验证，具有转化潜力，尚未进入临床。

S 级 综合及其他 基础机制 IF 48.5
IgA抑制上皮增殖与肿瘤发生
Suppression of epithelial proliferation and tumorigenesis by IgA.
Nature · 2026-11 · Donaldson GP, Lima Dos Reis G, Saad M, Wichmann C, Mamede I, Chen G, et al.
研究背景：IgA是哺乳动物产生最多的抗体同种型，在黏膜免疫稳态中具有专门作用，但其对上皮细胞增殖和肿瘤发生的直接调控作用尚不清楚。
核心结果：该研究发现IgA能够抑制上皮细胞增殖和肿瘤发生，提示IgA除经典免疫防御功能外，还通过调控上皮增殖参与黏膜组织稳态维持，从而抑制肿瘤起始。
意义与启示：该研究揭示了IgA在黏膜上皮稳态与肿瘤抑制中的新功能，为理解结直肠癌等黏膜相关肿瘤的免疫调控机制提供了新视角，并提示IgA信号通路可能成为黏膜肿瘤预防或治疗的潜在靶点。
评分明细：设计 18/30 · 验证 8/15 · 机制 14/15 · 影响力 20/20 · 契合度 12/20 = 72/100 ｜ 等级理由：基础机制研究，发表于高水平期刊，但尚处临床前阶段，暂不改变临床实践。

S 级 综合及其他 指南/共识 IF 16.4
NCCN结肠癌指南2026年第3版更新要点
NCCN Guidelines® Insights: Colon Cancer, Version 3.2026.
Journal of the National Comprehensive Cancer Network : JNCCN · 2026-11 · Benson AB, Venook AP, Adam M, Ambelil M, Bray A, Chang GJ, et al.
研究背景：结直肠癌是美国第四大常见癌症和第二大癌症死因，局限期以手术±辅助全身治疗为主，晚期/转移性则依据生物标志物状态进行多线系统治疗。NCCN结肠癌指南Version 3.2026基于最新证据对多个关键环节进行了更新。
核心结果：本次更新主要包括三方面：①推荐在氟尿嘧啶类治疗前进行DPYD基因检测，以降低严重氟尿嘧啶毒性风险；②依据近期临床试验结果更新非转移性结肠癌的辅助治疗方案；③按生物标志物状态重新组织晚期/转移性疾病的系统治疗推荐，并重点修订了BRAF V600E突变阳性患者的治疗建议。
意义与启示：该指南更新将药物基因组学（DPYD）、辅助治疗循证优化和分子分型精准治疗整合进结肠癌全程管理，提示课题设计应关注DPYD检测的落地可行性、辅助治疗人群分层，以及BRAF V600E等分子亚型的靶向联合策略。
评分明细：设计 25/30 · 验证 10/15 · 机制 5/15 · 影响力 11/20 · 契合度 20/20 = 71/100 ｜ 等级理由：NCCN指南为国际权威临床实践指南，基于最新临床试验证据更新，直接影响临床决策。

S 级 转化研究 基础机制 IF 15.6
超声驱动裂解肿瘤内细菌唤醒先天免疫用于系统性癌症治疗
Ultrasound-Driven Lysis of Tumor-Resident Bacteria Awakens Innate Immunity for Systemic Cancer Therapy.
Journal of the American Chemical Society · 2026-11 · Zhou W, Zhu H, Liu Y, Li H, Wu M, Li S, et al.
研究背景：肿瘤内定植细菌（如具核梭杆菌）营造免疫抑制微环境，削弱免疫治疗效果；广谱抗生素会导致全身菌群失调，且革兰阴性菌外膜限制传统声敏剂进入，制约声动力疗法（SDT）的抗菌效力。
核心结果：本研究设计聚精氨酸功能化肽-声敏剂偶联物，通过静电作用嵌入革兰阴性菌膜造成结构预破坏，超声辐照下声化学氧化与机械剪切力协同彻底粉碎肿瘤内具核梭杆菌，释放大量病原体相关分子模式（PAMPs）；在细菌定植的小鼠结直肠癌模型中，该局部治疗显著抑制原发肿瘤生长，并引发针对远端肿瘤的远隔效应和抗肿瘤免疫记忆。
意义与启示：该策略将肿瘤内细菌转化为内源性佐剂，逆转细菌介导的免疫抑制，为治疗微生物定植的实体瘤（如结直肠癌肝转移）提供了变革性范式，并提示靶向清除瘤内细菌可增强系统抗肿瘤免疫。
评分明细：设计 18/30 · 验证 8/15 · 机制 14/15 · 影响力 10/20 · 契合度 16/20 = 66/100 ｜ 等级理由：研究发表于高影响力期刊，但为临床前动物实验，尚未进入临床验证，实践改变潜力有限。

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Self-expandable metal stents (SEMSs) are used as a bridge to surgery (BTS) or for palliation (PAL) in malignant colorectal obstruction, but high axial force may contribute to perforation. We prospectively evaluated the efficacy and safety of the low-axial-force Naturfit colonic stent in both settings. This prospective multicenter single-arm study enrolled 208 patients at 11 Japanese institutions between 2019 and 2022 (BTS, Technical success and clinical success of colorectal stenting were both 99.0%, with perforation in three patients (1.4%). In the BTS cohort, clinical success of BTS was 97.1%; no perforations occurred, and early and late adverse-event rates were 1.5% and 3.7%. All patients underwent elective surgery; colostomy and laparoscopic surgery rates were 4.4% and 87.6%. In the palliative cohort, clinical success of colorectal stenting was 98.6%, late adverse events occurred in 16.9%, and 12-month overall survival and stent patency were 46.6% and 67.6%. Naturfit achieved high technical and clinical success of colorectal stenting with a low perforation rate. These findings support its feasibility for malignant colorectal obstruction in both BTS and palliative settings, although comparative studies are needed to determine relative advantages over other SEMSs. University Hospital Medical Information Network Clinical Trial Registry: UMIN000035224.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To compare relative research funding and basic and translational science publications for gynecologic cancers vs. other common cancers, normalized to incidence and mortality rates. SEER data were used to investigate incidence and deaths in the US from 2004 to 2024. Research funding was derived from National Cancer Institute (NCI) data. Google Scholar was utilized to identify oncology and medicine related journals with the highest H-indices. All abstracts on PubMed were reviewed and number of basic and translational science articles manually calculated. In 2024, new diagnoses of breast, prostate, lung, and colorectal cancers totaled 313,510, 299,010, 234,580, and 152,810, respectively. Endometrial, ovarian, and cervical cancers accounted for 67,880, 19,680, and 13,820, respectively.NCI funding in 2023 was approximately $542.0 million for breast, $258.6 million for prostate, $435.0 million for lung, and $238.6 million for colorectal cancers, compared to $20.0 million, $132.0 million, and $20.7 million for endometrial, ovarian, and cervical cancers, respectively.Across the highest impact journals from 2004 to 2024, 24,169 basic/translational science publications were found: 8859 (breast), 4161 (prostate), 3537 (lung), 4321 (colorectal), 412 (endometrial), 2231 (ovarian), and 648 (cervical). When adjusted for incidence, ovarian cancer had the highest number of publications, at 220.9 publications per 100,000 cases. When adjusted for funding, endometrial cancer had the highest number of publications, at 23.1 publications per $1 million average annual NCI funding. Funding relative to disease burden varies considerably among gynecologic cancers. Endometrial cancer receives the lowest NCI funding of any cancer studied when adjusted by incidence and mortality. Despite this, endometrial cancer produced the most basic and translational science publications per dollar.

Metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) shows organ-specific patterns of dissemination. Approximately 20% of patients develop disease confined to the liver throughout the course. Early recognition and characterisation of this phenotype may inform therapeutic stratification and improve outcomes. We retrospectively analysed patients with unresectable mCRC. Patients were classified by metastatic distribution into liver-limited, liver plus extrahepatic, or extrahepatic-only disease. Clinicopathological features, genomic alterations assessed by next-generation sequencing, and immune contexture based on a 12-gene signature from the primary tumour were evaluated. Among 1026 eligible patients, 20% had permanently liver-limited disease, 51% had both hepatic and extrahepatic involvement, and 29% had extrahepatic-only metastases. Liver-limited cases were enriched for synchronous presentation and nonrectal primaries, with a lower prevalence of KRAS mutations ( Permanent liver-limited mCRC defines a clinically and biologically distinct subgroup characterised by synchronous onset, nonrectal primaries, and reduced KRAS mutation frequency. The immune landscape of the primary tumour was associated with metastatic organ pattern.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Patients with gastrointestinal (GI) malignancies and hyperbilirubinemia secondary to liver metastases are routinely excluded from clinical trials, leaving their management without evidence-based guidance. Oxaliplatin, cleared through non-enzymatic biotransformation and renal excretion, is a rational candidate in this setting. The present study examined the feasibility, safety and outcomes of folinic acid, fluorouracil and oxaliplatin (FOLFOX)-based chemotherapy in this population. The present retrospective, single-center analysis included 27 patients with histologically confirmed metastatic GI cancers (gastric, biliary tract, pancreatic and colorectal) with serum total bilirubin of ≥4.5 mg/dl at treatment initiation who received individualized FOLFOX-based chemotherapy at Etlik City Hospital (Ankara, Türkiye) between July 2023 and March 2025. Bilirubin response was defined as a ≥50% reduction within 4-8 weeks or normalization to ≤1.2 mg/dl within 12 weeks. Survival was estimated by Kaplan-Meier analysis; Cox regression identified predictors of progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS). Median baseline bilirubin was 6.9 mg/dl. Bilirubin declined significantly at weeks 4, 8 and 12 (medians 3.0, 2.5 and 0.8 mg/dl; P<0.001, P=0.009 and P=0.001 vs. baseline). Among Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors-evaluable patients (11/27), the objective response rate was 72.7% and disease control rate 81.8%. Median PFS was 2.56 months [95% confidence interval (CI) 1.81-3.65] and median OS 3.65 months (95% CI 2.56-5.72). A ≥50% bilirubin reduction at week 4 was associated with longer PFS [univariable hazard ratio (HR) 0.37; 95% CI 0.14-0.93; log-rank P=0.028] and longer OS (univariable HR 0.37; 95% CI 0.14-0.94; log-rank P=0.030) in a week 4 landmark analysis performed to address immortal time bias. In the present cohort of patients with Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group Performance Status 0-1 and severe hyperbilirubinemia due to liver metastases, FOLFOX achieved rapid bilirubin reductions without grade ≥3 hepatotoxicity. Early bilirubin response was associated with longer survival in the present small, exploratory analysis; these hypothesis-generating findings warrant prospective validation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a common malignancy with a rising global incidence. While genetic alterations such as mutations in APC, KRAS and TP53 are well-established in CRC pathogenesis, the role of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and cell adhesion molecules in tumor progression has gained increasing attention. Among key regulators, p53 and β-catenin serve critical roles in EMT and tumor behavior. In the present study, 171 patients with CRC who underwent curative resection between 2000 and 2007 were retrospectively analyzed. Immunohistochemistry was performed to evaluate p53 expression and β-catenin localization (nuclear vs. cytoplasmic). β-catenin staining intensity was classified as negative, weakly positive or strongly positive. Overall survival (OS) was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis and the log-rank test, and independent prognostic factors were identified using multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression analysis. Neither p53 expression nor nuclear β-catenin intensity was significantly associated with OS in either colon or rectal cancer. By contrast, among patients with rectal cancer (n=103), those with lower cytoplasmic β-catenin intensity exhibited significantly worse OS compared with those with higher intensity (median OS, 94 months vs. not reached; P=0.026). This association remained significant in multivariate analysis (hazard ratio, 2.27; 95% CI, 1.06-4.85; P=0.034), independent of TNM stage and other covariates. These findings indicated that β-catenin intensity may serve as a clinically relevant prognostic biomarker in rectal cancer, whereas p53 expression and nuclear β-catenin intensity have limited prognostic value.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
5-Fluorouracil (5-FU) is a key drug in the treatment of advanced colorectal cancer (CRC). Although 5-FU is generally well tolerated, a small subset of patients may experience life-threatening neurotoxicity. Among these complications, 5-FU-induced encephalopathy accompanied by severe hyperlactatemia is a particularly serious metabolic emergency. Impaired drug clearance, especially due to underlying renal insufficiency, may substantially increase this risk. In the present study, the cases of three patients with advanced CRC who developed acute, severe impairment of consciousness 48 h after receiving 5-FU-based chemotherapy were retrospectively reviewed. Clinical presentations ranged from aphasia and confusion to deep coma. All patients exhibited marked hyperlactatemia, with peak blood lactate levels of 18.0, 18.19 and 15.56 mmol/l for Cases 1, 2 and 3, respectively. A total of two patients had marked baseline renal impairment (one with chronic kidney disease, the other with end-stage renal disease on maintenance hemodialysis). Neuroimaging (CT/CT perfusion/CT angiography/MRI) excluded acute cerebrovascular events in all cases. Chemotherapy was immediately discontinued and intensive supportive care was initiated. For the patient with anuric renal failure, early continuous venovenous hemofiltration was initiated. All three patients achieved complete neurological recovery and normalization of metabolic parameters. Notably, the hemodialysis-dependent patient subsequently underwent successful 5-FU rechallenge using a 50% dose reduction combined with prophylactic post-chemotherapy hemodialysis, without recurrence of neurotoxicity. 5-FU-induced severe hyperlactatemic encephalopathy is a potentially fatal oncological emergency. Underlying renal impairment may lead to the accumulation of toxic metabolites. For patients presenting with extreme hyperlactatemia (>10 mmol/l) and profound impairment of consciousness, early initiation of continuous renal replacement therapy may be an effective strategy to resolve neurological dysfunction. In patients with end-stage renal disease requiring subsequent fluoropyrimidine therapy, substantial dose reduction combined with prophylactic hemodialysis may offer a feasible rechallenge approach. Furthermore, clinicians must consider genetic mutations related to hepatotoxicity and nephrotoxicity. Evaluation of these organ-vulnerability genes before chemotherapy warrants further clinical investigation to prevent severe toxicity.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Perforated colorectal carcinoma may present with inflammatory and septic features that obscure the underlying malignancy. Tumors arising at the hepatic flexure are particularly challenging because of their close anatomical relationship with the liver, allowing perforation-related inflammation and necrotic hepatic metastases to mimic pyogenic hepatic abscesses on imaging. A 58-year-old man with hypertension and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection receiving antiretroviral therapy presented with acute abdominal pain, fever, chills, and systemic inflammatory symptoms. Ultrasound demonstrated hepatic lesions and irregular hepatic flexure wall thickening suspicious for malignancy, while contrast-enhanced CT showed multiple abscess-like hepatic lesions with features of both metastatic disease and perforation-related inflammation. Emergency laparotomy revealed a perforated hepatic flexure tumor densely adherent to the liver, with fibrinopurulent exudate, an inflammatory tract between the hepatic flexure and adjacent liver, multiple hepatic nodules, and peritoneal tumor seeding; histopathology confirmed moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma with hepatic and nodal metastases and central necrosis in the hepatic lesions (pT4N2M1). This case highlights the diagnostic overlap between pyogenic hepatic abscesses and necrotic hepatic metastases associated with perforated colorectal carcinoma. When abscess-like hepatic lesions coexist with irregular colonic wall thickening, regional lymphadenopathy, or loss of normal tissue planes, colorectal malignancy should remain an important consideration despite accompanying inflammatory features.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Immunotherapy has revolutionized the treatment landscape of colorectal cancer (CRC), improving clinical outcomes in microsatellite instability-high tumors. In contrast, microsatellite stable (MSS) CRC exhibits intrinsic resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), driven by reduced neoantigen load, resulting in an immunologically 'cold' tumor microenvironment (TME). To overcome these barriers, combination strategies integrating ICIs with tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) have been investigated based on their ability to inhibit multiple oncogenic and angiogenic signaling pathways. Beyond their antiangiogenic effects, preclinical evidence has demonstrated that TKIs can induce immunological reprogramming of the TME, promoting proinflammatory macrophage polarization, antigen presentation, vascular normalization, and T-cell infiltration. This evidence supported several early-phase clinical trials evaluating TKI-ICI combinations, showing encouraging signals of clinical activity in refractory MSS CRC. Recently, the interim analysis of the phase III STELLAR-303 trial demonstrated an overall survival benefit with the combination of zanzalintinib plus atezolizumab compared with regorafenib in pretreated MSS CRC. Notably, a consistent exploratory finding across the TKI-ICI trials was the potential role of liver metastases in driving local and systemic immunosuppression. Preclinical MSS CRC mouse models confirmed this suggestion, highlighting the association between the presence of liver metastases and impaired effector T-cell responses and antigen presentation. Overall, the heterogeneity of clinical outcomes underscores the complexity of immune resistance in MSS CRC and supports the development of multimodal biomarkers integrating spatial pathology, immune profiling, and artificial intelligence. This review discusses current preclinical and clinical evidence on TKI-ICI combinations in MSS CRC, exploring emerging mechanisms of immune resistance and potential therapeutic vulnerabilities.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Radiotherapy remains underutilized in colon cancer despite the intrinsic radiosensitivity of colon cancer cells, largely because accurate targeting of tumors within the highly mobile colon is technically challenging. Tumor motion caused by peristalsis, bowel motility, and respiration limits the precision of radiation delivery and increases the risk of damage to surrounding radiosensitive tissues. Current endoscopic tattooing agents used for tumor localization are used for operative localization only and lack radiographic visibility, may diffuse from the injection site, and can induce local inflammation. Here, we developed a thermo-responsive, CT-detectable, injectable fiducial marker composed of Poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (PNIPAM) loaded with barium sulfate (BaSO₄) for potential application in tumor localization during image-guided radiotherapy. The PNIPAM-BaSO₄ formulation remained injectable at room temperature and rapidly underwent in situ gelation within approximately 15 s at physiological temperature. Micro-CT imaging demonstrated strong dose-dependent radiopacity both in vitro and in vivo, supporting the potential of the marker for CT-based visualization. The marker exhibited stable mass retention for up to 280 days in vitro, and maintained stable localization and radiographic signal for 3 months in vivo without detectable diffusion. Histopathological analysis revealed no evidence of local inflammation, fibrosis, necrosis, or systemic toxicity, demonstrating excellent biocompatibility. Collectively, these findings establish the feasibility of the PNIPAM-BaSO₄ platform as a stable, CT-detectable fiducial marker and support its further development for potential application in image-guided radiotherapy. Future studies will evaluate its performance under clinically relevant radiotherapy imaging and treatment conditions, including its potential use for interfractional localization of mobile tumors.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To describe anticipated supportive post-discharge navigation service needs and examine associated factors among postoperative patients with colorectal cancer and comorbid diabetes discharged home. This cross-sectional study included 212 patients discharged home from a tertiary hospital in Shanghai between May and October 2025. Questionnaires were completed on the day of discharge. Data were collected using a demographic questionnaire, a self-developed supportive navigation service needs questionnaire, and measures of readiness for hospital discharge, patient activation, social support, and illness perception. Random forest and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) analyses with resampling procedures were used for exploratory variable selection, followed by multiple linear regression with bootstrap confidence intervals. The median supportive navigation service needs score was 148.00 (interquartile range, 140.25-160.00). The highest-scoring items concerned information about further treatment, glycemic management, and dietary guidance. In the adjusted model, female sex and diabetes duration of more than 10 years were associated with lower needs scores than male sex and diabetes duration of 5 years or less, respectively. Greater readiness for hospital discharge and social support were associated with lower needs scores, whereas greater perceived illness threat was associated with higher scores. Patient activation was not significantly associated with needs in the adjusted model. Patients with colorectal cancer and comorbid diabetes discharged home after surgery reported substantial anticipated needs for navigation support. These findings may inform post-discharge needs assessment and service development. Interpretation should remain cautious because the outcome was measured using a self-developed, study-specific composite needs index.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Primary colorectal cancer (CRC) biopsies and intestinal organoids are frequently compared to define tumor-associated epithelial alterations; however, these systems differ in malignant status, tissue composition, developmental state, and epithelial maturation. In this study, transcriptomic profiling of CRC biopsies, matched normal intestinal tissue, and iPSC-derived intestinal organoids (iIOs) was performed to define the biological axes separating primary tissue from organoid epithelial states. Transcriptome-wide analysis revealed strong separation between CRC biopsies and iIOs, with iIOs diverging from primary tissue more extensively than tumors differed from normal mucosa. Pathway enrichment and cell deconvolution showed that biopsies were dominated by immune, inflammatory, and stromal programs reflecting tissue complexity, whereas iIOs were enriched for proliferative, biosynthetic, and metabolic programs. Projection onto a malignancy axis placed iIOs at a neutral position, indicating that their divergence stems from developmental state rather than malignant transformation. Compared to normal mucosa, organoids reproducibly lost adult tissue-associated immune/stromal programs while gaining proliferative, fetal-like epithelial programs. Gut Cell Atlas scoring, crypt-surface positioning, and lineage deconvolution showed that iIOs retain intestinal epithelial identity but occupy a developmentally immature, crypt/progenitor-biased state dominated by transit-amplifying programs with limited differentiated lineage diversity. Metabolic module analysis and anabolism-proliferation correlation showed that elevated metabolic activity in iIOs, including biosynthetic and nucleotide synthesis programs. These reflect proliferation-coupled anabolism rather than malignancy-like metabolic reprogramming; the glycolysis-OXPHOS balance did not differ significantly between groups. Consequently, iIOs represent metabolically active, fetal-like, crypt/progenitor epithelial reference models rather than direct transcriptomic surrogates of adult intestinal mucosa or primary CRC tissue. These results clarify the utility and limitations of iIOs as epithelial reference models for colorectal cancer research.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a common malignant tumor of the digestive tract, and its incidence and mortality rank among the top three human cancers globally, posing a serious threat to human health. Dogs are considered to be translationally valuable, naturally occurring models for many types of cancer research. Dogs and humans share significant molecular homology in key pathways associated with CRC. The course of canine CRC often presents asymptomatically in its early stages, which is similar to the diagnostic dilemma of human CRC. At present, human clinical medicine is analyzing potential markers of CRC through advanced bioinformatics and multi-omics approaches, with a view to providing specific directions for diagnosis and treatment. However, most of the existing research on canine CRC is based on the results of human tumor research. While cross-disciplinary research is well-established in human medicine, its systematic application in veterinary oncology is growing and requires broader integration. With the completion of genome analyses of different animals, researchers have further leveraged the established field of cross-species comparative oncology. Canine CRC and human CRC have similar pathological characteristics and molecular mechanisms. In this review, we will conduct a detailed comparative analysis of canine CRC and human CRC, which can provide valuable insights to understand the difference and relationship between the two species and provide a comparative oncology basis for the occurrence and development of human CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) are two of the most frequently occurring and lethal cancers. Although numerous studies have investigated their transcriptional, molecular, and immunological landscapes, our current understanding remains incomplete. Both cancers pose major clinical challenges, and better understanding of their molecular and immunological profiles is needed to improve patient outcomes. We conducted total RNA sequencing and liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry-based proteomic profiling of 29 diagnostic biopsies from both primary tumors and metastatic sites in 16 CRC and 11 PDAC patients. Due to a lack of tissue, PDAC primary tumors were only analyzed by proteomics. Data analysis involved RNA-to-protein correlation analysis, multidimensional scaling, sample-to-sample Pearson correlations visualized as heatmaps with unsupervised clustering, differential expression analysis, gene ontology (GO) enrichment analysis, and immune cell deconvolution using CIBERSORTx. Analyzing all available biopsies, RNA sequencing identified 46,492 expressed transcripts and proteomic analysis detected 6973 proteins, with 5563 genes common to both datasets. The mean absolute RNA-to-protein Spearman correlation was 0.241. In CRC, exploratory differential expression analysis identified 5 transcripts and 99 proteins differing between metastases and primary tumors. In PDAC, metastasis-to-primary tumor comparison was limited to proteomics and identified 305 differentially expressed proteins. In unsupervised clustering based on sample-to-sample correlation, CRC and PDAC biopsies formed two separate clusters. GO enrichment analysis demonstrated distinct patterns of up- and downregulation across molecular functions, cellular components, and biological processes in metastases compared with primary tumors. Inferred immune cell fractions indicated high levels of CD4 T memory resting cells and M0 macrophages. This exploratory study supports the feasibility of combined RNA sequencing and proteomic profiling from limited FFPE diagnostic biopsies and highlights proteomics as an important complement to transcriptomics. These findings enhance our understanding of biological and immunological heterogeneity and require further validation in larger independent cohorts for future development of prognostic markers and novel immunotherapeutic strategies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR T-cell) therapy is an encouraging immunotherapeutic approach that involves the genetic modification of T lymphocytes to recognize and eliminate cancer cells in a major histocompatibility complex (MHC)-independent manner. Although CAR T-cell therapy has gained significant success in many cancers, its application remains challenging. Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) is a promising therapeutic target because of its overexpression in many cancers such as gastric, breast, lung, pancreatic, colorectal, ovarian, and other cancers. The central hypothesis of this review is that HER2 represents a uniquely valuable target for solid tumor CAR T-cell engineering because its dense clonal overexpression is essential to maintain tumor suitability and drive cancer stem cell renewal, providing a specific target that can be exploited to bypass resistance mechanisms. Maximizing its clinical potential requires shifting from descriptive platforms to a unified bioengineering paradigm that solves key translational barriers like antigen density discrimination, stromal delivery blockades, heterogeneity-driven escape, and microenvironmental suppression using optimized receptor design. This review provides an overview of CAR T-cell technology and discusses the structure, signaling pathways, and oncogenic role of HER2 in cancer progression. Here, we highlight the preclinical and clinical development of HER2-directed CAR T-cell therapy across different malignancies and highlight the outcomes of ongoing clinical trials. In addition, we discuss the major challenges limiting therapeutic efficacy, including on-target off- tumor toxicity, antigen heterogeneity, limited tumor infiltration, immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments, and T-cell exhaustion. Moreover, we cover the emerging strategies designed to overcome these barriers, such as advanced CAR T-cell designs, armored CAR T-cells, dual-targeting approaches, and combination therapies with immune checkpoint inhibitors and radiotherapy. Overall, all of these developments can potentially improve the effectiveness and safety of HER2-targeted CAR T-cell therapy and ensure its future use in oncological treatment.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Visualization of colorectal cancer (CRC) lesions is complicated by their location in the colon and tumor morphology. Reliance on a single surface biomarker for direct identification risks false negatives due to temporal changes and/or tumor heterogeneity. We developed a multiplexed system of complementary biomarker targets to capture a broader range of lesions with diverse temporal and/or phenotypic expression. We identified Mucin-1 (MUC1) and epithelial cell adhesion molecule (EPCAM) as useful targeting pairs by phenotyping CRC subtypes in a standard tissue array and surveying CRC cell lines in 2D and 3D formats to confirm expression of these surface biomarkers. Through a "universal" approach using Antibody-Protein L Microparticles (APL-MPs), we functionalized microparticle surfaces with antibodies recognizing either MUC1 or EPCAM. We generated heterogeneous CRC tumoroids and orthotopic animal models, expressing both MUC1 and EPCAM, and demonstrated that: (1) APL-MPs identified MUC1- and EPCAM-positive tumoroids in proportion to antigen expression; (2) APL-MPs detected CRC surface antigens on the luminal colon surface in vivo, and (3) concurrent targeting of multiple surface antigens enhanced detection sensitivity for heterogeneous CRC lesions. This approach supports broader applications of APL-MPs for detecting heterogeneous cancer lesions and offers a promising strategy for accurate tumor visualization in complex environments.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Organized cancer screening programs can reduce morbidity and mortality through early detection. However, participation remains suboptimal and unequal across Europe. To map the predisposing and limiting factors influencing participation in organized breast, cervical and colorectal cancer screening among screening-eligible adults in Europe. This scoping review followed the JBI framework and PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Studies published from 1 January 2011 to 7 January 2026 were identified through PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, EMBASE and CINAHL. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data and appraised methodological quality using QuADS. Findings were synthesized through inductive thematic analysis. Overall, 118 studies were included. Participation reflected interacting socioeconomic, cultural-linguistic, psychological, organizational and vulnerability-related determinants. Lower income, lower education and deprivation were consistently associated with lower uptake. Migrant and minority ethnic populations faced language, cultural and health system barriers, while participation was also lower among people with disabilities or chronic conditions, those with a history of substance use and those in institutional settings. Fear, embarrassment, fatalism and limited health literacy further reduced engagement. Fixed appointments, proactive reminders, provider recommendation, tailored communication, self-sampling, accessible pathways and continuity after abnormal results were associated with higher participation or improved follow-up. Universal program availability alone is insufficient to ensure equitable participation. In upcoming screening cycles, programs should stratify uptake and follow-up completion by socioeconomic position, migration background, disability and other vulnerability indicators. Fixed appointments, reminder-based recontact, tailored communication, self-sampling where appropriate and structured follow-up should be evaluated through changes in participation gaps and pathway completion.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The clinical demand for point-of-care (POC) detection of ophthalmic biomarkers, such as microRNA-21 (miR-21) for diabetic retinopathy (DR), is hampered by current assays that are often time-consuming, operationally complex, or prone to high background noise. To address this, we developed an ACH-based One-step Isothermal Instantaneous Cascade Amplification (ACH-OIICA) strategy. This platform relies on a single Autonomous Catalytic Hairpin (ACH) functioning as an "all-in-one" DNA nanomachine, which integrates target recognition, cascade amplification templating, and signal reporting, thereby eliminating the need for exogenous primers. Upon binding to miR-21, the ACH undergoes a conformational change that triggers a self-sustained cycle of polymerization and nicking, rapidly generating abundant G-quadruplex DNAzymes. The assay achieves a detection limit of 15.6 pM with a naked-eye distinguishable colorimetric readout. It demonstrates single-base specificity and robust performance in complex biological matrices. Crucially, ACH-OIICA proved its broad diagnostic utility across two distinct disease cohorts: it successfully differentiated patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) from healthy controls, and accurately distinguished patients with DR from healthy controls (HC). This work offers a streamlined, rapidly initiated, and highly sensitive platform, providing a robust framework for next-generation molecular diagnostics in clinical environment.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Minimally invasive laparoscopic surgery remains the predominant approach in colorectal procedures, while robot-assisted surgery has been increasingly adopted since its inclusion in the national insurance system in Japan for its safety and reliability. However, postoperative pressure injuries have been observed in patients without conventional high-risk factors, suggesting specific risks related to robotic surgery. This study aimed to describe the characteristics of pressure injuries following robotic colorectal surgery. We retrospectively reviewed patients who underwent robot-assisted colorectal surgery between April 2022 and March 2024 and subsequently developed pressure injuries. Data collected included patient demographics, comorbidities, medications, body mass index, laboratory results, and sacral subcutaneous fat thickness. Pressure injury characteristics (location, morphology, severity) and operative details (operative time, patient positioning, intraoperative temperature, pressure relief intervals) were also extracted. Of 150 patients, nine (6.0%) developed pressure injuries. Eight cases were classified as DESIGN-R®2020 depth d1 (persistent redness) and one as DDTI (suspected deep tissue injury). The mean body mass index was 24.5 kg/m Postoperative pressure injuries developed in 6.0% of patients who underwent robotic colorectal surgery. All injuries were localized to the sacral or gluteal regions and occurred in patients without conventional preoperative high-risk factors who had undergone operations lasting more than 7 h. Because this study was descriptive and had no comparison group, risk factors could not be identified; comparative studies are needed.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Timing of diverting ileostomy reversal after sphincter-preserving rectal cancer surgery varies in practice. This single-center retrospective cohort included 243 patients who completed reversal after diversion between January 2022 and January 2025. Delayed reversal was defined as reversal >6 months after ileostomy creation. Median time to reversal was 6.3 months; 128 patients (52.7%) underwent delayed reversal. Delayed reversal was associated with anastomotic leakage or leakage-related pelvic events and adjuvant treatment status. Stoma-period complications were more frequently documented with delayed reversal but interpreted descriptively because the time of first occurrence could not be reliably established. Delayed reversal was also associated with higher odds of overall 30-day complications, slower early recovery, and bowel-function and quality-of-life differences that attenuated over time. Among patients who completed reversal, delayed reversal was common and reflected complication-related and treatment-pathway burden, with associations mainly involving early recovery and functional outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Hypoxia drives chemoresistance in colorectal cancer (CRC), yet the underlying epigenetic mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we identify CARM1 as a key mediator of this response. Single-cell sequencing and patient cohort analysis show that CARM1 is overexpressed in malignant epithelial cells and correlates with poor prognosis. Mechanistically, hypoxia transcriptionally upregulates CARM1 via activation of the ERK-EGR1 signaling pathway, while concomitantly suppressing dual-specificity phosphatase 2 (DUSP2) to sustain the activation of this axis. Forced expression of wild-type but not phosphatase-dead (C257S) DUSP2 abrogated ERK-EGR1-mediated CARM1 induction. Functionally, elevated levels of CARM1 contribute to drug resistance, while knockout of CARM1 sensitized both p53 wild-type (HCT116) and p53 mutant (HT-29) cells to chemotherapy. Chromatin immunoprecipitation PCR demonstrated that CARM1-mediated asymmetric dimethylation of histone 3 arginine 17 at the FUS promoter upregulates FUS expression, thereby promoting drug resistance by reducing genotoxic stress-induced DNA damage. Notably, oxaliplatin-resistant cells, which also exhibit cross-resistance to 5-fluorouracil, maintain high CARM1/FUS levels via sustained DUSP2 suppression even in normoxia, indicating that drug-resistant cancer cells phenotypically share signaling features with hypoxia-adapted cells to maintain chemoresistance. Pharmacological inhibition of CARM1 with EZM2302 disrupted this axis and enhanced the chemotherapeutic efficacy in refractory orthotopic mouse models. Our findings demonstrate that the EGR1-CARM1-FUS axis is a critical driver of CRC chemoresistance and a potential therapeutic target.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cytoreductive surgery (CRS) with hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC) improves survival in selected patients with colorectal peritoneal metastases. However, outcomes remain heterogeneous, and tumor molecular biology may influence prognosis. We retrospectively reviewed patients with colorectal cancer and peritoneal metastases treated with CRS and HIPEC at Royal Hospital between May 2013 and August 2024. Patients were grouped by presence of genetic mutations (GM) versus no mutations (no-GM). Primary outcomes were overall survival (OS) and recurrence-free survival (RFS). Secondary outcomes included morbidity and prognostic factors for recurrence. Among 159 patients, 73 (45.9%) had a documented genetic mutation. Genetic mutation was associated with a shorter median RFS (8 months in the GM group vs. 27 months in the no-GM group; p < 0.001), with 5-year RFS of 6.0% and 45.3%, respectively. Genetic mutation was also associated with a shorter median OS on univariable analysis (37 months vs. not reached; p = 0.001). On multivariable analysis, genetic mutation status (HR 3.821, 95% CI 2.270-6.432; p < 0.001), PCI > 15 (HR 1.073; p = 0.005), and pre-HIPEC chemotherapy (HR 2.194; p = 0.003) were independently associated with recurrence. For OS, PCI (HR 1.066; p = 0.037) and poorly differentiated tumor grade (HR 2.946; p = 0.045) were independently associated with survival, whereas genetic mutation status was not (HR 1.477; p = 0.197). Genetic mutation was associated with shorter RFS after CRS and HIPEC, and this association persisted after multivariable adjustment. The association with OS was not independent of PCI and tumor grade, suggesting that disease burden may be the main driver of survival. Molecular status may complement established clinicopathological factors in patient assessment; larger prospective studies stratified by mutation type are needed.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Histotripsy is an emerging noninvasive, nonthermal ablative therapy recently introduced for the treatment of hepatic malignancies. This systematic review evaluated the efficacy and safety of histotripsy for primary and secondary liver tumors. PubMed and Scopus were searched from inception through August 2026 in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. Search terms included combinations of subject headings and keywords such as "histotripsy," "hepatic," and "metastases." Ten clinical studies published between 2022 and 2026 met inclusion criteria. Study populations included hepatocellular carcinoma and metastases from colorectal, neuroendocrine, pancreatic, breast, and other malignancies. Technical success ranged from 68.8% to 100%, although definitions varied across studies. Early treatment efficacy and local control were generally high among successfully treated tumors, with several studies reporting rates exceeding 90%. Longer-term oncologic data were limited by heterogeneous imaging criteria, treatment intent, and patient populations. Major complications were uncommon, although vascular thrombosis and acute kidney injury emerged as potential safety concerns. Current evidence supports the technical feasibility and short-term efficacy of hepatic histotripsy. However, standardized outcome definitions, longer follow-up, and comparative studies are needed to establish its durability and role relative to existing liver-directed therapies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Curcumin, a bioactive polyphenol, exhibits high therapeutic potential, but its poor solubility and bioavailability restrict its application. Furthermore, conventional nanocarriers face cumbersome fabrication, poor biocompatibility, and insufficient tumor extracellular matrix penetration. Here, we constructed a hyaluronidase-driven, curcumin-loaded food-grade Janus zein nanomotor (HAase-CZ-JNs) via Pickering emulsion templating and genipin crosslinking. Its asymmetric "half-hydrophilic, half-hydrophobic" topology minimizes mass transfer resistance and stabilizes the enzyme's active conformation, boosting immobilized HAase catalytic efficiency (kcat/Km) 4.01-fold over free enzyme. Driven by endogenous HA, HAase-CZ-JNs exhibit robust substrate-dependent self-propulsion (effective diffusion coefficient: 63.69 μm2/s), 8.2-fold higher than that of fully modified nanoparticles (HAase-CZ-NPs). In vitro, these nanomotors actively penetrate dense 3D spheroids, enhancing deep cytotoxicity against HT-29 cells (IC50 = 1.364 μg/mL) with a 12-h core-killing efficacy 7.9-fold greater than HAase-CZ-NPs. Utilizing biosafe natural materials, this system offers a promising nanokinetic strategy for targeted curcumin delivery in colorectal microenvironments.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Lung cancer surgery creates a vulnerable perioperative window where anesthetic and physiological interventions may modulate recurrence. This review evaluates the oncological impact of perioperative strategies in non-small-cell lung cancer, proposing a comprehensive 'oncoanesthesia care bundle'. Current clinical data expose a persistent gap between compelling preclinical rationales and observable clinical outcomes. The recent General Anesthetics in CAncer REsection Surgery (2026), a large-scale evaluation of propofol versus volatile anesthesia, enrolled mixed cancer cohorts and demonstrated no oncological advantage of propofol, underscoring that the ongoing Inhalational Gas Anesthesia and Propofol-based Total IntraVenous Anesthesia trial will provide the first adequately powered, lung cancer-specific evaluation. Similarly, prospective randomized data regarding regional anesthesia have failed to show a significant recurrence benefit in lung cancer surgery. For nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, the Adjuvant Low-dose ASpirin in Colorectal CAncer trial's recent biomarker-driven success in colorectal cancer highlights the urgent necessity for analogous molecularly tailored investigations in non-small-cell lung cancer. Beyond pharmacological agents, meticulous physiological optimization remains critical: lung-protective ventilation, restrictive-to-euvolemic fluid management, and maintaining normothermia are biologically coherent strategies that preserve the endothelial glycocalyx, optimize interstitial fluid pressure, and maintain natural killer cell function. Current clinical evidence does not justify selecting individual anesthetic agents solely for oncological benefit. Nevertheless, combining tailored pharmacological strategies, specifically opioid-sparing multimodal analgesia, with meticulous physiological optimization into a structured 'oncoanesthesia care bundle' provides a biologically coherent, low-risk framework available for immediate implementation. Future oncological trials must shift from pragmatic pan-cancer designs toward large-scale, patient-, cancer-, and gene-expression-specific trial protocols to truly capture personalized oncological outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Dietary fibre (DF) is essential for health, with higher levels of DF consumption being associated with reduced risk of cardiovascular diseases, type 2 diabetes and colorectal cancer. However, most UK consumers fall far below the recommended dietary intake of 30 g of DF a day for adults. Wheat is an important source of DF, with white bread and other products made from white flour being most widely consumed. White bread is an excellent vehicle to deliver increased intake of DF, being widely available and consumed and affordable to all socio-economic groups. Modern elite bread wheat genotypes differ in their content of DF, particularly soluble DF, in white flour and wheat breeders are now able to select for higher DF in their breeding programmes. This paper is the outcome of a 1-day discussion meeting, which focused on identifying and removing barriers to the development and cultivation of wheat types with high fibre in white flour and the delivery of high fibre products to consumers and makes recommendations for future research.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Locally advanced rectal cancer is increasingly managed through prolonged neoadjuvant pathways, including total neoadjuvant therapy and, in selected patients, non-operative organ-preservation strategies. Although these approaches have improved opportunities for tumor response and organ preservation, they also extend the period during which nutritional decline, altered bowel function, fatigue, and loss of physiological reserve may occur. Nutritional vulnerability during this interval is heterogeneous and may not be adequately captured by body weight or body mass index alone. This state-of-the-art narrative review examines nutritional phenotypes relevant to patients with locally advanced rectal cancer during neoadjuvant therapy. It first outlines why this interval should be regarded as a period of dynamic nutritional vulnerability. It then summarizes key phenotypes that may inform risk stratification and care, including overt malnutrition, sarcopenia, sarcopenic obesity, myosteatosis, and treatment-related decline. Finally, it proposes a practical framework for phenotype-based assessment and targeted dietetic intervention prior to restaging and definitive management. Current evidence suggests that adverse body-composition change during neoadjuvant therapy may be associated with poorer treatment tolerance, inferior tumor response, and worse oncological outcomes. For dietitians, this supports a shift from one-off screening toward longitudinal assessment that integrates oral intake, symptom burden, body-composition risk, and treatment trajectory. Although intervention evidence remains heterogeneous, nutritional care during neoadjuvant therapy should be proactive, individualized, and embedded within modern rectal cancer pathways.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
During the past two decades, increasing evidence has indicated that sessile serrated lesions (SSLs) contribute to "interval" colon cancers. These cancers occur more frequently in women and develop predominantly in the proximal colon; however, our understanding of the risk factors contributing to the development and progression of proximal SSLs remains incomplete. We performed a cross-sectional study of 3746 consecutive patients who underwent high-definition endoscopy from 2011 to 2015 at John Dempsey Hospital. Proximal serrated lesions (SLs) were divided into high- and low-risk groups based on current recommendations. Multivariate logistic regression analysis was performed to determine independent risk factors for proximal SL occurrence, with a secondary analysis specific to high-risk SLs. 233 patients (6.2%) had at least one proximal SSL. Sixty-five (1.7%) showed histological evidence of high-risk SLs. Older age, non-Hispanic white, and colonoscopy indication were each independently associated with the presence of proximal SLs. Smoking history (odds ratio (OR) 1.4, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.13-1.61) and daily aspirin use (OR 0.5, 95% CI: 0.33-0.68) were also associated with the risk of proximal SLs. Upon secondary analyses, high-risk SLs were found to occur more frequently in women (OR 1.8, CI: 1.12-3.05) and smokers (OR 1.5, CI: 1.12-2.09). In conclusion, female gender and smoking represent a higher risk group for high-risk SLs in the proximal colon. Considering the higher prevalence of right-sided colorectal cancer (CRC) among women, these data add to the growing literature implicating proximal SLs in disease pathogenesis that may influence CRC screening guidelines.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) is characterized by molecular heterogeneity and the development of adaptive resistance to systemic therapies. Biomarkers have become central to understanding resistance biology and guiding treatment selection, spanning established genomic alterations, circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA)-based monitoring, and emerging molecular classifications. Herein, we provide a synthesis of biomarker-driven resistance mechanisms across major therapeutic classes in mCRC, including anti-EGFR, anti-VEGF, BRAF-targeted, KRAS-targeted, HER2-directed, and immunotherapy-based approaches. PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar were searched for relevant literature published through August 2026. Resistance to targeted therapies converges on reactivation of key signaling pathways, particularly MAPK, through genomic and microenvironmental factors. ctDNA represents an important tool for longitudinal assessment of tumor evolution and has demonstrated clinical validity in selected settings, including molecular selection for anti-EGFR rechallenge. Across other therapeutic classes, ctDNA dynamics and resistance profiling are primarily prognostic or investigational, and prospective evidence that ctDNA-guided treatment adaptation improves outcomes remains limited. Emerging biomarkers, including immune-related gene expression patterns, features of the tumor microenvironment, and metabolic adaptations, may improve prediction of therapeutic response. Integration of longitudinal biomarker assessment with ctDNA profiling may enable earlier detection of resistance and more individualized treatment strategies, although the clinical benefit of ctDNA-guided treatment adaptation remains to be established.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
BACKGROUND Colonic schwannomas are rare benign neurogenic tumors originating from Schwann cells of the peripheral nerve sheath, and account for a very small proportion of gastrointestinal mesenchymal neoplasms. Their nonspecific clinical and radiological appearance often leads to diagnostic dilemma. Definitive diagnosis relies on histopathological and immunohistochemical evaluation. Preoperative diagnosis remains particularly challenging because colonic schwannomas may mimic other mesenchymal or cystic lesions, including gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GISTs) and duplication cysts. CASE REPORT We present the case of a 67-year-old asymptomatic male patient with a schwannoma of the transverse colon wall diagnosed only after surgical excision, through histopathological and immunohistochemical examination. After upper and lower endoscopy revealed no mucosal abnormalities, computed tomography suggested a duplication cyst, while magnetic resonance imaging favored a GIST arising from the transverse colon. Due to the uncertain preoperative diagnosis and the size and location of the lesion, transverse colectomy with primary anastomosis was performed. Histopathological examination demonstrated a spindle-cell tumor with very low mitotic activity and no necrosis. Immunohistochemistry showed positivity for S-100 and SOX10 and negativity for CD117, CD34, and DOG1, confirming the diagnosis of schwannoma. Complete R0 excision was achieved, and the patient remained recurrence-free 2 years later. CONCLUSIONS This case emphasizes the diagnostic challenge and the importance of considering schwannoma in differential diagnosis of colonic intramural masses extending into the transverse mesocolon. The predominantly intramural and exophytic growth pattern may account for both the normal endoscopic findings and the misleading radiological appearance. Complete surgical excision with negative margins is associated with an excellent prognosis for benign colorectal schwannomas.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major therapeutic challenge, despite substantial advances in molecular characterization and targeted treatment. The heterogeneity of CRC and the development of treatment resistance highlight the need for novel therapeutic strategies and rational drug repurposing approaches. Imatinib, a well-established tyrosine kinase inhibitor, exerts pharmacological activity beyond ABL1/ABL2, targeting KIT, PDGFR, DDR1, and potentially LCK, which may contribute to distinct mechanisms of CRC progression. This review examines the emerging evidence on the potential role of imatinib in CRC, including its effects on tumor-cell proliferation and survival, invasion and metastasis, extracellular-matrix remodeling, tumor-stroma interactions, treatment resistance, and immune regulation. Preclinical studies indicate promising antitumor activity in selected molecular and biological contexts, particularly in KIT-positive tumors, PDGFR-rich stroma, mesenchymal/CMS4 tumors, and models characterized by aberrant DDR1 signaling. However, clinical evidence remains limited and does not currently support imatinib as a standard treatment for unselected CRC. Biomarker-guided patient selection, rational combination strategies, and tumor microenvironment-directed approaches may enhance its therapeutic potential. Further well-designed clinical studies are required to determine whether these biological effects can translate into meaningful clinical benefit.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Angiogenesis is a key process in colorectal cancer (CRC) progression, with vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGFA) being a major pro-angiogenic mediator. miR-195-5p has previously been identified by our group as a tumor-suppressive miRNA downregulated in CRC. Here, we aimed to investigate whether miR-195-5p contributes to CRC-associated angiogenenic processes through VEGFA regulation. Potential miR-195-5p targets were investigated through bioinformatic predictions and miRNA Target RNA immunoprecipitation. VEGFA expression was evaluated in public CRC datasets and paired tumor/adjacent tissues of a cohort of CRC patients by quantitative real-time PCR and immunohistochemistry. miR-195-5p gain- and loss-of-function experiments were performed in CRC cells to assess VEGFA and VEGFR2 expression and extracellular VEGF-A levels by ELISA. Endothelial tube formation assays using HUVECs were conducted to evaluate paracrine angiogenic effects. VEGFA expression was also analyzed in an AOM/DSS-induced murine CRC model treated with a miR-195-5p mimic. VEGFA was predicted as a conserved miR-195-5p target and was enriched in miR-195-5p-associated RISCs. VEGFA was overexpressed in CRC tissues compared to normal or adjacent non-tumor tissues. miR-195-5p restoration reduced VEGFA mRNA and protein expression, extracellular VEGF-A levels, and VEGFR2 protein levels in the HCT116 CRC cell line, whereas miR-195-5p inhibition produced the opposite molecular profile. Conditioned media from miR-195-5p-overexpressing CRC cells significantly impaired endothelial tube formation. Consistently, miR-195-5p in vivo administration reduced colonic Vegfa expression in AOM/DSS-treated mice. Overall, these findings indicate that miR-195-5p negatively modulates VEGFA expression and reduces the ability of CRC cell-derived conditioned media to support endothelial tube formation. This study extends the tumor-suppressive functions previously attributed to miR-195-5p by supporting its involvement in the regulation of angiogenesis-related processes in CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cancer diagnosed before the age of 50 is rising across many countries, and the rise is not accounted for by population growth alone. India carries one of the world's largest cancer burdens, and it varies greatly between its states, variation camouflaged by the national average. We characterised early-onset breast, cervical, colorectal and stomach cancer across the states of India. Secondary ecological analysis of Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 estimates, ages 15-49 years, 1990-2023; rates per 100,000 population of both sexes. Trends were summarised as the estimated annual percentage change, with autocorrelation-robust confidence intervals, and by segmented regression. Gradients across 30 states were assessed against the 2023 Socio-Demographic Index (SDI). Case growth was decomposed into population growth, within-band ageing and rate change. In 2023, breast cancer had the highest early-onset incidence, 9.63 per 100,000 (19.63 per 100,000 women), and cervical cancer 8.18 (16.87). Breast incidence rose 2.72% per year and colorectal 1.11%; stomach fell 0.52%. Cervical incidence fell until 2011 and rose unevenly thereafter, with a near-zero net trend (-0.09% per year). Within-band standardisation shifted it downward (-0.39%; 95% confidence interval -0.87 to 0.09), and separating within-band ageing turned its rate-change share negative (-8.1%). Breast cases rose from 15,550 to 76,806: 59.0% of the rise was rate change, 51.8% after separating ageing. Point estimates suggested a stronger inverse SDI gradient for cervical disability-adjusted life years (ρ = -0.43) than incidence (ρ = -0.31). Neither survived multiple-testing correction, and the two were not distinguishable. No association was detected between burden rate and caseload across the states (ρ = +0.02). The early-onset cancer burden in India is not uniform. Breast cancer cases are growing faster than the population, with a rising recorded rate. The cervical gradient is exploratory. The states with the highest rates and the states with the most cases differ, and each answers a different planning question.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Medical plasma is a promising therapeutic approach in oncology due to its ability to generate reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (RONS) and modulate tumor cell viability and phenotype. Therefore, medical plasma could expand the treatment options for highly prevalent or difficult-to-treat cancer entities such as gastrointestinal cancers. This study investigated the effects of medical plasma generated by the clinically certified argon plasma jet kINPen on two gastrointestinal tumor cell lines (HT-29, MUG-CCArly) with a focus on cytotoxicity, immunomodulation, and redox-dependent mechanisms. Plasma produced a mixture of reactive species under the applied experimental conditions and was able to reduce metabolic activity and cell viability via a redox-dependent induction of apoptosis in both cell lines. Plasma exposure altered the expression of cell-surface markers with potentially immunostimulatory roles such as CD40, CRT, and HMGB1, as well as more immunoregulatory markers like CD47 and PD-L1 (CD274). Additionally, modulated secretion profiles marked by increased pro-inflammatory molecules such as IL-8 and MIP-3a (CCL20) were detected. Overall, congruent but also cell line-dependent responses to plasma treatment were observed that featured a modified immunological phenotype of tumor cells with potentially immunostimulatory but also immunomodulatory aspects, highlighting the potential of medical gas plasma technology as a multimodal therapeutic approach in gastrointestinal oncology.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The diagnosis of colorectal cancer encompasses nine complementary modalities: stool-based screening, blood-based biomarkers, cross-sectional imaging, endoscopic evaluation, histopathology, liquid biopsy, molecular and genetic profiling, microbiome analysis, and nanotechnology-based diagnostics. This narrative review synthesizes 160 references spanning seven task-specific artificial intelligence domains, including computer-aided detection, optical diagnosis, invasion depth prediction, computational pathology and radiogenomics, metastasis forecasting, neoadjuvant treatment response prediction, and surgical workflow analysis. We propose a conceptual multimodal pipeline comprising data ingestion, preprocessing and harmonization, feature representation, multimodal fusion, forecasting, explainability, and validation. A structured evidence grading framework classifies each clinical task by evidence level, consistency, and clinical readiness. We further catalog public datasets, challenge benchmarks, and five reporting standards: TRIPOD-AI, CONSORT-AI, SPIRIT-AI, DECIDE-AI, and CLAIM. Computer-aided detection and optical diagnosis demonstrate the highest maturity with Level 1 evidence from randomized controlled trials, while computational pathology, radiogenomics, and metastasis prediction remain at Level 2 with retrospective validation (internal or external). Microbiome screening, nanotechnology diagnostics, and surgical phase recognition are exploratory. The principal barriers to clinical adoption are domain shift, data scarcity, calibration, prospective validation, and workflow integration. We conclude that clinically useful artificial intelligence requires robust external validation, uncertainty quantification, explainable outputs, standardized reporting, and a structured translational pathway from retrospective evidence through regulatory clearance to post-deployment monitoring.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Rates of young-onset colorectal cancer (CRC) are on the rise globally. Despite this growing burden, the drivers of young-onset adult CRC remain largely unknown. This study aimed to compare risk factor profiles between younger-onset and late-onset CRC to evaluate differences in their risk factor profiles. The Prostate, Lung, Colorectal and Ovarian Cancer Screening Trial dataset, comprising ∼155,000 US participants including 1219 CRC cases, was analysed. Participants were stratified by age (≤59 vs. ≥60 years). Associations of demographic, clinical and behavioural risk factors with CRC were computed using multivariable Cox regression with the multiplicative interaction of exposures. Reduced rank regression was used to derive dietary patterns (DPs). Among the ≤59-year cohort, no individual risk factor (excluding age) was independently associated with the risk of CRC. However, the multiplicative effect of hypertension and smoking had a nominal association with younger-onset CRC (p = 0.047). In contrast, in the ≥60-year cohort, individual (sex, body mass index, diabetes and alcohol) as well as combinations of risk factors were associated with CRC. Significant DPs appeared exclusively to impact the risk of CRC in the ≥60-year cohort. However, no interactions remained significant following correction for multiple testing; findings should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating. These findings suggest that the drivers of CRC in younger individuals may be different from their older counterparts. These exploratory findings offer novel insight into CRC risk in the young and highlight the need to reconsider interactions between CRC risk factors.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Participation in cancer screening is crucial to maximise its benefit. In colorectal cancer (CRC) screening, stool tests or colonoscopies are commonly offered worldwide screening tests. In the German CRC screening programme, the insured can primarily choose between stool test and colonoscopy. However, sigmoidoscopy is also an evidence-based procedure to reduce CRC mortality and even prevent CRC. Based on individual preferences, we aim to estimate the uptake for either colonoscopy, sigmoidoscopy, or stool test in CRC screening. In 2020, statutory insured individuals aged 50, 55, and 60 in Germany, Lower Saxony, were invited to participate in a discrete choice experiment (DCE). Each participant received 8 choice tasks, each of which presented two unlabelled (procedure A and B) screening alternatives defined by 6 attributes (CRC incidence and mortality, complications, preprocedural bowel preparation, need for transportation home, colonoscopy following a positive test result). Each attribute had 3 levels. To calculate the indirect utility and probability of uptake of stool testing, sigmoidoscopy, colonoscopy, and 'no screening', the preference weights of the attribute levels used to define the 4 alternatives were summed. Estimates were compared between standard screening (stool test or colonoscopy) and extended screening (+ sigmoidoscopy). External validity of the DCE was checked by comparing predicted and intended (2 items in the questionnaire) participation. From n = 666 valid respondents, a greater proportion of women (22.5%; 95%CI 16.2-28.9%) than men (13.4%; 95%CI 9.6-17.2%) preferred sigmoidoscopy in an extended screening scenario. Compared with standard screening, the predicted uptake for colonoscopy and the stool test as well as for 'no screening' was slightly lower when sigmoidoscopy was offered as an additional option. The extended screening could yield a slightly higher non-significant total participation in CRC screening in both women (+ 5.8%; 95%CI -0.4-12.0%) and men (+ 3.1; 95%CI -3.4-9.6%) than standard screening. Intended and preferred uptake did not differ substantially. A relevant proportion of the eligible population, more women than men, appears to prefer sigmoidoscopy for CRC screening when given the option. This additional option tends to increase overall predicted participation in CRC screening. Future studies are needed to evaluate the acceptance and feasibility of the additionally offered sigmoidoscopy in today's CRC screening. DRKS00019010, 2019-11-18.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a highly malignant disease characterized by insidious onset and a high propensity for metastasis. With the advancement of single-cell technologies, the tumor microenvironment (TME) of CRC has been thoroughly analyzed. However, the prognostic characteristics of the various cell subtypes within the TME have not been comprehensively described. In this study, we integrated single-cell sequencing, bulk RNA sequencing, and spatial transcriptomics to elucidate the relationship between different cell types and prognosis in CRC. We identified three cell subtypes significantly associated with patient survival: CTHRC1-expressing cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), TREM2-expressing tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), and SELE-expressing endothelial cells. Based on these findings, we developed a CTS score to assist in creating a prognostic nomogram for CRC. Furthermore, we stratified patients based on their CTS scores and conducted drug sensitivity predictions. These discoveries enhance our understanding of the molecular characteristics of CRC and provide potential therapeutic targets for the disease.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Endoscopic vacuum therapy (EVT) is increasingly used for colorectal anastomotic leaks (AL), but its role within the preceding operative and clinical course remains poorly defined. We described EVT as part of a staged, time-centered pathway anchored to the index operation. This retrospective single-center cohort linked a colorectal resection database with an EVT registry. AL was classified by ISREC grade and by anastomotic height, circumferential extent, and initial sponge count. The index operation, including intraoperative colonoscopy (IOC) when performed, was defined as time zero. Among 422 left-sided colorectal or rectal resections, 38 early AL occurred (9.0%): 9 ISREC A (23.7%), 11 B (28.9%), and 18 C (47.4%). IOC was performed in 26/38 patients (68.4%); 19/26 (73.1%) had a well-constructed anastomosis at the index operation. EVT was used in 17/38 patients (44.7%) (10 ISREC B and 7 C). Morphology was available in 14/17 (82.4%): median anastomotic height was 8 cm (IQR, 6-10), 13/14 defects (92.9%) were posterior or posterolateral, and 8/14 (57.1%) involved ≥50% of the circumference. Pelvic peritoneal closure was present in 15/17 EVT-treated patients (88.2%). No EVT-related complications occurred, and 11/17 patients (64.7%) had a restorative outcome. EVT was used mainly for ISREC B leaks and selected ISREC C leaks after operative source control. Linking defect morphology, EVT sessions, and clinical endpoints to the index operation frames EVT as one component of a staged management pathway rather than an isolated endoscopic intervention.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Mitochondrial protein turnover is crucial for metabolic adaptation to changing demands, while the dysfunction of this process in human cancer remains poorly defined. MARCH5, RNF185 and MUL1 are the three E3 ubiquitin ligases specific to the mitochondrion. However, their oncogenic functions in colorectal cancer (CRC) remain unexplored. In this study, we found that RNF185 was significantly upregulated and correlated with an unfavorable prognosis in CRC patients, while no alterations in the expressions of MARCH5 and MUL1 were observed in CRC. Functional studies demonstrated that RNF185 promotes CRC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion by enhancing glycolysis. Mechanistically, RNF185 directly interacts with and downregulates the mitochondrial CoA transporter SLC25A42. This leads to reduced acetylation of mitochondrial pyruvate carrier subunit 2 (MPC2) at lysine 19, which facilitates ARIH1-mediated degradation and subsequent downregulation of MPC2 to enhance glycolysis. Collectively, our study identifies RNF185 as a critical oncogene in CRC progression by suppressing MPC2-mediated mitochondrial pyruvate import and consequently enhancing glycolysis, thereby positioning RNF185 as a promising therapeutic target for CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a common malignancy associated with Wnt/β-catenin pathway dysregulation. While miRNAs are known to influence cancer, miR-646's role in CRC remains unclear. This study employed qPCR, Western blot, IHC, CCK-8, and Transwell assays to assess miR-646 expression, protein levels, and CRC cell functions. Wnt/β-catenin activation was analyzed using IF, TOP/FOP reporter assays, and gene interactions were examined through ChIP and dual-luciferase systems. Nude mouse models and clinical samples were used to further evaluate the biological and clinical relevance of miR-646 in CRC. Results showed miR-646 was downregulated in CRC. Its upregulation suppressed CRC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion by inhibiting WNT2B and Wnt/β-catenin activation. CTCF negatively regulated miR-646 expression, potentially through its binding to the miR-646 promoter. In vivo, miR-646 knockdown promoted CRC xenograft tumor growth, accompanied by increased WNT2B expression and enhanced Wnt/β-catenin signaling. Additionally, higher miR-646 expression was associated with a better prognosis in patients with CRC. These findings support a role for miR-646 in regulating WNT2B/Wnt/β-catenin signaling in CRC and demonstrate its negative regulation by CTCF, suggesting the potential of miR-646 as a prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Preoperative oral carbohydrate (CHO) loading has become an important component of enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) protocols to reduce the metabolic stress associated with prolonged fasting. However, evidence regarding its effects on metabolic, inflammatory, and postoperative recovery outcomes following colorectal surgery remains inconsistent. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the impact of preoperative CHO loading on metabolic, inflammatory, and clinical recovery outcomes in patients undergoing elective colorectal surgery. A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library was conducted from database inception through May 2026. Randomized controlled trials comparing preoperative oral CHO loading with conventional fasting or placebo in adults undergoing elective colorectal surgery were included. Data extraction and risk of bias assessment were performed independently by multiple reviewers via standardized methods and the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool. Meta-analysis was performed via Review Manager, and pooled effect estimates are expressed as the mean difference (MD) with 95% confidence interval (CI). Twelve randomized controlled trials involving 762 patients were included. Preoperative CHO loading was associated with significantly lower postoperative C-reactive protein levels (MD -45.25 mg/L; 95% CI -89.26 to -1.24) and a shorter hospital length of stay (MD -1.60 days; 95% CI -2.43 to -0.77). No significant differences were observed in postoperative glucose levels or time to first flatus. Individual studies also reported improvements in postoperative quality of life, patient comfort, and selected inflammatory markers, including the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio. Serum albumin levels differed significantly between groups. Preoperative carbohydrate loading was associated with lower postoperative CRP levels and shorter hospital stay. However, substantial heterogeneity and the absence of significant differences in some metabolic and recovery outcomes warrant cautious interpretation. Further randomized controlled trials are needed to confirm these findings and clarify their underlying mechanisms.
