ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Candida-associated infected aortic aneurysms (AAs) are exceptionally rare and frequently fatal. A 76-year-old man developed Candida glabrata candidemia after surgery for ascending colon cancer; the postoperative course was complicated by an anastomotic leak and intra-abdominal infection. Echinocandin therapy was discontinued because of profound neutropenia after 12 days of treatment, following negative blood cultures. Approximately 1 year later, an enlarging descending thoracic AA was detected and treated with thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR). Despite initially negative blood cultures, a normal or only minimally elevated serum β-D-glucan concentration, and negative Candida antigen testing, the aneurysm subsequently enlarged and required repeat TEVAR. Periaortic soft-tissue changes transiently regressed, further obscuring the diagnosis. Three months after the second TEVAR, computed tomography revealed renewed aneurysm enlargement and perigraft gas. C. glabrata was recovered from one of five blood culture sets. On the fifth day of admission, the patient experienced abrupt circulatory collapse with hemoptysis and died, likely due to aneurysm rupture through an aortobronchial fistula. All available intra-abdominal and bloodstream isolates of C. glabrata obtained throughout the clinical course had identical six-locus multiple-locus variable-number tandem-repeat analysis (MLVA) profiles. A prior episode of candidemia remains clinically relevant when a new or progressive aortic lesion develops, even after prolonged culture negativity. Serial aneurysm enlargement, periaortic inflammation, and delayed perigraft gas should outweigh apparently reassuring blood cultures or fungal biomarkers and should prompt early multidisciplinary reassessment, pursuit of tissue diagnosis when feasible, source control, and prolonged antifungal therapy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
For RAS/BRAF wild-type (WT) metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC), the optimal maintenance strategy following first-line cetuximab-based chemotherapy remains controversial. This retrospective study enrolled 162 patients who completed ≥8 cycles of first-line cetuximab combined with FOLFOX or FOLFIRI. Patients were stratified into cetuximab maintenance (n = 53), capecitabine maintenance (n = 27), and observation (n = 82) groups. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS). Median PFS was 5.4 months in the observation group, 12.0 months in the cetuximab maintenance group, and 9.2 months in the capecitabine maintenance group. Compared with observation, both maintenance strategies significantly reduced the risk of progression (cetuximab: HR = 0.514, P = 0.001; capecitabine: HR=0.541, P = 0.018), whereas no significant between-group difference was observed (HR = 0.971, P = 0.916). Maintenance therapy was an independent significant prognostic factor. Grade 1-2 skin reactions were unique to cetuximab, and grade 3-4 gastrointestinal adverse events were restricted to capecitabine. Overall adverse event rates were comparable, and no severe adverse events resulted in treatment discontinuation. Single-agent maintenance with cetuximab or capecitabine is associated with improved PFS versus observation after first-line cetuximab-based chemotherapy in patients with RAS/BRAF WT mCRC, with a favorable safety profile. No significant difference in PFS was identified between the two maintenance agents, though therapeutic equivalence cannot be confirmed given the limited sample size. Capecitabine provides a convenient oral alternative for long-term maintenance, which may facilitate individualized clinical decision-making.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To investigate the effect of isorhamnetin (Iso) on colitis-associated colorectal cancer (CAC) and the possible mechanisms involved. The AOM/DSS-induced CAC mouse model was used to examine the effects of Iso on CAC. Colonic histopathology and proliferation were assessed by H&E staining and Ki67 immunohistochemistry. Pro-inflammatory cytokine levels were measured by ELISA. Transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses were used to explore the possible mechanism, and immunofluorescence and Western blotting were used to examine the related protein changes. In CAC mice, Iso reduced body weight loss, colon shortening, tumor formation, and splenomegaly. It also attenuated mucosal damage and aberrant proliferation and lowered colonic pro-inflammatory cytokine levels. Omics analyses suggested that the effects of Iso may involve S100A8/A9 and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Immunofluorescence and Western blot showed that Iso restored E-cadherin and ZO-1 expression, suppressed Vimentin expression, and downregulated S100A8/A9 levels. These results suggest that Iso may ameliorate CAC progression by downregulating S100A8/A9 and inhibiting EMT. Iso may therefore be worth further study as a candidate agent for CAC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Oxaliplatin, widely used in the treatment of gastrointestinal cancers, particularly colorectal cancer, can cause a range of adverse effects, including rare but clinically significant ocular toxicity. Ocular complications are diverse and can affect the retina, optic nerve, cornea, and eyelids. They most often manifest as transient and reversible visual disturbances, sometimes accompanied by eye pain, ptosis, or tearing. These symptoms generally occur early, as early as the first treatment cycles, and resolve spontaneously within a few hours to a few days. In most cases, ophthalmological examination is normal, suggesting functional impairment without detectable anatomical abnormalities. However, more severe presentations have been reported, including persistent retinal lesions, toxic optic neuropathy, and, more rarely, posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES), which may result in long-term sequelae. Management may therefore require adjustment to the treatment regimen or even discontinuation of oxaliplatin. This review summarizes the available evidence on clinical manifestations, diagnostic approaches, proposed pathophysiological mechanisms, and management strategies. It highlights the importance of appropriate ophthalmologic monitoring and multidisciplinary collaboration to ensure early diagnosis and prevent complications.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
After induction therapy, maintenance strategies in metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) remain uncertain. Treatment breaks and a chemotherapy-free interval (CFI) may be considered when tumour control is achieved as well as maintenance therapy. Identifying variables of a short/intermediate/long CFI would be useful to guide therapeutic decisions. CFI-SCORE is an individual patient data meta-analysis assessing clinical and biological factors of short (<3 months), intermediate (3-6 months) or long (≥6-12 months) CFI after induction chemotherapy. Data from 6 international trials comparing observation with continued systemic therapy were pooled. An exploratory score was developed using significant variables. A total of 1188 patients were analysed. Median CFI was 3.67 months; 406 (34.2%), 503 (42.3%), and 279 (23.5%) patients had short, intermediate, and long CFIs, respectively. In multivariable analysis, male sex (adjusted OR [95% CI]: 1.36 [1.04-1.79]), age ≥ 75 years (1.52 [0.99-2.35]), left-sided or rectal primary tumour (1.38 [1.01-1.87]), prior resection of the primary tumour (1.38 [1.06-1.79]), a single metastatic site (1.51 [1.16-1.97]), and absence of thrombocytosis (1.41 [1.00-2.00]) were associated with longer CFI. The exploratory score showed modest discrimination for 6-month CFI prediction (bootstrap-corrected C-statistic, 0.56); the OS C-index was 0.59. CFI-SCORE is the first meta-analysis assessing CFI after induction therapy in mCRC. Six parameters were associated with CFI in patients with responding/stable disease and were combined into an exploratory score and nomogram. These results are hypothesis-generating: prospective validation is needed to determine whether CFI-SCORE could guide treatment-break vs maintenance strategies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the most common malignancies worldwide. Since 2006, the Lombardy Region has implemented a population-based CRC screening programme with biennial faecal immunochemical test. This study describes twenty years of programme performance, impact on CRC burden and associated costs. Population-based longitudinal observational study. We analysed 2006-2023 data, collected from the eight Health Protection Agencies in Lombardy and validated at regional and national levels. Key performance indicators were computed following national standards. Screening programme costs were derived from regional health budgets (2021-2024) and CRC incidence was estimated from hospital discharge data for 2002-2023. Invitation coverage remained above 90% across most biennial screening rounds, with participation rates averaging 45-50% before the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic and recovering to 42% afterward. Positivity rates ranged from 4% to 5%, with approximately 1000 cancers detected per biennium. Detection rates for advanced adenomas decreased over time, while low-risk adenomas increased. The average cost per screened participant ranged from €10 to €12. Adjusted CRC incidence declined from 68.8 per 100,000 in 2007 to 38.2 in 2023. The programme has maintained high invitation coverage and sustained screening activity over two decades, with a substantial reduction in observed CRC incidence over the same period. Persistent participation and equity gaps highlight opportunities for further improvement.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Patients who previously had a normal colonoscopy may subsequently undergo colorectal cancer (CRC) screening with multitarget stool DNA (mt-sDNA) testing. The yield of advanced neoplasia following a positive mt-sDNA test in this subgroup is not well defined. We compared colonoscopy outcomes after positive mt-sDNA tests in patients with and without a prior normal colonoscopy. We conducted a registry-based analysis using data from the population-based New Hampshire Colonoscopy Registry (NHCR). The primary outcome was an ordered four-level categorical variable reflecting colonoscopy findings: CRC, advanced colorectal neoplasia, non-advanced colorectal neoplasia, and no neoplasia. Ordinal logistic regression models were used to evaluate the association between prior normal colonoscopy and severity of findings. Patients with a prior normal colonoscopy (n=739) were approximately half as likely to have more advanced findings compared with patients without a prior colonoscopy (n=994); prior normal colonoscopy was associated with lower odds of more advanced versus less advanced outcomes (OR 0.51; 95% CI 0.41-0.62; P < 0.001). However, the absolute prevalence of advanced colorectal neoplasia among patients with a previous colonoscopy remained substantial (19.1%; 95% CI 16.3-22.1%). Although prior normal colonoscopy is associated with lower odds of advanced findings after a positive mt-sDNA test, the residual prevalence of advanced neoplasia remains clinically meaningful. Regardless of prior screening history, there is a high yield of neoplasia, which could be attributed in part due to missed lesions on the prior colonoscopy. Our data provide potential benchmarks for expected lesion yield in this population.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
An association has been found between alliin and reduced risks of various cancers; however, evidence for these causal relationships remain limited. This study utilized Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis to assess the potential causal relationships between circulating alliin levels and the risks of 22 common cancers. We selected instrumental variables from the latest and largest European genome-wide association study (GWAS) datasets. First, we comprehensively assessed the causal relationships between blood alliin levels and the risks of 22 common cancers through two-sample MR analysis. Subsequently, we repeated the validation of instrumental variables using cancer GWAS statistics from different studies and merged the results by meta-analysis. Two-step MR analysis was used to investigate whether 91 inflammatory proteins mediate the effect of alliin on the risk of cancer. Finally, multivariable MR analysis was conducted to determine the direct effects of alliin on the risk of cancer, with adjustment for potential mediators. Inverse variance weighted results were considered the primary observation outcome, and additional sensitivity analyses were conducted. Increased blood alliin levels were significantly causally associated with decreased risks of prostate cancer, ovarian cancer, breast cancer, cervical cancer, lymphoma, and colorectal cancer, with the corresponding meta-analyses also showing significant associations. In the two-step MR analysis, chemokine ligand 23 (CCL23) and oncostatin M (OSM) as well as interleukin-12B (IL12B) were the key mediators of the inverse causal relationships between blood alliin levels and the risk of prostate cancer as well as the risks of ovarian and colorectal cancers, respectively. STAM-binding protein was a key mediator of the causal relationships between blood alliin levels and the risk of lymphoma. The results of this study support that increased blood alliin levels can reduce the risks of multiple cancers, with circulating inflammatory proteins potentially mediating this association.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Metabolic abnormalities are plausible and modifiable contributors to colorectal cancer (CRC), but genetic evidence and population-level burden data are often reported separately. This integrated secondary analysis triangulated Mendelian randomization (MR), Global Burden of Disease 2021 estimates, metabolic risk attribution, estimated annual percentage change analyses, geographic and Socio-demographic Index (SDI) comparisons, and observed age-standardized mortality trends to characterize the relationship between metabolic abnormalities and CRC from 1990 to 2021. Genetically predicted body mass index (BMI), diabetes, and familial combined hyperlipidemia (FCHL) were positively associated with CRC risk in inverse-variance weighted MR analyses, with the strongest association observed for BMI. The diabetes (odds ratio = 1.002, 95% confidence interval = 1.001-1.003) and FCHL (odds ratio = 1.0010, 95% confidence interval = 1.0003-1.0017) estimates were statistically significant but extremely close to the null, indicating minimal individual-level effect sizes on the genetic-liability scale and no basis for inferring clinically meaningful risk differences. Globally, CRC incident cases increased substantially from 916,584 in 1990 to 2,194,143 in 2021, while the age-standardized death rate declined from 15.56 to 12.40 per 100,000 population. China showed a particularly steep increase in incident cases and age-standardized incidence rate. Across SDI strata, CRC incidence rose in all strata except high-SDI settings, whereas diabetes incidence increased in every region and stratum. Low-middle SDI settings showed the clearest ecological co-burden, with rising CRC and diabetes burden occurring together. Age-specific analyses showed that CRC burden attributable to high BMI and high fasting plasma glucose increased sharply with age, with the highest attributable death and disability-adjusted life-year rates in the oldest age groups. Observed global CRC age-standardized death rates declined from 1990 to 2021 for both sexes combined, males, and females. These findings support metabolic health as an important and actionable component of CRC prevention, particularly in settings where CRC and diabetes burdens are rising in parallel. The population-level findings should be interpreted as ecological co-burden rather than proof of interaction, and the MR estimates reflect lifelong genetic liability rather than clinical relative risks. In particular, the diabetes and FCHL estimates should not be interpreted as clinically meaningful individual-level effects.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Postoperative management after curative-intent treatment of colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) remains controversial because improvements in recurrence-related outcomes have not consistently translated into longer overall survival (OS). This critical narrative review examines randomized evidence for systemic chemotherapy and hepatic arterial infusion (HAI), together with emerging evidence on circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA). Trial-based findings, prognostic associations, and unvalidated treatment-effect hypotheses were critically distinguished. Postoperative fluoropyrimidine- or oxaliplatin-based treatment can delay recurrence in some settings, but a durable OS benefit has not been consistently demonstrated. Contemporary HAI trials differ in patient selection, regional drugs, systemic therapy, and endpoints. PACHA-01 reported improved hepatic recurrence-free survival in a selected population, HARVEST was terminated early, and PUMP did not meet its primary endpoint. These findings neither establish routine HAI nor identify validated predictors of benefit. Postoperative ctDNA is strongly prognostic, but nonrandomized associations between adjuvant treatment and outcomes cannot establish the clinical utility of ctDNA-directed treatment allocation. A conceptual distinction between hepatic and systemic recurrence risk may support multidisciplinary deliberation and prospective trial design, but should not be used as a validated postoperative treatment-selection algorithm. Clinical decisions must also account for prior chemotherapy, postoperative recovery, toxicity, local treatment opportunities, institutional expertise, and patient preferences.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Transanal minimally invasive surgery(TAMIS) enables local excision of selected rectal neoplasms. Robotic TAMIS(R-TAMIS) may overcome technical constraints of conventional laparoscopic TAMIS(L-TAMIS), but whether these capabilities translate into better outcomes remains uncertain. We compared R-TAMIS and L-TAMIS, examining the evidence in the context of robotic procedural maturity. PubMed, Scopus, and Cochrane Library were searched through 2026 for comparative studies of adults undergoing TAMIS for rectal neoplasm. Risk of bias, certainty of evidence, and procedural maturity were assessed using ROBINS-I, GRADE, and the IDEAL framework. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed. Six retrospective comparative cohorts including 314 patients were identified. R-TAMIS was associated with a higher likelihood of full-thickness resection (OR 11.77, 95%CI 1.40-98.85; P = 0.02), an outcome not appropriate for every lesion. R0 resection was comparable(OR 1.30, 95%CI 0.49-3.47; P = 0.60), with no significant differences in operative time, estimated blood loss, complications, conversion, readmission, or length of stay. Hospital costs tended to be higher with R-TAMIS(I²=99%). All outcomes were supported by very-low-certainty evidence. IDEAL assessment showed that R-TAMIS was introduced in centres with established L-TAMIS experience, while the robotic technique remained in an earlier phase of development. Comparative evidence shows broadly comparable outcomes. Difference in achieved excision depth requires confirmation using standardized outcome definitions and clinically appropriate case selection. These results were achieved despite greater procedural maturity of L-TAMIS and, in some cohorts, more challenging robotic case selection. This developmental asymmetry highlights the need to determine whether maturation and standardization of R-TAMIS will translate its technical capabilities into clinically meaningful advantages in appropriately selected, technically demanding lesions.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Previous studies investigating gastrointestinal (GI) diseases have primarily focused on the composition, gene expression, and specific strains of gut microbiota. However, the impact of genetic variations, especially structural variations (SVs) in microbial genomes, on the development of GI tumors has been largely overlooked. In this study, we analyzed 1,027 fecal metagenomes from seven data sets and identified 8,278 coverage-defined SVs across 51 bacterial species in the gut microbiomes. We found that SVs were prevalent in the gut microbiota of studied cohorts. Surprisingly, the genetic makeup of SV-based clusters differed significantly between healthy individuals and those with colorectal cancer (CRC), indicating substantial intra-specific diversity within these populations. By integrating taxonomic-SV markers, we achieved optimal accuracy in early CRC detection, and the SVs also displayed regional heterogeneity. Microbial genetic variation provides additional insights into taxonomy and functionality, allowing us to have a more precise understanding of the microbiota associated with CRC. Notably, our study uncovered potential links between microbial SVs and metabolic disorders of CRC, including SV regions that encode glycoside hydrolases associated with disordered carbohydrate metabolism in CRC. We integrated a framework called MicroSVsProfiler to identify and classify SVs in individuals diagnosed with CRC, as well as in healthy controls. Our findings underscore the importance of considering SVs in microbiome studies, especially in the absence of strain-specific differences in abundance. Future research should explore the deeper layer of the microbiota's structural variantome for a better understanding of the occurrence and characteristics of CRC across different stages.IMPORTANCEMost microbiome studies of colorectal cancer focus on which bacterial species are more or less abundant, potentially overlooking genetic differences among strains of the same species. By analyzing 1,027 fecal metagenomes from seven independent cohorts, we show that large-scale changes in bacterial genomes, known as structural variations, provide disease-related information that is not captured by species abundance alone. These strain-level SV signatures distinguished healthy individuals from patients with colorectal cancer, improved early-cancer classification when combined with taxonomic markers, and varied across geographic populations. We also found that cancer-associated structural variations were linked to altered microbial metabolic functions, particularly carbohydrate metabolism and glycoside hydrolases. Together, these findings establish microbial structural variation as a complementary dimension of the gut microbiome and provide a framework for developing more precise, population-aware biomarkers and for investigating how strain-level genetic changes may contribute to metabolic disturbances associated with colorectal cancer.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Major low anterior resection syndrome (LARS) affects approximately 60% of rectal cancer survivors, causing urgency and decreased bowel control, reducing quality of life. Bile acid malabsorption (BAM) is an under-recognized contributor whose prevalence and treatment efficacy remain unclear. This proof-of-concept study evaluated the effectiveness of colesevelam for treating LARS and described the prevalence of BAM. This double-blind randomized placebo-controlled crossover trial was conducted between 2021 and 2024 in New Zealand. Adults aged 18-85 years with major LARS received colesevelam (up to 1.25 g, three times daily) or placebo for 5 weeks, separated by a 6-week washout period. A subset of patients underwent 75-selenium homocholic acid taurine (SeHCAT) testing for BAM. The outcomes of interest included changes in the LARS score, Fecal Incontinence Quality of Life Scale (FIQL), and Short-Form 12 (SF-12) questionnaire, with a composite outcome reflecting clinically important improvements. Of 80 eligible patients, 49 were randomized. However, 36 patients completed the study after washout and were included in a per-protocol analysis (mean age 71 years; 69% male). In these 36 patients, colesevelam did not significantly improve LARS scores, but did significantly improve the SF-12 mental component summary (median +2.36; 95% confidence interval 0.00 to 10.25; P < 0.01) and FIQL depression/self-perception. Eight of 19 patients (42%) had BAM and exhibited significant improvements in SF-12 physical and mental item scores with colesevelam. Using composite criteria, colesevelam produced a 33% response rate, versus 8% for placebo, with higher rates in BAM-positive (50%) than BAM-negative (11%) patients. BAM is a treatable contributor to LARS, present in 40% of tested patients. Although treating all LARS patients with bile acid sequestrants provides limited benefit, SeHCAT testing identifies patients likely to respond. BAM assessment would be beneficial if incorporated into LARS management.

ABO blood groups have a certain correlation with the incidence of many diseases. We aimed to explore the association between ABO blood groups and the top 25 fatal diseases in China. We constructed a retrospective cohort of 1,704,333 blood donors to investigate the association between ABO blood groups and the top 25 fatal diseases among Chinese individuals. We summarised differences in disease patterns across blood groups using multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression models. Among the enrolled participants, type A (HR = 1.07; 95% CI = 1.03-1.09, P = 0.004) and type B (HR = 1.06; 95% CI = 1.02-1.09, P = 0.045) donors were more likely to develop ischaemic heart disease (I20-25) than type O donors. Mean hospital stay differed significantly among blood groups for C18-20 (P = 0.045) and I20-25 (P = 0.008). We found a significant correlation between ABO blood groups and the top 25 fatal diseases in China, including ischaemic heart disease, diabetes, and colorectal cancer among blood donors. The associations should be considered exploratory and require independent validation for the general population. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Therapeutic resistance remains a major limitation to the durable control of cancer despite advances in chemotherapy, radiotherapy, targeted therapy, and immunotherapy. Resistance is shaped not only by tumor-intrinsic genetic and epigenetic alterations but also by extrinsic factors, including the gut microbiota. The intestinal microbial ecosystem can influence treatment response through direct drug biotransformation, modulation of host immunity and inflammation, production of bioactive metabolites, alteration of epithelial barrier function, and interactions with the tumor microenvironment. This narrative review synthesizes these mechanisms across chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and immune checkpoint blockade, with particular emphasis on Colorectal Cancer (CRC), while incorporating evidence from breast, lung, melanoma, and other relevant tumor types. Microbial metabolites, including short-chain fatty acids, bile-acid derivatives, tryptophan metabolites, and microbially generated organic acids, can influence signaling, immune-cell function, redox balance, and treatment sensitivity. We further evaluate microbiome-directed approaches, including dietary modulation, probiotics, fecal microbiota transplantation, antibiotic stewardship, and inhibition of microbial drug-metabolizing enzymes. Particular attention is given to the translational challenges of patient-to-patient microbiome variability, safety, biomarker reproducibility, treatment timing, and cancer-type specificity. Collectively, current evidence supports the gut microbiota as a biologically plausible and potentially modifiable determinant of cancer therapy response, but clinical implementation will require mechanism-based biomarkers and rigorously controlled prospective studies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Ferulic acid (FA), a naturally occurring phenolic compound widely distributed in plants, exhibits diverse pharmacological activities, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antiviral, anticancer, and metabolic regulatory effects. However, its therapeutic application is limited by challenges including poor bioavailability, rapid metabolism, and inadequate tissue-specific delivery. This review aimed to critically evaluate the therapeutic potential of FA in combination with novel natural and synthetic scaffolds, with particular emphasis on synergistic or complementary effects beyond FA monotherapy in cancer, viral infections, and metabolic diseases. The objective was to delineate the molecular mechanisms underlying these combination strategies and assess their potential for improving therapeutic efficacy, targeting, and translational applicability. A comprehensive literature search was conducted using major scientific databases, including PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar, National Library of Medicine (NLM), and Relemed. Published studies investigating FA alone or in combination with natural or synthetic scaffolds, including polymeric micelles, lipid-based nanocarriers, phytochemical combinations, and synthetic therapeutic systems, were critically evaluated. Evidence relevant to oncology, viral infections, metabolic disorders, and associated complications was synthesized according to therapeutic outcomes and molecular mechanisms. Particular emphasis was placed on miRNA-target interactions, oxidative stress, mitochondrial signaling, inflammatory and immunomodulatory pathways, lipid metabolism, and fibrotic signaling networks. The reviewed evidence indicates that scaffold-assisted and combination-based delivery can enhance the therapeutic activity and biological availability of FA across multiple disease settings. In colorectal cancer, FA incorporated into polymeric micellar systems was associated with modulation of the miR-221/TP53INP1 axis, promoting apoptotic responses and suppressing proliferative signaling. FA combined with natural and synthetic antiviral scaffolds demonstrated inhibitory effects on viral replication through modulation of host-virus signaling interactions and cellular stressresponse pathways. In metabolic disorders, FA-based formulations were associated with attenuation of visceral adiposity, improvement of endothelial dysfunction and atherosclerotic changes, and reduction of hepatic lipid accumulation through regulation of genes involved in lipid metabolism. Furthermore, FA-loaded lipid nanoformulations showed therapeutic potential in diabetic nephropathy through modulation of TGF-β1/Hippo pathway interactions, with associated effects on mitochondrial homeostasis and fibrotic signaling. Collectively, the evidence suggests that combining FA with natural or synthetic scaffolds may overcome several limitations associated with conventional FA administration and enhance its pharmacological effects through improved delivery, bioavailability, and pathway-specific activity. The observed effects across cancer, viral, and metabolic diseases are consistent with FA's ability to simultaneously influence oxidative stress, inflammation, mitochondrial function, cell survival, metabolism, and immune signaling. Importantly, scaffold-based delivery may provide opportunities to achieve more sustained or tissue-directed exposure, while combination strategies may permit modulation of interconnected pathological pathways that are unlikely to be adequately controlled by single-agent therapy. FA represents a promising multifunctional bioactive compound whose therapeutic potential may be substantially enhanced through rational combination with natural and synthetic scaffolds. Evidence from preclinical studies supports its potential application in cancer, viral infections, and metabolic diseases through coordinated modulation of multiple molecular and cellular pathways. Scaffold-assisted FA delivery and synergistic combination strategies therefore provide a potential foundation for developing next-generation multimodal therapeutics with improved bioavailability, targeting, and therapeutic precision. Well-designed clinical studies are warranted to establish their safety, efficacy, optimal formulations, and translational value.

Following publication of the article entitled "The Role of Noncoding RNAs in the Prognosis and Diagnosis of Colorectal Cancer: An Emerging Biomarker" [1], certain phrases and expressions were identified that were unclear or inconsistent with established scientific terminology. Corrected text: The long non-coding RNA Linc00707 is another example of non-coding RNA dysregulation in tumor cells. A protein called linc00707, which has been linked to a number of biological processes, is elevated and eliminates miRNAs in mesenchymal stem cells in human bone marrow as well as in hepatocellular carcinoma, gastric disease, and breast cancer growth. It does this via increasing osteogenesis, which causes hepatocellular carcinoma and its metastasis [55]. The original article has been updated accordingly. This corrigendum is published to ensure transparency and accuracy of the scholarly record. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Brain metastases (BM) affect nearly 30% of patients with solid tumors. Despite this prevalence, the mechanisms underlying brain tumor-related epilepsy (BTRE) in this population remain incompletely elucidated. This study aims to investigate risk factors associated with seizure occurrence in patients with BM, focusing on histology and molecular markers of the primary tumor. We conducted a retrospective cohort study on 325 patients who underwent surgical resection of BM between 2014 and 2019. Clinical, radiological, and molecular data were analyzed using univariate and multivariable regression models to assess seizure risk factors. Overall Survival (OS) was assessed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression models. Seizures occurred in 32% of patients. Frontal (P<0.001) and parietal (P=0.05) locations were significantly associated with seizure occurrence. Ovarian cancer exhibited the highest seizure prevalence (80%, P=0.001), followed by melanoma (44%), breast (35%), and colorectal cancer (34%). Regarding molecular status, we found a significant association between seizures and both BRAF mutations in melanoma (P=0.03) and HER2 positive subtype breast cancer (P=0.01). Seizure occurrence at onset correlated with improved OS (P=0.01). Our findings suggest an association between seizure risk and molecular status of the primary tumor, specifically BRAF mutations in melanoma and HER2+ breast cancer subtype. Additionally, we found an improved OS in BM patients experiencing seizures at onset of disease. These findings are exploratory and warrant confirmation in larger cohorts; this could help refine seizure-risk estimation and prognostic assessment in surgically treated patients with brain metastases.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The exploration of cellular heterogeneity within the tumor microenvironment (TME) via single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) is essential for understanding cancer progression and response to therapy. Current scRNA-seq approaches, however, lack spatial context and rely on incomplete datasets of ligand-receptor interactions, limiting accurate cell type annotation and cell-cell communication inference. This study addresses these challenges using a novel graph neural network model that enhances cell-type prediction and cell-interaction analysis. Our study utilized a dataset consisting of 49 024 cells from 19 patients across three cancer types: leukemia, breast invasive carcinoma, and colorectal cancer. The proposed scGSL model demonstrated robust performance, achieving an average accuracy of 84.83%, precision of 86.23%, recall of 81.51%, and an F1 score of 80.92% across all datasets. These metrics represent a significant enhancement over existing methods, which typically exhibit lower performance metrics. Additionally, by reviewing existing literature on gene interactions within the TME, the scGSL model proves to robustly identify biologically meaningful gene interactions in an unsupervised manner, validated by significant expression differences in key gene pairs across various cancers. The source code and data used in this study can be found at https://github.com/LiYuechao1998/scGSL.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To evaluate sex differences in liver metastases at diagnosis across major gastrointestinal adenocarcinomas and assess variation by primary site and age. Population-based cross-sectional study using Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results data (2012-2022). Patients aged 15 years or older with colorectal, esophagogastric, pancreatic, or biliary adenocarcinoma and known status of liver metastasis at diagnosis were selected. Patients with concurrent extrahepatic metastases were included. Sex and age. Prevalence of synchronous liver metastases documented at diagnosis. Prevalence ratios (PRs) were estimated using modified Poisson regression with robust variance, adjusting for age, primary site, and year of diagnosis. Effect modification by primary site and age was assessed. Among 410,439 patients, the overall prevalence of liver metastases was 22.2% and higher in males than females (23.5% vs 20.6%). Female sex was associated with a lower prevalence of liver metastases (adjusted PR 0.86; 95% CI, 0.85-0.87; P < 0.001). Effect modification by primary site was observed (P for interaction < 0.001): females had lower prevalence in colorectal (PR 0.84), esophagogastric (PR 0.69), and pancreatic (PR 0.89), higher prevalence in extrahepatic biliary (PR 1.14), and no significant difference in intrahepatic biliary cancers (PR 1.04). There was also evidence of effect modification by age (P for interaction < .001), with sex differences in liver metastasis prevalence attenuating across older age groups. Sex differences in liver metastases at diagnosis vary by primary site and age across gastrointestinal adenocarcinomas. Female sex is associated with lower prevalence of liver metastases in most tumor types, particularly in early-onset disease, except extrahepatic biliary cancers. These findings highlight sex as a clinically relevant variable associated with metastatic presentation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Physical activity is associated with reduced colorectal cancer (CRC) risk. Preclinical models suggest that the mechanism responsible for these beneficial effects may be due to reducing inflammatory bone marrow-derived cell production and migration to the colon by CCL2 signaling. However, whether CCL2 signaling is a mechanism for exercise-induced early CRC protection is unknown. We sought to establish this link by inducing bone marrow-derived cell mobilization via the CCL2 signaling axis during exercise training in a chemically induced CRC model in which aberrant crypt foci (ACF) are a measure of early CRC. Mice were randomized to sedentary (SED) or exercise training (EX; treadmill: 3x/week, up to 1hr/d conditions; n=9-17/group) at age 21 weeks after having received 4 weekly doses of azoxymethane to initiate ACF. From age 21-24, mice received nine CCL2 recombinant (CCL2r) injections to induce marrow-derived cell mobilization during CRC initiation, with control mice injected with PBS. Tissues were collected at age 47 weeks to quantify CRC initiation, marrow-derived immune cells, and colon proliferative (β-catenin), and inflammatory (STAT3, NF-κB) signaling. EX reduced CRC in control mice; however, ACF were significantly more abundant in EX-CCL2r compared to EX-PBS (n=6/group). In the colon, the exercise-induced significant reduction of non-classical monocytes was prevented by CCL2r, and total and bone-marrow derived M2 macrophages trended lower with exercise independent of CCL2r (P = 0.095). Colon β-catenin trended lower in EX compared to SED (P = .0734). Our results recombinant CCL2 injections reverses the protective effects of exercise training on ACF formation, suggesting that CCL2 signaling is a relevant mechanism for exercise-induced protection.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To evaluate whether integrated primary tumor biology, combining primary tumor location and RAS/BRAF status, defines recurrence phenotypes and survival trajectories after liver resection for colorectal liver metastases (CRLM). Selection for resection remains largely morphology-based, although tumor biology strongly influences post-hepatectomy outcomes. Primary tumor site and RAS/BRAF status are individually prognostic, but whether their integration identifies distinct post-resection trajectories is unclear. An international multicenter cohort of patients undergoing liver resection for CRLM between 2017 and 2023 was analyzed. Integrated biology was defined a priori as left-sided-wild-type, right-sided-wild-type, rectal-wild-type, left-sided-RAS-mutant, right-sided-RAS-mutant, rectal RAS-mutant, and BRAF-mutant disease. Primary outcomes were recurrence-free survival (RFS) and overall survival (OS). Secondary outcomes included early recurrence, disseminated first recurrence, and first recurrence phenotype. Among 3162 patients from 44 centers, 2415 (76.4%) developed recurrence and 1342 (42.4%) died. Integrated biology was independently associated with both RFS and OS (global P<0.001 for both). Compared with left-WT tumors, the highest mortality risks were observed in BRAF-mutant disease [hazard ratio (HR): 2.68, 95% CI: 2.02-3.57, P<0.001] and right-RAS-mutant disease (HR: 2.32, 95% CI: 1.94-2.79, P<0.001). Integrated biology was also associated with early recurrence, disseminated first recurrence, and first recurrence phenotype. Rectal-RAS-mutant tumors had the strongest association with lung-only recurrence [relative risk ratio (RRR): 3.38, 95% CI: 2.22-5.13, P<0.001] and disseminated recurrence (RRR: 2.57, 95% CI: 1.86-3.55, P<0.001) relative to liver-only recurrence. Integrated primary tumor biology identifies clinically distinct post-hepatectomy disease trajectories after CRLM resection. Combining primary tumor site with RAS/BRAF status may support preoperative counseling, surveillance planning, and trial stratification.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Accurate polyp segmentation is critical for early colorectal cancer detection, yet models trained on one endoscopic dataset often degrade during cross-domain evaluation. One major source of this gap is acquisition-induced appearance variation, where imaging settings and post-processing pipelines introduce color shifts that encourage models to rely on domain-specific cues. Existing image-level Fourier amplitude approaches reduce global appearance discrepancy but align the entire image spectrum before feature extraction, which risks coupling mucosal background statistics with polyp-relevant signals. We instead modulate the Fourier amplitude of encoder features. Specifically, we decompose the feature amplitude into low- and high-frequency bands and recalibrate their second-order amplitude statistics in a projected space, while preserving the original phase. Since spectral modulation can attenuate fine boundary-related high-frequency responses, we complement it with directional edge refinement guided by an auxiliary luminance signal. Extensive experiments across five polyp segmentation benchmarks under cross-domain protocols show consistent improvements over strong baselines. Quantitatively, the proposed method attains the highest Dice on all five benchmarks (0.930 on Kvasir-SEG and 0.938 on CVC-ClinicDB in-domain; 0.891, 0.805, and 0.830 on the unseen CVC-300, CVC-ColonDB, and ETIS datasets).

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a highly heterogeneous malignancy. Although surgery-based multimodal therapy provides durable benefits for a subset of patients with localized disease, a considerable proportion of patients still experience recurrence or progression post-treatment. Delineating the molecular mechanisms underlying CRC progression and chemoresistance is imperative for identifying therapeutic targets and thereby improving treatment outcomes. Using single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), we identified C-C motif chemokine ligand 7 (CCL7) as a key mediator of intercellular communication between tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) and CRC cells within the tumor microenvironment (TME). TAMs express and secrete high levels of CCL7, which reprograms lipid metabolism in CRC cells, induces the accumulation of lipid droplets (LDs), and markedly promotes CRC cell proliferation and chemoresistance. Elevated CCL7 expression is associated with poor prognosis in patients with CRC. Bulk RNA-seq revealed that CCL7 markedly upregulates the expression of the transcription factor BATF3. Integrating CUT&Tag profiling, HOMER de novo/known motif enrichment analysis, FIMO prediction, co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP), and dual-luciferase reporter assays, we demonstrated that BATF3 interacts with JunD to synergistically activate the USP22 promoter, thereby upregulating USP22 expression. Furthermore, USP22 deubiquitinates and stabilizes DGAT2, thereby promoting LD accumulation and lipid metabolic reprogramming, which accelerates malignant progression and acquired chemoresistance in CRC. By dissecting the intricate crosstalk within the CRC microenvironment, we elucidated the molecular cascade through which the CCL7-dependent BATF3/USP22/DGAT2 axis drives tumor progression and chemoresistance. Targeting this axis may block lipid metabolic reprogramming and thereby curb these malignant phenotypes, highlighting a promising therapeutic strategy for CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Lynch syndrome is the most common inherited cancer predisposition syndrome, affecting approximately one in 350-450 individuals, yet the majority of carriers remain undiagnosed, representing a substantial and preventable public health burden. Caused by germline pathogenic variants in DNA mismatch repair (MMR) genes, Lynch syndrome confers markedly elevated and heterogeneous risks of colorectal, endometrial, and multiple extracolonic cancers. Advances in molecular diagnostics, particularly universal tumour testing for MMR deficiency, have transformed case identification and enabled targeted germline testing and cascade screening of relatives at risk. Despite these advances, implementation remains inconsistent, with substantial attrition across diagnostic pathways and inequities in access to care. Preventive strategies-including colonoscopic surveillance, aspirin chemoprevention, and risk-reducing surgery-are effective but require gene-specific and individualised application. Therapeutically, the immunogenic biology of MMR-deficient tumours has positioned Lynch syndrome at the forefront of precision oncology, with immune checkpoint inhibitors delivering substantial benefit and emerging vaccine strategies offering promise for cancer interception. In this Review, we provide an integrated overview of Lynch syndrome across the continuum of care, highlighting advances in biology, diagnosis, prevention, and treatment, while emphasising the crucial need to align scientific progress with equitable and effective health-system delivery.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (PAI-1), encoded by the SERPINE1 gene, is a key regulator of the fibrinolytic system through inhibition of the plasminogen activators urokinase (uPA) and tissue-type plasminogen activator (tPA). Although this canonical function would be expected to limit extracellular matrix degradation and tumor invasion, elevated PAI-1 expression is consistently associated with tumor progression and poor clinical outcomes across multiple cancer types. This apparent contradiction, known as the "PAI-1 paradox," highlights the diverse biological functions of PAI-1 beyond fibrinolysis. Within the tumor microenvironment, PAI-1 regulates several hallmarks of cancer through interactions with extracellular matrix components and receptors such as LRP1, uPAR, and integrins. These interactions influence angiogenesis, apoptosis resistance, tumor cell migration, and extracellular matrix remodeling. Emerging evidence also indicates that PAI-1 shapes the immune microenvironment by modulating immune cell recruitment and macrophage polarization, although the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Clinically, SERPINE1 overexpression correlates with poor prognosis in numerous malignancies, including colorectal, lung, breast, and gastric cancers. Pharmacological targeting of the PAI-1 axis with small-molecule inhibitors or neutralizing antibodies shows antitumor activity in preclinical models, and the oral inhibitor TM5614 has reached phase III clinical trial in chronic myeloid leukemia and melanoma. This narrative review summarizes current knowledge of PAI-1 regulation and function in cancer and discusses therapeutic strategies targeting this pathway.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) develops not only through malignant epithelial cells but also through immune-cell reprogramming within the tumour microenvironment. Tumour-associated macrophages (TAMs) play a central role in mediating immune suppression, but how tumour-associated cues drive their immunosuppressive programming remains poorly defined. Public CRC single-cell transcriptomic analysis, 20 paired CRC and adjacent non-tumour tissues, THP-1-derived macrophage polarisation models, and HCT116-conditioned TAM-like macrophages were analysed. Selected findings were validated in primary human monocyte-derived macrophages and SW480 CRC cells. S100A11 gain- and loss-of-function assays, SIRT6 rescue experiments, coimmunoprecipitation, immunofluorescence, Western blotting, quantitative PCR, flow cytometry, SMAD3 immunoprecipitation, TGF-β neutralisation, and CRC-cell functional assays were performed to investigate the underlying mechanism and functional consequences. An immunodeficient HCT116 xenograft tumour-growth model and an in vitro HCT116/CD8+ T-cell co-culture system were further used to assess tumour growth and CD8+ T-cell activation and effector-marker expression, respectively. S100A11 was recurrently detected in monocyte/macrophage compartments across CRC single-cell datasets and was elevated in CRC tissues. High S100A11 expression was associated with CD206+ macrophage-related features. S100A11 enhanced an immunosuppressive macrophage phenotype with increased expression of CD206, PPARG/PPARγ, IL-10, TGF-β, PD-L1 and PD-L2 in macrophage models. Mechanistically, S100A11 associated with SIRT6 and was accompanied by reduced SIRT6-SMAD2/3 association, increased SMAD3 acetylation, and increased SMAD2/3 phosphorylation. SIRT6 overexpression partially reversed S100A11- and TGF-β-induced macrophage polarisation. Conditioned medium from S100A11-overexpressing TAM-like macrophages increased HCT116 proliferation, clonogenicity, migration, and invasion, reduced apoptosis, promoted HCT116 xenograft growth, and suppressed CD8+ T-cell activation and effector-marker expression in vitro. These effects were attenuated by SIRT6 overexpression in TAM-like macrophages. TGF-β neutralisation attenuated the conditioned-medium-induced increase in HCT116 proliferation and partially restored CD8+ T-cell CD69 expression. S100A11 is a macrophage-associated regulator of immunosuppressive TAM polarisation in CRC and may contribute to tumour-promoting macrophage reprogramming within the tumour microenvironment. These findings suggest that the S100A11-SIRT6-SMAD3 pathway warrants further investigation as a potential target for macrophage reprogramming in the colorectal cancer immune microenvironment.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer is the fourth most frequently diagnosed cancer and the second leading cause of cancer death in the United States. Treatment of localized disease usually includes surgery, sometimes followed by adjuvant systemic therapy, while advanced or metastatic disease is often treated with multiple lines of systemic therapy, based on biomarker status. These NCCN Guidelines Insights detail recent updates to the NCCN Guidelines for Colon Cancer, including recommendations for pretreatment DPYD testing to decrease the risk of severe fluoropyrimidine toxicity; updates to adjuvant therapy of nonmetastatic colon cancer based on the results of recent clinical trials; and a reorganization of the systemic therapies for advanced or metastatic disease based on biomarker status, highlighting changes to the treatment recommendations for BRAF V600E mutation-positive disease.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
In-hospital operative delay may reflect patient complexity and perioperative care processes, but its association with outcomes after colorectal surgery remains incompletely characterized. We evaluated whether surgery after the day of admission identified a clinically distinct subgroup with worse inpatient outcomes and greater resource utilization. Using the Nationwide Inpatient Sample, adults undergoing colorectal surgery following elective hospital admission between 2016 and 2022 were identified. Patients were categorized as same-day surgery (hospital day 0) or operative delay (surgery after admission). Delay duration was categorized as day 1, days 2-5, and days 6-10. Outcomes included postoperative complications, non-home discharge, length of stay, in-hospital mortality, and total hospital charges. Survey-weighted multivariable models adjusted for patient demographics, socioeconomic factors, transfer status, procedure type, All Patient Refined Diagnosis Related Group severity of illness and risk of mortality, and hospital characteristics. Sensitivity analyses excluded transferred patients, evaluated postoperative length of stay, replaced APR-DRG measures with individual Elixhauser comorbidities, and assessed robustness to unmeasured confounding using E-values. Among 175,515 patients, 14,336 (8.2%) underwent surgery after admission. Patients with operative delay were older and more frequently had major or extreme illness severity, major or extreme risk of mortality, and interhospital transfer. After adjustment, operative delay was associated with higher probabilities of postoperative complications (14.91% vs. 12.95%; adjusted difference, 1.96 percentage points), non-home discharge (27.45% vs. 22.25%; adjusted difference, 5.20 percentage points), and in-hospital mortality (0.78% vs. 0.58%; adjusted difference, 0.19 percentage points), as well as longer length of stay (6.82 vs. 5.01 days; adjusted difference, 1.81 days) and higher total hospital charges ($96,656 vs. $87,823; adjusted difference, $8833). Complications, length of stay, and charges increased across longer delay intervals, with the largest differences after delays of 6-10 days. In-hospital operative delay among adults undergoing colorectal surgery was associated with worse inpatient outcomes and increased resource utilization. Longer total length of stay appeared to reflect hospital days accrued before surgery rather than prolonged postoperative recovery. Operative delay may reflect patient complexity and perioperative care processes although the clinical necessity or modifiability of longer preoperative intervals could not be determined.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Hemorrhoidal disease is a common colorectal condition affecting millions. Recently, minimally invasive approaches have gained popularity for their faster recovery. However, current literature lacks a comprehensive comparison between these two methods. This systematic review and meta-analysis compares the efficacy and outcomes of stapled hemorrhoidopexy (SH) and laser hemorrhoidoplasty (LH). A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus identified studies comparing SH and LH. Patient cohorts were analyzed for recovery, perioperative outcomes, and complications. Meta-analysis was performed using R to calculate pooled Odds Ratios (OR) and Weighted Mean Differences (WMD). LH demonstrated a significantly shorter mean operative time compared to SH (25.9 vs. 33.0 min; MD = 7.14). The stapled approach was associated with significantly higher rates of postoperative urinary retention (7.7% vs. 3.0%; OR = 1.92), stenosis (4.5% vs. 0%; OR = 9.74), and longer hospital stays (MD = 16.32). No significant differences were observed regarding estimated blood loss (MD = 2.49), return to normal activity, readmission, postoperative bleeding, or overall VAS pain scores at any time point (12 h, 24 h, 1 week, 2 weeks, and 3 months). Subgroup analyses indicated LH yielded significantly lower pain at 3 months in severe cases. LH and SH showed no statistically significant differences across several reported short-term outcomes, including postoperative pain, bleeding, and time to return to normal activities. While LH was associated with shorter operative times, reduced hospital stays, and lower rates of urinary retention and stenosis in the available studies, these findings must be interpreted with caution. Crucially, the true comparative therapeutic efficacy of these techniques remains uncertain. Because relevant variables like symptom resolution, patient-reported outcomes, disease-specific functional outcomes were insufficiently assessed, while recurrence data are limited by heterogeneous and inadequately reported follow-up, this analysis permits conclusions regarding short-term perioperative recovery, but not robust conclusions regarding comparative long-term success and efficacy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Adenosine signaling through A2A and A2B adenosine receptors (ARs) suppresses antitumor immunity and promotes tumor progression, limiting immune checkpoint blockade in microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer (CRC). Here, we identified imidazo[1,2-a]pyrazine-urea derivatives as a new chemotype of dual hA2A/hA2B AR antagonists. SAR studies revealed that 3-iodination of the core scaffold enhanced receptor affinity and functional antagonism, with 5p emerging as a representative lead. MD simulations showed that 5p can be accommodated in the orthosteric pockets of both AR subtypes through distinct binding modes, with the 3-iodo substituent occupying adjacent subpockets. Representative compounds inhibited adenosine-induced CREB phosphorylation, restored Th1 cytokine production, and increased CD4+ and CD8+ T cell infiltration. In CD73-high CRC models, 5p suppressed tumor growth and potentiated anti-PD-1 efficacy. These findings support dual A2A/A2B AR antagonism as a strategy to reprogram the adenosine-rich tumor microenvironment and improve CRC immunotherapy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Using inducible forward genetics, we recently discovered a dibenzothiazepinone (1) with activity against cancer cells via inhibition of the ribosome biogenesis factor NVL (nuclear valosin-containing protein-like). Herein, we delineate a comprehensive structure-activity relationship (SAR) study that explores the structural space surrounding the dibenzothiazepinone scaffold. A series of 115 analogs were synthesized and evaluated for activity against the colorectal cancer cell line HCT116 and counter-screened against cells CRISPR engineered to express a compound-resistant mutation in NVL. Our initial medicinal chemistry-driven campaign focused on improving potency, metabolic stability, and in vivo exposure and clearance. A fluorescence polarization assay with recombinant human NVL established a correlation between NVL-binding and antiproliferative activity. Cryo-EM structures of human NVL with select inhibitors revealed a binding mode that is consistent with the SAR data. This study led to the in vivo analog 100 (MM927), which we reported to suppress tumor growth in vivo without detectable toxicity via targeting the NVL.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
G-Quadruplexes are non-canonical nucleic acid structures mostly located in gene promoters and telomeres. Although G4 stabilization with synthetic/natural ligands is a promising anticancer approach, dense distribution throughout the genome restricts their selective targeting. Additionally, cationic G4 ligands are widely used for good aqueous solubility and G-quadruplex binding, yet the charges reduce the ligand's cellular permeabilization. In this work, the first example of a histone deacetylase-activatable G4 ligand, displaying a significant stabilization upon activation (26 °C, ΔTm), was developed. Having 1.8-fold more cellular uptake, the ligand increased G-quadruplexes in the cell almost 3-fold as verified by the G4-specific antibody. Oncogene expression including anti-apoptotic BCL-2 and telomerase was significantly suppressed, more selectively in HDAC2/HDAC6-overexpressing microsatellite unstable colon cancer, leading to a 73% decrease in proliferation. With a versatile chemical structure and a very large activity difference between ON and OFF states, the ligand has a promising therapeutic potential and can be a useful building block for the development of novel activatable G-quadruplex ligands.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Deep bowel endometriosis (DE), a severe infiltrative form mainly affecting the rectum and sigmoid colon, often requires surgery. We compared conservative (shaving, full-thickness discoid resection) and radical (segmental resection) techniques for postoperative complications and pain reduction. We retrospectively analyzed 91 consecutive patients who underwent surgery for colorectal deep endometriosis (November 2020-October 2024) at a single center. Patients received conservative (shaving or full-thickness disc resection) or radical (segmental resection) treatment. Complications were graded by Clavien-Dindo classification, and pain was assessed preoperatively and at 6 months using a visual analogue scale (VAS). Among 91 patients, 40 (44%) underwent conservative and 51 (56%) radical surgery. Clavien-Dindo grade III complications occurred in 19/91 (20.9%) with 6/40 (15%) patients in the conservative group and 13/51 (25.5%) in the radical group (p = 0.22). Bowel leakage rates were comparable, occurring in 10% (4/40) patients following conservative and in 6/51 (11.8%) following radical surgery (p = 0.405); one rectovaginal fistula occurred after radical surgery (1/51, 1.9%), none after conservative. No grade IV complications were recorded. Radical surgery had longer operative time (295 min, 95% CI 267-322 vs 201 min, 95% CI 184-217; p < 0.0001) and hospital stay (mean: 11.57 ± 10.96 days vs mean: 5.78 ± 4.2 days; p < 0.001). Pain scores decreased significantly in both groups (including dysmenorrhea, non-cyclic pelvic pain, dyspareunia, dyschezia; p < 0.001). Radical procedures are linked to longer operative time and hospital stay, neither technique appears clearly superior.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Older adults recovering after fecal ostomy surgery may require substantial care-partner support, yet the activities requiring assistance and barriers to obtaining support are poorly understood. We sought to identify care-partner contributions to recovery and opportunities to improve care-partner involvement. Purposive sampling captured experiences across the aging spectrum and benign and malignant indications. Interviews were analyzed using hybrid inductive-deductive coding and a modified Framework method until thematic saturation was reached. Twenty-one participants completed interviews; median age was 73 years (IQR 68-77), 13 (61.9%) were female, 11 (52.4%) underwent surgery for benign disease, and 10 (47.6%) for colorectal malignancy. Most participants supported an intervention to identify care-partners and organize anticipated recovery tasks. Explicit preoperative identification of anticipated tasks and available care-partners may improve preparation for postdischarge recovery.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) survivorship involves multifaceted challenges, yet evidence remains limited and fragmented. To evaluate unmet supportive care needs, associated factors, lived experiences, and preferred modes of supportive care delivery among Chinese CRC survivors. This mixed-methods study involved 216 CRC survivors who completed the validated Chinese version of Supportive Care Needs Survey Short Form, covering five domains: physical and daily living (PDL), psychological (PSY), sexuality (SEX), patient care and support (PCS), and health system and information (HSI). Participants rated delivery modes (i.e., face-to-face consultations, group sessions, printed materials, and mobile apps). Multivariable linear regression and Firth's penalized logistic regression identified factors associated with unmet needs. Semi-structured interviews were thematically analysed and integrated with quantitative findings. Unmet needs were most prominent in the HSI domain, followed by PSY, PCS, PDL, and SEX. Most frequently reported individual items were from the PSY domain. Female and advanced stage were associated with higher PSY and PDL needs; living with a colostomy markedly increased odds of SEX needs. Mobile apps and printed materials were preferred for SEX needs, whereas face-to-face consultations and mobile apps were preferred across other domains. Qualitative findings highlighted persistent dietary information gaps, emotional concealment, and long chemotherapy waiting times. HSI needs, especially dietary guidance, remained the most pressing domain-level needs, while item-level analyses highlighted certain PSY concerns among Chinese CRC survivors. Mobile apps may be a scalable solution for delivering culturally relevant dietary support and facilitating identification of masked PSY needs among male survivors and SEX needs in colostomy patients. Routine distress screening, community referrals, and reducing chemotherapy delays are also necessary.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Organ/space surgical site infections, including intra-abdominal abscesses and anastomotic leaks, are among the most severe complications after ileocolic resection for Crohn's disease. Biomarker cutoffs validated in oncological colorectal surgery may not translate to Crohn's disease because of modified inflammatory responses due to chronic inflammation and immunosuppressive therapies. Ileocolic resection with primary anastomosis between January 2021 and May 2025. Development of organ/space surgical site infections within 30 days postoperatively, defined according to Centers for Disease Control/National Helathcare Safety Network criteria. Organ/space surgical site infections occurred in 15.7% (18/115) of patients. The C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio on postoperative day 3 demonstrated excellent diagnostic accuracy (area under the curve = 0.932). At an optimal cutoff of 51.77, C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio on postoperative day 3 yielded 94.1% sensitivity, 82.1% specificity, and a negative predictive value of 98.6%. C-reactive protein on postoperative day 3 also showed good accuracy (area under the curve = 0.871) with a negative predictive value of 97.1%. Procalcitonin and leucocyte-based indices showed poor-to-limited discrimination. Retrospective, monocentric design without external validation. In Crohn's disease surgery, C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio on postoperative Day 3 is a strong early predictor of organ/space surgical site infections. Together with C-reactive protein, its exceptionally high negative predictive value provides high "rule out" utility, supporting postoperative surveillance and safe discharge pathways. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Distal rectal transection during laparoscopic ultralow anterior resection or intersphincteric resection is technically demanding and may affect internal anal sphincter preservation, contributing to low anterior resection syndrome. Conformal resection after eversion with asymmetric twice stapling was developed to refine distal transection and stapled coloanal anastomosis in ultralow rectal cancer. Between 2012 and 2021, 448 eligible patients with ultralow rectal cancer underwent laparoscopic ultralow anterior resection or intersphincteric resection (conformal resection after eversion with asymmetric twice stapling, n = 80; double-stapling technique, n = 368). After propensity score matching, 168 patients were included (conformal resection after eversion with asymmetric twice stapling, n = 60; double-stapling technique, n = 108). Operative variables, anastomotic leakage, anastomosis height, low anterior resection syndrome scores at 6, 12, and 24 months after stoma reversal, and 3-year disease-free survival and overall survival. After matching, conformal resection after eversion with asymmetric twice stapling showed a higher anastomosis (3.0 vs 2.0 cm from the anal verge, p < 0.001), a shorter distal resection margin (1.0 vs 1.2 cm, p < 0.001), and a shorter operative time (153 vs 175 min, p = 0.04). Anastomotic leakage occurred more frequently in the double-stapling technique group (1.7 vs 6.5%), although the difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.31). Low anterior resection syndrome outcomes were more favorable with conformal resection after eversion with asymmetric twice stapling at 6 months (major 42.9 vs 72.5%, p = 0.01) and 12 months (35.3 vs 66.7%, p = 0.007), with no differences at 24 months (p = 1.00). Three-year disease-free survival (88.4 vs 86.1%, p = 0.94) and overall survival (89.3 vs 91.5%, p = 0.60) were comparable between groups. Selective eligibility for conformal resection after eversion with asymmetric twice stapling and functional assessment limited to patients who underwent stoma reversal and completed low anterior resection syndrome evaluations. CREATE was associated with a higher anastomosis and faster early functional recovery without increasing perioperative risk or compromising 3-year oncological outcomes. See Video Abstract.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Anastomotic leakage remains a major cause of morbidity, reoperation, and failure to rescue after colorectal surgery. Enhanced recovery pathways have shortened hospitalization, yet clinically important leaks may become apparent after discharge, creating an interval during which subtle deterioration can remain unrecognized. Emerging evidence suggests that delayed recognition, particularly after the onset of sepsis, is associated with worse outcomes. This editorial examines the limitations of relying on operative prevention, isolated clinical features, single inflammatory marker measurements, or unstructured patient-initiated presentation. It proposes a Risk, Trend, and Trigger pathway for closed-loop postoperative surveillance. This framework combines predischarge risk stratification with longitudinal assessment of clinical recovery, vital signs, bowel or stoma function, and C-reactive protein trajectories. Predetermined escalation criteria connect concerning changes with timely surgical review, laboratory assessment, cross-sectional imaging, and source control evaluation. Remote monitoring may extend surveillance into the home, but current evidence primarily supports its feasibility and acceptability rather than its ability to reduce leak-related sepsis or mortality. Technology should therefore complement clinical ownership rather than replace it. Discharge should be treated as an active diagnostic handoff supported by documented clinical baselines, accessible contact routes, explicit response times, and reassessment after negative or indeterminate investigations. Prospective multicenter studies should determine whether this approach reduces diagnostic delay and failure to rescue without increasing unnecessary imaging, alert burden, or inequity.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Nodal staging plays a vital role in pathological staging of colorectal cancer (CRC). According to AJCC guidelines, at least 12 lymph nodes are required for nodal staging. However, many previous studies have shown the importance of retrieving as many lymph nodes as possible. In this study, we evaluated an optical imaging-based device (Cision InVision) to increase lymph node yield in CRC specimens. The device utilizes infrared light to differentiate lymphoid tissue from other tissue. We recruited 31 colorectal resections. A senior resident or pathologist's assistant conventionally grossed the recruited specimens. Thereafter, the remaining fatty tissue was scanned with the device to identify additional lymph nodes. Overall, the device increased the lymph node numbers, with an average increase of 48%. This increase was particularly notable for smaller lymph nodes (<3 mm). In the entire study, a total of 1422 lymph nodes were harvested, including 33 positive lymph nodes from 10 nodal-positive cases. Conventional grossing retrieved 29 positive lymph nodes, whereas the device retrieved 4 additional positive nodes, resulting in two upstaged patients. Among these two patients, one patient was upstaged from node-negative to node-positive disease. In this "proof-of-concept" study with a limited number of subjects, our findings demonstrate that the Cision InVision device increases lymph node yield, especially for smaller nodes, leading to stage changes in 2 out of 31 patients, with one case upstaged from node-negative to node-positive disease. Whereas further research with larger cohorts is needed to address the limitations and explore broader clinical implications, our findings preliminarily highlight its probable value in CRC lymph node assessment.

Colorectal cancer incidence is rising rapidly in Asia, with dietary factors being major modifiable risk factors. High-income Asia Pacific recorded the highest diet-attributable ASDR and ASMR in 2023, while South Asia recorded the lowest. A single-center cohort study using a historical control design was conducted between January 2018 and January 2026. Elderly patients (defined as ≥65 years) undergoing elective high-complexity colorectal surgery were included. Exclusion criteria included synchronous liver metastasis resection, urgent/emergency surgery, or a World Health Organization performance status of 4. The primary outcome was overall postoperative complications within 30 days after surgery. The risk analysis of the outcomes was performed using crude and adjusted risk ratios (aRR) with robust Poisson regression, adjusted for demographic and clinical confounders. A total of 192 patients were included (non-ERAS: 83; ERAS: 109). The median age was 74 years [interquartile ranges (IQR): 70-79], and 52.6% were women. The most common procedures were anterior rectal resection (39.6%) and right hemicolectomy (29.7%). ERAS patients had a significantly shorter hospital stay [3 days (IQR: 2-5) vs. 4 days (IQR: 3-9); ERAS implementation in elderly patients undergoing high-complexity colorectal surgery was associated with lower postoperative morbidity, intensive care unit admission rates, and hospital length of stay, without any documented adverse outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Iliopsoas abscess (IPA) is frequently attributed to tuberculosis in endemic regions, particularly when associated with vertebral involvement. Secondary IPA due to colorectal cancer is rare, accounting for <4% of perforated carcinomas, and can closely mimic infectious etiologies. We report a case of sigmoid mucinous adenocarcinoma (MAC) presenting as a recurrent IPA that was initially managed as presumed Pott's spine. A 69-year-old man presented with a 2-year history of recurrent left iliopsoas collections associated with abdominal swelling and difficulty walking, without rectal bleeding or altered bowel habits. He underwent four drainage procedures and received prolonged empirical anti-tubercular therapy (ATT) despite negative acid-fast bacilli smear, Xpert MTB/RIF assay, and mycobacterial culture. At our institution, magnetic resonance imaging suggested Pott's spine; however, contrast-enhanced computed tomography demonstrated irregular sigmoid wall thickening communicating with a large retroperitoneal collection. Colonoscopic biopsy revealed glandular intraepithelial neoplasia, while serum carcinoembryonic antigen level was markedly elevated (92.23 ng/mL). Exploratory laparotomy yielded 2000 mL of gelatinous necrotic material, followed by segmental sigmoid resection with end colostomy (Hartmann's procedure). Histopathology confirmed pT4bN0Mx MAC. This case illustrates how IPA secondary to colorectal carcinoma can mimic the clinical and radiological features of Pott's spine, making the diagnosis challenging. Sequential diagnostic reassessment was prompted by persistently sterile cultures, gelatinous aspirates, a lack of response to ATT, and cross-sectional imaging demonstrating communication between the sigmoid colon and the retroperitoneal collection. Recurrent or atypical IPA unresponsive to appropriate therapy, should prompt an evaluation for underlying malignancy. Integrating microbiological, radiological, endoscopic, and histopathological assessments is essential to prevent delayed diagnosis of aggressive colorectal cancers presenting as IPA.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
This study identifies and validates serum EPHB2 as a non-invasive candidate biomarker for early detection of colorectal cancer (CRC) and precancerous adenomas. Through integrative analysis of multi-cohort transcriptomics, pan-cancer databases, and single-cell RNA sequencing, EPHB2 was identified as a CRC-specific marker predominantly localized to malignant epithelial cells, with expression progressively elevated from precancerous lesions through advanced carcinoma. Clinical ELISA validation in prospective local and independent external cohorts, supported by tissue immunohistochemistry, demonstrated robust diagnostic performance across both cohorts: serum EPHB2 achieved AUCs of 0.794-0.839 for adenoma detection and 0.816-0.897 for distinguishing CRC from healthy controls, and effectively discriminated neoplastic from benign inflammatory lesions (AUCs of 0.817-0.874). Mechanistic analyses further revealed that EPHB2 expression is associated with Wnt/β-catenin signaling activation in colorectal tumorigenesis. Collectively, these findings establish serum EPHB2 as a promising candidate biomarker that warrants further prospective evaluation for early detection of colorectal neoplasia.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) often requires aggressive multimodal therapy, yet pathological complete response (pCR) to standard chemoradiotherapy remains low. Transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) enables targeted locoregional delivery of chemotherapy to tumor-feeding arteries, and its recent extension, chemo-immunoembolization, permits intraarterial delivery of immune checkpoint inhibitors. This updated systematic review searched MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Web of Science from inception to June 2026 for studies of TACE or transcatheter rectal arterial chemoembolization (TRACE) in LARC, with quality appraised using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Nine studies encompassing 822 patients, 582 of whom received TACE or TRACE, were included, predominantly from China; one further trial is ongoing. pCR rates ranged from 10% to 44.74%. In comparative studies, TRACE with oxaliplatin was associated with lower tumor regression grade 3 (TRG3) rates, reaching significance in the largest comparison, and with a survival benefit in an exploratory TRG3 subgroup analysis, suggesting a possible role in chemoradiotherapy-resistant disease. The highest pCR occurred in a phase II trial of intra-arterial tislelizumab plus TACE in mismatch repair-proficient LARC, with no grade 3-4 immune-related adverse events. Major complications were uncommon. TACE may improve pathological response with an acceptable safety profile in LARC, although comparative evidence is limited and non-randomized; CIETAI provides first-in-human proof-of-concept for intra-arterial delivery of immunotherapy.
