ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
BACKGROUND 5-Fluorouracil (5-FU) is a mainstay chemotherapeutic agent for gastrointestinal malignancies but carries a recognized risk of cardiotoxicity, most often manifesting as coronary vasospasm that can mimic acute myocardial infarction. This report describes the case of a 50-year-old woman with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) due to coronary artery vasospasm during continuous infusion of 5-FU as part of the first round of FOLinic acid (leucovorin), Fluorouracil (5-FU), and OXaliplatin (FOLFOX) chemotherapy for colorectal carcinoma. CASE REPORT A 50-year-old woman with colorectal carcinoma receiving her first cycle of FOLFOX developed severe chest pain during a continuous infusion of 5-FU. Initial emergency department evaluation was reportedly unremarkable, and she was discharged after symptomatic improvement with ketorolac. She returned emergently with recurrent crushing chest pain; a repeat electrocardiogram showed hyperacute T waves and ST-segment elevation, prompting ST-elevation myocardial infarction activation and transfer for emergent catheterization. Coronary angiography revealed no obstructive coronary artery disease. Echocardiography demonstrated a severely reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 30% to 35% with apical akinesis, consistent with 5-FU-induced cardiomyopathy. 5-FU was permanently discontinued, and the patient was treated with vasodilator therapy, with complete resolution of symptoms and normalization of ventricular function on follow-up echocardiography. CONCLUSIONS 5-FU can precipitate life-threatening coronary vasospasm and a fully reversible cardiomyopathy even during a first chemotherapy cycle, in the absence of obstructive coronary artery disease. Early recognition, prompt drug interruption, and a multidisciplinary cardio-oncology approach, including an individualized decision between permanent discontinuation and carefully supervised rechallenge, are essential to guide safe oncologic decision-making.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Fruquintinib is approved, including in the United States and Europe, for previously treated metastatic colorectal cancer, regardless of biomarker status. Using in vitro and clinical data, physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models were developed for fruquintinib and M11, a major metabolite of fruquintinib. The models were applied to evaluate the potential impact of strong/moderate/weak cytochrome P450 (CYP) and 3A4 (CYP3A4) inhibitors and inducers on the pharmacokinetics of fruquintinib and M11. In addition, the PBPK models were applied to evaluate the potential for P-glycoprotein or breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP)-mediated drug-drug interactions, with fruquintinib and M11 as precipitants (inhibitors). The simulations indicated that the changes in plasma exposure of fruquintinib area under the curve (AUC) geometric mean ratio (GMR) during administration with strong/moderate/weak inhibitors of CYP3A4 are negligible (< 1.25), and M11 interactions are weak with strong inhibition. Simulated changes in plasma exposure of fruquintinib in the presence of rifampin (a strong CYP3A4 and moderate CYP2C9 inducer) were > 0.20, but ≤ 0.50 (no significant change in M11). Fruquintinib AUC GMRs were > 0.50, but ≤ 0.80 with moderate CYP3A4 inducers, while the ratio fell between > 0.80 and 1.00 in the presence of weak CYP3A4 inducers. The effects of fruquintinib on the pharmacokinetics of P-glycoprotein or BCRP substrates were not clinically significant. These analyses support avoiding concomitant use of strong, and if possible, moderate CYP3A4 inducers with fruquintinib. In addition, no dose adjustments for fruquintinib are required in the presence of CYP3A4 inhibitors, or for medications that are substrates of P-glycoprotein or BCRP when used concomitantly with fruquintinib.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Patients who prefer a language other than English (LOE) experience well-documented differences in health care access and quality. How care delivery and utilization differ for those requiring professional interpreter services in resident continuity clinics is not well characterized. To compare primary care delivery, preventive screening, chronic disease management, and utilization between patients who did and did not require interpreter services. Retrospective cohort study using electronic health record data, October 2022 to October 2024. Setting and Participants An urban internal medicine resident continuity clinic in St. Louis, MO, with in-person interpreter services; 14,457 adults, of whom 1058 had documented interpreter use (LOE; > 50 preferred languages) and 13,399 did not (English-proficient). Main Measures Demographics, area-based socioeconomic indicators, comorbidity burden, screening adherence, clinic attendance, emergency department (ED) visits, and hospitalizations. No primary outcome was pre-specified. Key Results LOE patients were older and more often uninsured or Medicaid-insured, yet resided in less-deprived, higher-income areas (median ADI national percentile 71 vs 85) and had lower comorbidity burden. Colorectal, breast, and cervical cancer screening did not differ. Among those with diabetes, glycemic control was worse (A1c < 7%: 49.3% vs 56.8%; difference - 7.5%, 95% CI - 12.9 to - 2.1), as were tetanus vaccination and HIV screening. They had lower no-show rates (14.0% vs 21.0%; difference - 7.1%, 95% CI - 7.9 to - 6.2), more completed visits (mean 4.6 vs 3.9; difference + 0.7, 95% CI 0.5 to 0.9), fewer ED visits (36.2% vs 56.3%; difference - 20.1%, 95% CI - 23.1 to - 17.1), and fewer hospitalizations (26.5% vs 37.3%; difference - 10.8%, 95% CI - 13.6 to - 8.0). In this single clinic, LOE patients had greater primary care engagement and lower acute care utilization, with residual gaps in glycemic control and vaccination. These descriptive, hypothesis-generating findings may reflect who reaches care as well as language-access supports and warrant prospective study.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted visualization may support recognition of surgical anatomy, but its influence on dissection line selection remains unclear. We evaluated whether EUREKA-assisted visualization of loose connective tissue and nerve-like structures affects agreement with an expert-defined reference line and surgeons' confidence during total mesorectal excision (TME). This single-center simulation study included six TME scenes with potential ambiguity in dissection line selection and 20 surgeons. Each scene was presented in a fixed order under four conditions: Original, Connective Tissue, Nerve-like Structures, and Combined Overlay. Participants selected the next intended dissection line and rated confidence on a 0-4 scale. Agreement with the reference line was assessed using the Dissection Line Accuracy Score (DLAS; 0-4) and Dissection Line Deviation Area (DLDA). DLAS and confidence were analyzed using ordinal logistic mixed-effects models, and DLDA was analyzed separately by scene using linear mixed-effects models. A total of 480 evaluations were analyzed. Confidence was higher with Connective Tissue (OR, 4.05; 95% CI 2.35-6.95), Nerve-like Structures (OR, 10.49; 95% CI 5.87-18.78), and Combined Overlay (OR, 29.99; 95% CI 15.85-56.71); all Holm-adjusted P < 0.001. Combined Overlay was most consistently associated with reduced DLDA across the six scenes. EUREKA-assisted visualization of Nerve-like Structures, alone or combined with loose Connective Tissue, was associated with closer agreement with the expert-defined reference line during TME. Confidence was higher under all AI-assisted conditions, but higher confidence with Connective Tissue was not accompanied by closer agreement with the reference line, indicating a potential mismatch between confidence and measured performance. Because conditions were presented in a fixed order, learning and recall effects may have influenced these findings.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Neoadjuvant immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) produce unprecedented pathological responses in localised dMMR/MSI-H colon cancer, and organ preservation is now proposed by analogy with dMMR rectal cancer. This analogy is misleading. Upfront colectomy is a short, safe procedure that cures most patients, since most are stage I-II. Segmental colectomy carries very low morbidity, 5-year overall survival exceeds 85%, and functional impairment or stoma-related issues are almost non-existent. Organ preservation requires around six months of ICI, exposes patients to immune-related toxicity and to obstruction or perforation of the primary tumour, relies on response assessment blind to nodal status, risks inappropriate treatment of a misdiagnosed MSI status, is expensive, and leaves an at-risk colon in Lynch syndrome. Partial colectomy should remain the standard - upfront for most patients, after neoadjuvant ICI for selected cases such as cT4 or tumours at risk of R1 resection - with organ preservation confined to randomised trials.

Oxaliplatin is widely used in colorectal cancer treatment, but it may also cause cognitive and emotional problems that reduce patients' quality of life. Neuroinflammation and hippocampal dysfunction are thought to contribute to these effects, yet effective preventive strategies remain limited. Oxaliplatin impaired recognition memory, increased anxiety-like and passive coping-like behavior, and altered several hippocampal molecular measures without affecting locomotion. These findings provide preliminary evidence that maropitant may help limit the neurobehavioral and hippocampal alterations associated with oxaliplatin exposure, although neither the mechanism of this effect nor its dependence on neurokinin-1 receptor blockade was established. Further studies using repeated chemotherapy protocols, both sexes, and complementary molecular methods are needed to confirm these findings and clarify their potential relevance.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality worldwide, with its progression and therapeutic resistance increasingly recognized as consequences of complex metabolic and immune interactions within the tumour microenvironment (TME). Recent advances in single-cell and spatial multi-omics technologies have enabled detailed characterisation of metabolic heterogeneity among TME components, uncovering how distinct metabolic states influence immune function and therapeutic responses. In this review, we summarize recent advances in our understanding of metabolic regulation in the CRC microenvironment, with a particular focus on how distinct immune cell populations contribute to tumour progression and immune suppression through diverse metabolic pathways. We discuss key metabolite-driven signalling networks involving lactate, short-chain fatty acids, bile acids, and amino acid derivatives, and examine how these pathways influence immune cell function and tumour-immune interactions. Furthermore, we highlight emerging therapeutic approaches targeting the metabolic-immune axis, including glutaminase inhibitors, CD36 antagonists, and combination regimens integrating metabolic intervention with immune checkpoint inhibitors. By integrating recent mechanistic discoveries with therapeutic perspectives, this review provides an updated overview of the metabolic-immune landscape in CRC and discusses potential strategies to exploit metabolic vulnerabilities for improving immunotherapy efficacy and overcoming treatment resistance.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Despite effective screening, colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a leading cause of cancer death in the United States. Patient navigation is an evidence-based approach to increasing CRC screening and colonoscopy completion. The study examines how participants who completed colonoscopy experienced relational components of navigation and perceived the role of these relational elements in supporting colonoscopy completion, with the goal of informing navigation program design and implementation. This qualitative study was conducted as part of the Colonoscopy Outreach for Rural Communities (CORC) trial, which evaluated a centrally delivered navigation program supporting colonoscopy completion among rural primary care patients. Using maximum variation sampling, we conducted semi-structured interviews and brief surveys with 55 navigation participants. Two analysts applied deductive and inductive coding with consensus meetings. Iterative, display-based thematic analysis (Miles and Huberman) was used to identify relational components of navigation. Navigation functioned not just through logistical support, but through five interrelated relational components: personal engagement, gentle guidance, care for participant's well-being, partnership in the screening process, and ongoing availability. Participants linked these practices to increased trust, reduced fear, enhanced self-efficacy, and greater perceived support, all contributing to colonoscopy completion. Relational components of navigation were valued by participants as supporting the colonoscopy process. Navigators could be trained to make time for personal, conversation engagement, encourage patients with gentle probing, and demonstrate care for patients' well-being and that they are partners in the process. Additionally, navigation programs could structure workloads to promote availability and continuity for patients. Relational components could be measured as part of the evaluation of navigation programs. Trust scales, patient-reported relational ease, and emotional support could be explored as assessments for these critical aspects of navigation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Tumors with defective DNA-repair machinery accumulate somatic mutations at a high rate, and some of these mutations give rise to neoantigens, short peptide fragments that the immune system can recognize as foreign elements. While the connection between repair deficiency and tumor immunogenicity is well established, few analyses ask which missense neoepitopes encoded by mutations in the repair genes themselves are generated by more than one mutation, and where such shared peptides sit between fully personalized and off-the-shelf vaccine designs. We curated 1419 missense mutations across 29 DNA-repair genes from three TCGA cohorts: invasive breast carcinoma (BRCA), colorectal adenocarcinoma (COAD), and ovarian serous cystadenocarcinoma (OV). For each variant, we generated 8-11mer mutant peptides and ran them through a consensus prediction pipeline (NetMHCpan 4.1, MHCflurry 2.0, and pVACseq), restricted to eight population-frequent HLA class I alleles. Peptides were ranked using a composite score that combined binding affinity (IC50), mutant-versus-wild-type fold change, the number of distinct mutations that produce the same peptide, and gene-level oncogenic relevance. A bipartite mutation-epitope graph was then projected onto the peptide layer to study connectivity. The analysis is purely in silico, covers only missense substitutions, and uses a population-based HLA panel rather than patient genotypes. The pipeline yielded 33,405 unique candidate neoepitopes from 429,464 peptide-HLA predictions. About one in six (5420, 16.2%) were produced by more than one mutation, and the resulting network had a heavy-tailed degree distribution. We identified 836 hub peptides (2.5% of nodes) linked to more than five mutations, and 342 peptides linked to more than ten; the most connected are nested TP53 windows shared by 71 recurrent calls at a single genomic site. Hub and non-hub peptides did not differ meaningfully in predicted affinity (median best IC50 16,774 nM versus 16,671 nM; Cliff's delta -0.02; P = 0.26, Mann-Whitney U), and within the binding subset (IC50 < 5000 nM) hub peptides were marginally weaker binders (1735 nM versus 1420 nM; Cliff's delta +0.08), a difference that did not survive correction across the five comparisons. All 836 hubs derive from TP53. Composite scoring ranked fourteen TP53 peptides at the top, and a stringent affinity filter (IC50 < 50 nM, fold change at least 10x) retained 73 unique MHC-I peptides, 32 of which also showed a wild-type IC50 above 5000 nM, with a class II tier of 127 peptides, as candidates for experimental testing. Among the strongest were XRCC6-derived RYTGIFLDL (IC50 34.4 nM, 558-fold mutant preference) and ATR-derived KLMPMVTDI (IC50 7.7 nM, 1627-fold mutant preference). Treating the missense neoepitope landscape as a mutation-peptide network identifies peptides shared by more than one mutation, concentrated at TP53 hotspots. These shared peptides illustrate design options between fully personalized and off-the-shelf vaccines, but all results are predictions from a population HLA panel and require experimental and patient-level validation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Liquid biopsy as a non-invasive diagnosis tool for tumor genotyping, was limited by its low sensitivity. Ultrasound targeted microbubble destruction (UTMD) technique could temporarily alter tissue permeability, but its role in circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) released remains poor understood. This study included mouse experiments and a prospective clinical study, aimed to investigate whether UTMD could increase the release of ctDNA and thus enhance the sensitivity of liquid biopsy. To establish the safety profile, H&E staining, PCR and Flow cytometric assays were conducted to evaluate liver injury and tumor dissemination after UTMD treatment. To evaluate UTMD-induced ctDNA release, droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) was used to measure ctDNA copies at baseline and 5-30 min post-UTMD in BALB/c nude mice bearing liver metastases established with the human SW1463 colorectal cancer cell line (n = 28) and in patients with colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) (n = 10). In mouse models, UTMD under safety parameters (3∼3.3 MHz frequency, 2 cycles pulse length, 500 Hz PRF, 52.5%∼60% acoustic power and 0.5 MI) did not cause liver inflammation and tumor dissemination. UTMD treatment induced a transient, significant increase in human KRAS ctDNA copies (5-fold increase, P = 0.007), which returned to baseline within 30 min. In human participants with CRLM, sonication of the liver tumors resulted in a 2.2-fold increase (P = 0.045) in KRAS ctDNA mutant allele frequency measured 5 min after the procedure. These findings highlight the clinical utility of diagnostic ultrasound in liquid biopsy for detecting specific oncogene mutations in abdominal diseases, which are critical for personalized cancer therapy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is the third most frequently diagnosed cancer and the second leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. The epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) signaling pathway plays a critical role in CRC pathogenesis and has emerged as an important therapeutic target. This study aimed to evaluate the expression of EGFR and two EGFR-related lncRNAs, ZEB1-AS1 and PITPNA-AS1, in CRC tissues compared to matched adjacent non-tumor tissues (ANTs) to elucidate their potential involvement in colorectal carcinogenesis. Tissue samples from 40 CRC patients and their matched ANTs were obtained from patients undergoing colonoscopy or tumor resection. Relative expression levels of EGFR, ZEB1-AS1, and PITPNA-AS1 were measured using quantitative real-time PCR with ACTB as the internal reference gene. The ZEB1-AS1 expression was also assessed using bioinrmatic tools. ZEB1-AS1 expression was significantly downregulated in CRC tissues compared to ANTs (expression ratio: 0.14, 95% CI: 0.04-0.51, P = 0.003). PITPNA-AS1 showed a trend toward downregulation that did not reach statistical significance (expression ratio: 0.33, 95% CI: 0.08-1.24, P = 0.09), while EGFR expression was not significantly different between the two tissue types (expression ratio: 1.29, 95% CI: 0.36-4.68, P = 0.68). Significant positive correlations were observed in CRC tissues between ZEB1-AS1 and PITPNA-AS1 (r = 0.49, P < 0.001) and between PITPNA-AS1 and EGFR (r = 0.41, P < 0.05). ROC curve analysis revealed that ZEB1-AS1 demonstrated the best diagnostic performance with a sensitivity of 87.18%, specificity of 52.5%, and AUC of 0.69. BMI was significantly associated with ZEB1-AS1 expression (P = 0.018), while no other clinical parameters showed significant associations with the expression of any of the three genes. Our findings demonstrate that ZEB1-AS1 is significantly downregulated in CRC. The significant correlations among the studied genes in tumor tissues suggest potential regulatory interactions within the EGFR signaling network. Further investigations are warranted to elucidate the functional roles of these lncRNAs in CRC pathogenesis and their potential as therapeutic targets.

Spatial omics enables analysis of tissue microenvironmental heterogeneity, but most spatial tools are optimized for transcriptomics and poorly suited to proteomics data. We developed Sphinx, an R package providing a comprehensive workflow for spatial proteomics, including preprocessing, cell annotation, adaptive spatial neighborhood modeling, and functional characterization. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Robot-assisted surgery for colorectal cancer has gained prominence in Japan since its insurance coverage in 2018. The recent da Vinci Single-Port (SP) system enables single-incision surgery, which is expected to improve cosmesis and reduce invasiveness. We analyzed the initial 100 cases performed using the da Vinci SP system to evaluate safety and feasibility. Patients with resectable primary colorectal cancer operated at our institution between January and August 2025 using the SP system were retrospectively reviewed. The surgeons had experience with more than 40 da Vinci Xi cases. Patient demographics, surgical history, procedure type, additional port use, operative time, blood loss, docking and console times, postoperative complications, length of hospital stay, and pathologic findings were assessed. The cohort comprised 47 men and 53 women (median age: 74 y). The tumors were located in the colon (72) and rectum (28). An additional assistant port was required in 29 cases. The median operation time was 187 minutes, blood loss was 0 mL, docking time was 15 minutes, and console time was 103 minutes. Despite the absence of intraoperative complications, conversion to laparoscopy was required in 2 cases. Postoperative complications of Clavien-Dindo grade ≥II occurred in 7 patients. The median hospital stay was 8 days, and the median number of harvested lymph nodes was 18. Colorectal surgery using SP is safe and feasible, with short-term outcomes comparable to those of multiport robotic surgery. Right-sided colon surgeries were safely performed with minimal use of additional ports. Additional studies are required to compare SP with other robotic platforms, such as the da Vinci Xi, and to evaluate long-term outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Immunotherapy has transformed the treatment of several malignancies but provides durable benefit in colorectal cancer (CRC) primarily for mismatch repair-deficient or microsatellite instability-high tumors. Most microsatellite-stable (MSS) CRCs remain resistant because of a profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME), necessitating new therapeutic strategies. This review examines mechanisms of immune resistance within the CRC TME and evaluates current therapeutic approaches, including stromal remodeling, vascular normalization, metabolic reprogramming and immune modulation. It then critically assesses aberrant glycosylation as a regulator of tumor-immune interactions. We discuss how O-glycosylation, sialylation and fucosylation are associated with epithelial differentiation, immune suppression and stromal remodeling, and propose the CRC glycocode as a hypothesis-generating framework linking glycosylation programs with tumor biology, therapeutic vulnerability and patient stratification. Emerging glycan-directed biomarkers and therapies are reviewed in the context of precision immuno-oncology. Literature was identified through PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and Google Scholar (2006-2026). Glycosylation represents an emerging area of investigation in colorectal cancer immunotherapy. Experimental and translational evidence supports further evaluation of glycan-mediated immune regulation and its potential therapeutic targeting. Whether glycosylation-directed interventions can improve outcomes in MSS CRC remains uncertain and requires biomarker-informed prospective clinical trials.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Robotic surgery is increasingly used in rectal cancer treatment, potentially improving precision in the narrow pelvic space. However, evidence on its oncological advantages remains limited. This study evaluated short- and long-term oncological outcomes of robotic total mesorectal excision (TME) in a tertiary referral center, focusing on the prognostic value of circumferential resection margin (CRM), including evaluation of a 5 mm threshold. A retrospective analysis included 135 consecutive patients undergoing robotic TME for rectal cancer between January 2018 and June 2024. Clinic-pathological, perioperative, and oncological data were collected. Short-term oncological outcomes included distal margin, CRM status, and TME quality (Quirke classification). Long-term outcomes were overall survival (OS), local recurrence-free survival and distant metastasis-free survival (LRFS, DMFS). Survival analyses identified prognostic factors. No positive distal margins were observed. CRM negativity was achieved in 94.8% of patients, while complete or near-complete TME was obtained in 96.3%. Reoperation rate was 4.4%, with no 30-day mortality. After a median follow-up of 38 months (mean 44 months), local recurrence occurred in 6% and distant metastases in 21% of patients. CRM positivity and incomplete TME were significantly associated with worse OS and higher metastatic risk. No prognostic benefit has been demonstrated for a CRM ≥5 mm compared to the traditional cutoff. In our case series, robotic total mesorectal excision (TME) ensures high-quality oncological dissection and favorable perioperative and survival outcomes. The predictive value of the CRM and Quirke's mesorectal dissection quality index is confirmed, whereas a favorable prognostic role of a CRM ≥5 mm could not be demonstrated.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Postoperative aspirin has produced inconsistent results in molecularly unselected colorectal cancer, whereas ALASCCA supports a biomarker-selected strategy. We synthesize randomized, molecular, and mechanistic evidence and propose a cautious framework for clinical consideration. This clinically oriented narrative review searched PubMed/MEDLINE, ClinicalTrials.gov, jRCT, PROSPERO, ASCO and ESMO materials, and reference lists, with a final update on September 27, 2026. Randomized trials and prospective biomarker-selected evidence were prioritized. ASCOLT and EPISODE-III/JCOG1503C did not meet their primary disease-free survival endpoints in unselected populations. SAKK 41/13 was underpowered but directionally supportive. In ALASCCA, aspirin 160 mg daily for 3 years reduced 3-year colorectal cancer recurrence in group A PIK3CA exon 9/20 hotspot tumors (7.7% vs. 14.1%; HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.24-0.98). Group B showed a favorable estimate (7.7% vs. 16.8%; HR 0.42, 95% CI 0.21-0.83) but was secondary and molecularly heterogeneous. Low-dose platelet COX-1/thromboxane inhibition is pharmacologically established; direct tumor-cell COX-2/PI3K effects remain less certain. Mature overall-survival data are lacking. Adjuvant aspirin should not be used universally after colorectal cancer resection. The strongest evidence applies to ALASCCA group A, while group B requires variant-level caution. Any use should preserve standard adjuvant therapy and incorporate bleeding risk, local guidance, and shared decision-making.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Programmed cell death (PCD) is a metabolically controlled decision point that shapes antitumor immunity, and its dysregulation is increasingly recognized as a central driver of immune‑checkpoint‑blockade (ICB) resistance in microsatellite‑stable (MSS) colorectal cancer (CRC). Mechanistically, this review focuses on the cell-type-specific molecular switches that determine whether PCD drives immunosuppression or immunogenic cell death. In this review, we propose a unified mechanistic framework centered on a dual PCD imbalance: dysregulated tumor microenvironment (TME) metabolism predominantly activates pyroptosis, ferroptosis, and apoptosis in antitumor immune cells-an immunosuppressive outcome that depends on cell type, stimulus, and tissue context-while tumor-intrinsic epigenetic silencing preferentially abolishes necroptosis, cuproptosis, and PANoptosis in tumor cells, blocking DAMP release and de novo T cell priming. Four stromal and immune subsets drive distinct metabolic cascades: cancer‑associated fibroblasts fuel lactate‑mediated dendritic cell pyroptosis and CD8⁺ T cell ferroptosis; tumor‑associated macrophages amplify lipid‑peroxidation‑driven ferroptosis; myeloid‑derived suppressor cells induce T cell apoptosis via amino acid deprivation; and regulatory T cells exploit kynurenine and adenosine signaling to eliminate antitumor lymphocytes. These cellular insults are reinforced by soluble amplifiers (TGF‑β, IL‑10/IL‑35, adenosine) and VEGF‑driven hypoxia, forming a redundant immunosuppressive network. We hypothesize that this dual PCD imbalance-sustained suppressive PCD of antitumor immune cells combined with silenced immunogenic PCD of tumor cells-locks MSS CRC in an immune‑cold state and explains why single‑agent therapies consistently fail. Accordingly, CMS‑stratified combinatorial regimens that concurrently restrain suppressive PCD and awaken immunogenic tumor cell death may be required to overcome ICB resistance. Emerging approaches spanning spatial multi‑omics, gut microbiota targeting, and myeloid checkpoint inhibition provide opportunities to remodel the cold TME and translate this metabolic‑PCD framework into subtype‑tailored precision immunotherapy for MSS CRC. This dual-PCD-imbalance framework is a testable working hypothesis requiring further combinatorial validation in MSS-CRC-relevant systems.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Tumor-resident bacteria establish a profound immunosuppressive microenvironment that compromises cancer immunotherapy. While ablating these microbes holds therapeutic promise, broad-spectrum antibiotics can cause systemic dysbiosis, and the Gram-negative outer membrane can restrict the entry of conventional sonosensitizers, limiting the antibacterial efficacy of sonodynamic therapy (SDT). Here, we report an ultrasound-driven, bacteria-targeted immunotherapy utilizing polyarginine-functionalized peptide-sonosensitizer conjugates to achieve the in situ pulverization of the tumor Fusobacterium nucleatum (F. nucleatum), thereby eliciting potent innate antitumor immunity. The cationic conjugates electrostatically intercalate into Gram-negative bacterial membranes, inflicting a structural predisruption. Subsequent ultrasound irradiation synergizes localized sonochemical oxidation with mechanical shear forces to thoroughly shatter the bacteria. This targeted microbial fragmentation liberates massive quantities of pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) that, unlike tumor-derived signals from conventional SDT, decisively reprogram macrophages toward an antitumor M1 phenotype to awaken innate immunity. Synchronized with tumor-specific antigens released via conjugate-induced immunogenic cell death, the liberated PAMPs synergistically amplify antigen presentation and optimally drive dendritic cell maturation. In a bacteria-colonized murine colorectal cancer model, this localized therapy markedly suppressed primary tumor growth and elicited both a pronounced abscopal effect against distant tumors and antitumor immune memory. By repurposing complicit bacteria into potent endogenous adjuvants, this ultrasound-driven strategy reverses bacteria-mediated immunosuppression, offering a transformative paradigm for treating microbiome-colonized solid tumors.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Anal cancer is a human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated malignancy that disproportionately affects high-risk populations, including people living with HIV, men who have sex with men, and women with a history of high-grade lower genital tract neoplasia. Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) is the primary cause of anal high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (aHSIL), the precursor to anal cancer. Current screening approaches, including anal cytology and high-resolution anoscopy (HRA), have important limitations related to diagnostic performance, cost, accessibility, and the availability of trained providers. There is a critical need for improved screening strategies and biomarkers capable of identifying individuals at greatest risk of persistent disease and progression. The screening strategies among high-risk populations for anal cancer (ACCESS) study is a prospective, multisite, longitudinal cohort study that will enroll 500 high-risk adults from Emory University and the University of Miami. Participants will undergo annual screening for up to 2 years using anal cytology, hrHPV genotyping, CINtec®PLUS dual staining, HRA, and biopsy when indicated. Anal swabs, biopsies, and optional peripheral blood samples will be collected for molecular and immunologic analyses. DNA methylation markers, inflammatory biomarkers, immune profiling by multicolor flow cytometry, and single-cell RNA sequencing will be evaluated to assess their association with aHSIL prevalence and clearance. Diagnostic performance measures, multivariable regression analyses, and biomarker-based predictive models will be used to evaluate study outcomes. The ACCESS study will evaluate the performance of emerging screening biomarkers and characterize molecular and immune pathways associated with anal carcinogenesis in diverse high-risk populations. By integrating clinical, epigenetic, immunologic, and environmental data, this study aims to improve risk stratification, identify biomarkers associated with persistent disease, and inform the development of more effective and targeted anal cancer prevention strategies. © 2026 The Author(s). ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Health stories in the media often contain relative risks, for example, 'Eating bacon increases your risk of colorectal cancer by 20%'. While the reported changes in risk may be accurate, they do not allow the reader to know the relevant absolute risks (i.e. their chances of developing cancer if they do, or do not, eat bacon). We investigated what people infer the absolute risks to be when they are only given relative risks. Visitors to the British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) news website read a story about the protective effects of mushroom consumption against mild cognitive impairment. Participants either saw the change in risk presented in relative format (50% decrease) or absolute format (from 19 per 100 to 9 per 100). Over 1000 people took part in the study and their data were analysed according to a pre-registered plan. We found that the median estimates of the absolute risks were correct even when participants only saw relative information, indicative of a 'wisdom of the crowd' effect. However, the relative format led people to have much larger errors in their estimates of the true risks when compared to the absolute format. Furthermore, the absolute format did not reduce participants' self-reported comprehension or interest in the story.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Truncating mutations in the adenomatous polyposis coli (APC) gene-a key driver of colorectal cancer (CRC) initiation-frequently lead to the production of a truncated APC protein (Trunc-APC). However, its post-transcriptional roles and oncogenic potential remain largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate that Trunc-APC functions as an RNA-binding protein, directly associating with pre-mRNA via its N-terminal 1-169 amino acid region to regulate widespread alternative splicing (AS) in CRC cells. Specifically, Trunc-APC promotes exon inclusion in ARHGEF11, producing an oncogenic isoform that is associated with enhanced Bcl-xL/BAX complex formation and reduced apoptosis. Mechanistically, Trunc-APC interacts with the RNA helicase DDX21 and facilitates SF3B complex recruitment to pre-mRNA, thereby modulating splicing patterns. Notably, treatment with the splicing inhibitor Madrasin significantly reduced tumor burden in ApcMin/+ CRC mice, indicating strong antitumor efficacy. Collectively, these findings establish Trunc-APC as a novel regulator of alternative splicing and a promoter of CRC progression, and highlight the therapeutic potential of targeting the Trunc-APC/DDX21/SF3B axis in CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Accurate single-CpG methylation analysis in dense regions is critical for cancer diagnostics but challenged by adjacent CpG interference. Here, we developed EPICATCH, an interference-tolerant ratiometric Cas13a biosensor to overcome this limitation. Exploiting LbuCas13a's asymmetric mismatch sensitivity, we established a dual-zone recognition framework. Positioning the target CpG in the strictly sensitive 5'-zone guarantees single-base resolution, while placing adjacent CpGs in the tolerant 3'-zone masks epigenetic noise, achieving a 7-bp spatial resolution for the tested MYO1G construct. Integrated with recombinase polymerase amplification, ssDNA generation, and a dual-channel ratiometric readout, EPICATCH eliminates sample concentration biases, achieving a 100 aM limit of detection. Applying EPICATCH to quantify MYO1G methylation in clinical plasma cfDNA from colorectal cancer patients yielded a clinical sensitivity of 80.0% and specificity of 84.6%. This dual-zone recognition system provides a robust strategy for precise single-CpG analysis and cancer screening.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is among the leading causes of cancer-related deaths globally. While surgical resection remains the primary treatment, the inaccurate identification of tumor margins and the presence of undetectable occult metastases pose significant clinical challenges. Near-infrared (NIR) fluorescence guided surgery (FGS) presents a potential solution to these issues; however, currently available clinical probes suffer from insufficient targeting specificity and limited overall imaging performance. This study introduces a novel NIR fluorescent probe, E-PEG4-S0456, designed to target fibroblast growth factor receptor (FGFR) for precise imaging of CRC. This probe demonstrates excellent photophysical properties and a strong binding affinity to FGFR, allowing for long-term, high-contrast imaging of both primary and metastatic CRC lesions across various animal models, achieving high tumor-to-background ratios and favorable biosafety profiles. Given these advantages, E-PEG4-S0456 has been validated as a promising tool with the potential to advance NIR-FGS technology and enhance the precision of diagnosis and treatment for CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Although the carbohydrate biomarker CA19-9 is widely used for cancer screening, its diagnostic specificity is severely compromised by false-positive elevations in benign inflammatory conditions. Characterizing specific CA19-9 protein carriers provides a promising alternative, yet high-throughput, micro-volume profiling directly from serum remains a challenge. Here, we present a 96-well chemical proteomic platform for the high-throughput profiling of CA19-9-modified proteins. Utilizing a tailored trifunctional chemical probe, photo-activated covalent crosslinking between anti-CA19-9 antibodies and target carriers enables high-stringency enrichment within streptavidin-coated microplates. The workflow identified 509 carriers in cancer cell lines and achieved highly sensitive quantification of established targets, including CD44, LGALS3BP, and mucin family, using as little as 10 μL serum. Notably, this represents the first mass spectrometry-based direct identification of mucin family in peripheral serum. In a clinical cohort of 91 hyper-CA19-9 individuals, CA19-9-modified CD44 was enriched in healthy controls, whereas CA19-9-modified MUC5B was significantly elevated in benign lesions over colorectal cancer (CRC), validated by ELISA across two independent cohorts with AUCs 0.715 and 0.756. Integrating the protein carrier dataset into a random forest machine learning classifier effectively discriminated CRC from benign lesions with an AUC of 0.864. Furthermore, comparative sub-analysis resolved a critical clinical dilemma by identifying 59 upregulated protein carriers in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma relative to benign gallstone-induced cholangitis. Overall, this 96-well chemical proteomic strategy enables parallelized isolation of CA19-9 modified proteins from low-volume samples, establishing a reproducible and scalable tool for the differential profiling of clinically relevant carbohydrate antigen carriers.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Accurate quantification of microRNAs in complex biological fluids remains a challenge due to two intertwined analytical artifacts: false-positive signals from sterically bulky interferents and systematic signal underestimation from nanometal surface energy transfer (NSET) quenching. Here, we report a fluorescence lifetime (FL)-based decoupling strategy that mathematically isolates the NSET quenching bias and retrieves the true catalytic turnover number (TON ≈42.2) from conventionally quenched plasmonic readouts. Integrated with a dense DNA polymer brush that enforces strict size-exclusion selectivity (σ ≈ 0.22 chains/nm2), this approach enables absolute, calibration-free quantification of microRNA-21 directly in untreated human serum. The method achieves a limit of detection of 0.4 pM, excellent correlation with RT-qPCR (R2 = 0.978), and high diagnostic accuracy for colorectal cancer (AUC = 0.945 and threshold 1.55 pM). This FL decoupling protocol provides a standardized calibration method for eliminating optical artifacts in surface-tethered biosensing across different nanoprobe batches.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Human breath volatile organic compounds (VOCs) reflect alterations in cellular metabolism, inflammatory responses and oxidative stress, providing potential molecular readouts for noninvasive disease monitoring. However, conventional breath sampling commonly relies on whole-breath collection, which readily mixes with oral and upper-airway dead-space air, diluting disease-associated VOC signals that originate from alveolar exchange and limiting its application in noninvasive diagnosis. To address this limitation, we developed a CO2-gated intelligent end-tidal breath sampler (iEBS) based on dynamic changes in end-tidal CO2 partial pressure and coupled it with TD-GC-MS/MS to establish an end-tidal breathomics platform for VOC profiling. Using breath profiles from 273 participants, including healthy controls and individuals with gastritis, polyps, gastric cancer and colorectal cancer, we reproducibly identified and quantified 73 VOCs. By integrating topological data analysis, multistage risk modeling, chemical structure enrichment and single-cell transcriptomic mapping, we constructed a visualization framework for gastrointestinal malignancy risk. This framework revealed a gradient of volatile metabolic remodeling from early gastrointestinal abnormalities to malignant states and nominated propanal, butyric acid and 1-butanol as representative VOC markers with potential mechanistic relevance. The multistage risk model achieved stable disease stratification performance (AUC = 0.78-0.94), and a proof-of-concept pre-endoscopic triage simulation estimated that the average waiting time for malignant cases could be reduced by 20%. Overall, this study establishes an iEBS-based breath VOC profiling approach for phase-controlled end-tidal collection, reproducible quantification and interpretable visualization of alveolar-derived breath signals, providing an analytical framework for the noninvasive assessment of gastrointestinal diseases.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
With rising global incidence and improved survival, colorectal cancer (CRC) survivors face an increasing risk of developing multiple primary cancers (MPCs). Despite the growing clinical significance, the epidemiology, molecular basis and optimal clinical management of MPCs remain incompletely understood. This narrative review summarises historical perspectives on the definition of MPCs and synthesises current epidemiological, clinical and molecular evidence on MPCs among CRC survivors, focusing on incidence, risk factors, biological mechanisms, mortality and clinical implications of MPCs in CRC survivors. Available evidence indicate that up to 20% of CRC survivors develop one or more subsequent MPCs, with risk influenced by age at diagnosis of the index CRC, sex, tumour characteristics, comorbidities and variation in tumour coding practices. Survivors diagnosed before the age of 50 years have the highest risk of MPCs. The most commonly reported MPCs include gastrointestinal, prostate, breast, lung, urinary tract, haematological and gynaecological cancers. The presence of MPCs is associated with substantially poorer outcomes and increased mortality, with deaths frequently attributable to lung, gastrointestinal, prostate, urinary tract and haematological cancers. The molecular mechanisms underlying MPC development are poorly understood. Although germline pathogenic variants account for a subset of cases, evidence suggest that somatic mutations, tumour mutational burden and field cancerisation may contribute to the development of multiple malignancies. However, no consistent molecular drivers of MPCs have been identified. Clinical management is further complicated by the absence of evidence-based guidelines, under-representation of cancer survivors in clinical trials, biological heterogeneity of tumours and the complexity of synchronous and metachronous disease presentations. In conclusion, MPCs represent an increasingly important challenge in CRC survivorship and contribute substantially to long-term morbidity and mortality. Future advances will require integration of large-scale clinical and molecular datasets, improved understanding of underlying biological mechanisms and development of risk-stratified surveillance and treatment strategies. Progress in preclinical disease models and targeted therapies may ultimately improve outcomes for the growing survivor population.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Existing tools for predicting delayed bleeding (DB) after colorectal endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) use only structured clinical variables, leaving information in post-ESD mucosal defect images unused. We developed and externally validated an explainable multimodal model integrating these images with clinical features. We retrospectively included 3,416 patients who underwent colorectal ESD at two hospitals from January 2022 through June 2026 (development cohort, n = 2,778; external validation cohort, n = 638). DB was active bleeding 6 h to 28 days after ESD, confirmed by repeat endoscopy and requiring endoscopic hemostasis. YOLOv11m-seg segmented mucosal defects, ResNet50 generated an image-derived prediction score (E-Score), and the E-Score was fused with clinical features. After LASSO feature selection, five algorithms with and without SMOTE were evaluated by fivefold stratified cross-validation. SHAP and Grad-CAM provided post-hoc feature- and image-level explanations. DB occurred in 224 patients (8.06%) in the development cohort and 53 (8.31%) in the external validation cohort (P = 0.839). The segmentation model achieved mAP50 and mAP50-95 values of 0.984 and 0.838. Six features were retained. XGBoost without SMOTE (PrismDB) performed best (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC], 0.804; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.769-0.837), with 64.73% sensitivity, 85.40% specificity, and 96.50% negative predictive value. In external validation, the AUC was 0.788 (95% CI, 0.724-0.850), sensitivity was 79.25%, specificity was 83.25%, and negative predictive value was 97.79%. Probability calibration in the development cohort under the natural event distribution showed a calibration slope of 1.101 and an intercept of + 0.227 (Brier score, 0.0584). E-Score had the highest mean absolute SHAP contribution, and representative activation maps overlapped with exposed vessels, adherent clots, and eschar. PrismDB showed stable discrimination for DB after colorectal ESD. Low-risk classification did not exclude DB. Probability calibration was acceptable in the development cohort but has not been evaluated externally, and the safety of model-guided changes to postoperative care remains to be established; the companion web application demonstrates the prediction workflow.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) is a strong prognostic biomarker in resectable colorectal cancer but remains poorly studied in patients with colorectal peritoneal metastases (CRPM). This study aims to report perioperative ctDNA dynamics in patients undergoing cytoreductive surgery (CRS) for CRPM and evaluate whether pre- and postoperative ctDNA detection was associated with recurrence and survival. Patients who underwent CRS for CRPM at a single center between 2021 and 2025 and had one or more perioperative ctDNA result available were included. Clinicopathological, recurrence, and survival data were retrospectively collected from electronic medical records. ctDNA results were extracted from a prospectively maintained institutional database. In total, 87 patients were included, with a median follow-up of 26.2 months. Pre-neoadjuvant therapy, post-neoadjuvant/pre-CRS, and post-CRS ctDNA was detectable in 65% (22 of 34), 27% (10 of 37), and 36% (30 of 83) of patients, respectively. Post-neoadjuvant/pre-CRS ctDNA positivity was associated with shorter recurrence-free survival (RFS; hazard ratio [HR] 2.59; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.06-6.34, p=0.037) and overall survival (HR 5.73; 95% CI 0.92-35.5, p=0.061). Post-CRS ctDNA positivity was associated with shorter RFS (HR 3.5; 95% CI 2.1-5.9, p<0.001), peritoneal RFS (HR 3.1; 95% CI 1.7-5.5, p<0.001), and overall survival (HR 6.7; 95% CI 2.3-19.7, p=0.001). A smaller proportion of patients with CRPM have detectable ctDNA at presentation compared with other anatomic sites. However, post-CRS ctDNA positivity is strongly associated with recurrence and poorer survival, and dynamic perioperative ctDNA changes may be prognostically informative. ctDNA response to neoadjuvant treatment may demonstrate favorable tumor biology and response to treatment.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Excess cholesterol accumulates in colorectal cancer (CRC) and promotes its progression, yet systemic cholesterol-lowering has limited benefits and safety concerns. Here we show that redirecting intestinal cholesterol metabolism through the gut microbiota generates a metabolite, 4-cholesten-3-one (4-C-3), which suppresses CRC growth. A screen of microbial cholesterol metabolites showed that 4-C-3 is depleted in faecal and tumour samples from patients with CRC. 4-C-3 suppresses tumour growth in CRC cell lines, patient-derived organoids and xenografts. Mechanistically, 4-C-3 suppresses two major oncogenic drivers of CRC by inhibiting epidermal growth-factor receptor activation and stabilizing mutant oncogenic KRAS in an inactive state, thereby overcoming KRAS-driven resistance to anti-epidermal growth-factor receptor therapy. As proof of concept, restoring 4-C-3 using either Oscillibacter ruminantium, a natural 4-C-3 producer reduced in CRC, or a non-pathogenic Escherichia coli engineered to convert intestinal cholesterol into 4-C-3, lowered intratumoral cholesterol and induced tumour regression in preclinical models without overt toxicity. These findings uncover a microbiota-cholesterol metabolic pathway that can be harnessed through microbiome engineering to selectively target CRC and overcome therapy resistance.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Whether p53-driven immune modulation represents a conserved biological programme or a context-dependent adaptation of the tumour microenvironment remains unresolved across human cancers. To address this question, we investigated the relationship between TP53 expression, p53 pathway activity and immune microenvironmental features in breast, colorectal and kidney cancers through integrated transcriptomic, histological and bioinformatic analyses. Our findings revealed striking tumour-specific patterns of p53-associated immune regulation. Breast cancer showed no significant relationship between TP53 expression, p53 pathway activity and immune infiltration or immune checkpoint expression, consistent with an intrinsically immune-cold microenvironment. In contrast, colorectal cancer exhibited a paradoxical immune-restricted phenotype in which p53 pathway activation coexisted with increased cytotoxic lymphocyte infiltration while simultaneously associating with the upregulation of the inhibitory checkpoints TIM-3 and VISTA. Analyses of public colorectal cancer datasets showed frequent TP53 mutations and higher TP53 transcript expression in primary tumours and metastatic lesions than in normal colon tissue. Kidney cancer displayed a distinct stromal-centred pattern, where TP53 expression, but not p53 pathway activity, was associated with fibroblast enrichment and increased expression of immunoregulatory checkpoints. In conclusion, this study reveals distinct associations between p53 signalling and immune microenvironmental features, supporting a context-dependent role of p53 in tumour immune regulation. These data may inform future studies exploring the integration of p53-related biomarkers with immunotherapeutic strategies.

展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Descriptive epidemiology characterizes the distribution of cancer in populations. Its indicators are neither self-explanatory as facts nor sufficient grounds for causal narratives. Cancer registries, vital statistics, and follow-up systems make incidence, mortality, survival, and prevalence observable, but these measures depend on how cases, deaths, and populations are defined and recorded. We propose an interpretive coordinate system that locates cancer patterns by person, place, time, complementary indicators, and the processes generating these indicators. This framework characterizes burden, identifies unusual patterns and inequalities, and generates and constrains hypotheses. It examines whether population patterns are compatible with changes in diagnosis, screening, treatment, or policy. It does not by itself establish causation, reveal mechanisms, or estimate intervention effects. Here, we clarify what the principal indicators describe, how they are constructed, and how common overinterpretations can be avoided. We present principles and examples from gastric, thyroid, colorectal, and lung cancer to distinguish observed patterns from competing interpretations, identify additional information needed, and clarify which conclusions remain unjustified. Particular attention is given to denominators, age structure, age-period-cohort interpretation, bias, and the assumptions required for comparison and modeling. The aim is to enable cancer researchers to use descriptive epidemiology as a disciplined framework for interpreting population patterns rather than as background statistics or a substitute for causal inference.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To develop and validate an artificial intelligence-enabled platform that combines efficient screening with explicit eligibility logic by converting unstructured cancer trial criteria into reusable structured queries, and illustrates potential eligibility using synthetic patients. We downloaded actively recruiting US interventional treatment trials for advanced/metastatic breast cancer, colon cancer, and non-small cell lung cancer from ClinicalTrials.gov. Medical oncologists created 24 synthetic patient vignettes. A large language model converted trial eligibility criteria into Structured Query Language (SQL) code and patient information into structured records, enabling rule-based matching without further LLM inference. Cancer details and treatment history were considered, but not laboratory results or comorbidities. Validation included physician editing of generated eligibility code for 30 trials and independent assessments by two physicians, followed by consensus adjudication, for eligibility across ten trials. We descriptively summarized potential eligibility by trial characteristics and when varying age, ECOG performance status, sex, and ZIP code. Of 833 candidate trials, 746 met inclusion criteria. Performing matching for all 746 trials took a median of 0.459 seconds per patient, excluding patient-data preparation. Against physician consensus, automated matching agreed on 230/240 patient-trial pairs (95.8%; sensitivity 83.3%, specificity 100%). Across synthetic patients, potentially eligible trials ranged from 10 to 258 without geographic restrictions. Counts decreased with worse performance status and geographic restriction and were relatively stable across ages 30-90. Later-phase, randomized, and molecularly selective trials generally matched fewer vignettes. LLM-generated SQL enables rapid, explicit rule-based screening for potential trial eligibility. Evaluation in synthetic vignettes supports feasibility, while missed matches underscore the need for further validation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Peritoneal metastasis is a common manifestation of advanced gastric cancer (GC) and colorectal cancer (CRC). Radiologic detection is often inconclusive, particularly with minimal ascites or subtle peritoneal thickening. Although ascitic fluid cytology is the diagnostic gold standard, it has low sensitivity, high observer variability, and depends on manual review. Artificial intelligence (AI) shows a promise for improving diagnosis, but patch-based models require segmentation and reconstruction, increasing computational load and reducing efficiency particularly with few malignant cells. We developed a whole slide image (WSI)-level diagnostic model for detecting metastatic GC and CRC in ascitic cytology using the Clustering-constrained Attention Multiple Instance Learning. This architecture identifies key regions without patch-wise annotation or reconstruction. We trained and validated it on the Open AI Dataset Project, a national cytology dataset comprising 243 malignant and 476 negative WSIs, divided into training, validation, and test sets. The model achieved accuracies of 1.00 (validation) and 0.933 (test), with area under the receiver operating characteristic curves of 1.00 and 0.925. WSI-level MIL approaches may conceptually reduce computational burden by avoiding explicit patch-level classification. Compared to five experienced pathologists, the model achieved superior or comparable accuracy, and AI assistance improved pathologists' average diagnostic accuracy from 76.5% to 91.5%, while reducing interpretation time by over 40%. No false negatives occurred, and attention maps confirmed the malignant areas. Our WSI-level AI model offers a robust, efficient solution for diagnosing metastatic GC and CRC in ascitic cytology. It addresses limitations of manual and patch-based methods, supports clinical decision-making, and enhances diagnostic accuracy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Molecular targets are common in metastatic colorectal cancer, yet Brazil's Unified Health System (SUS) does not fund any biomarker-matched therapy. Where each pathway is interrupted-evidence, regulatory indication, incorporation, testing, or price-and what would overcome each barrier remain unclear. We quantified actionable biomarker prevalence in TCGA-COADREAD (n = 459), mapped each biomarker-therapy pathway across the Brazilian access chain using primary regulatory sources (2025 national protocol, CONITEC, ANVISA, SIGTAP), and developed partitioned-survival cost-utility models (SUS perspective, lifetime horizon, 5% annual discounting), conditional on biomarker-positive patients, evaluating first-line pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-177), first-line cetuximab in left-sided RAS wild-type disease (CRYSTAL), and first-line encorafenib plus cetuximab plus mFOLFOX6 (BREAKWATER, interim survival), with second-line BEACON examined as a scenario. Drugs were costed at regulated government-purchase ceiling prices; results were assessed against Brazil's 2022 reference threshold of R$40,000/QALY, with the threefold value (R$120,000/QALY) as a scenario for specific circumstances. In the mixed-stage TCGA-COADREAD cohort - characterizing theoretical molecular opportunity - RAS wild-type status was observed in 51.4%, MSI-high in 16.6%, and BRAF V600E in 9.8%, yet every matched pathway was interrupted at or before national incorporation. Incremental cost-effectiveness ratios were R$314,000/QALY for pembrolizumab, R$761,000/QALY for cetuximab (exploratory), and R$836,000/QALY for first-line BRAF-targeted therapy. No non-negative encorafenib price alone brought the BRAF regimen below either threshold; achieving cost-effectiveness would require joint reductions of 75-84% in encorafenib and cetuximab prices. Precision oncology in SUS is constrained not by target scarcity, but by pathway-specific barriers to incorporation and affordability. Different pathways require different policy responses: negotiated pricing for pembrolizumab, substantial class-level price reductions for anti-EGFR antibodies, and regimen-level negotiation covering both targeted agents in the BRAF combination. Identifying each pathway's barrier turns a generic affordability problem into a concrete target for health technology assessment and pricing decisions in middle-income health systems.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The study evaluated the risk of grade ≥2 acute diarrhea of modern bowel-sparing intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT)-based neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT) for locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) versus three-dimensional conformal radiotherapy (3DCRT)-based nCRT. In this open-label, historically controlled, multicenter, single-arm phase II trial, patients with LARC, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status 0-2, and adequate organ function were recruited. Protocol treatment involved concurrent capecitabine and IMRT, consisting of 45 Gy (25 fractions) for elective nodes and an optional 5.4 Gy (3 fractions) boost for gross disease. Bowel-sparing constraints included small-bowel volume receiving 15 Gy (V15Gy) of <200 cc. Acute toxicities were graded in the protocol-defined primary outcome window. Grade ≥2 acute diarrhea was tested against a 26% historical benchmark from phase II trials of 3DCRT-based nCRT with capecitabine with a one-sided α-level of 0.05 and 80% power. Fifty-five patients were enrolled, including 48 patients with stage III disease and 25 patients with a positive circumferential resection margin on magnetic resonance imaging. Fifty-four patients (98.2%) completed protocol-defined nCRT. The median small-bowel V15Gy was 85 cc (interquartile range, 47-105). Grade ≥2 acute diarrhea occurred in four patients (7.3%; 90% confidence interval, 2.5-15.9; p < 0.001) in the intention-to-treat cohort. Fifty patients underwent radical surgery, and the pathological complete response and circumferential resection margin >1 mm rates were 6.0% and 88.0%, respectively, with grade ≥2 postoperative complications observed in 14% of patients. After median follow-up of 14 months, the 12-month locoregional progression-free and overall survival rates were 95.0% and 98.2%, respectively. Modern bowel-sparing IMRT in nCRT for LARC was associated with a low rate of grade ≥2 acute diarrhea with no obvious unfavorable signals for resectability, locoregional control, or safety; however, longer follow-up is needed to assess mature oncologic outcomes and late toxicities.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) has become a preferred approach for locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC), offering higher rates of complete response, the potential for organ preservation, and reduced distant metastasis. However, the trials establishing these benefits largely excluded older adults and patients with functional impairment, leaving limited guidance on who is fit enough to receive TNT. Improper selection of older patients for TNT poses dueling risks: exclusion of candidates based on chronological age allows for potential undertreatment while delivery of a prolonged, multimodal regimen to patients without adequate physiologic reserve raises concern for overtreatment. This review describes how TNT stresses older adults across systemic, social, functional, physical, and cognitive domains and how these domains should inform frailty assessment. We discuss available assessment approaches, including deficit accumulation indices (DAIs), point-of-care performance measures, chemotherapy toxicity prediction tools, and comprehensive geriatric assessment, and conclude that no single instrument is sufficient. Instead, frailty assessment in TNT candidates should be holistic and multi-domain, longitudinal, and involve several disciplines. We propose that frailty be treated as a modifiable baseline rather than an exclusion criterion, with potential for using the neoadjuvant interval for domain-targeted prehabilitation and as a dynamic stress test of physiologic reserve. Finally, we describe how frailty assessment can anchor shared decision-making, aligning treatment with the priorities of older adults, who frequently value quality of life, independence, and cognition over longevity. Individualized, frailty-informed decision-making can help ensure that the benefits of TNT reach appropriately selected older patients.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
We assessed the impact of menopausal hormone therapies (MHTs) on the risk of colorectal cancer (CRC) in Finnish women. In addition, we analysed various MHT characteristics in relation to risk and anatomic site of CRC. Users of MHT and age-matched non-users (both groups n = 364,304) in 1994-2019 were identified from the Finnish Medicine Reimbursement Register and the National Population Register. Cohorts were followed for the occurrence of primary CRC from the Finnish Cancer Registry. CRC risks were calculated as hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) with a Cox proportional hazards model. Over a mean 18-year follow-up (13 million person-years), 4602 MHT users (1.3%) and 5103 non-users (1.4%) were diagnosed with CRC (p < 0.001). Ever use of MHT for 5 years or more was associated with a decreased CRC risk (HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.85-0.92). Estrogen-only therapy (ET) (0.81, 0.76-0.87) showed a larger risk reduction than combined estrogen-progestogen therapy (EPT) (0.92, 0.88-0.96). Tibolone was accompanied by the greatest risk decrease (0.54, 0.41-0.73), but the number of users was modest. Dydrogesterone EPT tended to confer 31-36% lower CRC risk than EPTs containing norethisterone or medroxyprogesterone acetate. Risk reductions were of similar magnitude for right- and left-sided colon cancer, but rectal cancer risk was decreased only with 10 or more years of MHT use. The risk falls persisted for over 5 years after the cessation of MHT use. Use of ET or EPT for 5 years or more is associated with reduced CRC risk, likely mediated by estrogen, while some progestogens - but not dydrogesterone - may attenuate this effect.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To examine the differences in colorectal cancer (CRC) incidence between the US and Canada, among individuals aged 45 to 49 years, following expansion of screening eligibility in the US. This is an ecological analysis based on publicly available data for CRC incidence in the US and Canada. US data were based on the US Cancer Statistics Public Use Research Database, while the Canadian data were based on Statistics Canada tables (which represented all Canadian jurisdictions except for Nova Scotia). Descriptive analyses for cancer incidence rates per 100,000 among individuals aged 45 to 49 years were performed for Canada versus the US, with stratification performed for age group, sex, and subsite. Subsequently, a difference-in-differences (DiD) analysis was performed to further examine the differences between the US and Canada. Colorectal cancer rates per 100,000 (2016 to 2023) for individuals aged 45 to 49 years increased in Canada from 30.6 (2016) to 34 (2023), while in the US, rates increased from 34.9 (2016) to 53.1 (2023). For the US data, when calculating the percentage of localized disease out of all patients with known stages, this increased from 28.5% in 2016 to 40.8% in 2023. Furthermore, comparing US versus Canadian data and using pre- versus postexpansion policy means in both countries, DiD was 12.85 (95% CI: 10.13-15.57, P<0.001). Expansion of CRC screening eligibility in the US was associated with a significant increase in reported CRC incidence in the US versus Canada, among individuals 45 to 49 years old, which was principally driven by increasing rates of localized-stage diagnoses.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Kirsten rat sarcoma (KRAS), the most frequently altered oncogene, is a key target for T cell-based therapies. Mutant KRAS (mKRAS)-specific T cell receptors (TCRs) enable targeted treatment for patients with matching mKRAS/HLA allele pairs. We generated a TCR warehouse library covering approximately one-quarter of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma patients and 10% of colorectal cancer patients. Warehouse TCRs exhibit strong avidities and cytotoxicity, comparable to existing benchmark TCRs. Detailed characterization of each TCR revealed unique biology for specific KRAS neoantigens. TCRs with high sensitivity for KRAS G12V/HLA-C*01:02 also recognize the wild-type epitope. However, the wild-type epitope abundance appears to be significantly lower, potentially creating a therapeutic window, albeit necessitating deeper evaluation. Additionally, we show that TCRs recognize KRAS G12V on HLA-C*03:03 and HLA-C*03:04 interchangeably, thereby resulting in a single neoantigen with one of the highest frequencies. In summary, this mKRAS-targeted TCR library comprises candidates for further preclinical and clinical development.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To provide a comprehensive overview of lipid-based nanocarriers for oxaliplatin (OXA) delivery in colorectal cancer (CRC), with emphasis on their potential to improve pharmacokinetics, enhance tumour accumulation, enable controlled drug release, and overcome OXA resistance. Relevant literature on OXA, CRC, lipid-based nanocarriers, drug resistance, tumor targeting, co-delivery, and stimuli-responsive delivery systems was reviewed. The review focused on liposomes, solid lipid nanoparticles (SLNs), nanostructured lipid carriers (NLCs), lipid micelles, and advanced lipid-based systems, including passive and active targeting strategies and approaches for overcoming therapeutic resistance. Lipid-based nanocarriers demonstrated potential to improve OXA delivery through enhanced tumour accumulation, controlled release, prolonged drug exposure, and improved intracellular uptake. Active targeting using folate, CD44, peptides, or antibodies, along with co-delivery, tumor microenvironment modulation, and externally triggered release, may further enhance therapeutic efficacy and help overcome multidrug resistance. However, most evidence remains preclinical, and challenges including formulation stability, tumor heterogeneity, large-scale manufacturing, and regulatory requirements limit clinical translation. Lipid-based nanocarriers represent a promising strategy for improving OXA therapy in CRC, particularly for addressing toxicity, drug resistance, and inefficient tumor delivery. Nevertheless, the limited clinical evidence for OXA-loaded lipid nanocarriers necessitates further pharmacokinetic, toxicological, manufacturing, and well-designed clinical studies before their clinical effectiveness can be established.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Mutations in the adenomatous polyposis coli (APC) gene are a defining feature of colorectal cancer (CRC) and impose metabolic and stress adaptation requirements that may create exploitable vulnerabilities. Prolyl hydroxylase domain (PHD) inhibitors have been explored as therapeutic agents in CRC; however, their mechanisms of action and off-target effects remain elusive. Serendipitously, we found that Molidustat, a PHD2 inhibitor, induced cell death in human APC-mutant CRC cells. Ablation of PHD2 alone did not affect cell viability, suggesting an off-target mechanism. Using thermal proteome profiling and chemical proteomics, we identify glutathione S-transferase P1 (GSTP1) as a previously unrecognised off-target of Molidustat and demonstrate direct inhibition of its enzymatic activity. Genetic ablation of PHD2 alone did not phenocopy the cytotoxic effects of Molidustat, whereas combined loss of PHD2 and GSTP1 induced synergistic proteomic changes associated with cell-cycle suppression and apoptotic signalling. Integrated proteomic and metabolomic analyses further revealed energetic and metabolic perturbations specific to simultaneous GSTP1 and PHD2 loss. Consistent with these findings, APC-mutant mouse organoids displayed selective sensitivity to Molidustat that was not reproduced by hydroxylase inhibition alone, supporting a synthetic lethal interaction between GSTP1 and PHD2 in APC-mutant contexts. Together, these results identify a functional interaction between GSTP1 and PHD2 in a subset of CRC and suggest that off-target engagement of GSTP1 contributes to the anti-tumour activity of Molidustat.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Surveillance colonoscopy following adenoma detection is essential for colorectal cancer prevention, yet systematic tracking within electronic health record (EHR) systems remains challenging, as they rely on manual data entry. To determine if implementation of an automatic tool in the EHR is associated with improved health care maintenance table updates for patients needing repeat colonoscopy for cancer screening after adenoma detection. This cohort study at a single tertiary care center within a large health care organization with EHR functionality included patients undergoing colonoscopy between November 2017 and December 2024. Eligible participants were adults aged 50 to 75 years undergoing colonoscopy for screening, surveillance, or diagnostic indications. Exclusion criteria included patients with inflammatory bowel disease, known colorectal cancer, or hereditary cancer syndromes. Data were analyzed between January and May 2025. A decision support tool was implemented that allowed gastroenterologists completing colonoscopies for patients with adenoma to choose follow-up intervals that would automatically populate the health maintenance tab. Rate of updates of the health maintenance table and percentage completion from gastroenterology vs primary care. A total of 35 802 patients met criteria (20 049 female [56.0%]; median [range] age: preintervention, 61 years [50-75 years]; postintervention, 62 years [50-75 years]); adenomas were detected in 8004 of 18 027 patients (44.4%) in the preintervention period and 8396 of 17 775 patients (47.2%) in the postintervention period. Health maintenance updates for patients with adenomas requiring closer surveillance increased significantly, from 83.4% (6672 of 8004 patients) to 94.2% (7913 of 8396 patients) following the intervention (P < .001). Gastroenterology team completion of health maintenance updates increased postintervention from 67.6% (5413 of 8004 patients) to 91.9% (7717 of 8396 patients). Conversely, primary care team updates decreased significantly from 9.3% (746 of 8004 patients) to 1.4% (118 of 8396 patients) following the intervention (P < .001 for both). Population health automatic updates occurred in a small number of patients in both periods. Implementation of automatic updates to the health maintenance section of the EHR was associated with significantly increased the reliability of postadenoma surveillance documentation; after the intervention, gastroenterology reporting increased while the primary care burden was reduced. These findings suggest that clinical decision support implementation is critical for accurate adenoma surveillance intervals.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The optimal clinical implementation of comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) in metastatic colorectal cancer has not been fully established, and its clinical utility may differ according to genomic subtype. We aimed to evaluate genomic findings obtained from CGP according to baseline RAS and BRAF mutational status in patients with metastatic colorectal cancer. We retrospectively analyzed genomic data in patients with metastatic colorectal cancer who underwent plasma- or tissue-based CGP testing between 2018 and 2023 at St. Marianna University Hospital. Patients were classified into RAS/BRAF wild-type (WT), RAS-mutant (MT), or BRAF V600E-MT subgroups according to standard tissue assessment at baseline. Druggable/effective profiles detected by subsequent CGP were defined as newly identified actionable gene alterations (OncoKB level 1-2) or discordant RAS status. The druggable/effective profile rate was compared across subgroups. Among patients who underwent real-time plasma-based CGP testing, the druggable/effective profile rate was significantly higher in the RAS/BRAF-WT subgroup (27.6%) than in the RAS-MT (9.8%) and BRAF-MT (0%) subgroups (p = 0.04 and p = 0.03, respectively). In the RAS/BRAF-WT subgroup, druggable/effective profiles were mainly driven by discordant RAS alterations detected after anti-epidermal growth factor receptor antibody therapy. In contrast, among patients who underwent tissue-based CGP using archived samples, the druggable/effective profile rate did not differ significantly across RAS/BRAF subgroups. Plasma-based CGP identified clinically relevant genomic findings most frequently in patients with RAS/BRAF-WT metastatic colorectal cancer, including RAS alterations detected after anti- epidermal growth factor receptor therapy. These findings suggest that baseline RAS/BRAF status and prior treatment history may help guide the selection and timing of CGP testing.
