ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is shaped by complex genomic and tumor microenvironmental interactions. Charged multivesicular body protein 4 C (CHMP4C), a core ESCRT-III component involved in cytokinetic abscission and vesicular trafficking, has been implicated in chromosomal stability and cancer biology, but its relevance to CRC remains incompletely understood. We integrated cBioPortal genomic analyses, TCGA-COAD transcriptomic data, pathway and enrichment analyses, immune/stromal deconvolution, public proteomic datasets, and experimental validation in CRC specimens. CHMP4C alterations, predominantly amplifications and copy-number gains, were significantly enriched in chromosomal-instability categories, particularly CIN-HR and CIN-LR, and were comparatively uncommon in hypermutated tumors. Although altered tumors showed a directional representation within MSS and pMMR categories, neither MMR nor MSI status was significantly associated with CHMP4C alterations after multiple-testing correction. Higher CHMP4C expression was associated with reduced immune and stromal representation and an immune-excluded transcriptional phenotype. Pathway analyses placed CHMP4C within modules related to ESCRT-dependent cytokinetic regulation, endosomal remodeling, vesicular trafficking, and regulated cell-death processes. Proteomic findings were not uniformly concordant across independent datasets, whereas experimental analysis confirmed elevated CHMP4C expression in CRC tissue. CHMP4C alteration status was not consistently associated with conventional survival outcomes. CHMP4C alterations are associated with an amplification-enriched, CIN-associated genomic context, while elevated CHMP4C expression is associated with reduced immune and stromal representation. These findings support CHMP4C as a candidate marker of CIN-associated CRC biology and a hypothesis-generating link between genomic instability and immune exclusion. Functional and spatial studies and larger molecularly stratified cohorts are required to establish its mechanistic and clinical significance.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Among the 5 leading causes of cancer death in people younger than 50 years in the US, colorectal cancer (CRC) is the only one with increasing mortality. Using Global Burden of Disease 2023 estimates, we examined young-onset CRC mortality among persons aged 15-49 years from 1990 through 2023. Age-standardized mortality rates (ASMRs) and Joinpoint trends were calculated, with change summarized by the 2014-2023 mean annual percentage change (APC). In 2023, the ASMR was 3.25 per 100,000 and varied more than twofold across states; the mean APC was 1.06%. Ten of 13 states in the highest ASMR quartile were in the South, whereas the fastest increases were in the West. Five hotspot states had both highest-quartile ASMR and mean APC: Alaska, Kentucky, Missouri, New Mexico, and Tennessee. Overall, 65.5% of deaths were jointly attributable to assessed GBD risks; behavioral and metabolic PAFs were 56.1% and 21.6%, respectively.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Traditional 2D cell lines and mouse xenograft models have limitations in recapitulating the complexity of the tumor microenvironment (TME) and dynamic interactions between tumor and immune cells, creating an urgent need for models to evaluate immunotherapies. Patient-derived organoids (PDOs), which retain key features of original tumors, offer a platform for dissecting the TME when co-cultured with peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). However, challenges such as inter-batch variability of PBMCs and difficulties in autologous PBMC acquisition hinder their clinical translation. This study established four stably passaged colorectal cancer organoid models and developed an allogeneic PBMC-organoid co-culture platform to investigate the immune activation and cytotoxic potential of allogeneic PBMCs. Results showed that vacuolated-structured organoids are associated with the increased proportion of CD8+ T cells in PBMCs within the co-culture system. PBMCs exhibited stronger cytotoxicity against microsatellite-stable (MSS) organoids with low PD-L1 expression, while the anti-PD-1 antibody Keytruda significantly enhanced their antitumor effects on high PD-L1-expressing organoids. The allogeneic co-culture model developed here overcomes the limitations of autologous PBMC acquisition, providing an efficient and versatile proof-of-concept platform for pre-clinical screening of immunotherapeutic drugs. Distinct from prior allogeneic co-culture systems that rely on healthy donor immune cells, our platform uniquely integrates patient-derived allogeneic PBMCs with tumor organoids, providing preliminary proof-of-concept evidence that tumor-intrinsic features may influence immunotherapy responses based on tumor-intrinsic features while preserving the pathological relevance of cancer patient immune profiles.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Previous studies have indicated that diabetes mellitus may increase the risk of colorectal cancer (CRC), yet the precise associationremains unclear. To identify critical clinical predictors of CRC risk in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) using machinelearning (ML) and to subsequently evaluate their causal relationship with CRC via Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis. A retrospective cohort design was adopted, analyzing clinical records from patients with T2DM and CRC and from those with T2DM alone. Significant predictors were determined using univariate and multivariate Cox regression analyses. Four MLmodels were developed, with essential indicators defined by the overlap of top-ranked clinical variables and risk factors. Mendelian randomizationanalysis was then applied to assess causality between the key indicators (exposures) and CRC (outcome), supplemented bysensitivity tests and Steiger analysis. Reverse MR analysis was conducted to examine potential reverse causality between CRC (exposure)and the identified indicators (outcomes). Univariate and multivariate Cox regression revealed that age [p < 0.05, hazard ratio (HR) = 1.041, 95% confidence interval(CI) = 1.022-1.062] and hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c, p < 0.05, HR = 1.176, 95% CI = 1.094-1.264) were significant risk factors. Logistic regressionwas ultimately identified as the most suitable model, from which two key indicators (age and HbA1c) were derived. Mendelianrandomization analysis demonstrated a causal effect of HbA1c on CRC, confirming HbA1c as a risk factor [odds ratio (OR) = 1.14, 95%CI = 1.01-1.28, p = 0.0336]. Sensitivity analyses and Steiger testing supported the robustness and directionality of these findings. Notably,reverse MR analysis indicated no significant causal effect of CRC on HbA1c [p inverse variance weighted = 0.07853). Age and HbA1c were identified as pivotal indicators, with HbA1c exhibiting a unidirectional causal association with CRC, thereby offering insights for potential therapeutic strategies.

意义与启示：报道机器人同期切除食管胃结合部癌与肝转移的可行性，为肠癌肝转移合并其他原发癌的微创同期手术提供技术参考。

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
We report a rare case of a simultaneous robot-assisted resection for esophagogastric junction (EGJ) cancer and liver metastasis following colon cancer surgery. The patient was a 66-year-old male. He underwent laparoscopically assisted right hemicolectomy at a previous hospital for intestinal obstruction due to ascending colon cancer. A postoperative PET/CT scan revealed abnormal uptake at the EGJ in addition to the known liver metastasis. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy revealed a type 2 tumors at the EGJ. This cancer was diagnosed as cT2N0M0, cStage I. Three months after colectomy, a robot-assisted proximal gastrectomy (PG) and wedge hepatectomy were performed. Port placement was planned based on considerations for reconstruction after gastric resection. Hepatectomy was performed first. Subsequently, PG and lymph node dissection were performed. An esophagogastric anastomosis was performed using the double-flap technique. The patient was discharged on the eighth postoperative day without complications and has remained recurrence-free. Robot-assisted simultaneous resection of liver metastases and EGJ cancer was safely performed through careful preoperative planning, including port placement and surgical techniques.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Simultaneous robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) and rectal resection for rectal cancer with prostatic invasion may avoid total pelvic exenteration while preserving the bladder. This report highlights two stabilization strategies. Case 1 involved a 77-year-old man with cT4bN0M0 rectal cancer who received six cycles of folinic acid, fluorouracil, and oxaliplatin before undergoing abdominoperineal resection and RARP. Following posterior reconstruction and vesicourethral anastomosis, the perivesical tissue was fixed to the divided endopelvic fascia using continuous sutures. Urinary leakage, confirmed by computed tomography, was managed by maintaining the urethral catheter under continuous suction and retaining the existing pelvic drain. Penile metastasis was diagnosed 1 month postoperatively; the urinary catheter was retained, and the patient died 1 year later. Pathological staging was ypT4bN3, R1. Case 2 involved a 72-year-old man with a pre-existing cystostomy following Fournier's gangrene. Upfront surgery was performed; the original cystostomy tract was reused, and the perivesical tissue was fixed circumferentially to the parietal peritoneum. Drainage remained stable without cystostomy leakage, and the patient was recurrence-free at 1 year. Pathological staging was pT4bN2b, R1. The techniques were intended to support the bladder or re-anchor a pre-existing cystostomy. Neither patient resumed urethral voiding, and no objective voiding measurements were obtained. Simultaneous RARP and rectal resection are feasible in selected patients. However, these two heterogeneous, resection margin-positive cases, without objective voiding assessment, cannot confirm oncological or functional benefits. Such approaches require multidisciplinary evaluation, the absence of bladder invasion, and the expectation of margin-negative resection.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Primary colonic lymphoma (PCL) is a rare extranodal manifestation of non-Hodgkin lymphoma, accounting for a small fraction of colorectal malignancies. Due to its low incidence and nonspecific clinical and radiological features, PCL is frequently misdiagnosed as colonic adenocarcinoma. Optimal management remains poorly defined, and current treatment strategies rely on retrospective data and expert consensus. We report the case of a 69-year-old woman who presented with right lower quadrant abdominal pain and was found to have a near-obstructing ascending colon mass with extensive regional and retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy on computed tomography. Colonoscopic biopsies were nondiagnostic despite a malignant-appearing lesion. Given impending obstruction, the patient underwent an open right hemicolectomy with primary anastomosis. Histopathologic and immunohistochemical analysis of the surgical specimen revealed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). Postoperative staging with positron emission tomography demonstrated fluorodeoxyglucose-avid nodal disease. The patient was treated with adjuvant immunochemotherapy and radiotherapy, achieving a complete metabolic response on follow-up imaging. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges of PCL and emphasizes the importance of surgical resection in symptomatic patients for both definitive diagnosis and management. DLBCL is the most common PCL subtype and responds favorably to multimodal therapy, including rituximab, cyclophosphamide, hydroxydaunorubicin, oncovin, prednisone-based chemotherapy. Positron-emission tomography-computed tomography plays a critical role in staging and assessment of treatment response. PCL should be considered in the differential diagnosis of colonic masses, particularly when biopsy results are inconclusive. A multidisciplinary, multimodal treatment approach can lead to favorable outcomes. Further prospective studies are needed to establish standardized management guidelines.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cutaneous metastases from colorectal cancer (CRC) are rare and often indicate advanced disease. This case report highlights an uncommon pattern of recurrence from right-sided colon cancer and reviews the pertinent literature. A 57-year-old woman with a history of emergency right colectomy for perforated colonic adenocarcinoma developed a cutaneous nodule, rapidly increasing in size and measuring 3 × 4 cm, at the site of a previous drain 6 months after surgery. Biopsy confirmed metastatic adenocarcinoma. Apart from the cutaneous metastasis, imaging showed a deep retroperitoneal mass that did not communicate with the cutaneous nodule and no other visceral metastases. Systemic chemotherapy was reinitiated with bevacizumab. Due to refractory bleeding and transfusion-dependent anemia, surgical excision of the cutaneous lesion was performed, improving the patient's quality of life. Cutaneous metastases from CRC are unusual and generally associated with poor prognosis. Their management remains palliative in most cases. Drain-site metastasis is particularly rare and may reflect tumor cell seeding. Vigilance for nodular skin lesions in post-operative CRC patients is crucial. Prompt biopsy and imaging facilitate early diagnosis and appropriate management.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer most often presents with gastrointestinal problems such as obstruction and abdominal pain, or is detected early by screening colonoscopy. Retroperitoneal metastasis that mimics the findings of retroperitoneal fibrosis is rare and can cause diagnostic challenges, especially in patients in whom contrast-enhanced imaging is contraindicated. A 49-year-old woman was admitted with severe bilateral flank pain, oliguria, intermittent nausea, and loss of appetite without abdominal distention or constipation. Due to a known allergy to contrast media, a non-contrast CT scan was performed and showed bilateral hydronephrosis and evidence of retroperitoneal fibrosis. Although double-J ureteral stents were inserted, the patient's renal function progressively deteriorated, requiring hemodialysis. After that, the patient experienced intractable vomiting, and the evaluation confirmed gastric outlet obstruction (GOO) caused by mass effect from a retroperitoneal mass. Magnetic resonance imaging findings continued to favor retroperitoneal fibrosis despite the presence of some suspicious pulmonary nodules. Surgical intervention with retroperitoneal biopsy was performed, during which an incidental sigmoid mass was detected and resected. Histopathology revealed well-differentiated sigmoid adenocarcinoma with retroperitoneal metastasis. Malignancy-associated retroperitoneal fibrosis faces critical diagnostic challenges due to its radiologic findings that can mimic a benign fibroinflammatory process. Unlike previous reports that focus on retroperitoneal fibrosis in patients with known primary malignancies, this case presented without a history or symptoms of colorectal cancer. Additionally, the inability to perform a contrast-enhanced CT scan contributed to a delayed diagnosis. Failure of ureteral stenting and GOO symptoms were two main indicators of infiltrative malignant disease. Timely tissue diagnosis remains essential for atypical manifestations of retroperitoneal fibrosis. Occult sigmoid adenocarcinoma may rarely present with multi-level obstructive complications, even without typical large-bowel obstruction

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Laparoscopic ultra-low anterior resection (uLAR) remains technically challenging due to limited visualization and difficulty identifying dissection planes in the distal pelvis. Image-guided navigation has emerged as a potential tool to enhance intraoperative precision. A 52-year-old man with low rectal adenocarcinoma located 3 cm from the anal verge underwent laparoscopic uLAR with total mesorectal excision assisted by real-time computed tomography-magnetic resonance imaging (CT-MRI)-based intraoperative navigation. The patient had no significant comorbidities and had received neoadjuvant therapy. The navigation system enabled accurate tumor localization and facilitated dissection within the correct mesorectal plane in a technically demanding pelvic environment. The procedure was completed without intraoperative complications. Navigation-assisted surgery provided enhanced anatomical orientation and continuous spatial feedback during deep pelvic dissection, particularly in the presence of tissue edema and distorted anatomy. This approach may reduce the risk of positive margins and improve preservation of critical pelvic structures. Real-time CT-MRI-based intraoperative navigation is a feasible and safe adjunct in complex rectal surgery. This approach may be particularly valuable in anatomically challenging pelves or post-neoadjuvant settings.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic inflammatory disease associated with an increased colorectal cancer risk 8-10 years after diagnosis. Total proctocolectomy is usually elective and indicated for high-grade dysplasia or adenocarcinoma detected during surveillance colonoscopy. This report describes an unusual urgent case involving total mesorectal excision in a UC patient with intestinal obstruction due to a rectal lesion suspected of malignancy. A 38-year-old woman with UC presented with acute intestinal obstruction due to a rectal stenosis suggestive of neoplasia. She underwent total proctocolectomy with total mesorectal excision and terminal ileostomy. Histopathology revealed moderately differentiated rectal adenocarcinoma. The patient recovered well and initiated adjuvant chemotherapy, which was changed owing to radiological evidence of peritoneal implants detected 1 year after surgery. She has no further evidence of peritoneal involvement, as seen on a PET/CT scan performed 2.5 years after surgery. Patients with UC of more than 7 years' duration have up to a tenfold higher risk of malignancy, underscoring the need for annual colonoscopy from the eighth year onward, particularly in pancolitis. Total proctocolectomy is indicated when dysplasia or carcinoma is detected. Performing oncologic surgery with total mesorectal excision and high vascular ligation in an emergency setting is uncommon. This case illustrates a rare malignant rectal transformation in long-standing UC, presenting with acute intestinal obstruction. Oncologic total proctocolectomy was feasible as an urgent procedure, given the patient's condition and the colorectal surgery team's availability in the emergency unit. The case emphasizes the importance of continuous surveillance and individualized surgical decision-making in emergency settings.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Rectal cancer invading gynecologic organs, with a rectovaginal fistula and post-chemoradiotherapy fibrosis, is surgically challenging. Obliteration of the pouch of Douglas and the rectovaginal plane can render conventional posterior abdominal dissection unsafe. An 85-year-old woman with cT4b rectal cancer suspected of invading the posterior vaginal wall and uterus developed a rectovaginal fistula after chemoradiotherapy. Despite marked tumor regression, severe fibrosis obliterated the pouch of Douglas and rectovaginal plane; vaginal narrowing and radiation-induced contracture limited transvaginal manipulation. During laparoscopic, bladder-preserving posterior pelvic exenteration, the gynecologic team performed a vaginal-side, retrograde resection of the posterior vaginal wall to obtain controlled access to the rectovaginal space. This enabled en bloc resection of the rectum, uterus, and posterior vaginal wall. Pathology showed residual adenocarcinoma confined to the rectal submucosa, grade 2 response, ypT1bN0, and no viable tumor cells in the vagina or uterus. Postoperative pelvic peritonitis resolved with antibiotics; no recurrence was observed at 10 months. This approach adapts a gynecologic vaginal-side retrograde access concept to colorectal surgery rather than using posterior colpotomy. It may enable controlled entry when posterior abdominal dissection is unsafe, although contamination, tumor spillage, and pelvic infection remain concerns in patients with a rectovaginal fistula. Gynecologic-colorectal collaborative vaginal-side retrograde access may be a practical option for laparoscopic posterior pelvic exenteration in selected patients with severe pelvic fibrosis. Further cases and longer follow-up are needed to assess oncologic safety.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Accurate localization of peripheral pulmonary lesions is a prerequisite for lung-sparing minimally invasive resection. Indocyanine green (ICG)-dyed coils have emerged as an effective multimodal marker, detectable by near-infrared fluorescence, fluoroscopy, palpation, and ultrasound, but their placement currently relies on CT or cone-beam CT guidance, with the associated radiation exposure and logistical demands. For subpleural lesions, transthoracic ultrasound offers real-time, radiation-free guidance. We present our initial experience with ultrasound-guided percutaneous placement of ICG-dyed coils. Of 33 patients scheduled for ICG-coil marking between July 2025 and March 2026, eight were assessed for ultrasound-guided marking, and three (37.5% of those assessed; 9% of all scheduled) had a lesion with a suitable acoustic window. In these three patients (aged 52-67 years), an ICG-dyed coil was placed adjacent to the tumor under real-time transthoracic ultrasound guidance in the operating room under general anaesthesia, immediately before uniportal or biportal video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS). The lesions measured 17-19 mm and were located 2-4 mm below the visceral pleura in the left upper, right lower and right upper lobe. Coil placement was technically successful in all patients, with a median procedure time (first ultrasound contact to needle removal) of 12 minutes (range 11-13 minutes) and a median total added time, including preparation, of 33 minutes. The marker was identified by near-infrared fluorescence in every case, and all lesions were resected with R0 margins. Histology showed squamous cell carcinoma in two patients and metastatic adenocarcinoma of colorectal origin in one. No bleeding or other immediate complications were observed at thoracoscopy. Because the lung was collapsed for resection immediately after puncture, delayed pneumothorax and marker migration could not be assessed. In selected patients with solid subpleural lesions and an adequate acoustic window, ultrasound-guided placement of ICG-dyed coils was technically feasible and enabled fluorescence-guided localization at thoracoscopy. However, due to the small series, the safety of the technique or its added value over intraoperative palpation or thoracoscopic ultrasound cannot be established. Larger prospective studies, including marking with delayed resection, are needed to define patient selection and to compare the technique with CT-guided and bronchoscopic marking.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
For patients with RAS-mutant metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC), effective second-line therapies remain limited. In this multicenter, single-arm phase II trial conducted from March 2023 to November 2025, we enrolled 42 patients with RAS-mutant mCRC who had progressed after first-line therapy. All patients received fruquintinib (4 mg once daily on Days 1-21 of each 28-day cycle) combined with either FOLFIRI or FOLFOX chemotherapy based on prior treatment history. The median progression-free survival (PFS) was 8.08 months (95% CI: 6.18, 9.46), ranking among the longest reported in the second-line setting. The objective response rate (ORR) was 52.5% (95% CI: 36.13, 68.49) and the disease control (DCR) rate 97.5% (95% CI: 86.84, 99.94). Notably, this study reports the first conversion surgery outcomes in this setting, with three patients (7.14%) undergoing successful resection-a rate approaching that observed in first-line trials. The safety profile was manageable, with 7.1% of patients experiencing grade ≥ 3 adverse events including diarrhea (4.8%) and thrombocytopenia (2.4%); no treatment-related deaths occurred. Prior bevacizumab treatment did not affect the consistent efficacy of this regimen. These results support further randomized evaluation of this fruquintinib-based combination as a promising second-line option for patients with RAS-mutant mCRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The role of the human microbiome in cancer development, progression, and response to therapy has moved from correlative curiosity to demonstrated impact on tumor biology. This represents a critical factor for surgical oncologists as they not only resect these tumors, but also direct perioperative antimicrobial exposure and increasingly co-manage neoadjuvant and surveillance pathways in which microbial state may predict and modify response. This review summarizes the basis for therapeutic modulation of the cancer microbiome and metabolome in a contemporary clinical-trial landscape across four broad strategies: additive (fecal microbiota transplantation, defined consortia, and live biotherapeutic products), subtractive (targeted antimicrobials), dietary and metabolome-directed interventions, and engineered or next-generation platforms. Particular attention is given to subtractive approaches in colon and rectal cancer and to the underexplored perioperative interface between the microbiome and surgical outcomes such as anastomotic leak. We outline the principal methodological and translational obstacles, including low-biomass contamination, causal inference, unintended antibiotic effects, and product standardization. Looking ahead, we propose roles for surgeons across the care continuum, from biospecimen stewardship and trial referral to integration of microbiome and circulating tumor DNA signals in surveillance.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are effective in the approximately 5% of metastatic colorectal cancers (mCRC) that are microsatellite instability-high or mismatch repair-deficient (MSI-H/dMMR), whereas microsatellite-stable or mismatch repair-proficient (MSS/pMMR) disease rarely responds to ICI monotherapy. Stereotactic ablative radiotherapy (SABR) has been proposed to prime antitumor immunity in MSS disease. Preclinical studies show that high-dose-per-fraction radiation can induce immunogenic cell death, release tumor antigens and activate the cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) pathway, which may increase T-cell infiltration and, in some models, cause regression of non-irradiated lesions (the abscopal effect). Clinical data come mainly from small, single-arm, early-phase studies that report acceptable safety but modest response rates, and no colorectal-specific randomized trial has shown a survival benefit from adding SABR to immunotherapy. This review summarizes the biological rationale, critically appraises the clinical evidence, including chemo-immuno-radiotherapy in rectal cancer, and discusses toxicity, patient selection, dose-fractionation and sequencing. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from January 2000 to February 2026. SABR-induced immune priming in MSS mCRC is biologically plausible but should be tested in biomarker-stratified randomized trials.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Approximately 30% of patients develop liver-confined recurrences after local treatment for colorectal liver metastases (CRLM), which may be reduced by adjuvant therapy. Hepatic arterial infusion pump (HAIP) chemotherapy delivers high-dose liver-directed chemotherapy. To investigate adjuvant HAIP chemotherapy without systemic therapy in patients with resectable liver-confined recurrence after prior local treatment of CRLM. This multicenter, single-arm phase II trial enrolled patients with resectable recurrent CRLM across 3 centers in the Netherlands. Patients with prior or present extrahepatic disease were excluded. Adjuvant HAIP with floxuridine was administered up to 6 cycles. The primary endpoint was hepatic disease-free survival (hDFS) estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, with a prespecified efficacy boundary of 36 months. Forty-five patients underwent local treatment followed by adjuvant HAIP chemotherapy without systemic therapy. Twenty-eight patients(62%) were treated for a first recurrent CRLM, and 17 patients for a second or higher. Twenty-five patients (56%) had ≥3 CRLM. All patients started HAIP chemotherapy, with a median of 6 cycles (interquartile range: 4 to 6). After a median follow-up of 38.7 months (95% CI: 33.0-42.3), the median hDFS was 16.5 months (95% CI: 9.1-25.8). The median progression-free survival was 14.0 months (95% CI: 7.7-23.0), and the 3-year overall survival was 71% (95% CI: 58%-87%). Initial recurrence included the liver in 23 patients (51%). HAIP implantation-related complications (Clavien-Dindo grade ≥3) occurred in 4 patients (9%), and HAIP chemotherapy-related complications (Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events grade ≥3) occurred in 6 patients (13%). Biliary sclerosis occurred in 4 patients; 3 required stent placement. Adjuvant HAIP chemotherapy without systemic therapy did not achieve the hypothesized hDFS in patients undergoing repeat local treatment for recurrent CRLM.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Although public and patient involvement (PPI) is increasingly promoted in health research, its practical implementation remains rarely documented, especially in primary cancer prevention. The DIADEME group, aimed to address this gap through an empirical descriptive and process‑evaluation study reporting how citizens and patients involvement in research, governance, and preventive actions is organised and performed within the Department of Prevention Cancer Environment of a French Comprehensive Cancer Care Center (Centre Léon Bérard, Lyon). Citizens and patients with prior experience in PPI were recruited through associations, partners, flyers, to form a PPI resource group. A group manager coordinated the initiative, and a patient facilitator provided independent feedback on PPI to ensure balanced collaboration. The engagement framework (mission statement, engagement charter, and annual action plan) was co-developed during the first two meetings. PPI was evaluated using the Patient and Public Engagement Evaluation Tool framework and qualitative feedback. Five patients and five citizens were recruited as PPI resource group members, with associations being the most effective recruitment channel. Their contribution to 9 monthly meetings and additional tasks led to tangible outcomes: revisions to a colorectal cancer prevention study to better address patient needs, the development of an educational card game for Human Papillomavirus prevention, and updates of public information sheets on a public information portal. The patient facilitator had a critical role in improving meetings dynamic enabling more time for participant contributions. The PPI evaluation generated practical recommendations to improve group management, communication workflows, and impact tracking. The DIADEME group demonstrates that involving patients and citizens in cancer prevention research and communication activities is both feasible and valuable, though integration into governance remains challenging. This study provides lessons learned on structuring participatory processes that may support other teams and organisations implementing PPI initiatives in cancer prevention and beyond.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC; diagnosed <50 years) incidence is increasing globally; however, understanding of the epidemiology remains limited. We compared and contrasted EOCRC incidence patterns in England during 2012-2021 with late-onset colorectal cancer (LOCRC; ≥50 years). All primary colorectal cancer (CRC) cases (351,900) were identified from the English National Cancer Registration Database. Percentages and age-standardised incidence rates were calculated by socio-demographic and geographical variables, tumour subsite, stage and route to diagnosis. Trends were assessed for 2012-2021, two quinquennia (2012-2016; 2017-2021) and COVID-19 pandemic-specific periods (1/1/2012-31/3/2020; 1/4/2020-31/12/2021). Incidence rate ratios (IRR) were derived using Poisson regression. EOCRC accounted for 6% of CRC. Whilst more males were diagnosed with LOCRC (55.9%), EOCRC incidence varied little by sex. EOCRC incidence increased over time. The COVID-19 pandemic was associated with a brief (~6 month) disruption in incidence trends for both EOCRC and LOCRC. For EOCRC, incidence of advanced stage disease rose markedly from 2012-2016 to 2017-2021 (IRR = 1.21 (1.16, 1.25)); incidence of both early and advanced-stage LOCRC fell slightly over time (early-stage IRR = 0.99 (0.98, 1.00); advanced-stage IRR = 0.97 (0.96, 0.98)). A greater proportion of EOCRC (25.4%) were diagnosed as emergencies compared with LOCRC (20.2%). Regional variations were minimal for EOCRC but more pronounced for LOCRC. EOCRC incidence continues to rise and displays distinct epidemiological features compared to LOCRC. Higher rates of advanced disease, more frequent emergency diagnosis, and the sharpest increases in the youngest adults underscore growing challenges for timely detection and diagnosis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a heterogeneous disease that results from the progressive accumulation and interactions at multiple levels of genetic alterations, which lead to the transformation of normal colonic epithelium into malignant colorectal tumors. Understanding the molecular basis of CRC pathogenesis, together with the interactions between genetic alterations, epigenetic modifications, environmental and lifestyle factors, is essential for improving prevention, diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment strategies. This review aims to provide a critical reference point for understanding the temporal dynamics of colorectal carcinogenesis, the evolution of molecular classification systems, including their computational and machine-learning foundations and emerging image-based prediction approaches, molecular drivers and the tumor microenvironment (TME) of CRC by summarizing the most investigated molecular pathways involved in CRC pathogenesis and their role as biomarkers for early CRC diagnosis based on the three main molecular mechanisms of colorectal carcinogenesis: chromosomal instability (CIN), microsatellite instability (MSI), and CpG island methylator phenotype (CIMP). Importantly, emerging evidence reveals that the TME acts as an important factor in driving CRC progression by regulating the immune system through dynamic cellular and molecular interactions. In particular, tumor metabolic reprogramming and microbiota-driven alterations act as major drivers of therapy resistance and immune escape. Combining these mechanisms will enhance biomarker discovery and aid in developing precision medicine for patients with CRC. This review also highlights the regulatory roles of key signaling pathways, including Wnt/β-catenin, epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), tumor protein p53 (TP53), and transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) signaling, during CRC initiation and progression, while further addressing current targeted therapies and emerging precision-based and experimental therapeutic strategies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Neoadjuvant immune checkpoint blockade has transformed localized mismatch repair-deficient/microsatellite instability-high (dMMR/MSI-H) colon cancer, producing unprecedented rates of major and complete pathological response. These results raise a question that until recently would have seemed premature: should colectomy remain mandatory in every complete responder? We argue that the next step is not routine omission of surgery, but prospective testing of response-adapted surgery. The central obstacle is no longer treatment efficacy, but reliable identification of a true complete response before resection. Unlike rectal cancer, colon cancer lacks a clinical complete response consensus framework, while residual nodal disease remains difficult to exclude. Endoscopy, imaging and circulating tumour DNA provide complementary information, but none is yet sufficient alone. Emerging trials are now directly testing non-operative strategies. Surgery should therefore remain standard outside clinical trials, while becoming a conditional intervention within carefully designed response-adapted studies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Autophagy plays a critical role in tumor immunity and therapeutic response, yet its prognostic and functional significance in colorectal cancer (CRC) remains incompletely understood. In this study, we constructed a prognostic model based on autophagy-related genes (ARGs) using transcriptomic and clinical data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA). Differentially expressed ARGs were identified, and those significantly associated with overall survival were selected via univariate Cox regression analysis, followed by multivariate Cox regression to establish a six-gene signature. This model effectively stratified patients into high-risk and low-risk groups, with high-risk patients showing significantly shorter survival and pronounced enrichment in tumor-related pathways, immune infiltration, and cytokine-cytokine receptor interactions. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) identified CXCL8 as a central hub gene showing weak to modest correlations with selected DNA-repair transcripts, and linked to metabolism and chemosensitivity, which was further validated in an independent GEO cohort (GSE39582), demonstrating the model's robustness and generalizability. Functional assays revealed that CXCL8 significantly promoted CRC cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) in vitro, as well as tumor growth in a subcutaneous xenograft model in vivo. Mechanistically, CXCL8-driven malignant phenotypes were associated with concurrent autophagic flux suppression and activation of the JNK/MAPK and AKT/mTOR pathways. Pharmacological inhibition of either pathway partially reversed CXCL8 mediated malignant phenotypes, supporting a cooperative role of these pathways in CXCL8-driven progression. Notably, lysosomal inhibitors reduced rather than enhanced malignant phenotypes in CXCL8-overexpressing cells, consistent with intrinsic drug-sensitivity effects; a causal mediatory role of autophagy therefore remains to be established by genetic rescue experiments. Collectively, these findings highlight the clinical relevance of autophagy-related signatures in CRC, provide a robust prognostic model with independent external validation, and identify CXCL8 as a potential therapeutic target showing weak to modest correlations with selected DNA-repair transcripts, whose malignant effects are associated with autophagy suppression via dual signaling pathways.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Nonylphenol (NP), an environmental endocrine disruptor, has been associated with changes in colorectal cancer (CRC) cell proliferation and motility. The contribution of NP-responsive long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) to these effects remains unclear. To investigate the role of MIR200CHG in NP-associated CRC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion and examine its relationship with EPS8L1 expression and ERK1/2 phosphorylation. MIR200CHG and EPS8L1 expression was examined in public CRC datasets and six paired CRC and adjacent noncancerous tissue specimens. After assessing MIR200CHG responses to NP at 10 MIR200CHG and EPS8L1 expression was higher in the CRC tumor tissues, consistent with the expression patterns observed in public CRC datasets. NP increased MIR200CHG expression in CRC cells. In cultured CRC cells, MIR200CHG overexpression enhanced proliferation, migration, and invasion, whereas knockdown reduced these phenotypes. These changes were accompanied by decreased E-cadherin and increased N-cadherin and vimentin after overexpression, with the opposite pattern after knockdown. Dual-luciferase reporter assays supported site-dependent regulation of EPS8L1, while actinomycin D assays indicated that MIR200CHG enhances EPS8L1 mRNA stability. EPS8L1 knockdown attenuated, whereas EPS8L1 overexpression restored, the MIR200CHG-associated phenotypes. MIR200CHG knockdown reduced subcutaneous xenograft growth, while NP treatment increased growth within the knockdown setting. Changes in ERK1/2 phosphorylation accompanied MIR200CHG and EPS8L1 manipulation. NP-responsive MIR200CHG contributes to CRC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion. Reporter, mRNA-stability, and rescue experiments support EPS8L1 as a downstream regulator of these cellular responses. ERK1/2 phosphorylation changes were associated with MIR200CHG and EPS8L1 manipulation, while the xenograft findings support a role for MIR200CHG in primary tumor growth.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Although an increased risk of colorectal cancer (CRC) among patients with ulcerative colitis (UC) is well established, the magnitude and determinants of excess risk remain ambiguous. This uncertainty hampers risk stratification and evidence-based endoscopic surveillance. We empaneled a population-based cohort of incident UC cases in Scandinavia, achieved a median follow-up of 15.0 years through record linkages, designed a case-cohort study, and undertook standardized data abstraction from hospital records of 566 patients with CRC and 720 patients from a sub-cohort randomly sampled at baseline. We fitted weighted multivariable Cox proportional hazard models to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) with 95%CIs, which approximates analyzing the full cohort of 90 780 subjects. We confirmed 2-fold higher CRC risk in patients with pancolitis compared with proctitis (HR 2.3, 95%CI 1.5-3.4). We saw no association between severe macroscopic (HR 1.1, 95%CI 0.7-1.8) or microscopic (HR 1.5, 95%CI 1.0-2.3) inflammation and CRC risk. In contrast, low grade dysplasia predicted a more than 3-fold, and adenomas an almost 10-fold excess rate of CRC (HR 9.8, 95%CI 5.2-18.6). Overall, HRs did not depend on follow-up time (0-1 years, 1-8 years, and >8 years). Pharmacologic treatments with biologic drugs (HR 2.4, 95%CI 0.7-7.7) or immunomodulators (HR 1.1, 95%CI 0.7-1.7) did not significantly reduce the CRC rate. In patients with UC, mucosal abnormalities rather than disease extent and inflammation were the strongest predictive factors of CRC. Our findings do not support prevailing recommendations for endoscopic surveillance.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The intratumoral microbiota plays a crucial role in cancer pathogenesis; however, the specific members involved and their mechanisms remain incompletely defined. Here, we identify Bifidobacterium dentium (B. dentium ) as a tumor-associated bacterium enriched in fecal samples from patients with melanoma and colorectal cancer (CRC) and detectable in human melanoma and CRC tissues. High intratumoral B. dentium abundance correlates with poorer survival in CRC patients. In mouse models, subgingival administration of live B. dentium enables tumor homing and accelerated CT26 and B16F10 tumor growth, including in an orthotopic CT26 colorectal tumor model. Mechanistically, B. dentium invades tumor cells, promotes proliferation through Akt/ERK activation, enhances metastatic potential through MMP3 induction, and increases resistance to key chemotherapeutic agents. B. dentium-derived GABA activates FOXA2-dependent P-gp upregulation, contributing to chemotherapy resistance. These findings establish B. dentium as a niche-dependent pro-tumoral pathobiont and a potential target for improving cancer treatment response.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Chemoresistance, cancer stem cell-associated plasticity, and migratory capacity limit the efficacy of FOLFOX-based chemotherapy in colon cancer. This study investigated the effects of two original isoeugenol-derived polyphenolic compounds, 1 and 2, alone and in combination with FOLFOX, in HT29 colon cancer cells and an HT29-derived cancer stem cell-enriched population. Cell viability was assessed by MTT assay, drug interactions were evaluated using the Chou-Talalay combination index method, wound closure was analyzed by scratch assay, and multidrug resistance-, stemness-, and migration/metastasis-associated gene expression profiles were examined by real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction. Molecular docking was performed against selected proteins related to drug transport, extracellular matrix remodeling, angiogenesis, and cancer stem cell biology. In HT29 cells, the half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC₅₀) of FOLFOX decreased from 191.80 μM at 24 h to 15.52 μM at 48 h, while FOLFOX +1 and FOLFOX +2 further reduced the 48-h IC₅₀ values to 13.30 and 14.95 μM, respectively. In the HT29-CSC-enriched population, FOLFOX showed a 48-h IC₅₀ of 26.80 μM, whereas FOLFOX +2 produced the lowest IC₅₀ value among all groups (17.97 μM). Both combinations showed synergistic interactions in cell viability response particularly at moderate effect levels. FOLFOX +2 consistently reduced wound closure in both cellular models. Gene expression analyses revealed target- and cell model-dependent modulation of drug transporter-, stemness-, and migration/metastasis-associated genes rather than uniform suppression. Docking analyses supported the predicted interaction potential of compounds 1 and 2 with multiple cancer-related targets. Overall, these findings suggest that isoeugenol-derived polyphenolic compounds may modulate FOLFOX-associated responses through cell viability-related, migration-related, multidrug resistance-associated, and stemness-linked mechanisms.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Nanoplastics (NPs) and bisphenols frequently coexist in food and environment, yet their interactions during intestinal uptake are unclear. Here, 80 nm polystyrene NPs were used to investigate the effects of bisphenols on NP uptake by colon cancer cells. PS-NPs were efficiently internalized by CT26.WT cells through predominantly caveolae-mediated endocytosis and mainly accumulated in lysosomes. Bisphenol AF (BPAF) significantly enhanced PS-NP uptake, increasing cellular accumulation at 0.01 μM, without altering uptake pathways or intracellular localization. BPAF adsorbed onto PS-NP surfaces (>70.5 ng/mg PS-NP), reduced zeta potential, promoted particle aggregation, and enhanced particle-cell interactions. BPAF increased PS-NP exocytosis by 20-68% and promoted transcellular transport across a cell monolayer model. Furthermore, Bisphenol B (BPB), BPAF, TBBPA mono (2,3-dibromopropyl ether) (TBBPA-MDBPE), and TBBPA mono (allyl ether) (TBBPA-MAE) showed similar promoting effects, which were associated with reduced particle surface charge. These findings reveal a pollutant-driven mechanism regulating NP uptake and transport through surface property modification.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
An 86-year-old man underwent radical prostatectomy for prostate adenocarcinoma (T3aN0M0) 5 years ago. He presented with recurrent constipation for 5 months. Pelvic MRI raised suspicion of rectal cancer. Serum prostate specific antigen (PSA) was mildly elevated (9.610 ng/mL). PET/CT revealed thickened rectal walls with no significant hypermetabolism on 18F‑FDG imaging, but marked radiotracer uptake on 68Ga‑PSMA imaging (SUVmax = 22.4). Final pathology confirmed metastatic prostate cancer to the rectum. For patients with a history of prostate cancer presenting with rectal occupying lesions, metastatic disease should be included in the differential diagnosis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
We present a patient with biochemical recurrence after salvage radiation and combined androgen deprivation therapy with abiraterone who underwent 18F-PSMA PET/CT for a rapidly rising prostate-specific antigen (PSA). The scan revealed an intense prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-avid focus in the cecum without an apparent CT correlate. Colonoscopy identified a smooth, 2 cm nonobstructing cecal mass, and biopsy confirmed metastatic prostate adenocarcinoma by morphology and immunohistochemistry. This case demonstrates 18F-PSMA PET/CT detection at a low PSA level of a clinically occult metastatic lesion involving the cecum, an exceptionally rare site for prostate cancer spread. Colonoscopy and biopsy confirmation of atypical PSMA-avid gastrointestinal lesions remain essential, as physiologic colonic uptake, PSMA-avid diverticula, and PSMA-expressing primary colorectal cancers are well-documented mimickers.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
We aimed to evaluate the effect of internet-based home treatment with electrical stimulation plus biofeedback training on pelvic floor rehabilitation. Subjects (315 in total) were selected from patients with pelvic floor dysfunction who were diagnosed from October 2022 to June 2023. A home rehabilitation group (n = 178, receiving the Internet-based home treatment with electrical stimulation plus biofeedback training) and an in-hospital rehabilitation group (n = 137, treated with electrical stimulation plus biofeedback training in hospital) were set up. After treatment, differences of statistical significance in POP-Aa, POP-Ba, POP-Gh, POP-Ap, POP-Bp, muscle potential, type I muscle fiber, type II muscle fiber, Pelvic Organ Prolapse Distress Inventory-6 (POPDI-6) subscale score, Colorectal-Anal Distress Inventory-8 (CRADI-8) subscale score, and Urogenital Distress Inventory-6 (UDI-6) subscale score were observed in the home rehabilitation group compared with those before treatment (p < 0.05). Significant differences were detected in the changes in POP-Ap, type I muscle fiber, and type II muscle fiber between the groups before and after treatment, and a greater decrease in POP-Ap and smaller increases in type I muscle fiber and type II muscle fiber were obtained from the home rehabilitation group after treatment in comparison with those from the in-hospital rehabilitation group (p < 0.05). Although the internet-based home treatment with electrical stimulation plus biofeedback training costs a longer time than in-hospital rehabilitation treatment, it can exert better therapeutic effects in terms of improving muscle potential, POP, and urinary symptoms.

展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a polyetiologic disease related to genetic changes, chronic inflammation, dysregulation of the intestinal barrier, diet and gut microbiota dysbiosis. Butyrate is a short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) produced by the microbiota that plays a crucial role in energy metabolism, epithelial homeostasis and mucosal immunity. Sodium butyrate (NaB), the sodium salt of butyric acid, has therefore been the subject of experimental investigation and appears to be a therapeutic option of potential interest. This review critically explores the biological, pharmacological and translational significance of butyrate and NaB in CRC. It details the origins and physicochemical properties, pharmacokinetics, effects on the intestinal barrier, and interactions with the intestinal microbiota, alongside immunomodulatory actions, molecular pathways underlying anti-cancer efficacy, clinical evidence, and patent holdings, and further explores prospective formulation and delivery methods. Butyrate/NaB exerts pleiotropic effects via inhibition of HDAC and activation of free fatty acid receptors (FFARs), such as GPR41/FFAR3, GPR43/FFAR2 and GPR109A/HCAR2.These processes regulate various inflammatory and oncogenic signaling pathways, including NF-κB, NLRP3, Wnt/β-catenin, PI3K/Akt, MAPK, and STAT3, as well as mitochondrial metabolism, oxidative stress, cell-cycle progression, apoptosis, epithelial-mesenchymal transition, and immune-cell function. Additionally, butyrate helps preserve gut barrier function and can influence CRC biology by interacting with the tumour microenvironment, microbial metabolism, and epithelial cells. There is extensive preclinical evidence of the barrier-protective, anti-inflammatory, immunomodulatory, and anticancer properties of butyrate/NaB in cell- and animal-based models. The strength of evidence, however, depends on the model, concentration/dose, duration of treatment and endpoint. The mechanistic and preclinical results should therefore not be interpreted as being equivalent to actual clinical efficacy. There is limited available human evidence for specific therapeutic uses of CRC. Various factors limit its translational application, including rapid metabolism, a short biological half-life, and low systemic exposure, as well as inherent butyrate fluctuations, formulation challenges, and a scarcity of stringent clinical trials tailored to CRC. Colon-targeted delivery systems, microencapsulation, nanotechnology-based delivery systems, microbiome-directed interventions, patient selection by biomarkers, and rational combination strategies may overcome these limitations. Butyrate/NaB offers a promising multitarget strategy for CRC research; however, further investigation into its mechanisms, pharmacokinetics, dosing, formulation, and large-scale clinical trials is necessary to validate its therapeutic efficacy and define its translational potential.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
This study aims to identify the key metabolism-related genes (MRGs) involved in colorectal cancer (CRC), and to explore their biological functions, prognostic value, and regulatory effects on the tumor microenvironment (TME). Based on the CRC-related datasets (GSE9348, GSE41328, GSE41657, GSE113513), differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were screened using the "Limma" R package, and the intersection was taken with the MRGs in the MSigDB database to obtain differentially expressed metabolism-related genes (DE-MRGs). Functional enrichment analysis was performed using the "clusterProfiler" R package. The hub genes of the DE-MRGs were further identified based on protein-protein interaction network construction and topological analyses. The expression level and prognostic value of the hub DE-MRGs were analyzed with GEPIA, UALCAN and Kaplan-Meier Plotter databases respectively. The correlation between fatty acid-binding protein 1 (FABP1) and TME as well as immunotherapy markers was also evaluated. The biological functions of FABP1 in regulating the proliferation and apoptosis of CRC cells were investigated through experiments including Cell Counting Kit-8 assay, flow cytometry and nude mouse tumor transplantation assay. The regulatory effects of FABP1 on the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARγ) pathway were evaluated by Western blotting, co-immunoprecipitation, luciferase reporter gene assay, and qPCR. FABP1 was identified as one of the hub DE-MRGs in CRC, which was significantly downregulated in CRC tissues and cell lines, and its low expression was associated with shorter overall survival (OS), post-progression survival (PPS), and recurrence-free survival (RFS) of patients. The expression of FABP1 was correlated with multiple TME indices and biomarkers of immunotherapy. Functional enrichment analysis suggested that FABP1 was positively correlated with the PPARγ pathway. Overexpression of FABP1 could inhibit the proliferation of SW480 and HT-29 cells, promote apoptosis and upregulate the expression of PPARγ. Additionally, FABP1 could bind with PPARγ, and promoted the transcription of the target genes of PPARγ. However, the PPARγ antagonist SR11023 could reverse the effects of FABP1 overexpression on the proliferation and apoptosis of SW480 and HT-29 cells. FABP1 may exert tumor suppressor effects in CRC by activating the PPARγ signaling. It is expected to serve as a potential prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target for CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal liver metastasis (CRLM) develops through malignant-cell plasticity and microenvironmental remodeling, yet the spatial principles by which epithelial, stromal, vascular and myeloid states assemble remain poorly defined. We integrated a 136,995-cell single-cell atlas, four spatial transcriptomic sections and bulk-cohort survival analysis. cNMF resolved three recurrent malignant programs-C1 Proliferative-biosynthetic, C2 AP-1 stress-inflammatory and C3 Secretory-invasive immune-like-which recurred across donors (with a rare, patient-associated tuft/chemosensory component in C3) and followed a pseudotime-associated C1-to-C2-to-C3 ordering rather than a demonstrated temporal progression. C3 cells, rare overall and of donor-dependent abundance, showed epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and invasive features, and in exploratory analyses their signature was associated with shorter recurrence-free survival. Continuous RGS1/CTSL programs captured macrophage heterogeneity more robustly than discrete subclusters. Spatial deconvolution revealed recurrent Fib-COL10A1-Endo-GJA5 proximity and variable C3 integration, with focal CTSL-program macrophage interfaces; MAPK and VEGF pathway activity was higher in C3-rich regions, although this association depended on how C3 was measured. An INHBA-CST6-LBH-FSTL3 score, which aggregates C3 and stromal expression, was associated with recurrence in TCGA, with partial external support in GSE39582 and no demonstrated gain over clinical variables. Virtual knockout of CST6 and LBH and LINCS screening prioritized MEK inhibition (PD-0325901) as a candidate for reversing the C3-associated transcriptional state; no target-engagement claim is made. Together, these findings define a spatially variable, C3-centred multicellular ecology in CRLM and provide a testable computational framework nominating recurrence-associated signatures and network-level candidates for experimental validation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Direct comparative evidence on the hinotori and da Vinci robotic systems in colorectal cancer surgery remains limited. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to compare their short-term perioperative outcomes. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched for studies directly comparing hinotori with da Vinci robotic surgery in patients with colorectal cancer. Study-level data were pooled using random-effects models, with mean differences (MDs) for continuous outcomes and odds ratios (ORs) for dichotomous outcomes, each with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Five retrospective propensity-score-matched studies involving 462 patients (hinotori, n = 204; da Vinci, n = 258) were included. Operative time (MD 30.57 min, 95% CI 17.51-43.64; I² = 0%) and console time (MD 30.72 min, 95% CI 17.29-44.16; I² = 42%) were significantly longer with hinotori, whereas length of hospital stay was significantly shorter (MD - 1.58 days, 95% CI - 2.92 to - 0.24; I² = 63%). No statistically significant differences were detected for estimated blood loss (MD 3.42 mL, 95% CI - 6.98 to 13.82; I² = 66%) or for postoperative complications (grade I-II: OR 0.78, 95% CI 0.36-1.69; grade III-IV: OR 0.54, 95% CI 0.16-1.76; overall: OR 0.74, 95% CI 0.37-1.46). In this meta-analysis of propensity-score-matched studies, hinotori was associated with longer operative and console times and a shorter hospital stay than da Vinci, whereas no statistically significant difference was detected in blood loss or postoperative complications. Because clinically important differences in safety could not be excluded and residual confounding could not be ruled out, these findings should be regarded as preliminary; larger prospective comparative studies are warranted.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The 2018 World Cancer Research Fund (WCRF)/American Institute for Cancer Research Third Expert Report (TER) on diet, adiposity, physical activity, and risk of 19 cancers could be enhanced with new data. A framework is needed to prioritize future systematic reviews. We searched PubMed (January 2019-February 2024) for meta-analyses, pooled analyses, randomized controlled trials (RCTs), Mendelian randomization (MR) studies, and large (> 100,000 participants) cohort studies. We assessed TER findings using conditional power (CP) and fail-safe number (FSN) statistics. We developed an exposure-based prioritization score (PS) by awarding or subtracting points considering the quantity, statistical significance, direction, and novelty of associations. We compared 366 meta-analyses, 121 pooled analyses, 19 RCTs, 174 MR studies, and 391 cohort studies covering 151 exposures and 28 cancers with 1,371 TER meta-analyses. Based on CP, nonsignificant TER associations likely to become significant with additional evidence included folate and colorectal, waist circumference and lung, total fat and ovarian, tea and ovarian, and red meat and kidney cancers. The FSN indicated that most significant TER associations are unlikely to change with additional evidence. The median PS was 6 (range: - 15 to 163), with top scores observed for anthropometric measurements (PS The prioritization framework can help identify impactful systematic reviews to complement TER conclusions and enhance our understanding of emerging research.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Breast, cervical, and colon cancer are central to cancer control policy in Türkiye, yet their long-term incidence and mortality trends have not been described with formal trend-segmentation methods. We conducted a population-based Joinpoint regression analysis of age-standardized incidence (2009-2020; registry coverage rising from 23.4 to 50.6%) and mortality (2009-2023) rates for breast, cervical, and colon cancer in Türkiye. We estimated annual percentage change per segment and average APC (AAPC), overall and by age group, with 95% confidence intervals (CIs; in brackets). Breast cancer incidence rose [AAPC: 1.51% (0.14, 2.86)]; mortality rose until 2015 and then leveled off [AAPC: 1.13% (-0.16, 2.44)]. Cervical cancer incidence was stable overall [AAPC: 0.79% (-0.62, 2.18)] but rose at ages 30-49 years [AAPC: 1.99% (0.64, 3.40)], while mortality declined [AAPC: -1.44% (-2.37, -0.51)]. Colon cancer incidence rose in women [AAPC: 1.72% (0.20, 3.02)] and men [AAPC: 2.44% (0.52, 4.05)] mainly during 2009-2012. Colon cancer mortality rose until 2015 and then declined; the overall AAPC was significant in men [0.72% (0.25, 1.28)] but not in women [-0.19% (-0.68, 0.36)]. Cervical cancer mortality declined steadily despite rising incidence among younger women, while breast and colon cancer incidence increased and colon cancer carried a disproportionate mortality burden in men. Because registry coverage roughly doubled, the incidence increases may partly reflect wider coverage and case ascertainment rather than a true national increase. These ecological trends cannot be attributed to a single cause and should be read alongside screening-program coverage and performance.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The study aimed to examine the relationship between colorectal cancer (CRC) screening beliefs and general health-seeking behavior among hospitalized adults aged 50-70 years and to identify factors independently associated with general health-seeking behavior. This cross-sectional study included 435 hospitalized adults aged 50-70 years without prior CRC or colorectal symptoms at a tertiary hospital in western Türkiye. Data were collected using the Health Belief Model Scale for Colorectal Cancer Screening and the Health-Seeking Behavior Scale (HSBS), assessing professional, traditional, and online health-seeking behaviors. CRC screening uptake was not an outcome. Multiple linear regression was performed. Professional health-seeking behavior had the highest mean score. Total HSBS scores correlated moderately with perceived benefits and confidence (r = 0.576, P < 0.001) and weakly with health motivation (r = 0.323, P < 0.001), perceived susceptibility (r = 0.156, P = 0.001), and perceived severity (r = 0.140, P = 0.003). In regression (R2 = 0.375), perceived benefits and confidence (β = 0.451, P < 0.001), educational level (β = 0.119, P = 0.005), and perceived severity (β = 0.099, P = 0.020) were independently associated with general health-seeking behavior. CRC screening beliefs, particularly perceived benefits and confidence, and educational level were independently associated with general health-seeking behavior. General health-seeking behavior should be distinguished from actual CRC screening participation, as higher health-seeking does not necessarily indicate screening adherence. Hospitalization may provide an opportunity for nurses to address screening beliefs; prospective studies are needed to determine whether interventions translate into verified CRC screening uptake.

Accurate imaging-based response assessment is essential for proficient mismatch repair (pMMR) locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC). This study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of MRI, endorectal ultrasound (ERUS) and 18F-FAPI PET/MRI for identifying pathological complete response (pCR) after neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy (SCRT) followed by chemoimmunotherapy. This single-center retrospective study included 143 patients. Diagnostic performance was assessed using sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy with 95% confidence intervals. Cohen's κ assessed agreement between imaging-defined complete response (iCR) and pCR. Paired comparisons used Cochran's Q and Holm-adjusted exact McNemar tests. The pCR rate was 51.0%. MRI ( Neoadjuvant SCRT followed by chemoimmunotherapy achieved high pCR rates in pMMR LARC. Conventional MRI and ERUS showed limited sensitivity despite relatively high specificity. 18F-FAPI PET/MRI showed potential diagnostic utility in a small subgroup, but its moderate sensitivity and limited sample size warrant further validation. These findings highlight the limitations of imaging alone and the need for comprehensive response assessment.

These empty bacterial envelopes retain native surface structures and immunostimulatory properties, serving as both drug carriers and adjuvants. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Effective bowel preparation is crucial for accurate colorectal cancer (CRC) screening through colonoscopy. Many patients struggle with preparation, leading to inadequate results. The goal of this cost-effectiveness analysis is to compare oral SUTAB tablets and SUFLAVE osmotic laxative to polyethylene glycol-electrolyte solution (PEG-ELS) and over-the-counter (OTC) products in US adults 45 and older at average risk of CRC referred for colonoscopy. An 8-state Markov model was developed that follows the natural history in the average-risk population without screening from no adenoma to adenoma, localized, regional, distant, or posttreated CRC progression, and death. The model was calibrated to US Preventive Services Task Force microsimulation models. Incremental costs, quality-adjusted life years (QALYs), and incremental cost-effectiveness ratio were calculated for all comparisons. One-way sensitivity analysis assessed input uncertainty. For a 45-year-old over a lifetime, SUTAB and SUFLAVE were associated with cost savings per person of $439 and $361 compared with PEG-ELS, and $822 and $744 compared with OTC. Total discounted QALYs were nearly equivalent between comparators (differences <0.001). Due to cost savings and very small QALY improvements, incremental cost-effectiveness ratio analysis showed OTC was dominated by all comparators, PEG-ELS was dominated by SUTAB and SUFLAVE, and SUFLAVE was dominated by SUTAB. One-way sensitivity analysis identified colonoscopy adherence and preparation adequacy as the most impactful parameters. We found that using SUTAB or SUFLAVE was cost-effective compared with OTC or PEG-ELS. Improved bowel preparation with SUTAB and SUFLAVE reduces the need for repeated colonoscopies, associated costs, and adverse events, with minimal impact on life years, QALYs, and CRC detection rates.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Immunogenic cell death (ICD) converts dying tumor cells into an anticancer vaccine, yet whether protection depends on how those cells are prepared and when they are given has rarely been examined. Using mitoxantrone (MTX), a clinically approved small molecule classified as an ICD inducer, we examined both variables in the murine CT-26 colon carcinoma model. MTX reduced viability in a concentration-dependent manner and induced extracellular ATP release. The total extent of cell death, however, was similar across concentrations, indicating that the concentration-dependent loss of viability was not accompanied by a proportional increase in cell death. What differed was the composition of the dying population, which shifted from early to late apoptotic cells as the concentration increased. Prophylactic vaccination with MTX-treated cells protected BALB/c mice, leaving 75.0-87.5% of animals tumor-free after vaccination at 1 μM and 37.5-62.5% at 3 μM across independent experiments. Protection increased with the interval between vaccination and challenge, with 0%, 50.0%, and 87.5% of animals tumor-free after simultaneous injection, a 3-day interval, and a 7-day interval, respectively. Cells killed completely by freeze-thaw were inactive as a vaccine, and cisplatin-treated cells conferred only a marginal delay, whereas responders to MTX-treated cells resisted rechallenge for the remainder of the observation period. Taken together, these results show that use of an ICD-inducing drug alone is not sufficient for effective dying-cell vaccination and that protective efficacy is influenced by vaccine preparation and by the interval between vaccination and tumor challenge, rather than by the extent of cell death alone.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Metabolic plasticity limits mitochondria-directed cancer therapy by enabling glycolytic compensation during respiratory stress. Our previous nano-energy interference (NEI) platform showed that coupling azelaic acid (AZA)-induced mitochondrial disruption with restriction of glucose utilization suppresses colorectal cancer (CRC), but the upstream program coordinating this adaptive response remained unresolved. Here, we identify HIF-1α-dependent glycolytic adaptation as a key response to AZA-induced respiratory inhibition and develop glutamine-functionalized lipid nanoparticles (G-LNPs) to deliver dominant-negative HIF-1α (dnHIF-1α) mRNA. G-LNPs were approximately 105 nm in diameter, achieved >90% mRNA encapsulation, and enhanced uptake and functional reporter mRNA expression in ASCT2-expressing MC38 cells in a GPNA-sensitive manner. AZA suppressed mitochondrial respiration while activating HIF-responsive transcription, glycolytic activity, lactate production, and GLUT1, HK2, LDHA, and PDK1 expressions. G-LNP-delivered dnHIF-1α blocked this compensatory response without materially intensifying respiratory inhibition, thereby deepening ATP depletion and producing a distinct treatment-associated metabolomic state. Following treatment withdrawal and equal viable cell replating, the combination caused persistent impairment of regrowth and clonogenic capacity. In subcutaneous MC38 tumors, combined treatment produced the greatest tumor growth inhibition without overt systemic toxicity. Together, these findings support transient disruption of HIF-dependent metabolic adaptation as a strategy to convert partially recoverable mitochondrial stress into a durable loss of CRC cell fitness.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) develops through a multistep progression from normal colonic mucosa to adenoma and ultimately carcinoma. However, the cell-type-specific senescence-associated states during this transition remain incompletely understood. We performed an integrative analysis of single-cell RNA-sequencing and spatial transcriptomic datasets derived from normal mucosa, adenomatous polyps, and primary CRC tissues. Our analyses revealed a progressive increase in senescence-associated transcriptional scores from normal mucosa through adenoma to carcinoma, with the highest senescence scores observed in malignant tissues. This increase was particularly evident in epithelial cells and monocytes. Cell-cell communication analysis identified enhanced macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) signaling between high-senescence-score cells and B-cell populations, primarily through the MIF-CD74/CXCR4 receptor complex. Spatial transcriptomic analysis further showed that high-senescence-score regions were preferentially localized at or near the tumor invasive margin and in proximity to stromal regions, indicating that senescence-associated programs may contribute to the spatial organization of the CRC microenvironment. Together, these findings support a senescence-centered model of colorectal tumor evolution in which epithelial, myeloid, and lymphoid senescence-associated states progressively accumulate and interact through paracrine signaling networks. The MIF-CD74/CXCR4 axis may represent a candidate mediator of senescence-associated tumor-immune interactions and a potential therapeutic target.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Early detection is critical for improving survival in colorectal carcinoma (CRC), underscoring the need for reliable early-stage biomarkers. Plasma protein biomarkers may support the detection of early-stage CRC. In this study, we profiled plasma from 24 patients with stages I-III CRC and 10 non-tumor participants, together with paired tumor and distant-normal tissues from the patients with CRC, to identify proteins preferentially elevated in stage I disease. Seven plasma proteins had higher abundance in stage I CRC than in stages II and III CRC and non-tumor participants; three of these proteins, HSPA8, ALDOA, and PDLIM1, were also elevated in stage I tumor tissues. In the discovery comparison of stage I CRC with non-tumor participants, HSPA8 alone achieved an internally cross-validated random forest classification accuracy of 88.9%, matching the three-protein model. Tissue upregulation was further supported by Western blotting. ELISA assessment included 32 participants with matched proteomic measurements and was subsequently expanded to 108 participants. The HSPA8-score was calculated by dividing the dilution-corrected HSPA8 concentration by the total protein amount in 10 μL of plasma. In the expanded cohort, random forest classification using this score achieved internally cross-validated accuracies of 74.47% for stage I versus stages II-IV CRC and 56.67% for stage I CRC versus non-tumor participants. The corresponding exploratory reference cutoffs were 0.066 and 0.029. These findings identify HSPA8 as a potential plasma protein biomarker for stage I CRC detection.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Epidemiological research on ultra-processed food (UPF) consumption and cancer has expanded rapidly; however, the evidence is uneven across cancer sites. Associations were relatively consistent for colorectal cancer, modest and partly attenuated after adjustment for breast cancer, and limited, single-cohort, or largely indirect for lung, pancreatic, renal, and prostate cancers. Recent umbrella reviews have rated the certainty of this evidence as low to very low, reflecting heterogeneous exposure classification, residual confounding, and inconsistent findings. This narrative review synthesizes the current epidemiological evidence on UPF consumption and overall and site-specific cancer risk, evaluates the biological plausibility of three mechanism clusters-obesity-driven metabolic and inflammatory pathways, processing-derived contaminants and food-contact chemicals, and food additives and their mixtures-while distinguishing human evidence from experimental models, and critically examines the NOVA classification as an exposure framework, including its application to non-Western diets. Compared with previous reviews, we appraised the evidence site by site, integrated the most recent umbrella and dose-response meta-analyses, and mapped each proposed mechanism to the tier of evidence supporting it. Standardized NOVA-based exposure assessment, repeated dietary measurements, integration of exposure biomarkers into prospective cohorts, and causal inference frameworks that distinguish confounding from mediation are prerequisites for evidence-based, UPF-specific cancer prevention recommendations.

There is a rapid increase in early onset CRC worldwide. This incidence is profoundly influenced by biological aging in the colon, yet the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely defined. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains one of the most common malignancies worldwide and a leading cause of cancer-related mortality. Recent advances in CRC molecular biology have focused on biomarkers for early detection, prognostic stratification, treatment selection, and disease monitoring. Clinically validated biomarkers, including microsatellite instability (MSI), RAS and BRAF mutations, HER2 amplification, and carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA), guide targeted therapy and predict treatment response. However, tumor heterogeneity, clonal evolution, and microenvironmental influences limit the predictive value of single biomarkers. Recent molecular diagnostics therefore increasingly focus on dynamic and minimally invasive approaches. Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) is a promising biomarker for detecting minimal residual disease, monitoring recurrence, and assessing tumor evolution in real time. Multi-omics profiling, spatial transcriptomics, and artificial intelligence further expand tumor characterization except for conventional genomic alterations. Our review integrates common CRC biomarkers with developing liquid biopsy, multi-omics, spatial transcriptomics, and artificial intelligence approaches across early detection, prognosis, treatment selection, and longitudinal monitoring. Future biomarker strategies will likely rely on integrated molecular models combined with longitudinal liquid-biopsy assessment. However, most new biomarkers remain at the investigational stage, and assay heterogeneity, limited standardization, and insufficient prospective clinical validation currently restrict their routine clinical use.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Resistance to chemotherapy continues to be a significant challenge for cancer treatment and a contributing factor to treatment failures and tumor progression. Recently, the gut microbiome has emerged as an important modulator of the response to chemotherapy. Numerous pre-clinical and clinical studies have demonstrated a direct association between gut microbiota composition and therapy effectiveness in many cancer types, such as colorectal, breast, pancreatic, gastric, and lung cancers, melanoma, and hematological cancers. Gut microbiota effectively regulate the efficiency of chemotherapeutic agents in various ways, either by biotransformation of chemotherapeutic agents or modulation of host immunity. In addition, microbial metabolites such as short-chain fatty acids, secondary bile acids, and tryptophan metabolites are also involved in the regulation of chemotherapy response through modulating apoptosis, immunity, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition. Finally, dysbiosis induced by chemotherapy and antibiotics has also been reported to reduce the effectiveness of therapy. This review will emphasize the ways in which gut microbiota can modulate chemotherapeutic response and induce chemoresistance. Understanding the interactions between chemotherapeutic drugs and the gut microbiota can help to enhance the efficiency of chemotherapy and find more appropriate personalized treatments.
