ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Temperature is a fundamental physical variable affecting protein folding, proteostasis, cell-cycle kinetics, and immune function, yet cancer cell biology is performed almost exclusively at a fixed 37 °C, and distinct thermal phenomena are often conflated under the single term "hyperthermia." This review examines the biology of mild, fever-range temperature excursions of approximately 38-41 °C, which are mechanistically distinct from externally induced hyperthermia. We synthesize three strands of evidence that have rarely been considered together. First, tumor cells display heterogeneous thermal sensitivity, with differences in growth, cell-cycle responses, and thermal tolerance that may reflect intrinsic molecular features and proteostatic reserve, including the heat-shock response mediated by HSF1 and HSP70/HSP90. Second, fever-range temperatures remodel antitumor immunity across innate and adaptive compartments, affecting immune-cell trafficking, membrane organization, metabolism, and tumor-immune recognition. Third, the clinical record appears controversial: febrile infections have been associated with lower subsequent cancer risk, whereas postoperative fever has been associated with worse prognosis. We argue that these observations cannot be interpreted without considering host state, timing, and the biological context in which temperature elevation occurs. The three evidence streams are of unequal strength: cell-intrinsic thermal sensitivity and fever-range immune effects rest on direct experimental data, much of it from colorectal cancer, which we adopt as the principal proof-of-concept model, whereas the clinical associations are largely retrospective, and we treat them with correspondingly different confidence. We therefore frame a central testable question: is cell-intrinsic thermal sensitivity a cause or a correlate of fever's effects on cancer? We propose an experimental agenda that separates cell-autonomous thermal responses from host-mediated effects and establishes temperature as an explicit, biologically informative variable in cancer research.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Tumor budding, defined as single tumor cells or clusters of up to four cells at the invasive front, is a morphological marker of tumor-cell dissociation and stromal invasion in colorectal cancer. Standardization by the International Tumor Budding Consensus Conference (ITBCC) established a reproducible hematoxylin-and-eosin-based method and enabled broader incorporation of budding into pathology reporting and clinical risk assessment. Intermediate- and high-grade budding are associated with lymph node metastasis in pT1 colorectal cancer, while high-grade budding identifies a subgroup of stage II colon cancers with increased recurrence risk. Adverse prognostic associations have also been reported in stage III disease and in rectal cancer after neoadjuvant therapy, although evidence that budding predicts benefit from a specific treatment is still insufficient. At the biological level, budding is linked to partial epithelial-mesenchymal transition, altered cell adhesion, cytoskeletal remodeling, and interactions with fibroblasts, extracellular matrix, and immune cells. Digital pathology and artificial intelligence may improve hotspot selection, quantification, and spatial characterization, but their clinical use depends on external validation, control of domain shift, and continued pathologist oversight. Tumor budding is therefore best interpreted as a complementary morphological biomarker alongside TNM stage, established histopathological risk factors, molecular features, and clinical context.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Complete (R0) resection remains the primary surgical objective for colorectal liver metastases (CRLM), but margin width cannot be interpreted independently of tumor anatomy, biology, and the amount of functional liver sacrificed to obtain it. This focused narrative review re-examines surgical margins from the perspective of parenchymal preservation and longitudinal multimodal treatment. We distinguish parenchymal R1 exposure (R1par), an undesirable transection-surface event consistently associated with local recurrence in retrospective series, from planned vascular R1 detachment (R1vasc), which has shown more favorable outcomes than R1par in selected retrospective series but remains dependent on careful anatomical selection. Vessel-skeletonized parenchymal-sparing hepatectomy (VESPAH) is presented as one operative model for achieving complete macroscopic clearance while preserving intrahepatic vascular architecture; the evidence for this model is confined to retrospective series and is therefore illustrative and hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory. We further propose "treatment continuity"-preservation of the physiological and anatomical capacity to receive indicated systemic therapy and repeat local treatment-as a reportable surgical outcome. A four-axis framework integrating technical resectability, functional reserve, tumor biology, and future treatment options is outlined, together with a minimum set of reporting elements for margin phenotype and operational definitions for four candidate measures of treatment continuity. R0 resection should remain the goal, but the quality of hepatectomy for CRLM may be more comprehensively assessed by considering both the margin achieved at the index operation and the treatments that remain feasible thereafter.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC), defined as colorectal cancer diagnosed before age 50, has become an increasing global public health concern. Incidence rates have risen among younger adults in many countries, despite stable or declining rates in older populations. This review examines global EOCRC epidemiology, potentially modifiable risk factors, and projected future disease burden. Evidence from international cancer databases, population-based registries, and observational studies is synthesised, considering differences by age, sex, geographic region, and tumour location. Key risk factors include obesity, metabolic dysfunction, dietary patterns, physical inactivity, alcohol consumption, tobacco use, antibiotic exposure, and gut microbiome alterations. The review also evaluates temporal trends and projections of incidence, prevalence, and mortality. Although increasing incidence may reflect changing lifestyles, metabolic health, environmental exposures, and other early-life risk factors, their relative contributions remain incompletely understood. Improved understanding of EOCRC epidemiology and future burden may help identify high-risk populations, guide targeted prevention strategies, inform public health policy, and support discussions on earlier colorectal cancer detection and screening.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The gut microbiome influences colorectal cancer (CRC) progression and responses to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), with immunotherapy resistance remaining a major challenge in microsatellite-stable/mismatch repair-proficient (MSS/pMMR) CRC. This review examines the mechanisms and translational potential of fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) in CRC immunotherapy, focusing on the interplay among microbial functions, metabolic alterations, and immune microenvironment remodeling. Current evidence suggests that FMT may influence antitumor immunity beyond restoring microbial diversity by transferring functionally relevant microbial communities, metabolic profiles, and immunomodulatory signals. These changes may affect antigen presentation, inflammatory signaling, T-cell activity, and myeloid-cell states, thereby shaping the tumor immune microenvironment and potentially modulating responses to PD-1/PD-L1 blockade. However, the clinical efficacy of FMT in CRC, the determinants of successful microbial engraftment, and the mechanisms linking donor-derived microbial functions to therapeutic outcomes remain incompletely understood. Integrating defined microbial consortia, metabolite-based interventions, and multi-omics-guided patient stratification may help advance FMT toward mechanism-driven precision microbiome therapy and inform strategies to improve CRC immunotherapy outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Background Postoperative complications are important adverse outcomes after colorectal cancer (CRC) surgery. Preoperative C-reactive protein (CRP), an accessible marker of systemic inflammation, may provide useful information about the risk of postoperative morbidity. This study aimed to evaluate the association between preoperative CRP and postoperative complications in patients undergoing elective CRC surgery and to assess its ability to discriminate complication severity. Methods This prospective observational study included 64 patients undergoing elective, potentially curative CRC surgery at the Department of Colorectal Surgery, Bangladesh Medical University, Dhaka, between March 2024 and February 2025. Preoperative CRP was measured, with concentrations >5 mg/L considered elevated. Postoperative complications occurring during hospitalization were recorded and graded according to the Clavien-Dindo classification. Associations between CRP and postoperative complications were assessed using the chi-square test or Fisher's exact test, as appropriate. Results Among the 64 patients included, 42 (65.6%) were male patients. The mean age was 46.6 ± 15.3 years. Preoperative CRP was >5 mg/L in 24 (37.5%) patients. Overall, postoperative complications occurred in 43 (67.2%) patients, including wound infection in 17 (26.6%), anastomotic leakage in 6 (9.4%), respiratory complications in 6 (9.4%), and renal complications in 1 (1.6%). Patients with CRP >5 mg/L had significantly higher rates of wound infection (58.3% vs. 7.5%; P<0.001), respiratory complications (20.8% vs. 2.5%; P=0.024), and anastomotic leakage (25.0% vs. 0%; P=0.002) than those with CRP ≤5 mg/L. Among the 43 patients who developed postoperative complications, 10 (23.3%) had Clavien-Dindo grade ≥III complications. All patients with grade ≥III complications had CRP >5 mg/L, compared with 12 (36.4%) patients with grade I-II complications (P<0.001). Conclusion Elevated preoperative CRP was associated with postoperative morbidity and greater complication severity in this cohort. Preoperative CRP may serve as an adjunct to perioperative risk assessment, although larger studies with independent validation are needed.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Urethroperineal fistula (UPF) is a rare urological condition with significant heterogeneity and limited treatment consensus. Especially in patients with a history of radiotherapy, extensive tissue damage often leads to insufficient local tissue reconstruction. A 61-year-old male with a history of rectal cancer radiotherapy and abdominoperineal resection developed UPF, which recurred after robot-assisted prostatectomy combined with perineal fistula repair and scrotal dartos flap interposition. Imaging confirmed a 2 cm × 3 cm fistula defect at the prostatic urethra stump. We performed gracilis muscle flap transfer to repair UPF. Postoperative follow-up included urethrography, cystoscopy, and patient-reported outcome measures. At 1-year follow-up, the fistula was resolved without recurrence; the patient underwent artificial urinary sphincter implantation for pre-existing incontinence, achieving satisfactory urinary control and no limb mobility impairment. Surgical outcomes and long-term follow-up confirmed the efficacy of the procedure and high patient satisfaction. The key lessons include thorough scar excision for vascularization, and meticulous preservation of the gracilis muscle's neurovascular pedicle to ensure flap viability.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The complex organization of tissues is shaped by the spatial arrangement of diverse cell types executing specialized gene programs. Cell-type-specific spatial gene programs (SGPs) are transcriptional modules that capture spatial expression co-variation within cell types. However, identifying these SGPs remains challenging in spatial transcriptomics. Here we present MacSGP, a scalable framework that integrates deep graph neural networks with probabilistic modeling to identify cell-type-specific SGPs through low-rank structures while accounting for cell type mixtures. Through comprehensive simulations and real data analyses spanning diverse tissues and technologies, we demonstrate that MacSGP effectively distinguishes cell-type-specific SGPs from cell-type marker gene expression patterns while uncovering tissue architecture and cellular microenvironments. In a mouse brain dataset, we identify replicable SGPs reflecting subregional neuronal specializations, with these genes significantly enriched for heritabilities associated with brain-related phenotypes. Across colorectal cancer datasets from various platforms, MacSGP identifies consistent SGPs that define distinct cellular niches within the tumor microenvironment.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Venous thromboembolism (VTE), including deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, is a serious perioperative complication after colorectal cancer surgery. Although guidelines recommend prophylaxis, bleeding risks complicate decision-making, and evidence regarding Japanese patients remains limited. Therefore, this study aimed to identify perioperative risk factors associated with VTE in colorectal cancer surgery to inform effective risk stratification and targeted prevention strategies. A retrospective analysis of 397 patients who underwent elective colorectal cancer resection at a single institution between June 2014 and May 2024 was conducted. Preoperative and postoperative D-dimer levels were measured, and lower extremity venous ultrasonography was performed when indicated. When deep vein thrombosis was detected by venous ultrasonography, contrast-enhanced computed tomography was subsequently performed to evaluate the presence of pulmonary embolism. Univariate analyses were used to determine factors significantly associated with VTE, and a P-value < .05 was considered statistically significant. Preoperative VTE was observed in nine of 397 patients (2.3%), and postoperative VTE was observed in nine of 388 patients (2.3%). The univariate analysis suggested that age ≥75 years, female gender, albumin levels < 3.5 g/dL, and hemoglobin levels < 10 g/dL were significantly associated with preoperative VTE, while operative time ≥ 240 minutes and intraoperative blood loss ≥ 50 mL were significantly associated with postoperative VTE. Advanced age, female gender, hypoalbuminemia, anemia, prolonged operative time, and increased intraoperative blood loss were significantly associated with perioperative VTE in univariate analysis. Effective perioperative risk stratification and targeted surveillance may contribute to the early detection and prevention of VTE in Japanese patients undergoing colorectal cancer surgery.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Tumor budding (TB) and poorly differentiated clusters (PDCs) are invasive-front histopathological features associated with aggressive behavior in colorectal carcinoma. We evaluated their relationships with clinicopathological characteristics and overall survival (OS), including whether observed survival associations persisted after adjustment for established prognostic factors. TB and PDC were assessed in 101 surgically resected colorectal adenocarcinomas. Associations with clinicopathological variables were examined, and OS was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards regression. Because of the limited number of deaths, TB and PDC were evaluated in separate multivariable models adjusted for age, pathological stage, and histologic grade. High TB was associated with poor differentiation (P = .006) and lymphovascular invasion (P = .008). High TB showed shorter OS than low/intermediate TB, but the difference was not statistically significant (log-rank P = .083; univariable hazard ratio [HR] = 1.958; 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.903-4.247; P = .089). High TB was not independently associated with OS after adjustment (adjusted HR = 1.528; 95% CI = 0.633-3.689; P = .346). Intermediate/high PDC was associated with poorer OS on Kaplan-Meier analysis (P = .017) and univariable Cox regression (HR = 2.424; 95% CI = 1.144-5.136; P = .021), but the association was attenuated after adjustment (adjusted HR = 1.661; 95% CI = 0.733-3.762; P = .224). TB and PDC were associated with adverse tumor characteristics. High TB showed a nonsignificant trend toward poorer OS, whereas intermediate/high PDC was associated with poorer OS in unadjusted analyses but not after multivariable adjustment. Their independent prognostic value for OS could not be demonstrated in this cohort.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Abdominal pain is one of the most common presenting complaints in emergency medicine. This case report summarizes a 61-year-old male with worsening abdominal pain and no bowel movement for multiple days. Computer tomography (CT) scan demonstrated a large intraluminal mass at the anastomosis, concerning for a bezoar formation, with associated stercoral colitis and partial bowel obstruction. The patient was subsequently admitted to the general surgery service for further management. During hospitalization, the patient's stool burden improved with osmotic laxatives, and he underwent a colonoscopy. The patient was discharged with outpatient follow-up. This report will help inform management in a patient with a history of colon cancer presenting with a large bowel obstruction post-colectomy. Colon cancer, bezoar formation, stercoral colitis, bowel obstruction.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Oral microrobots as drug carriers have shown great promise in enhancing the therapeutic efficacy of colorectal cancer (CRC). However, existing platforms frequently lack the programmable temporal precision required to execute complex, multistage dosing regimens. Here, we report a programmable temporal-responsive microrobot (PTRM) that autonomously navigates across the gastric acid barrier under external magnetic guidance to execute a sequential drug-release program at orthotopic tumor sites. The PTRM is engineered with a logic-gated architecture, featuring a spatially specific shell for gastric-resistant shielding and exclusive intestinal pH-triggered activation. The system's internal 'timer' is governed by the precise modulation of crosslinking densities within its dual gelatin cores, enabling finely-tuned biphasic release kinetics. Phase 1 executes the programmed release of elesclomol to induce tumor cell cuproptosis, successfully priming the tumor microenvironment by recruiting infiltrating immune cells. Following a precisely tuned 5.5 h interval, Phase 2 triggers the release of PD-1 inhibitors to activate these cells, thereby amplifying immunogenic cell death. This orchestrated sequential cytotoxicity achieved a 76% remission rate in an orthotopic CRC mouse model. Furthermore, the PTRM architecture is highly scalable, accommodating up to six-core configurations for multiphase release-establishing a versatile robotic platform for complex combinatorial therapeutic strategies against recalcitrant cancers.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cancer is cited by most employers as the leading condition driving rising health care benefit costs. This study examined the components of and trends in health care costs for patients with 3 advanced cancers, focusing on employer-sponsored insurance. We evaluated how the costs of various cancer care modalities changed between 2013 and 2022 during a period marked by the introduction of novel therapies alongside generic and biosimilar competition. Retrospective observational claims analysis. Using MarketScan Commercial Claims and Encounters data, we compared 12-month health services costs for patients newly diagnosed with metastatic colorectal cancer, metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), or multiple myeloma in 2013 vs 2022. Metastatic colorectal cancer costs decreased 15% (from $239,003 in 2013 to $203,499 in 2022), coinciding with generic competition for chemotherapy and biosimilar entry for supportive medications. Conversely, costs for metastatic NSCLC increased by 25% (from $220,662 to $276,883), and costs for multiple myeloma increased by 51% (from $216,337 to $327,495), both due to immunotherapy. Censoring rates were lower in 2022 for all 3 cancers, significantly so for metastatic NSCLC. Cancer costs for employers are not uniformly increasing, but instead, shifting based on market competition and therapeutic innovation. Where costs are rising, they are driven by novel therapies that offer a potential value trade-off, coinciding with survival improvements reported in the literature.

The following case presents the clinical course of a 54-year-old female patient who presented with abdominal pain. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Early diagnosis and screening reduce cancer mortality and are increasingly delivered not only by physicians and general practitioners but also by pharmacists. Existing studies on the pharmacist's role in cancer screening have largely focused on a single cancer type. This review comprehensively examines the extended role of pharmacists across multiple cancer types, along with the associated interventions, facilitators, and barriers. A systematic review was conducted to identify the roles of pharmacists in cancer screening by searching Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), Scopus, Web of Science (WOS), and the Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health (CINAHL) using relevant MeSH terms. Data were extracted on study characteristics, pharmacist role, screening interventions, outcomes, barriers and facilitators, and the acceptability, willingness, and perceptions of both patients and pharmacists. Of the 2862 studies identified, 43 met the inclusion criteria, spanning North America, Europe, Asia, the Middle East, and Oceania, with the largest number from the USA (n = 18), and sample sizes ranging from small feasibility studies (n < 50) to large population-based programs involving over a million invitations. Colorectal cancer (CRC) was the most commonly studied cancer type, most often through fecal immunochemical test (FIT) or fecal occult blood test (FOBT) distribution. Breast and cervical cancer studies primarily evaluated pharmacist-led education, awareness, and referral, particularly in underserved populations, while skin cancer studies addressed prevention and early detection through counseling, risk assessment, and mole-scanning services. Pharmacists contributed across the screening pathway, including direct test distribution and point-of-care testing, patient education and risk communication, and support for screening uptake, completion, and follow-up. This systematic review identifies a growing role for pharmacists across cancer screening, prevention, and early detection, with the most consistent evidence supporting pharmacist-led CRC screening; evidence for other cancer types and for downstream outcomes such as diagnostic follow-up remains more limited. Structural, organizational, and reimbursement-related barriers were commonly reported. Co-designed implementation frameworks, training programs, and integration with existing cancer care pathways are likely necessary to realize pharmacists' potential contribution to cancer screening and the broader cancer care continuum. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Deficient mismatch repair/high microsatellite instability (dMMR/MSI-H) colorectal cancer (CRC) represents a distinct molecular subgroup with therapeutic implications, particularly in the context of immunotherapy and emerging targeted treatments. NTRK rearrangements are enriched in dMMR colorectal adenocarcinoma compared to pMMR tumors, creating a critical opportunity for targeted therapy with TRK-inhibitors. Our study aimed to evaluate the frequency of pan-TRK expression in dMMR colorectal adenocarcinoma. We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study of 211 patients with histologically confirmed dMMR CRC who underwent surgical resection at two tertiary centers in Ho Chi Minh City between 2020 and 2024. Mismatch repair status was determined by immunohistochemistry (IHC) using MLH1, PMS2, MSH2, and MSH6 antibodies. Tissue microarrays were constructed, and pan-TRK expression was assessed using IHC (clone EPR17341). Among the 211 analyzed cases, we identified 15 tumors (7.1%) with positive pan-TRK expression, including 12 cases that exhibited membranous staining, whereas 3 cases demonstrated cytoplasmic pattern. We did not observe nuclear staining in any tumor. Most of positive tumors (93%) exhibited a diffuse staining pattern. We observed a higher frequency of pan-TRK expression in tumors exhibiting specific clinicopathological features, including proximal colon location, mucinous histology, high-grade morphology, and lymphovascular invasion. Additionally, most positive cases exhibited concurrent MLH1/PMS2 loss. However, these associations did not reach statistical significance. To our knowledge, this study represents the first comprehensive analysis of pan-TRK expression in Vietnamese patients with dMMR CRC. Our findings highlight its potential clinical relevance and provide a basis for future molecular studies, with possible implications for targeted therapeutic strategies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Synchronous distant metastasis is a major determinant of prognosis in colorectal adenocarcinoma, but its associations with routine histopathological parameters at individual metastatic sites remain incompletely understood. This retrospective study included 382 patients who underwent surgical resection for colorectal adenocarcinoma between 2006 and 2018. Clinicopathological parameters were evaluated in relation to synchronous distant metastasis overall and to liver, peritoneal, lung, and bone metastases using univariable analyses, exact tests where appropriate, and multivariable logistic regression. Synchronous distant metastasis was present in 83 patients (21.7%). In two separate multivariable models, lymph node metastasis, positive proximal/distal resection margin, low peritumoral lymphocytic infiltration, and perineural invasion were associated with higher odds of synchronous distant metastasis, whereas deficient mismatch repair (dMMR) status was associated with lower odds. Liver metastasis was associated with lymph node metastasis and positive proximal/distal resection margin, whereas dMMR status was associated with lower odds. In restricted exploratory models, tumor deposits and non-conventional histological subtype were associated with peritoneal metastasis, and tumor perforation was associated with lung metastasis. Bone metastasis was too infrequent for multivariable analysis. These organ-specific findings should be considered exploratory and require validation in larger independent cohorts.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Lymph node metastasis (LNM) is a key determinant of prognosis and treatment decisions in colon adenocarcinoma. Among histopathological features associated with tumor aggressiveness, extramural venous invasion (EMVI) has been increasingly recognized as an adverse factor; however, its independent role in predicting nodal metastasis remains incompletely defined. In this retrospective study, 180 consecutive patients who underwent primary surgical resection for colon adenocarcinoma, excluding rectal tumors, neoadjuvant-treated cases, and histological subtypes other than adenocarcinoma NOS, were evaluated. Histopathological parameters, including EMVI, intramural venous invasion, lympho-vascular invasion (LVI), perineural invasion (PNI), tumor budding, and tumor deposits, were systematically reviewed, and elastic staining was used in equivocal cases. Associations with LNM were analyzed using univariate and multivariate logistic regression. Lymph node metastasis was identified in 47.8% of patients, and EMVI was present in 21.7% and was significantly more frequent in patients with nodal metastasis. In multivariate analysis, LVI was the strongest independent predictor of LNM, followed by PNI, EMVI, and high tumor budding. The model demonstrated good calibration and an overall accuracy of 80%. Extramural venous invasion is an independent predictor of LNM and reflects a biologically aggressive tumor phenotype. Its routine assessment, together with other high-risk features, may improve risk stratification and support more informed clinical decision-making.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
In Denmark, since 2011-2012, a national cancer patient pathway (CPP) has been in place for patients presenting with non-specific signs or symptoms of and signs of cancer (NSSC). Many cancer patients initially do not display organ-specific alarm symptoms when examined by general practitioners (GPs). To characterize referral symptoms in patients undergoing contrast-enhanced CT chest-abdomen-pelvis (TAP) for non-specific signs of cancer or vague symptoms, in relation to radiological findings and final diagnoses. Second, the study assessed diagnostic accuracy of CT TAP for detecting malignancy in these patient groups. This retrospective cohort study included all patients referred by GPs to CT TAP at Aarhus University Hospital, Denmark through NSSC or vague cancer symptoms from May to August 2024. Referral symptoms and radiology reports were compared to final clinical diagnosis at the end of NSSC-CPP. The study included 725 patients. The most frequent referral symptoms were weight loss (51.3%), pain (45.0%), and fatigue (39.4%). CT TAP reports indicated that 20.6% of cases had findings suggestive of cancer, most commonly lung cancer. Overall, 9.2% received a malignant diagnosis, most commonly lymphoma or lung, pancreatic, and colorectal cancer, while 11.3% received a benign diagnosis. Cancer was rare in patients with vague symptoms. This study demonstrates that CT TAP is a valuable tool for diagnosing patients with non-specific signs or symptoms of cancer in general practice. These findings support the continued use of CT TAP within the cancer pathway as an important tool for identifying patients who need further investigation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a form of cancer that, while initially slow to develop, becomes aggressive and poses significant treatment challenges in its later stages, often resulting in a low survival rate. This progression is evident, with patients having an approximate 90% five-year survival rate at the localised stage CRC, which drops dramatically to 12.5% for those with distant metastases. Epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) plays a pivotal role in metastases, as it facilitates the spread of cancer cells to migrate from the primary site to secondary locations. Autophagy further supports this process by enhancing cell survival under stress. Both EMT and autophagy are tightly regulated by calcium signalling, which is essential for cancer cell migration, invasion, and survival under unfavourable conditions. Targeting specific calcium channels and signalling pathways can inhibit EMT and regulate autophagy, thereby reducing cancer metastasis. This review explores the intricate relationship between endolysosomal (EL) calcium signalling, EMT, and autophagy in CRC, highlighting potential therapeutic strategies and the significance of these findings for improving treatment outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Mast cells (MCs) are multifunctional immune cells with context-dependent functions in cancer. In colorectal cancer (CRC), their contribution remains debated, suggesting that distinct MC subsets may either support tumor progression or promote anti-tumor immunity. Using single-cell RNA sequencing in a mouse model of inflammation-driven CRC, we uncovered extensive MC plasticity during tumor progression. Transcriptomic profiling and pseudotime trajectory analysis revealed a transition from precursor-like MCs exclusively present in adjacent tissue to differentiated tumor-associated MC (TAMC) subsets. TAMCs displayed a distinct repertoire of proteases and pro-inflammatory cytokines, contributing to increased vascular permeability and recruitment of additional immune cells. Moreover, TAMCs exhibited upregulation of molecules with immunosuppressive potential and underwent a tumor microenvironment (TME)-driven metabolic reprogramming. Accordingly, antibody-mediated MC depletion reduced tumor burden. Notably, most of the transcriptional features identified in a murine CRC model were recapitulated in human CRC, supporting the translational relevance of this MC program. Our findings identify a tumor-adapted MC state that orchestrates immune evasion and tissue remodeling during CRC progression, supporting the notion that MC are reprogrammed toward an immune-suppressive and pro-tumorigenic phenotype.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Beyond classical prognostic factors, the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) have emerged in recent years as prognostic indicators in colorectal carcinoma (CRC). Objective is to determine the relationship between preoperative NLR values and clinicopathologic parameters, survival, and mismatch repair (MMR) status. Over 532 patients diagnosed with colon adenocarcinoma between 2019 and 2023, none of whom had received neoadjuvant therapy. NLR values were calculated from preoperative complete blood counts, using ROC analysis, a population-specific optimal cut-off for NLR was determined and patients were classified into low and high NLR groups. High NLR was found to be significant associated with advanced T stage, lymph-node metastasis, distant metastasis, lymphovascular invasion and perineural invasion. No significant association was identified between NLR and age, sex, tumor location/size or histologic grade. Both overall and disease-free survival were significantly shorter in high-NLR group. Analyses also showed that proportion of patients with high NLR was higher in the mismatch-repair-proficient (pMMR) group than in the mismatch-repair-deficient (dMMR) group. The effect of NLR on survival was significant in tumors with pMMR. With its large sample size, this study is among the investigations in CRC that delineate the relationship of NLR with clinicopathologic parameters and survival. Considering NLR together with clinicopathological parameters and survival data can provide a more accurate and holistic approach for accurate diagnoses and such a multifaceted approach can also support patient treatment plan.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Detection of colorectal cancer (CRC) significantly improves survival, yet current screening methods face challenges regarding invasiveness and patient compliance. Liquid biopsy has emerged as a promising non-invasive alternative. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of liquid biopsy-based molecular diagnostics for colorectal cancer. We searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library for studies evaluating the diagnostic accuracy of molecular liquid biopsy for CRC. Using a bivariate random-effects model, we estimated pooled sensitivity, specificity, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Meta-regression and subgroup analyses were performed to identify key drivers of performance, focusing on diagnostic platforms, biomarker types, and specimen sources. A total of 43 studies were included in the final analysis. The pooled sensitivity and specificity for liquid biopsy techniques (qPCR, ddPCR, and NGS) were 75% (95% CI, 0.70-0.79) and 91% (95% CI, 0.89-0.92), respectively. The SROC analysis revealed an AUC of 0.9121 (95% CI, 0.864-0.904). In subgroup analyses, NGS demonstrated a higher diagnostic odds ratio of 80.51 (95% CI, 26.13-248.08) and an AUC of 0.937. Furthermore, mutation-based biomarkers showed a diagnostic odds ratio of 45.78 (95% CI, 17.79-117.8) with an AUC of 0.944, while plasma samples had a diagnostic odds ratio of 32.19 (95% CI, 21.02-49.29) and an AUC of 0.912, indicating relatively higher diagnostic accuracy. Subgroup observations suggest that plasma-based mutation analysis using NGS exhibits promising diagnostic accuracy for CRC. Overall, these findings indicate that molecular liquid biopsy may serve as a potential non-invasive adjunct to complement traditional screening strategies, though further validation is required to confirm its clinical utility. Not applicable.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Systematically evaluate the performance and methodological quality of predictive models for the risk of anastomotic stricture after rectal cancer surgery to provide evidence-based guidance for clinical practice. We comprehensively searched nine Chinese and English databases (CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, Sinomed, PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CINAHL, and Embase) for relevant studies published until June 7, 2025. Two independent researchers screened the literature, extracted data, and assessed methodological quality using the Prediction Model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool (PROBAST). Nine eligible studies were included, demonstrating AUC values ranging from 0.739 to 0.911 in derivation cohorts. Internal validation results were reported in three studies (AUC: 0.905-0.930), while two studies provided test-set validation (AUC:0.818-0.888). The most significant predictors included anastomotic leakage, the use of a protective stoma, and the anastomotic distance. All studies exhibited high risk of bias according to PROBAST criteria, primarily due to retrospective designs, inappropriate handling of continuous variables (dichotomization), inadequate sample sizes, improper management of missing data, univariate-based predictor selection, and insufficient model validation. However, two studies demonstrated good clinical applicability. Research on predictive models for anastomotic stricture after rectal cancer surgery is still in its early stages, constrained by methodological flaws and a lack of external validation that limit their clinical applicability. Future studies should prioritize external validation across diverse populations to confirm their generalizability.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Restorative proctocolectomy with a hand-sewn ileal pouch-anal anastomosis (IPAA) is a standard treatment for ulcerative colitis and familial adenomatous polyposis. However, achieving sufficient mesenteric length remains a significant challenge. This study aimed to validate the pouch extension distance (PED), a CT-based predictor for difficult ileal pouch extension specifically in planned hand-sewn IPAA. This refined retrospective cohort study was conducted at a single specialized academic institution. Fifty-seven consecutive patients undergoing total colectomy with a planned hand-sewn IPAA between 2008 and 2025 were included. The PED was measured on preoperative axial CT scans as the slice-to-slice distance from the junction of the ileocolic and marginal arteries to the anal verge. "Difficult pouch extension" (ED group) was defined as requiring the division of three or more mesenteric vessels or ligation of the ileocolic artery to achieve adequate reach. Clinical and anatomical factors were compared between the ED and normal groups. Seven patients (12.3%) were classified into the ED group. Difficult extension was significantly associated with higher body weight, higher BMI, higher serum albumin levels, familial adenomatous polyposis, and a longer PED. ROC analysis demonstrated that the PED possessed the highest predictive power (AUC 0.937). The optimal cut-off value for the PED was determined to be 21 cm. Preoperative PED measurement is a simple and highly accurate predictor of difficulty in achieving a tension-free hand-sewn IPAA. A PED of 21 cm or greater allows surgeons to optimize the surgical approach and prepare for advanced mesenteric lengthening maneuvers.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Mucinous adenocarcinoma (MAC) exhibits aggressive clinicopathological features, yet its prognostic significance in stage II colon cancer remains controversial, and current guidelines do not regard mucinous histology as a high-risk feature (HRF). We compared mucinous and non-mucinous (NMAC) stage II colon adenocarcinomas with respect to clinicopathological characteristics and cumulative HRF burden. In this retrospective single-center cohort, patients who underwent curative resection for stage II colon cancer between January 2023 and October 2025 were included. MAC was defined as greater than 50% extracellular mucin. Clinicopathological variables, cumulative HRFs, and postoperative outcomes were compared. DFS was evaluated exploratorily using Kaplan-Meier estimation and the log-rank test. Of 47 patients, 32 (68.1%) had NMAC and 15 (31.9%) had MAC. MAC tumors tended to be larger than 6 cm (47% vs. 16%, p = 0.073) and MSI-positive (27% vs. 13%, p = 0.20), whereas grade 3 histology was more common in NMAC (44% vs. 20%; overall grade distribution, p = 0.12). The distribution of pT3, pT4a, and pT4b disease was similar between groups (p = 0.875), and postoperative outcomes did not differ significantly. Among 45 patients with evaluable DFS data, five DFS events occurred, including four in the NMAC group and one in the MAC group. Estimated 24-month DFS was 87.2% for NMAC and 90.0% for MAC, with no statistically significant between-group difference (log-rank p = 0.423). In this small retrospective cohort, MAC and NMAC showed heterogeneous clinicopathological patterns, and no statistically detectable difference in DFS was identified. These findings are exploratory and do not establish mucinous histology as either an adverse or favorable prognostic factor in stage II colon cancer. Validation in larger cohorts with longer follow-up is required.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a major public health concern worldwide, and participation in screening programs remains inadequate in many rural and underserved populations. This study assessed the effectiveness of a culturally tailored educational intervention based on the PEN-3 model in improving uptake of the fecal immunochemical test (FIT) among adults in rural Iran. A community-based quasi-experimental pre-post study was conducted in Daran, Isfahan Province, Iran, in 2022. A total of 388 adults aged 50-70 years were recruited using stratified random sampling from two comprehensive health centers. The intervention was developed according to the PEN-3 model and addressed individual perceptions, family support, and community-level enabling factors. Data were collected before and three months after the intervention using a validated 51-item questionnaire assessing knowledge, perceived susceptibility, perceived severity, perceived barriers, response efficacy, and self-efficacy. Paired t-tests and chi-square tests were used for statistical analysis. Among the 365 participants who completed the study, 134 individuals (36.7%) underwent FIT screening within three months after the intervention. Significant improvements were observed in knowledge, perceived susceptibility, and self-efficacy (all p < 0.001). Women demonstrated higher screening uptake than men (46.1% vs. 27.8%, p < 0.05), and FIT participation was inversely associated with educational level. The findings suggest that FIT uptake and several PEN-3-related psychosocial constructs improved following implementation of the educational intervention. However, the absence of a control group limits causal inference. Further controlled studies are needed to confirm the effectiveness and long-term impact of culturally tailored educational interventions for colorectal cancer screening.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Recent studies have suggested that laparoscopic surgery for rectal cancer yields postoperative complications and long-term survival rates comparable to those of open surgery. Nevertheless, whether sphincter-preserving rates are equivalent between laparoscopic and open approaches remains a topic of debate. This retrospective study included patients with mid- and low-rectal cancer who underwent open or laparoscopic surgery at Fudan University Shanghai Cancer Center (2006-2021). Propensity score matching (PSM) was used to balance baseline characteristics. Sphincter-preserving rates and short- and long-term outcomes were compared. Data from 9405 rectal cancer patients were collected. After propensity score adjustment, 7738 patients (4993 open and 2745 laparoscopic) with mid- and low- rectal cancer were included. The sphincter-preserving rates were 60.7% in the open surgery group and 72.3% in the laparoscopic surgery group, corresponding to an odds ratio (OR) of 1.70 (95% CI 1.53-1.88, P < 0.001) in the PSM cohort. Subgroup analyses showed that higher sphincter-preserving rates were associated with laparoscopic surgery across different tumor positions. In a sensitivity analysis using multivariable logistic regression in the full unmatched cohort, the adjusted OR was 3.11 (95% CI 2.69-3.59) for laparoscopic versus open surgery. Regarding long-term outcomes, the laparoscopic group had 5- year overall and disease-free survival rates of 77.0% and 76.6% respectively, which were comparable to those of 75.2% and 74.5% for the open surgery group (P = 0.09 and P = 0.20). For mid- and low-rectal cancer, laparoscopic surgery was associated with higher sphincter-preserving rates than open surgery after PSM, with comparable long-term prognoses.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The molecular mechanisms underlying lung metastasis of colorectal cancer (CRC) remain largely elusive, and effective therapeutic agents are still lacking. In this study, we identify levistilide A (LeA) as a potential anti-metastatic agent against CRC lung metastasis. We demonstrate that heat shock protein 90α (HSP90α) is markedly upregulated in CRC and promotes lung metastasis by suppressing ferroptosis. Notably, combined treatment with LeA and the ferroptosis inducer RSL3 further alleviates lung metastatic burden in vivo. Mechanistically, we reveal that the E3 ubiquitin ligase ring finger protein 40 (RNF40) suppresses CRC cell proliferation by directly interacting with HSP90α, inducing ubiquitination at lysine 407 and promoting its proteasomal degradation. RNF40-mediated HSP90α downregulation leads to the accumulation of malondialdehyde (MDA) and reactive oxygen species (ROS), thereby inhibiting CRC cell growth. Collectively, our findings provide mechanistic insights into how LeA directly targets HSP90α or facilitates RNF40-HSP90α-mediated degradation of HSP90α to regulate ferroptosis in CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Chemotherapy for colorectal cancer (CRC) is frequently compromised by insufficient tumor selectivity and severe off-target gastrointestinal toxicity. Addressing these limitations, we have engineered a pH-responsive core-shell nanocarrier based on chitosan (CS)-functionalized mesoporous organosilica materials (CS-MOMs). This core-shell nanoplatform utilize a CS coating as a pH-sensitive gatekeeper enabling rapid doxorubicin (DOX) release within the acidic tumor microenvironment and lysosomal compartment (pH 5.4) while preserving structural integrity to prevent premature leakage under physiological conditions (pH 7.2). In colorectal cancer cells, DOX@CS-MOMs exert superior antiproliferative activity to free DOX through acid-triggered intracellular reactive oxygen species accumulation, shifting the Bcl-2/Bax balance toward apoptosis, and activating the Caspase-3 cascade. Crucially, via in vitro intestinal epithelium model, the nanocarrier preserve barrier integrity-maintaining trans-epithelial electrical resistance and tight junction protein expression (ZO-1 and Occludin), and the mucus layer-while mitigating oxidative stress. Confirmed by excellent biocompatibility in vivo, this work establishes a novel nanotherapeutic strategy that combines antitumor effects with active protection of the intestinal mucosa, offering a promising approach to enhance the precision and safety of CRC treatment.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The free triiodothyronine (fT3)/free thyroxine (fT4) ratio is an index estimating the peripheral activity of thyroid hormones. The prognostic role of the fT3/fT4 ratio in colorectal cancer, urothelial cancer, renal carcinoma, and lymphoma is well-recognized, but its effect in metastatic breast cancer remains unestablished. We conducted a retrospective study of metastatic breast cancer patients treated with cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) 4/6 inhibitors at Hacettepe University Hospital. Baseline fT3 and fT4 levels were recorded, and patients were categorized into two groups based on the median fT3/fT4 ratio: Low and High fT3/fT4 Ratio Groups. We included 162 h-positive/HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer patients. There were no significant differences between the Low and High fT3/fT4 Ratio Groups in terms of age, sex, tumor grade, histopathologic type, menopausal status, sites of metastases, lines of treatment prior to CDK4/6 inhibitors, type of CDK4/6 inhibitor, or endocrine backbone therapy. Of all patients, 47 (29.2%) received two or more lines of treatment before initiating CDK4/6 inhibitors. High fT3/fT4 ratios were associated with significantly longer progression-free survival (PFS) compared to Low fT3/fT4 ratios (median, 9.7 vs. 6.9 months; HR: 0.68; 95% CI: 0.47-0.97; p = 0.035) and significantly longer overall survival (OS) compared to Low fT3/fT4 ratios (median, NR vs. NR months; HR: 0.30; 95% CI: 0.15-0.60; p < 0.001). Our study showed that high fT3/fT4 ratios were independent factors associated with longer PFS and OS in metastatic breast cancer patients treated with CDK4/6 inhibitors, supporting the role of high fT3/fT4 ratios as a prognostic marker.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The rising incidence and poor prognosis of early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC) highlight an urgent need for effective diagnostic biomarkers. This study integrates RNA sequencing data with machine learning algorithms to identify EOCRC-specific genes and construct a diagnostic model to improve molecular diagnosis and explore the functional role of key genes. We analyzed RNA sequencing data from EOCRC patients (age ≤ 50) obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database. The differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between EOCRC and normal tissues were identified and subjected to construct a diagnostic model through random forest analysis and artificial neural network modeling. The diagnostic performance of the model was evaluated in a training set and validated in an independent set. CIBERSORT was utilized to investigate the immune cell infiltration patterns. The expression levels of key DEGs were further verified in 15 paired clinical tissues. Moreover, RT-qPCR and western blotting were applied to detect the expression of solute carrier member 26 family 2 (SLC26A2), which is one of the top-ranked genes, in CRC cell lines. The functional role of SLC26A2 was investigated in EOCRC cell lines (SW480 and HT29) through lentivector-mediated ectopic overexpression experiments assessing proliferation, migration and invasion. The association between SLC26A2 and the cytotoxicity of vanadium-containing compounds (BMOV, VO(acac)₂) was explored, focusing on redox modulation (ROS/GSH levels) using inhibitors (BSO) and antioxidants (NAC). We identified 22 DEGs between EOCRC tumor and normal tissues. A machine learning-based diagnostic model based on seven DEGs (SLC26A2, FCGBP, SLC7A5, CA2, STC2, SLC4A4 and THBS2) for EOCRC was constructed. The model achieved an AUC of 0.987 (training) and 0.874 (validation). Immune profiling revealed altered infiltration of monocytes, M0 macrophages, and γδ T cells in EOCRC. Experimental validation confirmed the dysregulation of the seven key genes. SLC26A2 was downregulated in EOCRC tissues and its overexpression significantly inhibited cell proliferation, migration, and invasion in vitro. Transcriptomic analysis linked SLC26A2 overexpression to glutathione (GSH) metabolism. EOCRC cells exhibited sensitivity to vanadium compounds, which was enhanced by SLC26A2 overexpression. SLC26A2 expression correlated with compound-induced cytotoxicity alongside modulation of ROS/GSH levels, as evidenced by the synergistic effect of BSO (GSH inhibitor) and the attenuating effect of NAC (antioxidant). We developed and validated a robust machine learning-based diagnostic model for EOCRC using a 7-gene signature. The downregulated gene SLC26A2 acts as a tumor suppressor in EOCRC and is associated with cellular sensitivity to vanadium-containing compounds, potentially through a redox-dependent mechanism linked to GSH metabolism. These findings provide novel insights into the identification of diagnostic biomarkers and highlight the therapeutic potential for EOCRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The rising incidence of colorectal cancer (CRC) and cardiovascular diseases, driven by aging populations and lifestyle changes, highlights congestive heart failure (CHF) as a critical comorbidity that significantly affects survival and treatment decisions in CRC patients. CHF not only affects survival outcomes but also complicates clinical decision-making. This study aims to investigate the impact of CHF on mortality among CRC survivors and explore potential factors of mortality. This cohort study analyzed data from the Taiwan Cancer Registry and National Health Insurance Research Database. CRC patients aged 20 years or older (ICD-10-CM: C18-C20) who survived at least five years after diagnosis were included. After a 1:4 exact matching based on age, sex, and clinical stage, Cox regression was used to estimate mortality risk between CRC survivors with and without CHF. A total of 535 CRC survivors with CHF and 2140 without CHF were enrolled in this study after matching. CRC survivors with CHF had a significantly higher overall mortality rate than those without CHF (36.64% vs. 15.23%, p < 0.001). After adjusting for potential confounders, CRC survivors with CHF had 1.93-folds risk of mortality (95% CI: 1.54-2.41, p < 0.001) compared to those without CHF. Subgroup analyses by sex, age, clinical stage, Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI), and treatment types also show that CRC survivors with CHF had significantly higher mortality risk than those without CHF. The top three highest mortality risk ratios were observed in subgroups with a CCI score of 0 (AHR: 2.63, 95% CI: 1.08-6.39), age < 65 years (AHR: 1.87, 95% CI: 1.23-5.57), and advanced clinical stage (AHR: 2.03, 95% CI: 1.51-2.72). CRC survivors with CHF demonstrated significantly higher overall mortality compared to those without CHF. This finding presented the prognostic impact of CHF in CRC survivors, so integrated care and early cardiovascular monitoring are essential to improve long-term outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) has been linked to specific members of the gut microbiota, including adherent-invasive Escherichia coli (AIEC), yet the strain-level features that underpin pathogenicity and clinical relevance remain incompletely defined. Here, we isolated E. coli directly from tumour and adjacent healthy colorectal biopsies of six CRC patients and performed whole-genome sequencing and functional phenotyping. Eight genetically distinct E. coli strains were identified, spanning phylogroups A and B2 and multiple pandemic sequence types, revealing substantial intra- and inter-patient heterogeneity. Only a subset of isolates displayed AIEC-like adhesion and invasion phenotypes. One isolate with increased recovery from tumour tissue exhibited pronounced cytotoxicity and harboured strain-specific oncogenic risk factors, including the pks colibactin genomic island and a high-virulence allele of the type 1 pilus adhesin FimH. In-depth analysis of fimH revealed intra-patient allelic variation, indicating that single representative isolates may not fully capture virulence potential within individual hosts. More broadly, comparative genomic analyses showed that chaperone-usher pilus repertoires and previously proposed AIEC and CRC biomarkers (chuA, eefC, fitA) were primarily associated with phylogroup rather than tumour-tropic colonisation. Together, these findings demonstrate that CRC-associated E. coli constitute a diverse population lacking uniform genetic signatures. Our results highlight the importance of strain-resolved genomic and functional profiling to better understand bacterial contributions to colorectal cancer.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To derive and externally validate a four-parameter blood-based TDCP (total bilirubin, direct bilirubin, creatinine, platelets) index that quantifies long-term oncological risk after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (CRT) and total mesorectal excision (TME) for locally advanced rectal cancer, with explicit emphasis on patients whose pre-CRT CEA and CA19-9 levels remain within the normal range. Among 577 patients with clinical stage II/III rectal cancer who completed long-course neoadjuvant CRT and curative TME, this retrospective analysis nested within the LASRE multicentre trial (22 Chinese centres, 2013-2018) derived and froze the TDCP cut-off in the derivation cohort (Fujian Union Hospital, n = 237) before prognostic evaluation in the geographically independent validation cohort (21 centres, n = 340). High TDCP (n = 114) predicted poorer 3-year DFS (derivation HR 3.093, 95% CI 1.691-5.659; validation HR 1.670, 95% CI 1.038-2.687) and doubled early-recurrence rates (42.9% vs 19.6% and 30.2% vs 18.5%). Within the biomarker-silent subgroup (343 [59.5%] with normal pre-CRT CEA and CA19-9), high TDCP remained associated with shorter DFS (derivation HR 3.310, 95% CI 1.542-7.105; validation HR 2.386, 95% CI 1.159-4.914). Multivariate Cox regression in the derivation cohort confirmed that TDCP-high was an independent predictor of shorter DFS, with prognostic weight equivalent to pathological stage II disease. Bootstrap optimism correction (HR 1.81) and head-to-head comparison against established inflammation-based indices (NLR, PLR, SII, PNI) confirmed the robustness and superior transportability of the prognostic signal, with consistent effect direction in both men and women. The TDCP index is an externally validated prognostic biomarker that stratifies long-term recurrence risk after neoadjuvant CRT/TME specifically in patients with normal pre-CRT CEA and CA19-9, independent of sex and pathological stage. While its prognostic association is robust across geographically distinct cohorts, prospective interventional trials are required to establish clinical utility. Parent trial: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01899547.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) develops over 10-15 years from normal mucosa to advanced adenoma (AA) and invasive carcinoma; however, noninvasive biomarkers capable of detecting premalignant lesions and predicting the patient prognosis are still urgently needed. Circulating small extracellular vesicles (sEVs, exosomes) are nanoscale lipid bilayer carriers that are stably enriched in body fluids and serve as ideal liquid biopsy substrates for tumor molecular profiling. Nevertheless, most existing exosomal biomarker studies adopt binary case‒control designs, lack sequential adenoma‒carcinoma cohorts, and rarely combine exosomal proteomics with single-cell transcriptomics to trace the cellular origins of the biomarkers or construct paired diagnostic‒prognostic models. We integrated EXODUS rapid sEV isolation technology with 4D-DIA quantitative proteomics to profile serum exosomal proteomes across four sequential cohorts: healthy controls (NCs), patients with AA, patients with early CRC (ECRC), and patients with advanced CRC. Time series clustering and cross-cohort differential screening identified annexin A7 (ANXA7) as a continuously upregulated exosomal protein that accompanies malignant transformation in CRC. Western blotting and commercial ELISA verified the progressive increase in circulating sEV-ANXA7 levels, while tissue immunohistochemistry further confirmed the increase in ANXA7 expression from normal epithelium to adenoma and carcinoma epithelium. A single ROC curve analysis demonstrated that serum sEV-ANXA levels achieved an AUC of 0.821 for distinguishing healthy individuals from those with high-risk advanced adenomas. The combination of sEV-ANXA7 levels with the levels of the traditional markers CEA and CA199 significantly improved the diagnostic accuracy for both premalignant and early CRC lesions. Single-cell transcriptomic mining of public CRC datasets revealed a unique ANXA7⁺ epithelial progenitor cell (EPC) subpopulation, a distinct epithelial subset containing precancerous abnormal epithelial cells and early malignant epithelial cells with elevated malignant transformation potential, which was highly enriched in tumor tissues, which featured elevated stemness signatures, increased malignant scores, and the activation of ferroptosis and the P53 signaling pathway. The results of the CellChat analysis further revealed that ANXA7⁺ EPCs mediate tumor immune escape via CD8A-CEACAM5 ligand-receptor crosstalk with T cells. In vitro CCK-8 and EdU functional assays confirmed that ANXA7 markedly accelerated the proliferation of HCT116 and SW480 CRC cells. Based on the overlapping upregulated genes from ANXA7-high bulk tumors and ANXA7⁺ EPC subsets, we established a 12-gene LASSO prognostic signature, which exhibited robust performance in predicting 1-5-year survival (AUC > 0.68) of patients in both TCGA training cohort and the independent GEO validation cohort. Collectively, the results of this multiomics study reveal serum exosomal ANXA7 as a dual-function nanovesicle biomarker for early adenoma screening and the prognostic risk stratification of CRC and reveal the oncogenic ANXA7⁺ epithelial progenitor cell population that drives malignant colorectal progression. Our work provides translational evidence and theoretical basis for the development of exosome-based noninvasive liquid biopsy strategies and targeted therapeutic interventions against CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the most common and life-threatening malignancies worldwide. Despite extensive research, the precise molecular mechanisms underlying CRC progression remain incompletely understood. Accumulating evidence indicates that complex interactions among oncogenic signaling pathways, non-coding RNAs, and the gut microbiota play a pivotal role in CRC pathogenesis. Among oral microbiota, Porphyromonas gingivalis (P. gingivalis) has been implicated in tumorigenesis through the induction of chronic inflammation and activation of oncogenic pathways. This study aimed to investigate the expression levels of the lncRNA CCAT2 and the c-MYC, as well as to evaluate the relative abundance of P. gingivalis and Bifidobacterium bifidum (B. bifidum) in colorectal cancer tissues compared with adjacent normal tissues. DNA and RNA were extracted from biopsy specimens obtained from 40 patients with CRC and 25 healthy controls. Complementary DNA (cDNA) was synthesized using commercial kits, and quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) was conducted to measure the expression levels of CCAT2 and c-MYC, as well as the relative abundance of the 16S rRNA genes of P. gingivalis and B. bifidum. Expression levels of lncRNA CCAT2 and c-MYC were significantly higher in CRC tissues than in normal samples (p < 0.05). Likewise, the relative abundance of P. gingivalis was significantly increased, whereas B. bifidum abundance was significantly decreased in CRC tissues (p < 0.05). In the combined study population (CRC and healthy controls), Spearman's rank correlation analysis demonstrated significant positive correlations between P. gingivalis abundance and both CCAT2 and c-MYC expression, as well as a significant inverse correlation between B. bifidum abundance and CCAT2 expression. However, in the CRC subgroup, only the positive correlation between P. gingivalis abundance and c-MYC expression remained statistically significant. These findings demonstrate significant associations between P. gingivalis colonization, B. bifidum depletion, and oncogenic molecular alterations in CRC. Although associations involving CCAT2 were evident in the combined cohort, only the relationship between P. gingivalis abundance and c-MYC expression persisted within the CRC subgroup, suggesting that some observed correlations may primarily reflect differences between CRC patients and healthy controls. Owing to the cross-sectional design, causal inferences cannot be drawn. Further mechanistic and longitudinal studies are warranted to validate these findings and to explore the clinical utility of microbiota-based biomarkers and therapeutic strategies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Given the highly aggressive nature of gastrointestinal cancers, the identification of novel biomarkers for diagnosis and prognosis is of considerable clinical importance. Candidate cancer-testis (CT) antigens were first screened using RNA-sequencing data from normal human tissues; candidates showing high commonality across tumor RNA-sequencing datasets publicly available in The Cancer Genome Atlas were subsequently prioritized, and POTEE was identified as a promising target. Recombinant POTEE protein was expressed in Escherichia coli, purified by affinity chromatography, and used as the antigen for serological analysis. Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis showed that the diagnostic performance of s-POTEE-Ab was comparable to that of s-p53-Ab, with area under the curve values of 0.832 versus 0.829 in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, 0.680 versus 0.698 in gastric adenocarcinoma, and 0.735 versus 0.706 in colorectal adenocarcinoma, respectively. In survival analyses, s-POTEE-Ab positivity was associated with poorer overall survival in ESCC and CRAC, but not in GAC. After multivariable adjustment, an independent prognostic association was retained only in CRAC. These findings suggest that s-POTEE-Ab may represent a promising exploratory serological biomarker for gastrointestinal cancers. Its prognostic relevance appears to be cancer-type dependent and requires further validation in independent cohorts.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) screening programs reduce incidence and mortality, but their success depends not only on clinical effectiveness but also on participants' experience and satisfaction. Understanding these dimensions is crucial, as poor satisfaction or limited involvement in shared decision-making (SDM) can undermine uptake and adherence. This study evaluated SDM and satisfaction among participants with a positive fecal immunochemical test (FIT) in an organized CRC screening program in Catalonia. A multicenter cross-sectional study was conducted from November 2020 to December 2021 across three hospitals. Participants aged 50-69 with a positive FIT result were surveyed after colonoscopy and diagnosis. SDM was measured using CollaboRATE and SDM-Q-9; satisfaction was assessed using Hatoum's and Colonoscopy Safety and Satisfaction Questionnaire questionnaires and custom tools. Multivariate analyses identified factors associated with SDM and satisfaction. Of 846 invited, 824 were included and 694 completed questionnaires (84.2% response rate). Overall, 39.8% achieved the CollaboRATE top score. Higher SDM was linked to shorter wait times, use of Moviprep®,a bowel preparation solution, and absence of complications. Among CRC-diagnosed patients, women and those with a personal cancer history reported higher SDM. Overall satisfaction was high (mean 9.4/10), though bowel preparation scored lowest. Satisfaction varied by hospital, preparation type, and patient characteristics, but not by final diagnosis. Participants reported high satisfaction but moderate SDM, revealing room for improvement. Factors such as preparation type, waiting time, and communication quality shaped patient experience. Differences across centers suggest organizational factors matter. Strengthening communication, reducing delays, and addressing patient diversity are essential to enhance satisfaction and engagement, key drivers of CRC screening program effectiveness.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Left hemicolectomy is the standard surgical procedure for the treatment of left-sided colon cancer. laparoscopy-assisted left hemicolectomy (LALH) combined with extracorporeal anastomosis (EA) is currently the preferred approach. However, performing total laparoscopic left hemicolectomy (TLLH) with intracorporeal anastomosis (IA) is technically challenging. This retrospective cohort study collected data from 178 patients diagnosed with left-sided colon cancer who underwent either totally laparoscopic left hemicolectomy utilizing self-pulling and latter transection(SPLT-TLLH) or LALH surgery at the First Affiliated Hospital of Chongqing Medical University between July 1, 2022, and June 30, 2025. Using propensity score matching, we compared and analyzed the perioperative parameters and short-term clinical outcomes between the two patient groups. In total, 178 patients with left-sided colon cancer who underwent SPLT-TLLH (n = 45) or LALH (n = 133) were enrolled. The results indicated that the operative time was significantly shorter in the SPLT-TLLH group than that in the LALH group. Additionally, the SPLT-TLLH group demonstrated lower intraoperative blood loss, a greater distal resection margin, a smaller incision size (P < 0.001),and a faster recovery of intestinal function (P < 0.05) compared to the LALH group. Applying SPLT reconstruction technique to TLLH surgery helped achieve favorable short-term therapeutic outcomes. SPLT-TLLH appears feasible and safe with promising short-term outcomes in this single-center retrospective cohort and helps simplify gastrointestinal reconstruction.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
In clinical practice, approximately 15-25% of patients with locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) achieve a pathological complete response (pCR), defined as tumor regression grade 0 according to the AJCC 8th edition, which is closely associated with favorable prognosis. However, noninvasive and accurate preoperative assessment methods remain a major clinical challenge. We aimed to develop an automated artificial intelligence (AI) system for predicting the response to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy and prognosis in LARC using pre-treatment T2WI. This multicenter retrospective study included 227 LARC patients from Center 1 as the development cohort and 72 and 55 patients from two separate centers as external validation cohorts 1 and 2, respectively. 3D Swin-UNETR was constructed to automatically identify LARC tumors. Based on the segmented tumor volumes, three analytical approaches were implemented to support downstream tasks. Specifically, 1,132 radiomic features (Rf) were extracted using PyRadiomics, while 2,048 deep learning features (Dlf) were derived by 3D ResNet-152 architecture. Following a series of feature selection steps, predictive response scores were generated, including RF scores (Rfs) and Dlf scores (Dlfs). Additionally, an end-to-end analysis was performed to automatically generate Dl scores (Dls). A multi-perspective feature engineering model was then developed by integrating Rfs, Dlfs, and Dls. The predictive performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curves (AUROCs). Prognostic indices, including disease-free survival (DFS) and overall survival (OS), were assessed using Kaplan-Meier (KM) analysis, with the Log-Rank test used to compare KM curves. The fusion model achieved moderate AUROCs of 0.756 and 0.751 in external validation cohorts 1 and 2, respectively. It effectively stratified OS risk, with p-values < 0.05 across all cohorts. For DFS, statistical significance was inconsistent across cohorts, being achieved in the development cohort (p = 0.0084) and external cohort 2 (p = 0.044), but not in external cohort 1 (p = 0.068). These findings are exploratory and require prospective confirmation. The proposed AI system demonstrates moderate, externally validated performance for assessing treatment response and OS risk stratification in LARC and may serve as a decision-support tool to assist clinical judgment.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Oral antibiotic bowel prophylaxis (OAP) is used to reduce infectious complications in colorectal surgery, but its effects on perioperative gut microbiota composition remain unclear. This systematic review evaluated the impact of OAP on intestinal microbiota composition in adults undergoing colorectal surgery. A systematic search of PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar was conducted up to November 18th, 2025, following PRISMA guidelines. Studies were eligible if they included adult colorectal surgery patients receiving OAP and reported microbiota composition using 16S rRNA sequencing and/or qPCR. Primary outcomes were changes in microbial diversity and taxonomic composition. Secondary outcomes were surgical site infection (SSI) and anastomotic leakage (AL). Eleven studies involving over 1500 microbiota samples met inclusion criteria. OAP regimens varied widely in agents, duration, and combination with mechanical bowel preparation (MBP) or probiotics. Across studies, OAP consistently reduced microbial diversity and altered taxonomic composition, some shifts, such as increased Enterococcus or decreased Bacteroides, persisted postoperatively. Only a minority of studies assessed microbiota recovery beyond the early postoperative phase. Clinical outcomes such as SSI and anastomotic leakage were inconsistently reported, with limited direct correlations to microbiota data. OAP substantially alters perioperative gut microbiota composition in colorectal surgery patients. Heterogeneity in sampling, analysis, and clinical correlation limits definitive conclusions. Standardized study designs are needed to clarify the relationship between OAP and microbiota composition changes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The inferior mesenteric artery (IMA) is a crucial artery that supplies the colon and rectum. As colorectal cancer is most commonly localized in the descending and sigmoid colon, as well as in the rectum, detailed knowledge of the anatomy of the IMA is of utmost importance for oncological surgeons performing hemicolectomies. An extensive search of major databases was performed up to April 2026 for studies detailing the morphometry, anatomy, and variations of the IMA. The study strictly adhered to the PRISMA guidelines. Out of 143,884 initial records, 66 original studies met the inclusion criteria. A random effects model was applied in the statistical analyses, and heterogeneity was evaluated using Chi-squared and I-squared statistics. The IMA most often originated at the L3 vertebral level (60.35%). The number of sigmoid arteries varied across the study groups, with 2 sigmoid arteries variant being the most common variant at 38.42%, followed by 3 sigmoid arteries variant at 31.30%. Across IMA branching pattern classification systems, the most prevalent anatomical variations were Type 1 in the modified Yada scale (47.39%), Type 1 in Latarjet scale (47.39%), Type 1B in McSweeney scale (45.51%), and Type B in modified Zebrowski scale (20.35%). To standardize complex branching patterns, we propose supplementing the modified Yada scale with the exact number of sigmoid arteries for clinical practice, while recommending the McSweeney scale for prospective research. Surgeons must account for significant anatomical variability, as IMA originates at the L3 level in only 60.42% of cases, and the number of sigmoid arteries varies widely, most commonly presenting as two or three. Ultimately, accurate preoperative visualization and standardized IMA categorization are crucial for optimal surgical outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cell death represents a critical process in the maintenance of cellular homeostasis. Paraptosis, a mechanism of programmed cell death, is distinguished by extensive cytoplasmic vacuolization. We have identified two commercially available compounds, IKK16 and SGI1027, which can induce cytoplasmic vacuolization leading to paraptosis in cancer cells. We have characterized and studied various cancer cell lines by applying molecular biology, proteomics, gene expression analyses, and microscopy-based techniques. Additionally, our gene expression analyses indicate that GADD45A, and NPC2 genes may serve as potential markers for identifying paraptosis, and validated their involvement in IKK16/SGI1027-mediated paraptosis with a cellular functional assay. Furthermore, the proteomics data revealed a novel set of proteins previously unassociated with paraptosis. We have substantiated our proteomics findings through western blotting and immunocytochemistry in breast and colorectal cancer cell lines, demonstrating similar effects. Moreover, we have shown that combining paraptosis-inducing compounds with anti-cancer drugs can reduce the required overall dosage concentration while preserving therapeutic efficacy, potentially revolutionizing cancer treatment.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The majority of patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) fail to respond to anti-PD-1/PD-L1 immunotherapy, highlighting an urgent need for alternative immunotherapeutic targets. The immunosuppressive ligand CD155 potently dampens natural killer (NK) cell cytotoxicity via inhibitory receptors, but how CRC cells sustain high CD155 surface levels remains elusive. Here, we identify aberrant CD155 N-glycosylation as a critical driver of CRC immune evasion. We find that the glycosyltransferase STT3A contributes to N-glycosylation of CD155. This modification is essential for maintaining CD155 protein stability, thereby sustaining its surface expression to suppress NK cell-mediated antitumor immunity. Consistent with a role for N-glycosylation in maintaining CD155 expression, pharmacological inhibition of oligosaccharyltransferase activity with NGI-1 promotes CD155 turnover, effectively abrogating its immunosuppressive function and enhancing NK cell-mediated tumor clearance in vivo. Collectively, these findings implicate the STT3A-CD155 glycosylation axis as a therapeutic vulnerability, providing a mechanistic rationale for reprogramming the immunosuppressive CRC microenvironment.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains one of the most prevalent malignancies worldwide, with persistently low rates of early-stage diagnosis, poor overall prognosis, and a propensity for therapeutic resistance-challenges that underscore the urgent need for deeper mechanistic insight. By integrating single-cell transcriptomic data (GSE161277) with multi-omics datasets from TCGA and GEO repositories, alongside an independent clinical cohort, we identified S100A11 as a consistently overexpressed gene in CRC that correlates significantly with adverse patient outcomes. Functional studies established that S100A11 drives tumour progression by promoting cell proliferation, suppressing apoptosis, and inducing epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Mechanistically, S100A11 engages the WD6-7 domain (residues 221-302) of STRAP through direct physical interaction, thereby recruiting the deubiquitylase OTUB1 to shield lysine K246 of STRAP from K63-linked polyubiquitination. This protection stabilises STRAP and facilitates its association with PI3K, culminating in activation of the PI3K/AKT/NF-κB cascade and nuclear translocation of p65. We further demonstrate that p65 binds directly to the promoter regions of both S100A11 and STRAP, transcriptionally upregulating their expression and establishing a self-reinforcing feedforward loop that sustains pathway activation. Collectively, these findings delineate a hierarchical regulatory network centred on the S100A11/STRAP/NF-κB axis and offer a mechanistic framework with potential implications for CRC diagnosis and targeted intervention.
