ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Despite its routine use in elective procedures, the role of laparoscopy in emergency colorectal surgery remains debated due to limited evidence. This study compared laparoscopic and open surgery regarding complications, mortality, and hospital stay following emergency colon operations. This retrospective study included adult patients treated at Päijät-Häme Central Hospital between 2010 and 2020 who underwent emergency colon resection. Propensity score matching was used to adjust for comorbidities, prior ICU admission, surgical indication, and contamination between laparoscopic and open surgery groups. All together 484 patients had an emergency colorectal resection of which 85 (17.6%) were carried out laparoscopically, 31 (6.4%) were converted and 377 (76.0%) were open. In the whole cohort, Comprehensive complication index was lower among laparoscopy patients than open surgery patients if intraoperative conversion to open surgery was avoided (25.8 vs. 34.9, p = 0.012). The subgroup analysis also showed lower CCI after laparoscopic resection for patients presented with obstruction (21.3 vs. 29.7, p = 0.046) or colorectal cancer (21.1 vs. 29.4, p = 0.020) A multivariable regression analysis also showed that starting the procedure laparoscopically predicted lower complication rates. Patients who had a laparoscopic resection also had shorter hospital stay (9.0 vs. 12.9 days, p < 0.001). Patients with open surgery had significantly more wound complications (10.3% vs. 1.2%, p = 0.010). Open surgery was also an independent risk factor for higher CCI (p = 0.008) and the need for intensive care (p = 0.027). Mortality was similar regardless of the approach in short term (30 days, p = 0.810; 90 days, p = 0.354) and in long-term survival (p = 0.466). The laparoscopic technique in colorectal emergencies may offer similar benefits as in elective surgery, with a lower burden of total complications, less wound complications and shorter hospital stay. Laparoscopy was not associated with any unexpected harmful events.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Active aldehydes are increasingly recognized as bioactive metabolites, but their roles in tumor immune regulation remain poorly defined. In colorectal cancer (CRC), prostaglandin metabolism contributes to immune suppression, whereas its upstream metabolic regulators are incompletely understood. Here, we investigated 2-methylbutanal (2-MBTL), a branched-chain small-molecule aldehyde, in CRC. The antitumor and immunoregulatory effects of 2-methylbutanal (2-MBTL) were examined in CRC cell systems and mouse models. Its molecular target and downstream pathway were investigated using target-identification assays, RNA interaction analyses, genetic manipulation, transcriptomic profiling, and PGE2 supplementation. 2-MBTL suppressed CRC growth at well-tolerated doses, increased tumor immunogenic signals, enhanced intratumoral CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration and effector activity, and reduced suppressive myeloid populations. Its direct antiproliferative effect was limited, whereas its antitumor activity was markedly weakened in immunodeficient mice or after CD8⁺ T-cell depletion. Mechanistically, 2-MBTL bound ENO1 and impaired its association with YAP1 mRNA, reducing YAP1 protein expression without substantially altering ENO1 abundance or glycolysis-associated readouts. This was accompanied by increased HPGD expression and reduced PGE2 levels. ENO1 overexpression attenuated the effects of 2-MBTL, while exogenous PGE2 partially reversed tumor suppression and immune remodeling. In human CRC tissues, ENO1 and HPGD showed opposing associations with CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration and survival. 2-MBTL also enhanced the efficacy of PD-1 blockade. 2-MBTL promotes CD8⁺ T-cell-dependent antitumor immunity by modulating ENO1-associated post-transcriptional regulation and suppressing YAP1-related PGE2 metabolism.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) liver metastasis (LM) is a leading cause of cancer-related death, with pre-metastatic niche (PMN) formation being critical for metastasis. Insulin-like growth factor binding protein 2 (IGFBP2) is overexpressed in metastatic CRC, but its role in intrahepatic fibrotic PMN formation and CRC-LM remains unclear. Bioinformatics analyses and tissue microarray samples were conducted to assess the expression level and prognostic significance of IGFBP2 in CRC patients. After overexpression of IGFBP2, its in vivo metastatic-promoting ability was evaluated by establishing a splenic injection liver metastasis model, while its in vitro malignant properties were assessed via colony formation, proliferation assay, flow cytometry, wound-healing assay and transwell assay. Furthermore, flow cytometry, RT-qPCR and ELISA were used to evaluate the effect of IGFBP2 overexpression on the polarization of intrahepatic macrophages. In addition, Western blot and immunofluorescence were performed to detect the effect of M2-polarized macrophages on hepatic stellate cells (HSCs). Finally, the splenic injection liver metastasis model was treated with CWI1-2 (IGFBP2 inhibitor) or pirfenidone (PFD, a TGF-β signaling modulator), and the therapeutic effects were observed. We found that IGFBP2 is overexpressed in CRC tissues, correlating with poor prognosis. Meanwhile, IGFBP2 overexpression significantly promotes CRC-LM progression in vivo. Mechanistically, it drives M2 polarization of intrahepatic macrophages to boost TGF-β secretion. Subsequently, TGF-β activates HSCs, elevates the deposition of extracellular matrix (α-SMA, COL1, FN), and ultimately contributes to the development of intrahepatic fibrotic PMN. Notably, CWI-2 or PFD could suppress CRC-LM, with combined treatment showing synergistic effects both in vitro and in vivo. IGFBP2 is highly expressed in CRC and correlated with patient prognosis. CRC-derived IGFBP2 drives intrahepatic fibrotic PMN formation via intrahepatic macrophages M2 polarization and TGF-β-mediated HSCs activation, which in turn facilitates CRC-LM. Furthermore, selective targeting of the process of intrahepatic PMN formation holds promise as a viable strategy for the prevention and treatment of CRC-LM.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The incidence and death rates of colorectal cancer (CRC), one of the world's largest health issues, are rising. These days, environmental contaminants such microplastics (MPs) are believed to play a role in the development of colorectal cancer. Small plastic particles (less than 5 mm) are referred to as MPs because they are persistent and may build up in human tissues, raising questions about their potential involvement in tumour biology. The objective is to systematically assess the prevalence of microplastics found in human colorectal membranes and their connections to biological processes and tumour type indicators in colorectal cancer. A systematic review was carried out using the Preferred Reporting Items of Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA). Peer-reviewed study sources published between January 2019 and December 2025 were located in MEDLINE, EMBASE, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library. The studies had to assess MPs in human colorectal tumours or surrounding tissues, as well as their associations with tumour biology, such as clinical, inflammatory, or molecular markers, according to the inclusion criteria. Two reviewers worked independently on the screening, selection, and data extraction processes. Thirteen papers make up the final qualitative synthesis, which is screened for full text and title/abstract. Study design, sample size, tissue type, MP detection techniques, polymer type, particle size, and tumour biology outcomes were among the data that were extracted. Particularly, MPs were detected in colon tissues, and their concentration was greater in tumour tissues than in nearby or control tissues. The most common polymers were polyethylene, polypropylene, and polystyrene, the majority of which were less than 100 μm. The advanced tumour stage, limited differentiation, elevated pro-inflammatory cytokine levels, signs of oxidative stress, disrupted immune infiltration, and disrupted epithelial barrier function were all associated with higher MP loads. According to mechanistic research, MPs can induce oxidative stress, inflammation, and immunological homeostasis, all of which can result in a pro-tumorigenic environment. MPs can affect the development of colorectal cancer (CRC) because they are found in human colorectal tissues and are preferentially accumulated in tumours. Multicenter studies with typical application are required to clarify causal processes and clinical consequences.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The expansion of minimally invasive surgery has transformed surgical practice and training worldwide. However, operative exposure to laparoscopic and open procedures may vary across healthcare systems. Comparative international data on operative autonomy and procedural experience during surgical residency remain limited. This study aimed to compare operative exposure, autonomy, and trainee perceptions regarding open and laparoscopic surgery among surgical trainees at selected centers in France and Morocco. A multicenter cross-sectional survey was conducted among surgical trainees at academic centers in France and Morocco. Participants were stratified by postgraduate year (PGY 1-8). Self-reported operative exposure and autonomy were assessed for common general surgical procedures (appendectomy, cholecystectomy, and inguinal hernia repair) and complex colorectal procedures (colectomy and proctectomy) performed using open and laparoscopic approaches. Trainee perceptions of preparedness for minimally invasive surgery and the value of prior training in open surgery were also evaluated. Comparisons were made according to country and level of training. A total of 131 trainees participated, including 67 from Morocco and 64 from France. Trainees at French centers reported significantly greater exposure to laparoscopic procedures across training levels (p < 0.001), whereas trainees at Moroccan centers reported greater exposure to open appendectomy, inguinal hernia repair, and proctectomy (p < 0.001). Operative autonomy increased with training seniority in both groups, although trainees at French centers reported greater autonomy in laparoscopic procedures. Trainees at Moroccan centers were significantly more likely to consider prior training in open surgery necessary before performing laparoscopic procedures (p < 0.01). These findings support context-adapted curricula that preserve competence in open surgery while expanding access to structured, supervised training in minimally invasive surgery.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Epigenetic dysregulation is increasingly recognized as a fundamental driver of cell cycle checkpoint failure in colorectal cancer. Beyond genetic mutations, epigenetic mechanisms provide a dynamic and potentially reversible layer of control over cyclin-dependent kinase activity and tumor progression. This mechanistic critical review examines how epigenetic alterations reshape cell cycle regulation in colorectal cancer and evaluates their translational relevance. This review adopts a critical mechanistic approach, integrating and interpreting evidence from experimental, translational and clinical studies addressing epigenetic regulation of cell cycle control in colorectal cancer. Rather than following a systematic review framework, the literature was evaluated conceptually to identify dominant mechanisms, areas of convergence and unresolved controversies. Evidence indicates that aberrant DNA methylation, histone modifications and chromatin remodeling converge to repress key cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitors including p16INK4a, p21Cip1 and p27Kip1. These epigenetic alterations sustain cyclin-CDK activity thereby promote bypass of G1/S checkpoint control and facilitate uncontrolled proliferation. Importantly, epigenetic heterogeneity across colorectal tumors contributes to variable therapeutic responses and resistance to both conventional and epigenetic-targeted therapies. Epigenetic control of cell cycle checkpoints represents a central and therapeutically exploitable mechanism in colorectal cancer. A mechanistic understanding of these regulatory networks highlights opportunities for rational combination strategies and precision-based interventions while underscoring current knowledge gaps that warrant further investigation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the most prevalent cancers worldwide, particularly affecting developed countries. Many pathways and mechanisms have been implicated in the development of CRC, and one of the targets of interest is the long non-coding ribonucleic acid (lncRNA), growth arrest specific 5 (GAS5). GAS5 has been observed to play an important role in many other cancers, and CRC is not an exception. This paper aims to understand the role and mechanisms played by GAS5 in relation to CRC progression. GAS5 has a complex role, with one of its major functions being its competitive endogenous nature that can downregulate multiple microRNAs such as miR-485-5p, miR-137, miR-26b, miR-21, miR-34a, miR-182-5p, miR-128-3p, and miR-221, which have implications in tumour growth and suppression. It is also observed to interact with proteins directly, such as the Yes-Associated Protein (YAP). Both clinical and laboratory evidence support the fact that in the context of CRC, GAS5 overexpression is a protective factor, while its underexpression is related to poorer prognosis and reduced survival. This has opened up its potential as a prognostic biomarker, as well as a therapeutic target to treat multiple cancers, including CRC. However, more research is still required to address existing knowledge gaps. In conclusion, GAS5 plays multiple roles and is an important player in cancer regulation, including CRC, and it holds good potential to be a biomarker and a therapeutic target.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Utilizing targeted drug delivery in oncology represents a valuable strategy to enhance the therapeutic efficacy of chemotherapy and simultaneously mitigate its adverse effects. Our present investigation focused on harnessing the therapeutic properties of melatonin as an anti-cancer agent and improving its bioavailability by employing a drug delivery system based on folic acid-decorated niosomal nanoparticles. To deliver melatonin, a niosomal and a folic acid decorated niosomal system was used. Nanoparticles were synthesized with the thin film hydration method and characterized by AFM, SEM, DLS, and FT-IR techniques. The cytotoxic effects and changes in gene expression were assessed using MTT and real-time PCR techniques, respectively. Additionally, flow cytometry experiments were conducted to investigate their impact on cell cycle arrest and apoptosis induction. Nanoparticle analysis revealed that the size distribution of blank niosomes, melatonin-loaded niosomal nanoparticles, and melatonin-loaded folic acid-decorated niosomal nanoparticles were 157±8.96 nm, 198±12.34 nm, and 239.9±39.64 nm, respectively. Controlled release studies indicated that over 96 hours, the maximum amount of melatonin released was approximately 60% at pH 7.4 and 73% at pH 5. The results demonstrated enhanced cell cytotoxicity of melatonin when encapsulated in melatonin-loaded folic acid-decorated niosomal compared to pure melatonin and niosomal nanoparticles. Furthermore, melatonin-loaded folic acid-decorated niosomal nanoparticles exhibited superior outcomes in terms of promoting apoptosis and cell cycle arrest compared to other tested substances. Overall, melatonin-loaded folic acid-decorated niosomal nanoparticles demonstrate a significant capability as an effective therapeutic strategy for targeting colorectal cancer cells.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The association between seborrheic keratosis (SK) and internal malignancies remains controversial, with findings from observational studies often confounded by reverse causality and unmeasured confounding factors. This study aimed to investigate the causal relationship between SK and common malignancies using a bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) approach. Genetic instruments for SK and malignancies (thyroid, breast, lung, colorectal, liver, gastric, prostate, renal, and pancreatic cancer) were derived from publicly available genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics based on individuals of European ancestry. Independent single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) significantly associated with SK were used as instrumental variables. Bidirectional two-sample MR analyses were performed, primarily using the inverse-variance weighted (IVW) method, supplemented by MR-Egger, weighted median, and other robust methods. Sensitivity analyses, including Cochran's Q test, MR-Egger intercept test, and leave-one-out analysis, were conducted to assess heterogeneity, pleiotropy, and the robustness of the results. In the present study, genetically predicted SK was associated with an increased risk of breast cancer (IVW OR = 1.075, 95% CI: 1.014-1.139, P = 0.015) and colorectal cancer (IVW OR = 1.211, 95% CI: 1.069-1.371, P = 0.003). No significant causal associations were found between SK and the other seven cancers. Sensitivity analyses revealed no significant horizontal pleiotropy, and the results were robust. Reverse MR analysis did not support a causal effect of the investigated cancers on SK. This study provides genetic evidence supporting a potential causal association between SK and increased risk of breast and colorectal cancer. These findings offer new insights into the clinical significance of SK, although the underlying biological mechanisms require further elucidation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) represents a significant global health concern, ranking as the third most diagnosed cancer and the second leading cause of cancer deaths in the UK. Although population-based bowel cancer screening programs (BCSP) facilitate early diagnosis, uptake remains variable. Blood-based biomarkers, such as human progastrin 80 (hPG80), offer a patient-friendly approach to enhance screening compliance and clinical management. This scoping review, conducted according to PRISMA-ScR guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420250654595), searched Ovid Medline/PubMed, Ovid Embase, and Cochrane databases from January 1990 to January 2025. Studies assessing plasma hPG80 as a CRC biomarker were included, while reviews, in vitro studies, and animal models were excluded. Quality assessment was performed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and findings were synthesized narratively. Five articles encompassing 2,692 participants met the inclusion criteria. The included studies consistently demonstrated significant overexpression of hPG80 in CRC patients compared to non-cancer controls, with an increased median progastrin concentration in the CRC group (27.5 pmol/L) compared to patients with polyps or normal controls. Furthermore, hPG80 levels decreased significantly post-surgery (from 272.3 ± 12.0 pmol/L to 161.3 ± 11.0 pmol/L), reflecting its sensitivity to tumor burden and potential for treatment monitoring. Methodologically, literature has shifted from early radioimmunoassays to safer, cost-effective enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISA). A meta-analysis was not feasible due to variations in analytes, assays, populations, thresholds, and a lack of CRC-specific sensitivity, specificity, or area under the curve data. This review highlights hPG80's promise as a reliable, reproducible blood-based biomarker for CRC integration into BCSPs and symptomatic pathways. However, optimal thresholds, stage-specific correlation, molecular subtypes, and cost-effectiveness remain unanswered. The ongoing MOTION trial (NCT07035691) is currently evaluating hPG80's performance within UK symptomatic suspected colorectal cancer referral pathways.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) ranks third in global incidence and second in cancer-related mortality, with the liver constituting the most frequent target organ for metastatic dissemination and distant organ involvement representing the predominant cause of death. Approximately 20-25% of patients present with synchronous hepatic metastases at initial diagnosis or within 3-6 months thereafter, whereas an additional 20-50% develop metachronous hepatic recurrence following curative-intent resection of the primary tumor, thereby positioning colorectal cancer liver metastasis (CRLM) among the most formidable challenges in oncology. With progressive advances in biological insight, the conceptual framework of CRLM has evolved from the classical 'seed and soil' hypothesis into an integrative, multi-dimensional paradigm encompassing the epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) of circulating tumor cells (CTCs), immunostromal crosstalk within the tumor microenvironment (TME), the remote regulatory functions of the gut microbiota and its metabolic products, and the contributions of metabolic reprogramming and epigenetic modifications. This review synthesizes recent advances in the molecular pathogenesis of CRLM, including the formation and modulation of the pre-metastatic niche (PMN), the influence of liver-intrinsic immune tolerance on immunotherapeutic responsiveness, the synergistic regulation of core signaling networks, the pathogenic role of the gut microbiota-metabolism-epigenetics axis, and the role of CTCs within the metastatic cascade. From a clinical perspective, we appraise the progress in surgical resection, immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) and their combination strategies, targeted therapies, locoregional interventions, and emerging metabolic-epigenetic therapeutics, with particular emphasis on the clinically challenging disparity in immunotherapy responses between hepatic and pulmonary metastases, a phenomenon largely attributable to organ-specific immune microenvironments. Furthermore, we delineate the limitations of current investigations, noting that much of the mechanistic evidence derives from preclinical models and that organ-specific clinical observations remain predominantly retrospective in nature, and We emphasize that developing precision treatment strategies based on multidimensional molecular profiling and organ-specific therapeutic regimens will constitute a critical research direction for improving the prognosis of patients with CRLM.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Piperacillin/tazobactam is a broad-spectrum antibiotic primarily indicated for the treatment of moderate-to-severe polymicrobial infections. Severe drug-induced liver injury (DILI) is a rare adverse event attributed to its use. We report the case of a 79-year-old male patient who underwent radical resection for rectal cancer and postoperatively received antineoplastic therapy. Due to the development of fever and surgical site infection, he was started on intravenous piperacillin/tazobactam. Twelve days after treatment initiation, the patient exhibited significantly elevated liver biochemical parameters, and an abnormal eosinophil percentage was noted on day 16. Despite interventions with hepatoprotective agents and glucocorticoids, his hepatic parameters continued to deteriorate, accompanied by jaundice of the skin and sclera. Integrating imaging, laboratory findings, and medication history, the multidisciplinary team suspected piperacillin/tazobactam-induced cholestatic DILI (R value < 2), with jaundice indicating potentially severe liver injury. Piperacillin/tazobactam was immediately discontinued, and hepatoprotective therapy was continued. The patient's liver function gradually improved, with liver enzymes and bilirubin levels returning to normal or near-normal by day 106 post-withdrawal. The causality assessment was determined as "probable" based on the Naranjo Adverse Drug Reaction Probability Scale (score 7) and the Roussel Uclaf Causality Assessment Method (score 8). Additionally, we reviewed the literature regarding the clinical manifestations, pathogenesis, susceptible genes, biomarkers, and treatment principles of piperacillin/tazobactam-induced DILI. As a rare yet severe adverse drug reaction, DILI demands heightened vigilance, early recognition, and effective management. Crucially, immediately stopping the suspected drug remains the paramount intervention once DILI is suspected. The underlying mechanisms, genetic predispositions, and specific biomarkers associated with piperacillin/tazobactam-induced DILI remain to be fully elucidated, underscoring the need for further investigation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a leading cause of cancer morbidity and mortality, and metastatic progression, recurrence, chemoresistance, and treatment-related toxicity continue to limit outcomes. Medical ozone has attracted interest as a potential adjunct because, after reacting with biological fluids, it generates short-lived redox mediators such as hydrogen peroxide and lipid oxidation products that may influence NRF2/Keap1, NF-κB, HIF-1α, mitochondrial apoptosis, cytokine signaling, and the tumor microenvironment. However, current CRC-specific evidence is limited and heterogeneous. Experimental studies using CRC cell lines and animal models suggest possible effects on apoptosis, oxidative stress, inflammatory modulation, hypoxia-related pathways, and chemosensitivity, but these findings remain preclinical and are not sufficient to establish antitumor efficacy. Clinical evidence in CRC patients is scarce and mainly relates to supportive care, including radiation-induced rectal injury, chronic treatment-related symptoms, and chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy, rather than tumor response or survival. Importantly, ozone biology is context dependent: activation of adaptive antioxidant responses may protect normal tissues but could also enhance tumor cell stress tolerance under certain conditions. Route-specific safety is also critical, as inhaled ozone is toxic, whereas non-inhalational approaches require standardized dosing and monitoring. Overall, ozone therapy should be considered an investigational adjunct in CRC, with future studies requiring rigorous trial design, biomarker stratification, standardized administration protocols, and clear separation of anticancer endpoints from symptom-control outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Readiness for stoma reversal is an important concept for patients with a diverting stoma during the transition from "living with a stoma" to "resumption of transanal defecation and adaptation to postoperative bowel function." However, its conceptual meaning remains unclear, limiting the development of related research and clinical practice. Therefore, it is necessary to clearly define the concept of readiness for stoma reversal in patients with a diverting stoma. To clarify the concept of readiness for stoma reversal in patients with a diverting stoma using Rodgers' evolutionary concept analysis. Relevant studies on readiness for stoma reversal in patients with a diverting stoma were systematically searched in PubMed, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, CINAHL, the Cochrane Library, Embase, CNKI, Wanfang Data, and VIP Database. Rodgers' evolutionary concept analysis was used to synthesize and analyze the included studies. The conceptual attributes, antecedents, consequences, and related concepts of readiness for stoma reversal in patients with a diverting stoma were extracted and summarized. The core attributes of readiness for stoma reversal in patients with a diverting stoma include pre-reversal assessment, physical and functional readiness, information and knowledge readiness, and psychological readiness. The main antecedents included rectal cancer control and anastomotic healing, systematic health education and health literacy, socioeconomic conditions and support systems, and multidisciplinary assessment and collaboration. For patients, adequate readiness may facilitate bowel function recovery, enhance engagement in rehabilitation and self-management, reduce anxiety and fear, lower the risk of postoperative complications, and improve quality of life. For healthcare systems, it may help shorten hospital stays, reduce readmissions and other unplanned healthcare use, and lower related medical costs. Readiness for stoma reversal is a multidimensional and dynamic state that develops before reversal in patients with a diverting stoma. It reflects the patient's ability to cope with stoma reversal, bowel function recovery after reversal, and related lifestyle changes. Clarifying the attributes, antecedents, and consequences of this concept may support the development of assessment tools for readiness for stoma reversal. It may also provide a basis for designing individualized and continuous nursing interventions.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Early diagnosis of ovarian cancer is a significant clinical problem, and this is mainly because there are no strongly sensitive early-detection biomarkers, and the standard screening parameters like CA-125 blood tests and transvaginal ultrasounds are very insensitive in making a diagnosis. This paper presents a machine learning architecture, which is organized and interpretable based on the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal, and Ovarian (PLCO) Cancer Screening data to enhance the risk stratification of ovarian cancer. The original analytical cohort comprised 78,209 participants, including 518 ovarian cancer cases. To select 20 informative pre-diagnostic predictors in a high dimensional feature space, a comprehensive feature selection pipeline with ANOVA (f classifier), Chi-square, Random Forest importance, and XGBoost importance were used. Several classification algorithms were tested and the boosting based methods proved to have a good predictive value. A stacking ensemble of K-Nearest Neighbors and AdaBoost was the highest performing overall (accuracy: 0.7644), and a test-set AUROC of 0.8399, with additional evaluation using sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, balanced accuracy, MCC, and PR-AUC. SHAP analysis and permutation importance were used to provide model interpretability and consistently regarded questionnaire-based screening variables, age, and CA-125 attributes as the strongest ones. The suggested framework offers a methodologically rigorous and transparent method of assessment of population level ovarian cancer risk, providing a foundation for future research toward a clinically useful ovarian cancer screening decision-support system, pending external validation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Spontaneous renal rupture (SRR) is a rare nontraumatic emergency, usually associated with renal neoplasms, vascular lesions, infection, coagulopathy, or obstruction. Diffuse malignant infiltration may be missed when it does not form a discrete mass. A 45-year-old man previously treated for sigmoid colon adenocarcinoma had chronic left ureteral obstruction and presented with sudden severe left flank pain and gross hematuria. Contrast-enhanced CT showed left renal rupture with a large perirenal and retroperitoneal hematoma, a chronic left ureteral stent, and moderate right hydroureteronephrosis. No enhancing renal or ureteral mass was visible. Hemoglobin was 108 g/L on arrival, and the extent of the hematoma raised concern for ongoing hemorrhage. Selective renal arterial embolization was considered, but open nephrectomy was chosen because the left kidney was chronically compromised and tumor-related rupture could not be excluded. The right ureter was stented first to protect the remaining renal unit. Gross examination identified a dorsal cortical tear but no discrete tumor. Histology disclosed diffuse poorly differentiated carcinoma with extensive necrosis and invasion of renal hilar vessel walls. Immunohistochemistry supported colorectal origin. Urinary tract and systemic recurrence followed, and the patient died of multiorgan failure in June 2024.Diffuse malignant renal involvement should remain in the differential diagnosis when a patient with previous colorectal cancer develops unexplained nontraumatic renal or perirenal hemorrhage, even if imaging shows no mass. If nephrectomy is required in the presence of contralateral upper urinary tract obstruction, drainage of the remaining renal unit should be planned beforehand.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Lymph node metastasis (LNM) is central to colorectal cancer staging and treatment decisions and marks a critical transition from local growth to regional dissemination. The molecular heterogeneity associated with lymph node metastasis and the corresponding intervention leads require systematic investigation. This study established the C1 to C4 molecular subtypes from lymph node metastasis-related expression features. Multiple transcriptomic cohorts, clinical composition, pathway features, and TIDE, IPS, and ESTIMATE scores were integrated to characterize subtype differences. Analyses across multiple cohorts were used to screen candidate genes associated with progression. Cellular and subcutaneous xenograft experiments were performed to evaluate GDI1 function. The GDI1 structure was used for virtual screening and molecular dynamics analysis, followed by phenotypic evaluation of Deslanoside in cellular and xenograft models. Four molecular subtypes displayed distinct expression profiles, clinical composition, and tumor microenvironment features. C4 showed coordinated enrichment of invasive, mesenchymal, hypoxia-related, and stromal programs together with algorithmic features associated with restricted immune effector activity. Analyses across multiple cohorts identified GDI1 as a candidate gene associated with adverse outcomes and progression. Two independent shRNAs reduced GDI1 expression, cell growth, and migration-related phenotypes in two colorectal cancer cell lines. GDI1 knockdown using shGDI1 #1 also reduced subcutaneous xenograft burden. Deslanoside ranked among the leading candidates in the computational screen. Deslanoside treatment produced antitumor phenotypes in cellular and xenograft models that were directionally concordant with those produced by GDI1 depletion. This study delineates the molecular heterogeneity associated with lymph node metastasis in colorectal cancer, supports a tumor-promoting role for GDI1, and provides a basis for further investigation of Deslanoside as a candidate compound.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Hepatoid adenocarcinoma (HAC) is a rare extrahepatic adenocarcinoma producing alpha-fetoprotein (AFP), with clinicopathological features resembling hepatocellular carcinoma, including aggressive behavior, poor prognosis, vascular invasion, and distant metastasis. It occurs mostly in the stomach and rarely in the colon. Due to its rarity, large randomized trials are lacking; thus, case reports provide valuable treatment information. Here, we report a 62-year-old woman initially diagnosed with massive hepatocellular carcinoma by computed tomography (CT) who underwent radical hepatectomy. Postoperative follow-up CT revealed lesions in the sigmoid colon and residual liver. Colonoscopic biopsy showed poorly differentiated carcinoma (adenocarcinoma with enteroblastic differentiation/hepatoid adenocarcinoma). She then received CAPOX (oxaliplatin plus capecitabine) combined with sintilimab and bevacizumab. After one year, follow-up imaging showed complete disappearance of the liver tumor and reduction of the sigmoid colon lesion. The final efficacy assessment was complete remission (CR) of the liver lesion and stable disease (SD) of the sigmoid colon lesion. This case report suggests that combined immune-targeted therapy and chemotherapy achieved excellent efficacy in a patient with intestinal hepatoid adenocarcinoma and liver metastases, and this combination regimen may provide a new treatment strategy for intestinal hepatoid adenocarcinoma (IHA).

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Mismatch repair (MMR) protein immunohistochemistry (IHC) and microsatellite instability (MSI) testing are central to colorectal cancer treatment stratification and hereditary-risk assessment, but a pMMR/MSS tumour phenotype does not exclude a germline predisposition in selected patients. We report a 41-year-old woman with low rectal adenocarcinoma whose pretreatment biopsy and resection specimen retained MLH1, PMS2, MSH2 and MSH6 expression and whose tumour was microsatellite stable (MSS) with low tumour mutational burden (TMB-L). Tumour-tissue sequencing initially identified the PMS2 frameshift variant NM_000535.7:c.1577del (p.Asp526AlafsTer69; GRCh37/hg19 chr7:6026819delT). A subsequent orthogonal assay using PMS2-specific three-step nested genomic PCR, TA cloning and Sanger sequencing of peripheral-blood DNA confirmed that the variant mapped to PMS2 and supported its germline origin; the clinical laboratory classified the variant as pathogenic using an ACMG/AMP-based interpretation. No dedicated analyses of tumoural PMS2 somatic second-hit events, loss of heterozygosity, copy-number alterations or promoter methylation were performed; therefore, biallelic PMS2 inactivation was not established. Postoperative circulating tumour DNA molecular residual disease was positive, and a left supraclavicular lymph-node biopsy subsequently confirmed metastatic adenocarcinoma consistent with colorectal origin. This case illustrates that pMMR/MSS findings should not be used in isolation to exclude hereditary risk in patients with early-onset disease or other clinical indications for germline assessment. These findings support selective germline assessment in patients with early-onset or otherwise high-risk pMMR/MSS colorectal cancer, but do not justify universal testing or establish that the tumour was caused by PMS2-associated Lynch syndrome.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Urachal adenocarcinoma is a rare malignancy without prospective treatment trials. Management of metastatic disease is typically extrapolated from colorectal cancer (CRC) due to histologic and molecular similarities. An 80-year-old woman with metastatic urachal adenocarcinoma received sequential CRC-based therapy including first-line CAPOX plus bevacizumab, second-line FOLFIRI plus bevacizumab, third-line trifluridine/tipiracil plus bevacizumab, in addition to brief administration of regorafenib and fruquintinib in the fourth- and fifth-line setting. Oxaliplatin was discontinued after one cycle due to worsening of vision on a background of pre-existing retinopathy. The longest disease control (time to progression ~11 months) occurred with trifluridine/tipiracil plus bevacizumab. To our knowledge, this represents the first report describing use of this combination in the third-line setting for metastatic urachal carcinoma. Overall survival was 27 months. This case is hypothesis-generating for the use of modern CRC-based therapies, including anti-VEGF-containing combinations.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To evaluate the efficacy and safety of thymosin preparations added to the same background anticancer treatment in patients with colorectal cancer. We searched nine bibliographic and trial-registration sources through 1 October 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and nonrandomized studies with concurrent controls were eligible. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and ROBINS-I. RCTs provided the primary evidence; nonrandomized studies were analyzed separately. Review Manager 5.4.1 calculated risk ratios (RRs) or mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), organized by treatment setting. Sensitivity analyses, GRADE and exploratory trial sequential analysis (TSA) assessed robustness and uncertainty. Thirty studies involving 2,514 participants comprised 25 RCTs (2,079 participants) and five nonrandomized studies (435 participants). In postoperative RCTs, CD4 percentage (MD 6.33, 95% CI 4.89 to 7.76), CD4/CD8 ratio (MD 0.25, 0.16 to 0.35) and NK-cell percentage (MD 6.41, 3.72 to 9.11) were higher with thymosin; CD3 and CD8 findings were inconclusive. KPS was higher in two postoperative RCTs (MD 8.50, 6.52 to 10.48) and two advanced or mixed-stage trials (MD 4.35, 1.90 to 6.80), with source-reporting concerns affecting the latter. Postoperative neutropenia was inconclusive in the RCT (RR 0.91, 0.82 to 1.01), whereas two nonrandomized studies reported a lower unadjusted risk (RR 0.65, 0.51 to 0.83). Comparable one-year survival evidence came from one trial. Certainty was low or very low. This review identifies RCT-based signals in circulating immune indices and performance status and clarifies the contribution of nonrandomized evidence. These findings inform the selection of outcomes and treatment settings for future trials. Current evidence is insufficient to support routine clinical use of thymosin preparations in colorectal cancer. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261467566, CRD420261467566.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To compare the long-term oncological outcomes and postoperative complications between local excision (LE) and intersphincteric resection (ISR) after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT) in patients with ultra-low rectal cancer (ULRC). Data were retrospectively collected from ULRC patients (tumor lower margin ≤5 cm from anal verge) who received nCRT followed by LE or ISR at two hospitals between 2016 and 2025. LE was selectively offered to patients achieving clinical complete response (cCR) or near-complete response (ncCR) after nCRT; ISR was the institutional default for incomplete responders. Propensity score matching (PSM) using 1:2 nearest-neighbor matching with a caliper of 0.2 on the standardized propensity score scale was performed. A total of 367 patients were enrolled (ISR, n=209; LE, n=158). After PSM, 91 and 56 patients remained, respectively. In the matched cohort, there were 20 deaths, 31 disease-free survival (DFS) events, 17 distant metastases (DM), and 12 local recurrences. No statistically significant differences were observed in overall survival (OS) (HR = 0.699, 95% CI: 0.247-1.977; P = 0.460), DFS (HR = 0.802, 95% CI: 0.369-1.745; P = 0.580), DM (HR = 0.260, 95% CI: 0.059-1.137; P = 0.054), or local recurrence (HR = 1.365, 95% CI: 0.432-4.310; P = 0.590). The LE group had higher rates of overall complications (55.4% vs. 29.7%; P = 0.002) and adapted wound dehiscence (32.1% vs. 13.2%; P = 0.006), predominantly driven by minor complications (Clavien-Dindo I-II: 44.6% vs. 17.6%); major complications were similarly infrequent (10.7% vs. 12.1%). Prophylactic stoma creation was performed in 90.1% of the ISR group versus 7.1% of the LE group (P<0.001). Among 24 LE patients with ypT2 or higher disease, 21 (87.5%) refused recommended salvage surgery. No statistically significant differences in OS, DFS, DM, or local recurrence were detected between an initial LE and ISR after propensity-score adjustment. However, limited event numbers, residual confounding related to post-neoadjuvant response selection, and incomplete adherence to recommended completion surgery preclude conclusions of oncological equivalence or noninferiority. LE was associated with substantially less initial diversion but more local-excision-defect morbidity under the definitions used. The incidence of postoperative complications was higher after LE, but this was mainly driven by minor complications; surgeons should pay close attention to rectal wound dehiscence.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To systematically retrieve and summarize the best available evidence on patient positioning management for the modified lithotomy position in laparoscopic colorectal surgery, in order to provide an evidence-based reference for standardizing positioning practices. Guided by the 6S evidence model, we searched resources such as UpToDate, BMJ Best Practice, the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) website, the Registered Nurses' Association of Ontario (RNAO) website, and the International Guideline Network for relevant clinical decisions, guidelines, evidence summaries, expert consensuses, systematic reviews, and meta - analyses. The search period for guidelines, evidence summaries, and expert consensuses spanned from database inception to October 7, 2025, while systematic reviews were restricted to those published between January 1, 2020, and October 7, 2025. The retrieved literature was appraised for quality, and evidence was extracted and synthesized.This study was registered with the Fudan University Evidence-Based Nursing Center (registration number: ER20259536). 17 publications were included, from which 18 best - practice evidence points were summarized across five domains: preoperative assessment, positioning procedure, positioning - related complications, postoperative handover, and education/training. This summary offers evidence - based guidance on patient positioning in the modified lithotomy position for laparoscopic colorectal surgery, intended to support clinical practice.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Rural populations experience higher mortality rates than urban populations for both heart failure (HF) and cancer, however, mortality involving both conditions has not been well characterized. We evaluated national trends and demographic differences in HF-related and HF + cancer-related deaths and assessed rural-urban disparities. Using U.S. death certificate data from 2011 to 2020, we calculated age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) per 100,000 persons for HF-related and HF + cancer-related deaths overall and stratified by rurality. During the study period, 3,453,655 HF-related deaths occurred, of which 274,715 (8%) also involved cancer. AAMRs increased over time for both outcomes. Rural areas consistently demonstrated higher mortality rates than urban areas for HF-related deaths (143.2 vs 110.1 per 100,000) and HF + cancer-related deaths (11.6 vs 8.8 per 100,000). Rural-urban disparities were evident across sex, age, and race/ethnicity groups. The largest rural-to-urban AAMR ratios were observed for lung/bronchus cancer (1.41), colorectal cancer (1.39), and leukemia (1.32). Mortality associated with both HF and cancer disproportionately affects rural populations. These findings highlight a growing dual burden of cardiovascular disease and cancer in rural communities and underscore the need for targeted prevention and care strategies addressing multimorbidity in these settings.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
We investigated the potential of the association between microencapsulated quercetin (MEQ) and the probiotic Bifidobacterium animalis in 1,2-dimethylhydrazine (DMH)-induced colorectal cancer (CRC) in Wistar rats with a focus on hepatic alterations and liver lobar heterogeneity. The rats were divided into 5 groups: control (C), CRC (CR), CRC treated with MEQ (CRQ), CRC treated with the probiotic (CRP), and CRC treated with MEQ + probiotic (CRQP). DMH (40 mg/kg) was administered intraperitoneally twice weekly for two weeks. MEQ (10 mg/kg) and the probiotic (5×107 colony forming units) were administered by gavage for 13 weeks. The liver was evaluated by histomorphometry and redox state analyses. CRC was confirmed by aberrant crypt foci in 100% of the DMH animals. The CR group showed increased hepatosomatic index (HSI) and lobe-specific cellular hypertrophy. The treatments reduced the HSI, with the association MEQ + probiotic being the most effective in preventing the physiopathological process associated with CRC. Deep learning-assisted cell quantification revealed a reduction of mononucleated hepatocytes in the CR group, a condition abolished by all treatments. DMH induced asymmetric glycogen accumulation and extracellular matrix remodeling, which were modulated by MEQ and the probiotic. Redox state analysis showed thiol depletion in the caudate lobe, where the quadrate lobe underwent lipid peroxidation and catalase inhibition. The treatments reestablished thiol levels and catalase activity in both lobes, thereby confirming antioxidant and hepatoprotective properties. In conclusion, the association of MEQ and probiotic exhibited lobar heterogeneity in attenuating hepatic damage reinforcing the importance of liver lobar analysis in the therapeutic evaluation of carcinogenesis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To evaluate the diagnostic performance and clinical implications of endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration (EBUS-TBNA) for assessing mediastinal or hilar lymph node involvement in patients with extrathoracic malignancies (ETMs). This was a single-center, ambispective observational study including consecutive patients with an ETM and abnormal thoracic lymph nodes (LNs), detected by CT or PET/CT, who underwent EBUS-TBNA between January of 2012 and December of 2022. Diagnostic performance was assessed by using predefined criteria, with surgical confirmation or long-term clinical and radiological follow-up (for ≥ 24 months) as the reference standard. We included 186 patients with a collective total of 237 LNs. The most common ETMs were colorectal, urological, and breast cancer (in 22.6%, 22.6%, and 20.4%, respectively). Most (72%) of the LNs sampled were mediastinal, predominantly subcarinal (in 33%) and right paratracheal (in 29%). We found that EBUS-TBNA had a sensitivity of 96.4% (95% CI: 90.98-98.62%), a negative predictive value of 94.6% (95% CI: 86.89-97.93%), and an overall accuracy of 97.8% (95% CI: 94.43-99.06%). No major complications were observed. Round shape and heterogeneous echogenicity were independently associated with LN malignancy. Overall survival was significantly shorter in patients with mediastinal LN metastases than in those without (log rank test, p = 0.008). The EBUS-TBNA procedure is a safe, highly accurate tool for evaluating thoracic lymphadenopathy in patients with an ETM. Its findings enable reliable identification of malignant involvement and may support clinical decision-making. Sonographic features may further assist in optimizing LN selection.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Anastomotic leakage is a clinically important complication after rectal cancer surgery, and preoperative nutritional and inflammatory status may be associated with anastomotic healing. This study aimed to evaluate the association between preoperative nutritional status, particularly the prognostic nutritional index (PNI), and postoperative anastomotic leakage in patients undergoing rectal cancer surgery. This retrospective study included consecutive eligible patients who underwent rectal cancer surgery between January 2023 and December 2025. Anastomotic leakage within 30 days was identified according to International Study Group of Rectal Cancer criteria. Preoperative nutritional status was primarily assessed using PNI, with Nutritional Risk Screening 2002 (NRS-2002), serum nutritional markers, and C-reactive protein (CRP) evaluated as complementary measures. Propensity score matching (PSM), multivariable logistic regression, unmatched-cohort analysis, sequential adjustment, subgroup analyses, and receiver operating characteristic analysis were performed. Among 2,468 patients, 308 developed anastomotic leakage. After 1:1 PSM, 308 patients with leakage and 308 without leakage were analyzed. Mean PNI was lower in patients with leakage (43.2 ± 5.1 vs. 46.8 ± 4.9; Lower preoperative PNI was independently associated with higher odds of postoperative anastomotic leakage after rectal cancer surgery. PNI may provide a readily available adjunct to multidimensional preoperative risk assessment but should not be considered a stand-alone predictor.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality worldwide, with therapeutic resistance representing a significant barrier to improved patient outcomes. Although tumor-intrinsic genetic alterations are important determinants of treatment resistance, emerging evidence suggests that the gut microbiome and its metabolites may also influence responses to chemotherapy, targeted therapy, and immunotherapy. The microbiome and metabolome function as an interconnected axis that can influence host immunity, microbial drug metabolism, epithelial homeostasis, and tumor-associated signaling pathways, thereby contributing to variation in therapeutic response. Despite advances in microbiome research, the mechanisms by which the microbiome-metabolome axis promotes therapy resistance are not fully elucidated, and clinical translation is limited by the absence of standardized biomarkers and validated therapeutic strategies. This review synthesizes current evidence on the molecular mechanisms through which the microbiome-metabolome axis contributes to CRC therapy resistance, with emphasis on microbial dysbiosis, bacterial metabolites, and host-microbial interactions in modulating treatment efficacy. Emerging microbiome-directed therapeutic approaches, including fecal microbiota transplantation, defined microbial consortia, dietary interventions, microbial metabolites, and engineered microbial therapies, are examined, along with the methodological and translational challenges that must be addressed before their integration into routine clinical practice.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Malnutrition is highly prevalent in patients with colorectal cancer and is associated with adverse postoperative outcomes and shortened survival. However, the comparative predictive performance of commonly used nutritional assessment tools-PG-SGA, ESPEN, and GLIM criteria-remains unclear. A total of 1,258 patients who underwent radical resection for colorectal cancer were retrospectively enrolled. Malnutrition was diagnosed simultaneously using the PG-SGA, ESPEN, and GLIM criteria. Agreement among the three tools was evaluated using Cohen's kappa coefficient. Multivariable logistic regression, an exploratory random forest analysis, and Cox proportional hazards models were applied. For the logistic regression models, ROC curve analysis and pairwise AUC comparisons using DeLong's test were performed; for the Cox models, bootstrap-based C-index comparisons were conducted. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed for the GLIM criterion as a The prevalence of malnutrition defined by PG-SGA, ESPEN, and GLIM was 24.7%, 15.7%, and 29.9%, respectively, with pairwise agreements ranging from moderate to substantial. All three criteria were independent risk factors for postoperative complications, with GLIM having the highest odds ratio (OR = 1.869, The three malnutrition diagnostic criteria are not interchangeable. For postoperative complications, GLIM demonstrated better discriminative ability than ESPEN but was comparable to PG-SGA. For long-term OS, GLIM provided modestly better prognostic discrimination than both PG-SGA and ESPEN, although the absolute improvement was small. These findings support the potential clinical utility of GLIM for perioperative nutritional risk assessment; however, the clinical relevance of these relatively small performance differences warrants further validation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer progression involves mitophagy, in which Prohibitin 2 (PHB2) regulates the PARL-PGAM5-PINK1 axis. Scutellarein has antitumor activity but poor bioavailability. We developed integrin αvβ3-targeted β-cyclodextrin-based scutellarein nanoparticles (Scu-NPs), which enhance the solubility, stability, and tumor-targeting of scutellarein, and investigated whether they suppress colon cancer via PHB2-mediated mitophagy inhibition and modulate tumor-associated depression and osteotropic migration. PHB2 expression and mitochondrial localization were examined in colon cancer cells. SW480 cells with PHB2 overexpression were treated with Scu or Scu-NPs. Proliferation, migration, invasion, apoptosis, mitochondrial function, and mitophagy-related proteins were assessed. Subcutaneous xenografts, a chronic unpredictable mild stress tumor-depression model, behavioral tests, osteotropic migration assays, and bioinformatics were used. PHB2 was highly expressed and mitochondria-localized in colon cancer cells. Scu-NPs downregulated PHB2, increased PARL, decreased PGAM5, PINK1, Parkin, and LC3-II/LC3-I, and increased P62, indicating mitophagy inhibition. Scu-NPs induced mitochondrial dysfunction, ROS accumulation, apoptosis, and inhibited proliferation, migration, and invasion; PHB2 overexpression partially reversed these effects. Scu-NPs suppress colon cancer by downregulating PHB2 and inhibiting mitophagy. PHB2 may serve as a shared molecular node linking tumor progression, depressive-like behaviors, and osteotropic migration, supporting Scu-NPs as a multi-target strategy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Rectal sarcomatoid carcinoma (RSC) is an exceedingly rare, aggressive malignancy characterized by a dismal prognosis, high recurrence rates, and truncated overall survival. Only 16 cases have been reported. Due to its rarity, optimal therapeutic strategies remain poorly understood. While current management typically mirrors rectal adenocarcinoma paradigms due to a lack of dedicated guidelines, clinical outcomes are frequently unsatisfactory, highlighting the challenges in managing this rare entity. A 66-year-old male presented with a 3-month history of hematochezia. Colonoscopy revealed a rectal mass, and subsequent biopsy confirmed a moderately-to-poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma(~95%), with only focal areas showing sarcomatoid differentiation(~5%). Immunohistochemistry (IHC) demonstrated proficient mismatch repair (pMMR) status and low HER-2 expression (1+). Pelvic MRI clinically staged the tumor as cT4aN2Mx (MRF-). Digital rectal examination palpated a hard, cauliflower-like mass 9 cm from the anal verge. On October 16, 2025, the patient initiated neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (CRT) (50 Gy/25 fractions with concurrent capecitabine), followed by two cycles of XELOX. On January 9, 2026, he underwent laparoscopic radical resection, right lateral pelvic lymph node dissection, and protective ileostomy. Postoperative pathology indicated downstaging to ypT3N0 with a tumor regression grade (TRG) of 2 (~70% overall regression). Notably, the residual tumor predominantly exhibited sarcomatoid differentiation(~70%) alongside intramucosal carcinoma components(~30%), confirmed as RSC via IHC. Postoperatively, the patient received four cycles of adjuvant XELOX(interrupted temporarily for stoma reversal following MDT evaluation). During adjuvant chemotherapy (May 10, 2026), he presented with significantly aggravated abdominal distension. Follow-up contrast-enhanced CT revealed right abdominal alterations highly suspicious of abscess or metastasis, with massive ascites and pelvic effusion. Cytological and IHC analyses of the ascites cell block confirmed peritoneal metastasis originating from the sarcomatoid component, showing focal positivity for CKpan, diffuse and strong positivity for Vimentin, and positivity for CDX2 while maintaining a pMMR/MSS status. Regrettably, the patient passed away on May 18, 2026. RSC is a rare, aggressive biphasic malignancy with a median overall survival typically under six months. It exhibits profound resistance to conventional colorectal CRT regimens, with a high propensity for recurrence and metastasis. Standard treatments are frequently inadequate, underscoring the urgent need for novel individualized therapeutic and targeted approaches.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To investigate the diagnostic performance of a computed tomography (CT)-based habitat radiomics model for discriminating between patients with rectal cancer (RC) with and without synchronous liver metastases (SLM). This retrospective study enrolled two independent patient cohorts. Cohort 1 (internal cohort) included 198 patients with pathologically confirmed RC with complete CT data from April 2022 to June 2025, comprising 46 SLM-positive and 152 SLM-negative cases. This cohort was divided randomly in a 7:3 ratio into a training set (140 patients: 33 SLM-positive, 107 SLM-negative) and an internal validation set (58 patients: 13 SLM-positive, 45 SLM-negative). Cohort 2 served as an external validation set, consisting of 55 patients with RC (18 SLM-positive, 37 SLM-negative). Regions of interest (ROIs) were delineated manually slice-by-slice on arterial-phase thin-slice CT images. Raw radiomics features were extracted from the ROIs and K-means clustering was implemented to segment tumor sub-habitats, followed by feature extraction for each sub-habitat. Feature-dimensionality reduction was performed on the training set using minimum redundancy maximum relevance and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator algorithms. Logistic regression classifiers were constructed to develop a conventional radiomics model and a habitat radiomics model, respectively. Model performance and clinical utility were quantified using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Univariate and multivariate logistic regression identified serum A CT-based habitat radiomics model could effectively identify patients with RC with SLM, with performance numerically better than that of conventional whole-tumor radiomics. Integrating clinical biomarkers with habitat radiomics further increased the predictive accuracy, offering a novel non-invasive preoperative risk-stratification strategy for RC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cyclovirobuxine D (CVB-D) is a steroidal alkaloid extracted from Buxus microphylla, widely used in traditional Chinese medicine for cardiovascular diseases. It has demonstrated significant pharmacological activities, including anti-arrhythmic, cardioprotective, neuroprotective, antiinflammatory, and anti-cancer effects. CVB-D modulates key signaling pathways, such as PI3K/Akt, NF-κB, MAPK, and calcium channel regulation, contributing to its therapeutic potential. Studies indicate that CVB-D induces apoptosis, inhibits cell proliferation, and suppresses tumor metastasis, particularly in lung, gastric, colorectal, and hepatocellular cancers. Additionally, its neuroprotective properties suggest potential applications in neurodegenerative disorders like Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases. Beyond its benefits, CVB-D poses challenges related to toxicity, bioavailability, and long-term safety. Reported side effects include hepatotoxicity, nephrotoxicity, and cardiovascular risks, necessitating further clinical investigations. Despite its promising pharmacological profile, preclinical and clinical trials are essential to determine its optimal dosage and therapeutic window. This review provides a comprehensive analysis of CVB-D, including its mechanisms of action, pharmacokinetics, therapeutic potential, and limitations. A deeper understanding of its molecular interactions and safety profile will help guide future drug development and clinical applications.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
M. tenacissima has been traditionally used to treat a variety of diseases, including relieving cough and dyspnea, eliminating stasis, unblocking meridians, increasing lactation, clearing heat, and removing toxins. Currently, the chemical structures of 248 compounds from M. tenacissima have been identified, predominantly C21 steroids. Modern pharmacological studies have demonstrated that its extract, formulated as Xiao-ai-ping injection, capsule, or tablet, exhibits broad clinical efficacy against various cancers (e.g., liver, lung, gastric, colorectal) and often enhances the effectiveness of conventional chemotherapy and radiotherapy while reducing toxicity. This review provides an overview of the traditional medicinal uses of M. tenacissima, its phytochemistry, and the antitumor mechanisms of its herbal preparation, Xiao-ai-ping. It also discusses the limitations of current research and future perspectives (such as the early-stage status of pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic studies, insufficient clinical evidence with a lack of high-quality, large-sample, long-term randomized controlled trials, and an incomplete understanding of the multi-target mechanisms of Xiao-ai-ping), offering guidance for those dedicated to advancing the plant's role in phytopharmaceuticals.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Skeletal muscle index (SMI) is considered an important prognostic factor in colorectal cancer (CRC); however, the factors associated with postoperative SMI changes in patients with CRC are not clear. This study aimed to explore the factors associated with delayed postoperative SMI recovery in patients with CRC. : This retrospective, observational, single-center study included 120 consecutive patients diagnosed with primary CRC and scheduled for surgery between October 2016 and September 2021. SMI was measured using computed tomography images at four perioperative time points (preoperatively, 3 months, 6 months, and 1 year postoperatively). To identify factors associated with delayed postoperative SMI recovery at 1 year, logistic regression analysis was performed with delayed postoperative SMI recovery at 1 year as the dependent variable. Sixty-four patients with a median age of 69 years were included. Multiple logistic regression analysis revealed rectal cancer [odds ratio (OR) 3.70] and sedentary time (OR 1.27) as preoperative factors associated with delayed SMI recovery at 1 year. In an exploratory postoperative course model, the percent SMI decline from preoperative to 3 months (OR 1.20) and the delayed recovery percentage from 3 to 6 months (OR 1.19) were also significantly associated with delayed SMI recovery at 1 year. Delayed postoperative SMI recovery at 1 year may be associated with preoperative factors including rectal cancer and sedentary time. Exploratory analysis suggested that early postoperative SMI decline and incomplete recovery between 3 and 6 months may also be related to delayed recovery at 1 year.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Drug resistance in cancer is shaped not only by tumor-cell-intrinsic mutations but also by spatially organized microenvironmental states. PLA2G2A, encoding group IIA secreted phospholipase A2 (sPLA2-IIA), is usually discussed as an inflammatory lipid enzyme; however, its cancer relevance depends strongly on cellular source, localization and disease stage. This Review uses a compartment-resolved framework that annotates four domains - source, spatial niche, linked biochemical output and functional or therapy-response phenotype - and separates PLA2G2A-specific mechanistic evidence from evidence for therapy or immune resistance. Several cancer studies provide PLA2G2A-specific functional evidence for invasion, proliferation/stemness, non-catalytic signaling or T-cell dysfunction, but direct demonstration that PLA2G2A changes response to a defined anticancer therapy remains sparse. The pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma cancer-associated fibroblast study provides the strongest resistance-proximal immune-functional evidence, whereas mucinous colorectal extracellular vesicles, ovarian ascites, invasive-front fibroblasts, treatment-remodeled stroma and prognostic signatures require more direct therapy-response validation. Gastric and intestinal epithelial data further caution that PLA2G2A may accompany differentiation, invasion restraint, antimicrobial defense or barrier protection. We therefore argue against treating PLA2G2A as a universal oncogenic target. Instead, it should be advanced as a mechanism-matched biomarker or therapeutic hypothesis only when compartment, biochemical-output, functional and perturbational evidence converge.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Thyroid dysfunction is a common adverse event during pembrolizumab therapy, but severe hypothyroidism accompanied by acute neuropsychiatric symptoms is rare. We present the case of a 78-year-old woman with metastatic colorectal cancer who developed agitation, hallucinations, and confusion three months after initiation of Pembrolizumab. Evaluation revealed profound hypothyroidism (TSH 37.9 mU/L, free T3 <0.60 pmol/L and free T4 <0.5 pmol/L) and moderate hyponatremia without acute findings on neuroimaging. Levothyroxine therapy led to complete remission of neuropsychiatric symptoms, and pembrolizumab was safely restarted with close monitoring and no recurrence. This case underscores the importance of assessing thyroid function in acute psychiatric presentations during immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy and supports cautious rechallenge after stabilization. Severe hypothyroidism was considered a major contributor, although a multifactorial delirium, including the contribution of hyponatremia and the absence of CSF/EEG evaluation, cannot be excluded.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) often experience multiple concurrent symptoms during the early post-chemotherapy period, and both symptom severity and inter-symptom associations may change over time. Previous low-frequency assessments may not adequately capture short-term fluctuations. To characterize the dynamic trajectories and network features of early symptoms in patients receiving postoperative adjuvant chemotherapy for CRC and to identify candidate symptoms for enhanced monitoring. A prospective longitudinal study was conducted. Ecological momentary assessment (EMA) was performed three times daily for seven consecutive days after infusion in the first and second chemotherapy cycles and covered 13 symptoms. Linear mixed-effects models characterized symptom trajectories, and a multilevel vector autoregressive (mlVAR) model estimated temporal and contemporaneous networks. Edge uncertainty, centrality stability, sensitivity analyses, and between-cycle differences were evaluated. A total of 110 patients contributed 4,134 valid assessments (completion rate, 89.5%). All 13 symptoms showed significant time effects. Fatigue, loss of appetite, gastrointestinal symptoms, and sleep disturbance fluctuated, whereas numbness/tingling and depression showed cumulative trends. Loss of appetite, dry mouth, and nausea had comparatively high outgoing temporal associations. The strongest individual temporal edge was modest (standardized coefficient approximately 0.12). No statistically significant between-cycle differences were found in overall network structure or global strength. Early post-chemotherapy symptoms showed dynamic changes and a broadly comparable network structure across the first two cycles. Loss of appetite, dry mouth, and nausea may be candidates for enhanced monitoring and future intervention research; the observational findings do not establish causal effects or intervention efficacy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To develop and validate an integrative prediction model for colorectal neoplasm (CN) screening to enhance detection effectiveness and provide a noninvasive diagnostic method. This cross-sectional study included 2,047 participants undergoing colonoscopy at Guangdong Provincial Hospital of Chinese Medicine between March 2022 and July 2023. Predictive models were constructed using epidemiological and Traditional Chinese Medicine factors via five machine learning algorithms. Performance was assessed using the area under the curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, DeLong test, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis. Among 1,814 included participants (39.25% with CN), significant predictors included male, age, hypertension, drinking, tongue features, and pigmented nevus of the facial and perioral triangle (all P <0.05). Ten features were selected through univariate and multivariate logistic regression. The Integrative Medicine Colorectal Screening (IMCS) model using extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) achieved the highest training-set AUC (0.817, 95% CI: 0.794-0.841), while the logistic regression (LR) model performed best on the validation set (AUC = 0.690, 95% CI: 0.644-0.736). The IMCS (LR) model outperformed existing models (APCS, M-APCS, CNP; Delong test, all P <0.05), demonstrated strong calibration (mean square error = 0.212, P = 0.425), and showed potential clinical utility (net benefit: 0.144-0.265). The IMCS model improves predictive capability for CN risk and may assist in CN risk stratification. Further large-scale prospective studies are warranted to validate its clinical applicability.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Microsatellite-stable (MSS) colorectal cancer (CRC), which accounts for most metastatic CRC, remains largely resistant to immune checkpoint inhibitors. Although low tumor mutational burden and limited neoantigen generation contribute to this resistance, the spatial organization of the tumor microenvironment may also influence antitumor immunity. This review examines mechanisms that establish immune-resistant architectures in MSS CRC, including insufficient T-cell priming, oncogenic signaling, suppressive myeloid niches, hypoxia, abnormal vasculature, and fibroblast-driven extracellular matrix remodeling. We discuss candidate spatial biomarkers, including compartment-specific T-cell distribution, T-cell-tumor-cell distances, multicellular immune neighborhoods, perivascular niches, and the organization and localization of tertiary lymphoid structures. We also examine how fibroblast heterogeneity, collagen architecture, hyaluronan accumulation, and vascular dysfunction can restrict T-cell access and function. Emerging studies associate selected spatial features with treatment outcomes, but the supporting evidence spans small treatment-specific cohorts, mixed CRC populations, and preclinical or non-CRC models. These findings therefore support spatial profiling as a complement to molecular and clinical biomarkers rather than an independently established basis for treatment selection. Prospective studies in defined treatment settings are needed to clarify the relationship between these spatial features and immunotherapy outcomes and to assess their potential to inform combination strategies in MSS CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cytokines are central to tumor immunity, yet their landscape and clinical utility across cancer types remain incompletely characterized. We selected a representative cytokine panel covering Th1/Th2/Th17, pro-inflammatory, regulatory, and chemokine functions. Using TCGA pan-cancer data, we derived a transcriptomic cytokine index (gCCI) as the difference between pro-tumor and anti-tumor ssGSEA scores and evaluated its associations with prognosis, immune microenvironment, and immunotherapy response. We further validated a protein-level cytokine index (pCCI) using the same formula in an independent cohort of 183 cytokine profiling assays from colorectal cancer patients. The gCCI effectively distinguished tumor from normal tissue in colorectal cancer and stratified survival in multiple cancer types. High gCCI was associated with activated inflammatory pathways by GSEA and showed cancer-type-specific correlations with MSI, TMB, and immune cell infiltration. Notably, low gCCI correlated with better immunotherapy response and prolonged survival in two independent cohorts. In protein-level validation, pCCI was significantly associated with T stage, N stage, M stage, and tumor location (all p < 0.05), with M1c (peritoneal metastasis) showing the highest pCCI levels among M substages. Dichotomized analysis by median pCCI further revealed that high pCCI was significantly enriched in colon cancer patients with M1c, whereas no such associations were observed in rectal cancer. The cytokine index, at both transcriptomic and protein levels, is associated with prognosis and immunotherapy response, with its utility being cancer-type and site-specific. Its particular relevance to colon cancer and peritoneal metastasis warrants further validation in prospective studies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Natural killer (NK) cells are key effectors in innate immunity and serve as early responders against disseminated tumor cells. In colorectal cancer liver metastasis (CRLM), the liver's unique immune landscape presents both challenges and opportunities for NK cell-mediated tumor control. While NK cells have long been considered uniform cytotoxic sentinels, recent studies have reshaped this view by uncovering a diverse spectrum of NK cell states with distinct migratory, transcriptional, and functional programs. These findings reveal a heterogeneous NK-cell compartment in the metastatic liver shaped by tissue context and microenvironmental cues, with distinct residency-associated and functional programs. Advances in high-dimensional single-cell technologies have accelerated the characterization of NK cell heterogeneity, plasticity, and interactions within the metastatic niche. In this review, we summarize recent insights into the evolving roles of NK cells in CRLM, highlighting how they contribute to immune surveillance, niche remodeling, and potential therapeutic modulation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Most microsatellite-stable or mismatch-repair-proficient colorectal cancers respond poorly to immune checkpoint monotherapy. This Mini Review examines whether C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 2 (CXCR2)-associated neutrophil recruitment and local stromal interactions contribute to immune exclusion: CD8+ T cells accumulate in stroma or at the tumor margin with limited entry into epithelial nests. We propose that, in a subset of excluded lesions, recruited neutrophils acquire local functions that impair T-cell activity or access. Human observations and experimental perturbations support parts of this model; the complete pathway has not been established as a major cause of checkpoint resistance. Recruitment dependence, tissue adaptation, and measured function provide a basis for comparing studies with different neutrophil labels. Lesions selected for mechanistic investigation would need confirmed microsatellite-stable or mismatch-repair-proficient status, spatial exclusion, and a relevant intratumoral CXCR2-associated neutrophil program. Primary tumors and metastatic sites require separate evaluation. The limited activity of navarixin plus pembrolizumab argues against unselected targeting. Combining CXCR2 inhibition, selected stromal or vascular modulation, and checkpoint blockade remains a preclinical hypothesis. Before clinical translation, comparative studies must link intratumoral target engagement to improved CD8+ T-cell access, function, and tumor control. The proposed tissue biomarkers are research tools whose predictive value requires validation.
