ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colitis-associated colorectal cancer (CAC) arises through the interaction of chronic mucosal inflammation, genetic evolution and durable changes in gene regulation. Among the inflammatory networks implicated in experimental and human studies, interleukin-6 (IL-6)/Janus kinase (JAK)/signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3) and tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α)/nuclear factor-kappaB (NF-κB) provide mechanistically informative routes by which cytokine exposure can influence DNA methylation, chromatin regulation and non-coding RNA programs. The best-supported examples include IL-6-associated DNMT1 activity and SOCS3 promoter hypermethylation, NF-κB p65/DNMT3A-associated miR-148a methylation, and STAT3-dependent miR-214 induction. These circuits should be regarded as representative mechanisms supported in specific model systems rather than universal initiating pathways in all human CAC lesions. Recent work further demonstrates that colonic stem cells can retain chromatin accessibility changes after experimental colitis resolves, providing direct evidence for durable inflammatory epigenetic memory. This review therefore separates evidence from human CAC or dysplasia, non-neoplastic inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) mucosa, inflammation-driven animal models, sporadic colorectal cancer (CRC) and cell-line systems. We integrate cytokine-linked epigenetic mechanisms with genetic and clonal evolution, define field cancerization operationally, and distinguish persistent epigenetic memory from transient inflammatory transcription. The translational sections are framed as an outlook: no epigenetic biomarker or epigenetic drug is currently established for CAC surveillance or prevention. We summarize the validation requirements for tissue, blood and stool biomarkers; classify therapeutic concepts by evidence level; and propose a patient-level roadmap for single-cell and spatial studies. The resulting framework emphasizes evidence-graded mechanisms and prospective validation rather than assuming that biologically plausible signals are clinically actionable.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Pulmonary metastasectomy (PM) is used in selected patients with pulmonary metastatic disease, but survival-focused reporting incompletely describes recovery and cumulative treatment burden. Following the parenchymal-preservation and repeatability principles discussed by Scanagatta et al. in 2024, this narrative review examines pulmonary function, patient-reported outcomes, repeat resection, treatment sequencing, and retained local-treatment options. A purposive synthesis was updated with six focused PubMed searches on 8 October 2026, including recent surgical studies and function and quality-of-life evidence for non-surgical local treatments. Functional cohorts document early impairment and variable recovery after PM; pulmonary-function data after stereotactic radiotherapy also caution against assuming that avoidance of resection means avoidance of functional loss. Contemporary repeat-resection and modality-comparison studies remain predominantly retrospective and do not establish equivalent recovery or causal survival benefit. Colorectal, sarcoma, and mixed-primary evidence is interpreted separately. We propose "future local-treatment eligibility" as a modality-specific record of technical feasibility, physiological tolerability, and oncological appropriateness, accompanied by a separate assessment of informed patient preference. "Future operability" denotes the surgical component. This organizing construct is unvalidated. Treatment-related limitations must be distinguished from progression, competing illness, patient choice, and access barriers; non-receipt of treatment cannot establish loss of capacity. Candidate longitudinal outcomes and illustrative assessment windows are proposed for stakeholder consensus and feasibility testing, not as an established core outcome set. Histology-specific prospective cohorts with serial function and symptom measurements, inclusive recurrence denominators, and explicit reasons for treatment decisions are needed to evaluate what patients retain after initial and repeat PM.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Acute mesenteric ischemia, including acute exacerbation of chronic mesenteric ischemia (CMI), is a life-threatening condition associated with a 50% in-hospital mortality risk and requires immediate diagnosis, revascularization, and resection of necrotic organs. In colorectal surgery, mesenteric artery stenosis can lead to anastomotic leakage which increases morbidity and mortality. Here, we describe a case of acute exacerbation of CMI caused by severe stenosis of the hepatosplenomesenteric trunk (HSMT) and ligation of the left colic and inferior mesenteric arteries in an earlier rectal surgery that was successfully treated with urgent reno-hepatic artery bypass. An 80-year-old woman was referred to our department with acute exacerbation of CMI after multiple procedures for rectal cancer. Contrast-enhanced CT revealed severe stenosis with calcification at the origin of the HSMT and hypoenhancement of the right hepatic lobe, spleen, and small intestine. Percutaneous antegrade endovascular stenting failed because the lesion was severely calcified. We opted to perform urgent open surgery, including revascularization and resection of the necrotic organs. A bypass from the right renal artery to the proper hepatic artery was selected because of the high risk of failure associated with retrograde open mesenteric stenting, the limited length of available saphenous vein, the risk of anastomotic failure secondary to infection, the patient's poor general condition, and the degree of calcification precluding aortoiliac clamping. Postoperatively, the patient developed Takotsubo cardiomyopathy and disseminated intravascular coagulation, both of which were successfully managed and resolved in the ICU. On POD 24, the patient underwent duodeno-jejunal anastomosis, ileostomy closure, and colostomy. The patient tolerated oral intake well 80 days after arterial bypass surgery and was discharged on POD 147 on single antiplatelet therapy. Although hepato-renal artery bypass is typically used for renal revascularization, reno-hepatic bypass can be useful for mesenteric revascularization in patients with anatomical variations, peritonitis, or severe aortoiliac calcification.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Frailty is recognized as an important predictor of adverse outcomes in older surgical patients. However, evidence regarding preoperative frailty among older patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) admitted to the ICU after surgery remains limited. This study aimed to investigate the prevalence, associated factors, and impact of preoperative frailty risk on in-hospital outcomes in this high-risk population. This single-center retrospective cohort study included 308 older CRC patients who underwent radical surgery and were admitted to the ICU postoperatively between June 2023 and March 2026. Preoperative frailty risk was assessed using the five-item modified Frailty Index (mFI-5). Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with frailty risk and evaluate the association between preoperative frailty risk and postoperative complications. Generalized linear models were applied to assess the associations of frailty risk with total hospital stay, ICU stay, and hospitalization costs. The prevalence of preoperative frailty risk was 55.52% in this study. Higher albumin levels were a protective factor, whereas higher blood glucose levels, elevated NLR, BMI ≥ 26.9 kg/m², polypharmacy, pain, and high fall risk were significantly associated with increased frailty risk. After adjustment for confounders, frailty risk remained an independent predictor of overall complications and severe complications and was significantly associated with prolonged total hospital stay, longer ICU stay, and increased hospitalization costs. Preoperative frailty risk is highly prevalent among older CRC patients admitted to the ICU after surgery and is independently associated with adverse in-hospital outcomes. These findings highlight the importance of incorporating frailty assessment into perioperative management. The mFI-5 is a simple and feasible tool for preoperative risk stratification in this high-risk population and may help guide prehabilitation strategies to ultimately optimize postoperative recovery.

CD24 Acts as an Evolutionarily Conserved Innate Immune Checkpoint in Colorectal Cancer

展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Checkpoint immunotherapy has transformed cancer treatment, yet current approaches targeting adaptive immunity benefit only a subset of patients, leaving innate immunity as a largely untapped therapeutic frontier. Here, we identify CD24 as an innate immune checkpoint that protects colorectal tumors from macrophage-mediated clearance through an evolutionarily conserved recognition mechanism. Using zebrafish xenografts of isogenic colorectal cancer (CRC) cell lines, SW480 and SW620, we show that high CD24 expression in SW620 correlates with an immune-evasive, macrophage-resistant phenotype. Loss of human CD24 dramatically sensitizes tumors to clearance in zebrafish, while pharmacological macrophage depletion abolishes this effect. Mechanistically, CD24 suppresses innate immunity in a multilayered fashion, by limiting myeloid recruitment, dampening TNF-driven macrophage inflammatory polarization, and blocking phagocytosis. Live imaging further revealed that CD24 constrains macrophages to a restrained, patrol-like state, and that its loss enables them to adopt a highly motile, tumor-directed, and functionally engaged state, characterized by increased fusion activity and myeloid intercellular interactions. We show that zebrafish macrophages respond to human CD24 despite extensive evolutionary divergence, and glycocalyx profiling revealed broad remodeling of the tumor cell surface upon CD24 loss, suggesting evolutionary conservation of sialic acid-dependent receptor recognition. Transcriptomic analyses identified the Siglec-like gene si:dkey-24p1.7 as a candidate zebrafish macrophage-expressed receptor mediating this response. Finally, analysis of TCGA CRC cohorts revealed that CD24 expression is a stage-dependent prognostic marker, underscoring the clinical relevance of this axis. Together, these findings establish CD24 as a critical orchestrator of innate immune evasion in CRC, while further validating zebrafish xenografts as a powerful platform for dissecting innate immuno-oncobiology in vivo.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Abstract. In recent years, single cell RNA sequencing (scRNA seq) has enabled the investigation of intercellular communication through Cell Cell Communication (CCC) tools such as CellChat. Despite their potential, these approaches remain challenging to interpret, particularly when global analyses generate complex interaction networks that may include biologically irrelevant signals. To address this limitation, we developed a framework termed CellChat Hotspot, designed to improve the biological interpretability of inferred communication networks. This approach integrates gene set enrichment analysis with a context driven filtering strategy, selecting both genes and cells based on their functional relevance prior to communication inference. Applied to stage II colon cancer data, CellChat Hotspot enabled the identification of condition-specific interaction patterns associated with recurrence. Non recurrent patients showed enrichment of immune related processes, whereas recurrent cases were characterized by pathways associated with invasion and metastasis. Notably, a loss of interaction in the HSPG pathway between CALB1+ and stromal cells was observed in recurrent patients, suggesting a potential disruption of cell matrix adhesion mechanisms. To verify the reliability of this finding, we applied the framework to spatial transcriptomics data, which confirmed the presence of the HSPG2 DAG1 interaction in non-recurrent tumors and its near absence in recurrent ones. Overall, this framework provides a biologically guided strategy for studying intercellular communication in complex systems such as the tumor microenvironment.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Abnormal DNA methylation patterning is a defining epigenetic hallmark of human cancers and is therapeutically targetable with DNA methyltransferase inhibitors (DNMTi's). However, epigenetic plasticity involving Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2)-dependent H3K27 methylation can constrain transcriptional responses to DNMTi's and may contribute to their limited activity in solid tumors. Here, we compare pharmacologic strategies targeting EZH1 and EZH2 in combination with DNMT inhibition in colorectal cancer (CRC) cells and define the molecular features that distinguish EZH2-selective from dual EZH1/2 inhibition. We find that dual EZH1/2 inhibition produces more robust transcriptional activation when combined with DNMT inhibition and more extensive depletion of H3K27 methylation states than EZH2-selective inhibition. Genetic and pharmacologic analyses implicate EZH1-dependent H3K27me1 as an adaptive chromatin barrier to PRC2 inhibitor-mediated chromatin remodeling. Dual EZH1/2 inhibition overcomes this barrier, increasing chromatin accessibility and H3K27 acetylation (H3K27ac) at previously silenced regulatory regions. EZH2 inhibition also induces a non-canonical bivalent chromatin state in which persistent DNA methylation maintains transcriptional repression despite acquisition of the activating H3K27ac mark. Combined DNMT inhibition resolves this additional drug-induced chromatin barrier, enhancing the activation of tumor-suppressive and stress response-associated transcriptional programs. Collectively, our studies reveal adaptive chromatin barriers that limit EZH inhibitor-mediated transcriptional activation and demonstrate how combined EZH1/2 and DNMT inhibition overcomes these consequences of drug-induced epigenetic plasticity in CRC cells. These findings provide a mechanistic framework for further evaluation of combined DNMT and EZH1/2 inhibition in solid tumors.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Background: Early-Onset Colorectal Cancer (EOCRC, < 50 years) is rising sharply in many parts of the world. The "obesity paradox", where overweight correlates with better outcome despite obesity being a risk factor, is established in colorectal cancer (CRC) overall but remains ambiguous in EOCRC. Aim: To investigate the association of Body Mass Index (BMI) at diagnosis and recurrence-free survival (RFS) in EOCRC and compare it to average-onset colorectal cancer (AOCRC, older than or equal to 50 years). Methods: A retrospective cohort study at Sahlgrenska University Hospital included 1,459 patients with curative-intent colorectal adenocarcinoma surgery comprising EOCRC (n=159) and AOCRC (n=1,300) cohorts. Cox proportional hazards models assessed the relation of BMI to RFS, adjusted for tumour stage, location, and differentiation. Restricted cubic splines were used to model BMI as a continuous variable, and model fit was assessed with likelihood-ratio tests (LRT). Results: In EOCRC, continuous BMI was significantly associated with RFS (LRT p=0.02), displaying a U-shaped association with the lowest hazard at BMI 27 and highest at BMI <20 and >30. In AOCRC continuous BMI was not associated with RFS (LRT p=0.15) and the spline curve was flat. An interaction analysis showed a significant difference between the cohorts (LRT p=0.046). Conclusion: Continuous BMI was significantly associated with RFS in EOCRC but not in AOCRC suggesting the "obesity paradox" may be specific to EOCRC. This may reflect differences in body composition, tumour biology and systemic metabolism between EOCRC and AOCRC or may be due to methodological biases. Future research should incorporate biomarkers, as well as refined measures of body composition.

意义与启示：更新证据显示T2DM使结直肠癌风险增加约27%，提示应将T2DM作为CRC风险分层与筛查加强的标记，但未直接涉及肝转移。

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Epidemiologic studies suggest that type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is associated with an increased risk of colorectal cancer (CRC). However, prior meta-analyses have relied heavily on studies published more than a decade ago and have often combined distinct epidemiologic effect measures. We conducted an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies published from January 2012 through January 2026 evaluating the association between T2DM and incident CRC. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, CENTRAL, and Scopus were searched, and eligible studies reporting associations between T2DM and CRC were included. Effect estimates were synthesized separately using random-effects models to calculate pooled estimates with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Sex-specific and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were also conducted. Fourteen studies were included, comprising nine cohort and five case-control studies; six reported odds ratios (ORs), seven reported hazard ratios (HRs), and one reported a standardized incidence ratio (SIR). T2DM was associated with higher odds of incident CRC (OR, 1.28; 95% CI, 1.13-1.46) and a higher hazard of incident CRC (HR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.23-1.31). The study reporting an SIR also showed higher CRC incidence among individuals with T2DM (SIR, 1.40; 95% CI, 1.39-1.45). Sex-specific analyses generally showed positive associations in both females and males, and sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of the pooled findings. Overall, T2DM was associated with an increased risk of incident CRC, with a consistent direction of association across distinct epidemiologic effect measures. These findings provide updated evidence supporting consideration of T2DM as a marker of increased CRC risk and may inform CRC prevention strategies among individuals with T2DM.

Fourteen studies were included, comprising nine cohort and five case-control studies; six reported odds ratios (ORs), seven reported hazard ratios (HRs), and one reported a standardized incidence ratio (SIR). T2DM was associated with higher odds of incident CRC (OR, 1.28; 95% CI, 1.13-1.46) and a higher hazard of incident CRC (HR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.23-1.31). The study reporting an SIR also showed higher CRC incidence among individuals with T2DM (SIR, 1.40; 95% CI, 1.39-1.45). Sex-specific analyses generally showed positive associations in both females and males, and sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of the pooled findings. Overall, T2DM was associated with an increased risk of incident CRC, with a consistent direction of association across distinct epidemiologic effect measures. These findings provide updated evidence supporting consideration of T2DM as a marker of increased CRC risk and may inform CRC prevention strategies among individuals with T2DM.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Plasma is a rich and accessible source for biomarkers. The analytical challenge of the steep dynamic range was recently addressed using enrichment technologies. Enrichment technologies have been shown to be sensitive to preanalytical variables, making this an active area of research. We established the P2 enrichment system as high-performing and robust for large scale studies, with reproducible identifications and precision across batches, days, operators and laboratories. We characterized P2-based enrichment for preanalytical variables (eight blood collection types, centrifugation, freeze-thaw and pathogen inactivation). K2EDTA-plasma resulted in the deepest proteome coverage with about 6000 protein groups on the timsTOF HT. We spiked 16 heavy-labelled proteins into platelet-poor and platelet-contaminated plasma. Importantly, linearity, accuracy, and precision were high in both platelet-poor and platelet-contaminated plasma for both P2-enriched and neat preparations. In a cancer cohort, we demonstrated that 97% of differentially abundant proteins retained the same direction of regulation after P2-based enrichment compared with the neat preparation. Differentially abundant proteins identified in a colorectal cancer pilot cohort remained largely conserved after platelet contamination, including previously reported biomarkers. We demonstrated that P2-based enrichment enables deep, large scale proteome profiling and preserves biological information despite preanalytical variation. Candidates emerging from P2-based discovery can be validated in independent cohorts with targeted assays.

意义与启示：SpOTr方法通过融合进化树与空间分布，将单细胞克隆映射到空间位置，为肠癌肝转移的克隆空间演化研究提供新工具。

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The spatial organization of evolving cell populations in tumors influences how they progress and respond to treatment. Spatially resolved transcriptomics data may be used to examine the locations of these diverse cell states in tumor sections. However, these technologies often lack single-cell resolution and instead capture groups of cells in spatial spots, making it difficult to resolve cancer clones. In contrast, dissociated single-cell transcriptomics data are better suited for obtaining cell lineages, but do not capture the locations of the cells in the tissue. Here, we introduce SpOTr, an optimal transport approach that leverages the concordance between the evolutionary tree and the spatial distribution of cancer cells to integrate single-cell and spatial transcriptomics data from tumors. SpOTr combines a spot deconvolution model with Fused Gromov-Wasserstein optimal transport, in which cells that are close in the tree are drawn to nearby spots. In simulations and in real spatial lineage tracing data, SpOTr recovered the spatial locations of clones better than methods that ignore the tree. In a human colorectal liver metastasis, SpOTr mapped copy number clones from dissociated cells to spatial spots, showing that it successfully maps the evolutionary history of tumors in space.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Background: Conventional chemotherapies remain the core therapeutic backbone of cancer treatment, yet the rapid emergence of chemoresistance often compromises their clinical efficacy. Although large-scale functional genomics has transformed precision oncology, existing reference maps rely predominantly on loss-of-function paradigms and lack systematic data on gain-of-function (GOF) events that commonly drive clinical resistance. Methods: To address this gap, we engineered a site-specific Bxb1 integrase landing-pad system in HeLa cells, enabling single-copy integration of a human proteome-wide library [18,388 open reading frames (ORFs)] at the AAVS1 locus under a uniform EF1 promoter. We systematically profiled cellular fitness across 16 chemotherapeutics. We integrated this GOF perturbation screen with bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, FACS-based lysosomal functional screening, clinical cohort survival analyses, and preclinical xenograft modeling. Results: Stratified modeling of over 230,000 gene-drug interactions defined distinct functional categories that are strongly enriched for clinical cancer biomarkers and prognostic relevance. Global network analysis and organelle-specific lysosomal functional screening uncovered that chemotherapeutic agents, most prominently the nucleoside analog TAS-102 (Lonsurf), converge upon a shared survival hub centered on the BCL-2 family-associated autophagy-endolysosomal network. Mechanistically, TAS-102 triggered lysosomal activation as an adaptive survival response. Co-treatment with the BCL-2 family inhibitor ABT-263 (Navitoclax) attenuated this TAS-102-induced lysosomal response and synergistically reversed TAS-102 resistance across colorectal and pancreatic cancer models in vitro and in colorectal cell line- and patient-derived xenograft (CDX, PDX) models in vivo. Conclusions: Our study establishes an open-access, proteome-wide GOF reference atlas that systematically maps chemotherapeutic responses, recapitulates canonical resistance biology, and nominates rational drug combinations. This systems-genomics resource bridges massive-scale perturbation mapping with actionable target discovery, providing a translational framework to overcome therapeutic resistance and reprogram cancer drug responses.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) in colorectal cancer (CRC) are commonly characterized at the gene level, obscuring processed RNA architectures and regional localization. In renal cell carcinoma, a processed CRNDE isoform retaining an ultraconserved element (UCE) with a C/D snoRNA-like region promotes pre-60S maturation. Here, we examined CRNDE UCE-region representation and integrated CRC tumor expression and clinical evidence with published HEK293 cross-linking and immunoprecipitation (CLIP) profiles for C/D small nucleolar ribonucleoprotein (snoRNP) proteins and long-read sequencing to identify retained CLIP-supported regions. CRNDE was upregulated in 49 of 50 paired tumors, and UCE-region signal was detected in 380 of 382 assessable primary tumors, although total CRNDE abundance showed little association with stage or outcome. Processed UCE-retaining CRNDE transcripts were identified in Caco-2 cells. Integration identified 1,714 disease-supported lncRNAs with CLIP overlap; among 576 non-CRNDE candidates, 188 CLIP-supported regions were retained within processed transcripts from 65 loci in both CRC cell models. Region-directed RT-qPCR following pre-ribosome sequential extraction revealed preferential enrichment of selected JPX, DLEU2, and LINC00630 RNA populations in the core nucleolar fraction relative to broader transcript-region measurements in both cell lines. These findings identify retained-region transcript architectures and reveal region-dependent nucleolar enrichment not apparent from broader transcript measurements.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Oncogenic alleles of KRAS drive colorectal cancers (CRC) growth and are associated with worse disease outcomes. Despite potent allele-specific and pan-RAS inhibitors targeting now in clinical test, CRC patients are not experiencing the same therapeutic benefit as patients with other cancers. PI3-Kinase (PI3K) is a direct RAS effector and is co-mutated in about 45% of CRC cases, raising the possibility that frequent oncogenic PI3K mutations contribute to the limited benefit of KRAS inhibition in CRC. Using isogenic colorectal cancer cells engineered to harbor either of the two most common activating PIK3CA mutations, we show that oncogenic PI3K promotes resistance to the pan-RAS inhibitor daraxonrasib (RMC-6236). Global phosphoproteomic profiling revealed that PIK3CA-mutant cells undergo a distinct adaptive response to RAS inhibition, characterized by sustained PI3K-AKT signaling and extensive remodeling of pathways controlling cell-cell adhesion and junction signaling, alongside suppression of apoptotic signaling. Combined RAS and PI3K inhibition overcame this resistance, suppressed signaling through both pathways and induced apoptosis in PIK3CA-mutant cells. Together, these findings identify oncogenic PIK3CA as a determinant of resistance to RAS inhibition in KRAS-mutant colorectal cancer and provide a mechanistic rationale for combined KRAS and PI3K inhibition in KRAS/PIK3CA co-mutant tumors.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Increased matrix metalloproteinase (MMP) expression has long been recognized as a common feature of colorectal cancers (CRCs), yet less is known about how these enzymes interact to impact cancer progression. Of particular interest is MMP expression overlap where multi-substrate targeting can accelerate extracellular matrix (ECM) breakdown. Taking advantage of single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data, we analyzed MMP expression in CRCs, focusing on cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), myeloid cells, and cancer cells. Single-cell RNA-seq data revealed that distinct CAF subtypes express different MMP combinations, including MMP1/2/3 and MMP2/11-expressing CAFs. Evidence was also obtained that the number of MMP1-expressing CAFs in CRCs is highly variable, likely impacting stromal ECM dynamics. In contrast to CAFs, myeloid cells (monocytes, macrophages, and dendritic cells) all expressed varying levels of the same myeloid MMPs 9, 12, and 14, with MMP expression correlated with a cells secretory potential, a phenotype that would facilitate MMP release. Finally, a subpopulation of cancer cells expressed high levels of MMP7, which was frequently co-expressed with several Wnt-related genes. Analysis of spatial transcriptomic data showed MMP expression clusters, driven largely by cell-type, with regions of notable MMP expression overlap. High resolution spatial analysis revealed clusters of cells at the cancer-stroma interface expressing a broad spectrum of MMPs. These multi-MMP expression clusters included cancer cells, CAFs, and myeloid cells all expressing MMP7 and a broad range of other MMPs. These multi-MMP foci also exhibited elevated Wnt signaling and EMT markers and may represent sites from which cancer cells escape the primary lesion.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The role of cytotoxic CD4+ T cells in cancer remains controversial, with both pro- and anti-tumor functionality described. Based on a prior observation that putatively cytotoxic KLRG1+ FoxP3- conventional T cells (Tconv) associated with tumor progression, we deeply investigated the phenotype and function of KLRG1+ Tconv in multiple murine tumor models and in human clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) specimens. We found KLRG1+ Tconv have a conserved, highly activated, terminally differentiated phenotype across species. In murine tumors, KLRG1+ Tconv resemble tumor-infiltrating regulatory T cells (Tregs) at both transcriptional and proteomic levels, upregulating a spectrum of exhaustion-related checkpoint receptors, producing IL-10 and granzyme B (GzmB), and silencing expression of IFN{gamma} and TNF. Functionally, KLRG1+ Tconv exhibited immunosuppressive function in ex vivo assays. Using an in vivo Treg fate mapping approach in tumor-bearing mice, we found a subset of KLRG1+ Tconv are derived from Tregs that have lost FoxP3 protein expression. Ex vivo functional assays demonstrated the exTreg component of the KLRG1+ Tconv compartment is responsible for IL-10 production and reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine expression. In treatment studies, we found that KLRG1-targeted antibody-mediated depletion was more efficient than anti-KLRG1 blockade at slowing tumor growth and improving survival, with responses associating with depletion of intratumoral KLRG1+ Tconv and Tregs. In sum, our study discovered a novel conserved pathway of CD4+ T cell plasticity, wherein intratumoral, cytotoxic KLRG1+ CD4+ Tconv cells can be derived from Tregs and maintain immunosuppressive function, despite loss of FoxP3, and that KLRG1-targeted depletion may outperform KLRG1 blockade as an immunotherapeutic strategy in cancer.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Abstract. In recent years, single cell RNA sequencing (scRNA seq) has enabled the investigation of intercellular communication through Cell Cell Communication (CCC) tools such as CellChat. Despite their potential, these approaches remain challenging to interpret, particularly when global analyses generate complex interaction networks that may include biologically irrelevant signals. To address this limitation, we developed a framework termed CellChat Hotspot, designed to improve the biological interpretability of inferred communication networks. This approach integrates gene set enrichment analysis with a context driven filtering strategy, selecting both genes and cells based on their functional relevance prior to communication inference. Applied to stage II colon cancer data, CellChat Hotspot enabled the identification of condition-specific interaction patterns associated with recurrence. Non recurrent patients showed enrichment of immune related processes, whereas recurrent cases were characterized by pathways associated with invasion and metastasis. Notably, a loss of interaction in the HSPG pathway between CALB1+ and stromal cells was observed in recurrent patients, suggesting a potential disruption of cell matrix adhesion mechanisms. To verify the reliability of this finding, we applied the framework to spatial transcriptomics data, which confirmed the presence of the HSPG2 DAG1 interaction in non-recurrent tumors and its near absence in recurrent ones. Overall, this framework provides a biologically guided strategy for studying intercellular communication in complex systems such as the tumor microenvironment.

bioRxiv (预印本) · 2026-11-10 · Wang, L.-M.; Kin, T. C.; Hung, W.-C.; Shi, Y.
意义与启示：该研究揭示益生菌来源胞外囊泡可缓解肠道细胞氧化损伤，为肠癌化学预防提供新思路，但尚需体内验证。

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Dietary trimethylamine (TMA) underwent gut microbiota-mediated catabolism and subsequent hepatic oxidation to generate trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO), a key metabolic factor linked to vascular and colorectal diseases. While the systemic effects of circulating TMAO were heavily investigated, the direct localized cellular interactions of its precursor, TMA, at the intestinal epithelial level required further elucidation. This study characterized extracellular vesicles isolated from Lactobacillus rhamnosus (Lr-EVs) and evaluated their cytoprotective potential in an in vitro human intestinal Caco-2 cell model under TMA-induced stress. Exposure to a high concentration of TMA (20 mM) significantly reduced Caco-2 viability to 78.8%, triggered intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, and compromised tight junction integrity as observed via the disruption of Zonula Occludens-1 (ZO-1) alignment. Co-treatment with Lr-EVs (100-300 g/mL) counteracted this cellular toxicity, enhancing cell survival up to 172%. Quantitative PCR analysis revealed that Lr-EVs suppressed the transcriptional upregulation of the pro-inflammatory gene IL-1{beta}, restored the expression of the metabolic regulator SIRT1, and stabilized transcript levels of key mitochondrial-encoded electron transport chain genes (ND6, CYTB, CO1, and ATP6). Additionally, Lr-EVs exhibited intrinsic radical scavenging activities in cell-free ABTS and DPPH assays. These preliminary in vitro findings demonstrated that Lr-EVs mitigated TMA-induced cellular injury, oxidative stress, and junctional disruption at the transcriptomic level, supporting further investigation of probiotic-derived EVs as prospective cell-free functional ingredients.

KLONE: An Imbalance-Robust k-NN Ensemble for Cross-Modal Single-Cell Clone Assignment
bioRxiv (预印本) · 2026-11-10 · Huang, X.; Ye, S.; Silva, A.; Nakhleh, L.
意义与启示：KLONE无需RNA克隆标签即可准确将scRNA-seq细胞分配至scDNA-seq克隆，并克服克隆不平衡，为肠癌肝转移的克隆-转录组关联研究提供新工具。
展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Single-cell DNA sequencing (scDNA-seq) and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enable the inference of copy number clones and transcriptional states in tumor studies. However, these two assays usually profile different cells of the same tumor, requiring computational assignment of unpaired scRNA-seq cells to clones identified by scDNA-seq to link clonal genotypes with transcriptional profiles. This task is challenging because the only connection between the two modalities is a weak, gene-dependent dosage effect, and the absence of clone labels for RNA cells precludes supervised learning of this relationship. Moreover, clonal distributions may differ between the two modalities because the cells are profiled independently, while the inherent clonal imbalance of real tumors can leave minority subclones underrepresented, further compromising assignment accuracy. To address these challenges, we present KLONE, a per-clone $k$-nearest-neighbor ($k$-NN) ensemble that assigns RNA cells directly to copy-number clones based on cross-modal Pearson similarity, without the need for a parametric model or clone labels for RNA cells. To ensure a fair assessment of each clone's compatibility with a given RNA cell, KLONE allocates an identical neighborhood budget to every clone, preventing majority clones from dominating the affinity assessment solely through their greater abundance. We compare KLONE with six existing methods on three colorectal cancer patients, using cells profiled in both modalities as ground truth. KLONE is the most accurate method and recalls minority clones at 100\%. Despite discrepancies in clonal distribution between the two modalities, KLONE recovers the clonal distribution of RNA cells almost perfectly ($\rho = 0.99$).

Statistical significance testing for spatial domain detection in spatial transcriptomics
bioRxiv (预印本) · 2026-11-10 · Wang, H.; Cao, F.; Shen, H.; Liu, Y.; Yan, G.
意义与启示：SigDoTS通过假设检验框架减少空间域过度分割，提升空间转录组分析的可靠性，为肠癌及肝转移微环境空间域划分提供更稳健的方法学工具。
展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
In spatial transcriptomics, domain-detection methods group platform-specific spatial measurement units--cells, bins or multicellular spots--into spatial domains for comparing molecular programs, cellular composition and interactions among tissue regions. However, the number of candidate domains detected in the same tissue can vary with user-specified parameters or model-selection criteria. Whether candidate domains should be merged can be framed as a test of a single-domain null hypothesis, under which each gene has constant mean expression across all spatial units in the combined region. However, testing candidate domains on the same gene-expression data used to detect them may induce post-selection bias and yield anti-conservative p-values, increasing the risk of oversegmentation. To address these challenges, we introduce SigDoTS (statistical Significance testing for Domain deTection in Spatial transcriptomics), a hypothesis-testing framework for spatial domain detection. SigDoTS uses hierarchical testing to determine which candidate domains to retain or merge, with adjustment for family-wise error control. It accounts for gene-gene covariance and spatial dependence and computes p-values by rerunning the upstream domain-detection pipeline on datasets simulated under the fitted single-domain null. In simulations, SigDoTS controlled the type I error rate at the root node under the single-domain null and improved recovery of the true spatial domains when multiple domains were present. In human dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, SigDoTS retained superficial and deep Layer 6 domains but merged Layer 3 candidate domains across different initial numbers of candidate domains. In ovarian and colorectal cancers, SigDoTS retained epithelial domains with different gene-expression programs and local immune environments, together with immune, stromal and vascular domains.

结直肠癌中细胞类型分辨的病毒信号图谱
Uncovering Viral Signals Across Cell Populations in Colorectal Cancer
bioRxiv (预印本) · 2026-11-10 · Mahmanzar, M.; Rahimian, K.; Kavousi, K.; Deng, Y.
意义与启示：该研究构建了结直肠癌中细胞类型分辨的病毒RNA信号图谱，揭示了病毒信号在肿瘤微环境中的分布差异，为病毒-宿主互作及免疫治疗策略提供了新视角。
展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Viral sequences have been detected in colorectal cancer, but their cellular and anatomical distribution remains poorly resolved. We aimed to establish a cell-type-resolved map of viral reference-associated RNA signals across colorectal cancer, tumour-adjacent normal tissue, and healthy colon. We repurposed human-unmapped reads from single-cell RNA sequencing libraries generated in ten publicly available studies. We retained cell-barcode and unique molecular identifier information, removed duplicate molecules, and aligned reads to a curated human-associated viral reference using three aligners. Viral signals were analysed across cell types, tissue conditions, and colorectal segments. We used participant-grouped repeated cross-validation to evaluate tissue-condition classification and screened an independent paired colorectal cancer proteomics cohort for compatible peptide matches. The study included 547 libraries from 112 participants, including 49 with matched colorectal cancer and tumour-adjacent normal samples, and approximately 415,000 cells spanning ten major cell populations. Viral reference-associated RNA signals differed across epithelial, immune, stromal, and vascular compartments, tissue conditions, and anatomical regions of the colon. Of 318 independent healthy-reference viral-load comparisons, seven involving six virus-cell-type groups remained significant after Benjamini-Hochberg correction, including plasma-cell HHV-7 and HHV-6B and mast-cell HCV-2. Cell-type-resolved viral features distinguished colorectal cancer, tumour-adjacent normal tissue, and healthy colon in participant-grouped validation; random forest achieved a macro-AUC of 0.957 (SD 0.028), with HERV-K113 as the leading quantitative feature. An independent proteomic screen identified peptide matches compatible with 20 candidate viral groups. We established a cell-type-resolved map of viral reference-associated RNA signals across colorectal tissue conditions and anatomical regions. By identifying candidate viral signals in epithelial and immune compartments, this map provides a basis for investigating virus-host pathways involved in tumour biology, immune regulation, and antigen-presentation states, and could help prioritise future combination strategies pairing virus-directed or virus-mimetic approaches with standard treatment or immune checkpoint blockade.

LingoCell：连接单细胞与空间转录组的语言基础模型
LingoCell interprets gene perturbations through natural language and tissue niches
bioRxiv (预印本) · 2026-11-10 · Yang, Y.; Xu, W.; Zhang, Z.; Cui, Y.; Yu, X.; Gu, W.; Wang, J.; Nakai, K.
意义与启示：LingoCell实现单细胞与空间转录组的语言对齐及可编辑扰动模拟，在结直肠癌中揭示同一成纤维细胞状态对T细胞、巨噬细胞和肿瘤细胞传递不同程序，为靶点组合与基质干预提供新框架。
展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Single-cell foundation models are general tools for resolving cell identities and disease states, but struggle to interpret changes in expression magnitude in biological language, to transfer to sparse spatial measurements, and to explain cellular niches. We introduce LingoCell, a foundation model connecting single-cell and spatial transcriptomics. It aligns cell representations with language while keeping gene expression editable, supporting cell annotation, cross-batch integration, description generation, and disease-language readouts of single-gene and combinatorial in silico perturbations. Extended to tissues, it annotates cells without single-cell references, learns identity-conditioned niche embeddings, and performs spatial in silico perturbation by replacing and editing neighbor expression. In lung adenocarcinoma, LingoCell revealed synergistic disease responses to jointly weakening alveolar differentiation programs and strengthening malignant programs. In colorectal cancer, it revealed different programs conveyed by the same fibroblast state to T cells, macrophages, and tumor cells. LingoCell provides a unified framework for prioritizing target combinations and stromal intervention programs.

Preclinical Evaluation of a Novel BOC-Modified Triazoloacridinone (TRA-01AR) in Combination with 5-Fluorouracil in Colorectal Cancer
bioRxiv (预印本) · 2026-11-10 · Switalska, M.; Czechowicz, P.; Milczarek, M.; Bartoszewska, S.; Filip-Psurska, B.; Wierzbicka, K.; Psurski, M.; Szczesny, D.; Turlej, E.; Krzyminski, K.; Gawronska, M.; Gebert, M.; Kalinowski, L.; Crossman, D. K.; Baginski, M.; Markuszewski, M.; Collawn, J. F.; Schaefer, L.; Bartoszewski, R.; Wietrzyk, J.
意义与启示：该研究揭示三唑吖啶酮类化合物可调控5-FU应答相关的转录与代谢程序，但TRA-01AR联合5-FU未显著增强疗效，提示需进一步优化联合策略。
展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
5-Fluorouracil (5-FU) remains a cornerstone of colorectal cancer (CRC) therapy, yet its clinical efficacy is limited by resistance, systemic toxicity, and unfavorable pharmacokinetics. Strategies that enhance tumor sensitivity while maintaining tolerability are therefore of considerable interest. Here, we evaluated 5-FU in combination with two triazoloacridinones, C-1305 and a novel BOC-modified derivative, TRA-01AR, using integrated cellular, transcriptomic, bioenergetic, and in vivo approaches. Both compounds induced cytotoxic effects across cancer cell models and produced overlapping but distinct transcriptional responses, primarily affecting DNA replication and cell cycle pathways. Bioenergetic profiling revealed a shift toward oxidative phosphorylation accompanied by reduced glycolysis, indicating modulation of cellular metabolism relevant to chemotherapy response. Interestingly, TRA-01AR exhibited delayed cytotoxicity relative to C-1305, although the underlying mechanism remains to be defined. In vivo, the combination of 5-FU with C-1305 significantly reduced tumor weight in HT-29 xenografts, whereas 5-FU combined with TRA-01AR did not result in a statistically significant reduction compared to 5-FU alone. TRA-01AR was associated with a more favorable systemic profile and increased intratumoral blood flow compared with C-1305. Collectively, these findings indicate that triazoloacridinones modulate transcriptional and metabolic programs relevant to the 5-FU response. While C-1305 demonstrated greater antitumor activity under the tested conditions, TRA-01AR exhibited distinct biological effects, including improved tolerability and vascular modulation. Further studies are required to clarify TRA-01AR's mechanism of action and assess its potential relevance in CRC-specific therapies.

Improving Consistency in Colorectal Cancer Genetic Risk Assessment and Return of Results Through an Integrated Polygenic Risk Score
medRxiv (预印本) · 2026-11-09 · Tran, H.; Mulford, A. J.; Wei, J.; Shi, Z.; Ashworth, A.; Zheng, S. L.; Helfand, B. T.; Hulick, P. J.; DePersia, A.; Suh, G.; Jones, B.; Sanders, A. R.; Xu, J.
意义与启示：整合多个已发表PRS可提高个体高风险分类一致性而不损失预测性能，为肠癌遗传风险评估的标准化和临床落地提供框架。
展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
BackgroundPublished colorectal cancer (CRC) polygenic risk scores (PRS) may demonstrate similar population-level predictive performance but often assign substantially different risk classifications to the same individuals. Such discordance presents challenges for clinical implementation and return of results (RoR). MethodsWe developed a stable PRS for CRC (stPRS-CRC) by integrating 28 published PRS using PRSmix in the All of Us (AoU) development cohort (n=321,703). Performance was evaluated in a held-out AoU validation cohort (n=80,423) and independently validated in the Genomic Health Initiative (GHI) (n=17,545). CRC associations were assessed using logistic regression, comparing individuals in the highest PRS decile with the remaining 90%. Individual-level concordance in high-risk classification was evaluated using mean Jaccard indices. ResultsPublished CRC PRS showed substantial discordance in individual-level high-risk classification despite generally consistent associations with CRC. stPRS-CRC integrated information from multiple published PRS and demonstrated CRC associations comparable to PGS003852, the strongest-performing individual PRS. The odds ratios for stPRS-CRC were 1.94 (95% CI, 1.79-2.11) in AoU development, 2.08 (1.76-2.45) in AoU validation, and 2.08 (1.55-2.79) in GHI. Mean Jaccard indices using stPRS-CRC versus PGS003852 as anchors, each compared with the same 27 published PRS, were 0.29 versus 0.20, 0.43 versus 0.25, and 0.27 versus 0.19, respectively (all P<0.001). ConclusionsIntegrating multiple published CRC PRS significantly improved individual-level concordance in high-risk classification while maintaining population-level predictive performance. stPRS-CRC may provide a more consistent framework for clinical genetic risk assessment and ROR.

展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer is the fourth most frequently diagnosed cancer and the second leading cause of cancer death in the United States. Treatment of localized disease usually includes surgery, sometimes followed by adjuvant systemic therapy, while advanced or metastatic disease is often treated with multiple lines of systemic therapy, based on biomarker status. These NCCN Guidelines Insights detail recent updates to the NCCN Guidelines for Colon Cancer, including recommendations for pretreatment DPYD testing to decrease the risk of severe fluoropyrimidine toxicity; updates to adjuvant therapy of nonmetastatic colon cancer based on the results of recent clinical trials; and a reorganization of the systemic therapies for advanced or metastatic disease based on biomarker status, highlighting changes to the treatment recommendations for BRAF V600E mutation-positive disease.

本周热点与趋势总结

由本期文献提炼的课题组可执行信号
  1. 【微生物组靶向治疗：F. nucleatum阳性MSS转移性CRC的去化疗联合策略】Cancer Cell发表的多中心单臂2期试验（NCT06356597）在33例F. nucleatum阳性、MSS转移性CRC患者中评估替雷利珠单抗+呋喹替尼+甲硝唑三联方案，达到主要终点，中位PFS 6.0个月，ORR 19.4%、DCR 83.9%；同期Cancer Cell配发评论指出，脉冲式、针对厌氧菌的甲硝唑可在不引发全局菌群失调的前提下选择性瓦解致病菌网络，逆转免疫检查点阻断耐药，为生物标志物驱动的MSS肠癌精准分层提供了可复制的范式。
  2. 【肠道菌群调控肿瘤内胆固醇代谢：4-cholesten-3-one的抑癌作用】Nature Metabolism报道，通过肠道菌群重定向胆固醇代谢生成的代谢物4-cholesten-3-one（4-C-3）在CRC患者粪便及肿瘤样本中显著耗竭，并在细胞系、患者来源类器官及异种移植模型中抑制肿瘤生长，机制上同时抑制两条主要通路；该研究提示避免全身性降脂、转而靶向菌群-胆固醇轴可能兼顾疗效与安全性，是代谢-微生物交叉领域向临床转化的重要一步。
  3. 【局部治疗与物理-免疫联合：超声驱动溶瘤细菌增敏系统免疫】JACS报道聚精氨酸功能化肽-声敏剂偶联物可突破革兰阴性外膜屏障，在超声驱动下原位粉碎肿瘤内F. nucleatum，唤醒固有免疫并实现系统性抗肿瘤效应；该策略与Cancer Cell的甲硝唑方案形成互补——前者追求局部精准去菌、避免广谱抗生素所致菌群失调，提示“菌群靶向+免疫治疗”正从全身用药向局部物理调控拓展。
  4. 【表观遗传与化疗耐药机制：CARM1-H3R17me2a/FUS轴】Drug Resistance Updates通过单细胞测序与患者队列分析发现，CARM1在恶性上皮细胞中高表达且与不良预后相关；缺氧经ERK-EGR1通路转录上调CARM1并抑制DUSP2以维持该轴激活，进而通过H3R17me2a上调FUS介导CRC化疗耐药，野生型而非磷酸化缺陷型CARM1可重现该表型，为缺氧相关耐药提供了可干预的表观遗传靶点。
  5. 【遗传易感与指南更新：Lynch综合征筛查与结肠癌NCCN v3.2026】Lancet综述指出Lynch综合征影响约1/350–450人群，但多数携带者未被诊断，通用肿瘤MMR缺陷检测已重塑病例识别路径；同期JNCCN发布的NCCN结肠癌指南v3.2026新增治疗前DPYD检测以降低氟嘧啶严重毒性风险，并更新辅助治疗推荐，二者共同强调分子分型（MMR/DPYD）应前移至治疗决策起点。
  6. 【免疫微环境与T细胞分化：外周CD4+干细胞样T细胞的分化与招募】Science利用成像质谱流式在CRC患者中观察到Th1样干细胞样CD4+ T细胞亚群，提出通过扩增外周T细胞并促进其向肿瘤募集来增强免疫治疗的新思路，突破了以往仅聚焦瘤内免疫抑制微环境的局限；该发现与IgA抑制上皮增殖与肿瘤发生的Nature研究共同提示，黏膜免疫与外周免疫区室是肠癌免疫干预尚未充分开发的靶区。
